title.en: Rape and sexual violence: national data
title.hg: Rape aur sexual violence: national data

text.en: Police in India registered 29,536 cases of rape in 2024, involving 29,742 women and girls, a rate of 4.3 cases per lakh women, according to the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB).
text.hg: National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke mutabik, 2024 mein India mein police ne rape ke 29,536 cases register kiye, jo 29,742 mahilaon aur ladkiyon se jude the; yeh har lakh mahilaon par 4.3 cases ka rate hai.

facts.caveat: Police-registered FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule); sexual violence is heavily under-reported. Rate uses projected female population (6,833.4 lakh). Most rape of girls under 18 is counted separately under the POCSO Act (see vio-pocso-girls-penetrative-2024). CII 2024 was released on 6 May 2026 and is the latest edition as of November 2026.

text.en: NCRB's Crime in India 2024 report, the latest edition available as of November 2026, was released by the Union Home Ministry on Wednesday, 6 May 2026.
text.hg: NCRB ki 'Crime in India 2024' report, jo November 2026 tak available sabse latest edition hai, Union Home Ministry ne Wednesday, 6 May 2026 ko jaari ki thi.

facts.caveat: Date inferred from ThePrint's 7 May 2026 article saying the report was released on Wednesday (6 May 2026).

text.en: Of the 29,536 rape cases registered in India in 2024, 19,683 were filed under the Indian Penal Code and 9,853 under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein register hue rape ke 29,536 cases mein se 19,683 Indian Penal Code (IPC) ke tahat aur 9,853 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke tahat file hue; BNS ne 1 July 2024 se IPC ki jagah li.

facts.caveat: 2024 is a transition year with two penal codes; Table 1.2 rates are per lakh total population (2.1), not per lakh women.

text.en: Police in India registered 4,41,534 cases of crime against women in 2024, a fall of 1.5% from 4,48,211 cases in 2023.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne mahilaon ke khilaf crime ke 4,41,534 cases register kiye, jo 2023 ke 4,48,211 cases se 1.5% kam hai.

facts.caveat: Includes IPC/BNS and special-law offences (e.g. POCSO with girl victims, Dowry Prohibition Act). 2022: 4,45,256 cases. A dip in registered cases is not proof of a dip in violence.

text.en: The rate of registered crime against women in India was 64.6 cases per lakh women in 2024, down from 66.2 in 2023.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein mahilaon ke khilaf registered crime ka rate har lakh mahilaon par 64.6 cases raha, jo 2023 ke 66.2 se kam hai.

facts.caveat: Rates by year: 58.8 (2018), 62.4 (2019, later revised 62.3), 56.5 (2020), 64.5 (2021), 66.4 (2022) per the respective NCRB editions.

text.en: Police in India registered 48,303 cases of assault on women with intent to outrage their modesty (Section 74 BNS / Section 354 IPC) in 2024, a rate of 7.1 per lakh women.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne mahilaon ki lajja bhang karne (outraging modesty) ke iraade se un par assault (Section 74 BNS / Section 354 IPC) ke 48,303 cases register kiye; yeh har lakh mahilaon par 7.1 ka rate hai.

facts.caveat: Narrow head: CII 2024 lists sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking separately. Up to CII 2023 these were inside a broader head (83,891 cases in 2023), so do not compare 48,303 with older headline figures. On the narrow basis the count was 44,867 (2022) and 45,086 (2023) per CII 2024 Table 1.2.

text.en: In 2024 police in India also registered 15,609 cases of sexual harassment of women, 9,865 of stalking, 8,409 of assault with intent to disrobe and 1,722 of voyeurism.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne mahilaon ke sexual harassment ke 15,609, stalking ke 9,865, kapde utaarne (disrobe karne) ke iraade se assault ke 8,409 aur voyeurism ke 1,722 cases bhi register kiye.

facts.caveat: IPC Sections 354A-354D / BNS Sections 75-78. Includes girls under 18 unless the case was registered under POCSO.

text.en: Under its broader definition used until 2023, NCRB counted 83,891 cases of assault on women with intent to outrage their modesty in India in 2023, 18.7% of all crimes against women.
text.hg: 2023 tak use hone wali apni broader definition ke tahat NCRB ne 2023 mein India mein mahilaon ki lajja bhang karne (outraging modesty) ke iraade se un par assault ke 83,891 cases gine, jo mahilaon ke khilaf kul crimes ka 18.7% the.

facts.caveat: Broad head = Sec 354 plus 354A-D IPC (harassment, disrobing, voyeurism, stalking). Not comparable with the narrow 2024 figure of 48,303.

text.en: Police in India registered 2,561 cases of attempt to commit rape in 2024, down from 2,796 in 2023 and 3,288 in 2022.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne rape ki koshish (attempt to rape) ke 2,561 cases register kiye, jo 2023 ke 2,796 aur 2022 ke 3,288 cases se kam hain.

facts.caveat: Police-registered FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule); sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: NCRB recorded 266 cases of murder with rape or gang rape in India in 2024, with 274 victims.
text.hg: NCRB ne 2024 mein India mein rape ya gang rape ke saath murder ke 266 cases record kiye, jinmein 274 victims the.

facts.caveat: Earlier editions: 284 (2021), 248 (2022), 230 (2023). Courts convicted in 76.4% of such trials completed in 2024, but 1,574 cases were pending trial at year end (Table 3A.7).

text.en: NCRB recorded 1,537 cases of gang rape in India in 2024 (Section 70 BNS / Section 376D IPC), including 30 cases involving girls under 18.
text.hg: NCRB ne 2024 mein India mein gang rape (Section 70 BNS / Section 376D IPC) ke 1,537 cases record kiye, jinmein 30 cases 18 saal se kam umar ki ladkiyon se jude the.

facts.caveat: Gang rapes of children are often registered under POCSO and gang rapes ending in death under 'murder with rape/gang rape', so this undercounts gang rape.

text.en: In 2024 police in India registered rape cases under the aggravated categories for rape by police personnel (27 cases), other public servants (15), members of the armed forces (2), staff of jails, remand homes or other places of custody (3) and hospital staff (8).
text.hg: In 2024 police in India registered rape cases under the aggravated categories for rape by police personnel (27 cases), other public servants (15), members of the armed forces (2), staff of jails, remand homes or other places of custody (3) and hospital staff (8).

facts.caveat: These categories (Section 64(2)(a)-(e) BNS / Section 376(2)(a)-(e) IPC) cover only the defined situations, such as rape by a police officer in a police station or on a woman in custody; police-registered FIRs only, and a case appears here only if police invoked that clause.

text.en: NCRB recorded 1,753 cases of gang rape (Section 376D IPC) in India in 2023.
text.hg: NCRB ne 2023 mein India mein gang rape (Section 376D IPC) ke 1,753 cases record kiye.

facts.caveat: Table 3A.11's all-India total column equals the 29,670 cases under the rape head. A further 19 cases under Section 376DA (rape or gang rape of a girl under 16) and 1 under Section 376DB (under 12) are counted separately. Same undercount caveats as 2024.

text.en: NCRB recorded 2,118 cases of gang rape (Section 376D IPC) in India in 2022.
text.hg: NCRB ne 2022 mein India mein gang rape (Section 376D IPC) ke 2,118 cases record kiye.

facts.caveat: Table 3A.11's all-India total column equals the 31,516 cases under the rape head (clarifications were pending from Nagaland in CII 2022). Same undercount caveats as 2024.

text.en: In the first six months of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (July to December 2024), police in India registered 1,325 cases of sexual intercourse by deceitful means or a false promise of marriage under the new Section 69.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke pehle chhah mahinon (July se December 2024) mein India mein police ne nayi Section 69 ke tahat dhokhe se ya shaadi ka jhootha vaada karke sexual intercourse ke 1,325 cases register kiye.

facts.caveat: Section 69 BNS: sex by deceitful means or a promise to marry without intent to fulfil it, 'not amounting to the offence of rape'; up to 10 years. New offence, no earlier series.

text.en: In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024 (28,597 of 29,536), the offender was known to the victim.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein register hue rape ke 96.8% cases (29,536 mein se 28,597) mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha.

facts.caveat: Police-registered FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule); sexual violence is heavily under-reported. Offenders were unknown or not identified in 939 cases.

text.en: Of the 28,597 rape cases in India in 2024 where the offender was known, 2,134 involved family members; 13,879 involved friends, online friends or live-in partners on the pretext of marriage, or separated husbands; and 12,584 involved family friends, neighbours, employers or other known persons.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein rape ke jin 28,597 cases mein offender jaan-pehchaan wala tha, unmein se 2,134 mein family members; 13,879 mein shaadi ka jhansa dene wale dost, online dost ya live-in partners, ya alag rah rahe pati; aur 12,584 mein family friends, padosi, employers ya doosre jaan-pehchaan wale log shaamil the.

facts.caveat: NCRB groups friends, online friends, live-in partners and separated husbands into one category, so 'promise of marriage' cases cannot be separated out. Married women raped by husbands who are not separated are not counted (marital rape exception).

text.en: In 97.5% of rape cases registered in India in 2023 (28,915 of 29,670), the offender was known to the victim.
text.hg: 2023 mein India mein register hue rape ke 97.5% cases (29,670 mein se 28,915) mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha.

facts.caveat: Family members 1,750; friends/online friends/live-in partners on pretext of marriage/separated husband 14,633; family friends/neighbours/employers/other known 12,532; unknown 755.

text.en: In 2012, offenders were known to the victims in 98.2% of rape cases recorded in India (24,470 of 24,915), according to NCRB.
text.hg: NCRB ke mutabik, 2012 mein India mein record hue rape ke 98.2% cases (24,915 mein se 24,470) mein offenders victims ke jaan-pehchaan wale the.

facts.caveat: Pre-2013 legal definition of rape. The 24,915 base differs slightly from the 24,923 cases registered.

text.en: Of the 29,742 victims recorded under the rape head in India in 2024, 792 were girls under 18 and 28,950 were women aged 18 or over, including 19,489 aged 18 to 30.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein rape head ke tahat record hui 29,742 victims mein se 792 ladkiyan 18 saal se kam umar ki thi aur 28,950 mahilayein 18 saal ya usse zyada umar ki thi, jinmein 19,489 ki umar 18 se 30 saal ke beech thi.

facts.caveat: NCRB counts child rape booked under POCSO Sections 4 and 6 (read with rape provisions) under the separate POCSO head: 43,313 cases with girl victims in 2024. Do not read 792 as the number of child rape victims.

text.en: Police in India registered 43,313 cases of penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault on girls under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act in 2024, involving 43,675 girls, more than the 29,536 cases recorded under the rape head.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne POCSO Act ke Sections 4 aur 6 ke tahat ladkiyon par penetrative ya aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke 43,313 cases register kiye, jo 43,675 ladkiyon se jude the; yeh sankhya rape head ke tahat record hue 29,536 cases se zyada hai.

facts.caveat: Girl victims only (boys are in the crime-against-children chapter). Sections 4 and 6 cover penetrative sexual assault on children, i.e. child rape. Each FIR is counted once under the principal offence rule.

text.en: Cases under the POCSO Act with girl victims numbered 67,809 in India in 2024, 15.4% of all crimes against women.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein POCSO Act ke tahat girl victims wale cases ki sankhya 67,809 rahi, jo mahilaon ke khilaf kul crimes ka 15.4% hai.

facts.caveat: Girl child victims only; includes non-penetrative assault, harassment and child sexual abuse material offences.

text.en: Police in India registered 40,046 cases of child rape with girl victims under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act (read with Section 376 IPC) in 2023.
text.hg: 2023 mein India mein police ne POCSO Act ke Sections 4 aur 6 (Section 376 IPC ke saath padhe gaye) ke tahat child rape ke aise 40,046 cases register kiye, jinmein victims ladkiyan thi.

facts.caveat: Girl victims only. CII 2022 recorded 37,511 such cases in 2022.

text.en: In 2018, 9,433 of the 33,977 rape victims recorded under India's rape head (27.8%) were girls under 18.
text.hg: 2018 mein India ke rape head ke tahat record hui 33,977 rape victims mein se 9,433 (27.8%) 18 saal se kam umar ki ladkiyan thi.

facts.caveat: Not comparable with recent years: the under-18 share of victims under the rape head was 9.5% in 2021, 3.2% in 2022 and 2.7% in 2024, while POCSO Sections 4 and 6 cases with girl victims reached 43,313 in 2024. The fall reflects where cases are counted, not a fall in child rape.

text.en: NCRB began collecting data on rape in 1971, when 2,487 cases were recorded in India.
text.hg: NCRB ne rape ka data 1971 mein collect karna shuru kiya tha, jab India mein aise 2,487 cases record hue the.

facts.caveat: Very different legal definition, population and reporting climate; long-run growth mostly reflects registration, not only incidence.

text.en: Police in India registered 24,923 rape cases in 2012, and courts convicted in about 24% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2012 mein India mein police ne rape ke 24,923 cases register kiye, aur us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se lagbhag 24% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: Last year before the 2013 widening of the legal definition of rape. NCRB's 2012 table rounds rates to whole numbers.

text.en: Police in India registered 33,707 rape cases in 2013, a rate of 5.7 per lakh women, and courts convicted in 27.1% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2013 mein India mein police ne rape ke 33,707 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 5.7 ka rate; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 27.1% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: First year under the widened definition (Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, in force from 3 February 2013) and after the December 2012 Delhi gang rape; the jump from 2012 is partly definitional and reporting-driven.

text.en: Police in India registered 36,735 rape cases in 2014, a rate of 6.1 per lakh women, and courts convicted in 28.0% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2014 mein India mein police ne rape ke 36,735 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 6.1 ka rate; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 28.0% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: Police-registered FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule); sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Police in India registered 34,651 rape cases in 2015, a rate of 5.7 per lakh women, and courts convicted in 29.4% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2015 mein India mein police ne rape ke 34,651 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 5.7 ka rate; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 29.4% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: Police-registered FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule); sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Police in India registered 38,947 rape cases in 2016, the highest annual count between 2012 and 2024, and courts convicted in 25.5% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2016 mein India mein police ne rape ke 38,947 cases register kiye, jo 2012 se 2024 ke beech kisi ek saal mein register hue sabse zyada cases hain; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 25.5% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: 'Highest' refers only to the 2012-2024 series confirmed in this facts bank; years before 2012 were not checked individually. Rate in CII 2018: 6.3 per lakh women.

text.en: Police in India registered 32,559 rape cases in 2017, a rate of 5.2 per lakh women.
text.hg: 2017 mein India mein police ne rape ke 32,559 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 5.2 ka rate.

facts.caveat: Police-registered FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule); sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Courts in India convicted in 32.2% of rape trials completed in 2017 (5,822 cases convicted).
text.hg: 2017 mein India mein rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 32.2% mein courts ne saza sunayi (5,822 cases mein conviction hua).

facts.caveat: Conviction rate = cases convicted / cases in which trials were completed.

text.en: Police in India registered 33,356 rape cases in 2018, a rate of 5.2 per lakh women, and courts convicted in 27.2% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2018 mein India mein police ne rape ke 33,356 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 5.2 ka rate; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 27.2% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: NCRB noted clarifications pending from West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Sikkim for 2018.

text.en: Police in India registered 32,032 rape cases in 2019, a rate of 4.9 per lakh women.
text.hg: 2019 mein India mein police ne rape ke 32,032 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 4.9 ka rate.

facts.caveat: Revised figure as published in CII 2020 and CII 2021. The original CII 2019 edition reported 32,033 cases (also rate 4.9), the figure most 2020 news reports used.

text.en: Courts in India convicted in 27.8% of rape trials completed in 2019 (4,640 cases convicted).
text.hg: 2019 mein India mein rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 27.8% mein courts ne saza sunayi (4,640 cases mein conviction hua).

facts.caveat: Conviction rate = cases convicted / cases in which trials were completed.

text.en: Police in India registered 28,046 rape cases in 2020, a rate of 4.3 per lakh women, the lowest count in the 2013-2024 period.
text.hg: 2020 mein India mein police ne rape ke 28,046 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 4.3 ka rate; cases ki yeh sankhya 2013-2024 ke period mein sabse kam thi.

facts.caveat: 2020 was the COVID-19 lockdown year; lower registration does not mean less violence.

text.en: Courts in India convicted in 39.3% of rape trials completed in 2020, but only 3,814 cases ended in conviction, fewer than the 4,640 in 2019.
text.hg: 2020 mein India mein rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 39.3% mein courts ne saza sunayi, lekin sirf 3,814 cases mein hi conviction hua, jo 2019 ke 4,640 cases se kam hai.

facts.caveat: The 2020 rate is an outlier: courts completed far fewer rape trials that year (9,713, versus 16,701 in 2019, per NCRB's court-disposal tables), so compare absolute convictions as well as rates.

text.en: Police in India registered 31,677 rape cases in 2021, a rate of 4.8 per lakh women, and courts convicted in 28.6% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2021 mein India mein police ne rape ke 31,677 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 4.8 ka rate; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 28.6% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: 1,73,716 rape cases were pending trial at the end of 2021 (pendency 93.5%).

text.en: Police in India registered 31,516 rape cases in 2022, a rate of 4.7 per lakh women, and courts convicted in 27.4% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2022 mein India mein police ne rape ke 31,516 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 4.7 ka rate; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 27.4% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: Provisional for Nagaland in CII 2022; CII 2024 confirms 31,516 as final.

text.en: Police in India registered 29,670 rape cases in 2023, a rate of 4.4 per lakh women, and courts convicted in 22.7% of rape trials completed that year.
text.hg: 2023 mein India mein police ne rape ke 29,670 cases register kiye, yaani har lakh mahilaon par 4.4 ka rate; us saal rape ke jin trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein se 22.7% mein courts ne saza sunayi.

facts.caveat: 22.7% is the lowest rape conviction rate in the 2013-2024 NCRB series checked here. 4,464 cases convicted, 14,158 acquitted, 1,055 discharged.

text.en: Police in India filed charge-sheets in 24,614 rape cases in 2024, a charge-sheeting rate of 81.3%, and 8,905 rape cases were still under investigation at the end of the year.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne rape ke 24,614 cases mein chargesheet file ki, yaani chargesheeting rate 81.3% raha, aur saal ke aakhir mein rape ke 8,905 cases ki jaanch ab bhi chal rahi thi.

facts.caveat: Charge-sheeting rate = cases charge-sheeted / cases disposed of by police (30,272). Pendency of investigation 22.7%. 2023: 80.3%; 2022: 77.9%; 2021: 80.4%.

text.en: Police in India closed 3,776 of the 30,272 rape cases they disposed of in 2024 with a final report calling the case false; 714 more were closed as a mistake of fact or law or a civil dispute, and 1,044 as true but with insufficient evidence or untraced.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne rape ke jin 30,272 cases ka niptara kiya, unmein se 3,776 ko final report mein jhootha batakar band kar diya; 714 aur cases mistake of fact ya law ya civil dispute batakar band kiye gaye, aur 1,044 cases sach paaye jaane ke bawajood insufficient evidence ya untraced hone ke aadhaar par band kiye gaye.

facts.caveat: 'False' is a police closure category at the investigation stage, not a court finding, and must not be presented as the share of complaints proven false. 2023: 3,959 such closures.

text.en: Courts in India convicted the accused in 5,032 rape cases in 2024 and acquitted in 13,980, a conviction rate of 24.4% of the 20,587 trials completed.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein courts ne rape ke 5,032 cases mein accused ko doshi thehraya aur 13,980 cases mein bari kiya; yaani jin 20,587 trials ki sunwai poori hui, unmein conviction rate 24.4% raha.

facts.caveat: Counted by case, not by accused. A further 1,575 cases ended in discharge. Conviction rate = convicted / trials completed.

text.en: In rape trials completed in Indian courts in 2024, the conviction rate was 31.4% when the victim was a girl under 18 and 23.7% when she was an adult woman.
text.hg: In rape trials completed in Indian courts in 2024, the conviction rate was 31.4% when the victim was a girl under 18 and 23.7% when she was an adult woman.

facts.caveat: Rape head only: most child-rape cases are tried under POCSO and are counted elsewhere. Girls: 608 convictions in 1,935 completed trials; women: 4,424 in 18,652. Counted by case, not by accused.

text.en: At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial in Indian courts, 89.8% of the 2,06,777 rape cases before the courts that year.
text.hg: 2024 ke aakhir mein India ki courts mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases ka trial pending tha, jo us saal courts ke saamne rahe rape ke kul 2,06,777 cases ka 89.8% hai.

facts.caveat: Do not confuse with 2,06,777, the total number of rape cases before the courts in 2024 (pending from earlier years plus newly sent for trial). Courts disposed of 20,992 rape cases in 2024.

text.en: At the end of 2018, 1,38,642 rape cases were pending trial in Indian courts, a pendency of 88.7%.
text.hg: 2018 ke aakhir mein India ki courts mein rape ke 1,38,642 cases ka trial pending tha; pendency 88.7% rahi.

text.en: 6% of women aged 18-49 in India said they had experienced sexual violence at some point in their lives, according to the National Family Health Survey 2019-21 (NFHS-5).
text.hg: National Family Health Survey 2019-21 (NFHS-5) ke mutabik, India mein 18-49 saal ki 6% mahilaon ne bataya ki unhone zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi sexual violence jheli hai.

facts.caveat: NFHS-5 (2019-21) household survey of women aged 18-49; face-to-face self-reports, likely under-reported; not comparable with police data. Prevalence fell with schooling (9% with no schooling vs 3% with 12+ years) and wealth (10% lowest vs 3% highest quintile).

text.en: Among ever-married women aged 18-49 in India who had experienced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband and 14% a former husband as the perpetrator (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
text.hg: India mein 18-49 saal ki un mahilaon mein, jinki kabhi shaadi hui hai aur jinhone sexual violence jheli thi, 82% ne apne maujooda pati ko aur 14% ne purane (former) pati ko hinsa karne wala bataya (NFHS-5, 2019-21).

facts.caveat: NFHS-5 (2019-21) household survey of women aged 18-49; face-to-face self-reports, likely under-reported; not comparable with police data. Marital rape is not a crime under Indian law (Exception 2, Section 63 BNS), so this violence is largely absent from NCRB rape data.

text.en: Among never-married women aged 18-49 in India who reported sexual violence, the most common perpetrators were relatives other than a father or brother (39%), a current or former boyfriend (16%) and a family friend (12%); only 5% named a stranger (NFHS-5).
text.hg: Among never-married women aged 18-49 in India who reported sexual violence, the most common perpetrators were relatives other than a father or brother (39%), a current or former boyfriend (16%) and a family friend (12%); only 5% named a stranger (NFHS-5).

facts.value: 39% other relatives; 16% boyfriend; 12% family friend; 5% stranger
facts.caveat: NFHS-5 (2019-21) household survey of women aged 18-49; face-to-face self-reports, likely under-reported; not comparable with police data. Fathers or step-fathers (3.5%) and brothers or step-brothers (3.9%) are counted separately from 'other relative' (39.3%). The never-married figures rest on a small base (176 women, weighted), so they are imprecise.

text.en: 6% of ever-married women aged 18-49 in India have experienced sexual violence by a husband (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
text.hg: India mein 18-49 saal ki un mahilaon mein se, jinki kabhi shaadi hui hai, 6% ne pati ke haathon sexual violence jheli hai (NFHS-5, 2019-21).

facts.caveat: NFHS-5 (2019-21) household survey of women aged 18-49; face-to-face self-reports, likely under-reported; not comparable with police data.

text.en: 32% of women aged 18-49 in India have experienced physical or sexual violence (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
text.hg: India mein 18-49 saal ki 32% mahilaon ne physical ya sexual violence jheli hai (NFHS-5, 2019-21).

facts.caveat: NFHS-5 (2019-21) household survey of women aged 18-49; face-to-face self-reports, likely under-reported; not comparable with police data. 25% physical only, 6% both physical and sexual, 1% sexual only.

text.en: Only 14% of women aged 18-49 in India who had experienced physical or sexual violence sought help, and 77% never sought help or told anyone (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
text.hg: India mein physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 18-49 saal ki mahilaon mein se sirf 14% ne madad maangi, aur 77% ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya (NFHS-5, 2019-21).

facts.caveat: NFHS-5 (2019-21) household survey of women aged 18-49; face-to-face self-reports, likely under-reported; not comparable with police data. Help-seeking was 26% among women who experienced both physical and sexual violence and 10-12% among those who experienced only one type.

text.en: Among women in India who experienced physical or sexual violence and sought help, only 6% went to the police; most turned to their own family (61%) (NFHS-5, 2019-21).
text.hg: India mein physical ya sexual violence jhelne ke baad madad maangne wali mahilaon mein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayi; zyadatar (61%) ne apne hi parivaar se madad maangi (NFHS-5, 2019-21).

facts.caveat: NFHS-5 (2019-21) household survey of women aged 18-49; face-to-face self-reports, likely under-reported; not comparable with police data. Base is only women who sought help (about 14% of those who experienced violence).

text.en: NCRB follows the 'principal offence rule': when one FIR includes several offences, only the most heinous one, the offence carrying the maximum punishment, is counted.
text.hg: NCRB 'principal offence rule' follow karta hai: jab ek FIR mein kai offences shaamil hon, to sirf sabse heinous (jaghanya) offence, yaani jis offence ki saza sabse zyada hai, gina jaata hai.

facts.caveat: Rapes that end in murder, or child rapes booked under POCSO, drop out of the rape head.

text.en: NCRB itself warns that a rise in registered crime is not the same as a rise in crime, and that police steps such as e-FIR facilities or women help desks can push the numbers up.
text.hg: NCRB khud warn karta hai ki registered crime mein badhotri ka matlab crime mein badhotri nahi hai, aur e-FIR facility ya women help desk jaise police ke kadam numbers ko badha sakte hain.

facts.caveat: Also warns against comparing states purely on crime figures.

text.en: A 2022 peer-reviewed study in BMC Public Health noted estimates that only about 1% of victims of sexual violence in India report it to the authorities.
text.hg: BMC Public Health mein chhapi 2022 ki ek peer-reviewed study mein un estimates ka zikr hai jinke mutabik India mein sexual violence ke sirf lagbhag 1% victims hi authorities ko iski report karte hain.

facts.caveat: The 1% is an estimate the authors cite from earlier studies, not a new calculation; treat as indicative.

text.en: Because of NCRB's principal offence rule, the 2012 Delhi gang rape case (the 'Nirbhaya' case) was recorded as murder rather than rape, according to a 2022 BMC Public Health study.
text.hg: BMC Public Health ki 2022 ki ek study ke mutabik, NCRB ke principal offence rule ki wajah se 2012 ka Delhi gang rape case ('Nirbhaya' case) rape ke bajaay murder ke roop mein record hua.

facts.caveat: Refer to the case only as the 2012 Delhi gang rape or 'Nirbhaya' case; never name the survivor. NCRB now has a separate 'murder with rape/gang rape' head (266 cases in 2024).

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, deemed to be in force from 3 February 2013, widened India's legal definition of rape beyond penile-vaginal intercourse to include penetration of the mouth, urethra or anus and insertion of any object or body part.
text.hg: 3 February 2013 se laagu maane gaye Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne India mein rape ki legal definition ko penile-vaginal intercourse se aage badhakar usmein munh, urethra ya anus mein penetration aur kisi bhi object ya body part ko daalna bhi shaamil kiya.

facts.caveat: Text of the Bill as passed by Lok Sabha on 19 March 2013, enacted as the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013. Registered rape cases rose from 24,923 (2012) to 33,707 (2013), partly because of the wider definition; trend lines that cross 2013 have a break.

text.en: The 2013 criminal law amendment raised the age below which sex with a girl is rape regardless of consent from 16 to 18 years.
text.hg: 2013 ke criminal law amendment ne woh umar 16 se badhakar 18 saal kar di, jisse kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex, consent ho ya na ho, rape maana jaata hai.

facts.caveat: The same threshold is retained in Section 63(vi) BNS ('with or without her consent, when she is under eighteen years of age'), so sex with a girl under 18 is rape in law even if she consents.

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, passed by Parliament in July-August 2018, raised the minimum punishment for rape of women from seven to ten years and allowed the death penalty for rape and gang rape of girls under 12.
text.hg: July-August 2018 mein Parliament se paas hue Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 ne mahilaon se rape ki minimum saza saat saal se badhakar das saal kar di, aur 12 saal se kam umar ki ladkiyon se rape aur gang rape ke liye death penalty (maut ki saza) ka provision kiya.

facts.value: min 10 years; death penalty for rape of girls under 12
facts.caveat: PRS notes punishment for rape of boys was left unchanged.

text.en: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the Indian Penal Code of 1860, came into force across India on 1 July 2024.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, jisne 1860 ke Indian Penal Code (IPC) ki jagah li, 1 July 2024 ko poore India mein laagu hui.

facts.caveat: NCRB's 2024 data include cases registered under both codes (for rape, 19,683 under the IPC and 9,853 under the BNS).

text.en: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, rape (Section 63) is punishable under Section 64 with at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, extendable to life, while gang rape (Section 70) carries at least 20 years and gang rape of a girl under 18 can carry the death penalty.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke tahat rape (Section 63) ke liye Section 64 mein kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment (sashram karawas) ki saza hai, jise umrqaid tak badhaya ja sakta hai; wahin gang rape (Section 70) mein kam se kam 20 saal ki saza hai, aur 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki se gang rape mein death penalty bhi ho sakti hai.

facts.value: min 10 years; gang rape min 20 years
facts.caveat: Rape of a girl under 12 (S.65(2)) also carries a possible death sentence; rape causing death or a vegetative state (S.66) carries 20 years to life or death.

text.en: Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita states that sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under 18, is not rape.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 63 ke Exception 2 mein kaha gaya hai ki kisi aadmi ka apni patni ke saath sexual intercourse ya sexual acts, agar patni 18 saal se kam umar ki na ho, rape nahi hai.

facts.caveat: Under the IPC text as amended in 2013, the exception covered wives aged 15 and above ('the wife not being under fifteen years of age'). The Supreme Court read it down to 18 in Independent Thought v Union of India (2017), with prospective effect, and the BNS writes 18 into the text. Section 67 BNS punishes non-consensual sex with a wife living separately (2 to 7 years). NFHS-5 finds husbands are the main perpetrators of sexual violence against married women.

text.en: As of September 2026, the Supreme Court of India had not ruled on the petitions challenging the marital rape exception; on 9 September 2026 a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant posted them for final hearing.
text.hg: As of September 2026, the Supreme Court of India had not ruled on the petitions challenging the marital rape exception; on 9 September 2026 a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant posted them for final hearing.

facts.value: pending; posted for final hearing on 9 Sep 2026
facts.caveat: Bar and Bench reported that hearings would begin the following month; LiveLaw said the hearing date would be notified. Neither outlet's marital-rape page reported a ruling or the start of hearings as of 20 November 2026; recheck before publishing. Per LiveLaw, the petitions include an appeal against the Delhi High Court's split verdict and a challenge to a Karnataka High Court ruling that allowed a husband to be prosecuted for raping his wife.

text.en: Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita makes it a crime, punishable with up to two years in prison and a fine, to print or publish the name or any matter that could reveal the identity of a rape victim.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ki Section 72 ke tahat rape victim ka naam ya koi bhi aisi baat print ya publish karna crime hai jisse uski pehchaan saamne aa sakti ho; iske liye do saal tak ki jail aur jurmaana ho sakta hai.

facts.caveat: Exceptions in Section 72(2) include publication by the investigating officer in good faith and publication with the victim's written authorisation.

text.en: In the first six months of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (July to December 2024), police in India registered 11 cases under Section 72 for disclosing the identity of a victim of rape or another sexual offence.
text.hg: In the first six months of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (July to December 2024), police in India registered 11 cases under Section 72 for disclosing the identity of a victim of rape or another sexual offence.

facts.caveat: New head in CII 2024 (BNS cases only, so no earlier series). Police-registered FIRs only.

text.en: In Nipun Saxena v Union of India (11 December 2018), the Supreme Court directed that no one may publish a rape victim's name in print, electronic or social media, or disclose even in a remote manner any facts that could identify her.
text.hg: Nipun Saxena v Union of India (11 December 2018) case mein Supreme Court ne nirdesh diya ki koi bhi rape victim ka naam print, electronic ya social media mein publish nahi kar sakta, aur na hi indirectly bhi aise koi facts bata sakta hai jinse uski pehchaan ho sake.

facts.caveat: Direction 2: where the victim is dead or of unsound mind, her identity must not be disclosed even with the next of kin's authorisation unless the competent authority (the Sessions Judge) finds justifying circumstances. Direction 3: FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain. Binding on this website's own content.

text.en: On 31 October 2022 the Supreme Court of India held that anyone conducting the 'two-finger test' on a survivor of rape or penetrative sexual assault is guilty of misconduct (State of Jharkhand v Shailendra Kumar Rai).
text.hg: 31 October 2022 ko India ke Supreme Court ne faisla diya ki rape ya penetrative sexual assault ki survivor par 'two-finger test' karne wala koi bhi vyakti misconduct ka doshi hai (State of Jharkhand v Shailendra Kumar Rai).

facts.caveat: Bench: Justices D Y Chandrachud and Hima Kohli. The Court referred to its 2013 ruling in Lillu v State of Haryana, (2013) 14 SCC 643, and restored the accused's conviction. Do not add details of the underlying crime or the victim.

text.en: Chandigarh had the highest registered rape rate of any State/UT in 2024 at 16.6 per lakh women, followed by Goa (13.3), Rajasthan (12.2), Delhi (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (9.9), Haryana (9.6), Himachal Pradesh (8.7), Chhattisgarh (7.7), Madhya Pradesh (7.2) and Lakshadweep (6.7).
text.hg: 2024 mein sabhi States/UTs mein rape ke darj cases ki sabse oonchi rate Chandigarh mein rahi, har lakh mahilaon par 16.6; iske baad Goa (13.3), Rajasthan (12.2), Delhi (10.3), Arunachal Pradesh (9.9), Haryana (9.6), Himachal Pradesh (8.7), Chhattisgarh (7.7), Madhya Pradesh (7.2) aur Lakshadweep (6.7) rahe.

facts.value: Chandigarh 16.6; Goa 13.3; Rajasthan 12.2; Delhi 10.3; Arunachal 9.9 per lakh women
facts.caveat: Small-population territories (Chandigarh 96 cases, Lakshadweep 2 cases) produce volatile rates. In Chandigarh (47 of 96), Goa (64 of 105) and Himachal Pradesh (194 of 324) about half or more of the cases counted under the rape head had victims under 18, whereas most states count such cases under POCSO. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: The lowest registered rape rates in 2024 were in Ladakh (0.8 per lakh women, 1 case), Puducherry (1.0, 9 cases), Tamil Nadu (1.1, 419 cases), Manipur (1.2, 19 cases), Nagaland (1.3, 14 cases) and Andhra Pradesh (1.7, 441 cases).
text.hg: 2024 mein rape ke darj cases ki sabse kam rates Ladakh (har lakh mahilaon par 0.8, 1 case), Puducherry (1.0, 9 cases), Tamil Nadu (1.1, 419 cases), Manipur (1.2, 19 cases), Nagaland (1.3, 14 cases) aur Andhra Pradesh (1.7, 441 cases) mein rahi.

facts.value: Ladakh 0.8; Puducherry 1.0; Tamil Nadu 1.1; Manipur 1.2; Nagaland 1.3; Andhra Pradesh 1.7
facts.caveat: Low registered rape rates should not be read as low incidence. All 419 of Tamil Nadu's rape cases had adult victims; child sexual abuse there is recorded under POCSO (6,969 cases in 2024, 33.7 per lakh children, among the highest rates). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Uttar Pradesh registered 3,209 rape cases in 2024, the second-highest count, but at 2.8 per lakh women its rate was below the national rate of 4.3.
text.hg: Uttar Pradesh mein 2024 mein rape ke 3,209 cases darj hue, jo ginti ke hisaab se doosre number par hai, lekin har lakh mahilaon par 2.8 ki uski rate 4.3 ki national rate se kam rahi.

facts.caveat: Uttar Pradesh holds 16.8% of India's projected female population but 10.9% of registered rape cases (computed). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Delhi registered 1,058 rape cases involving 1,089 victims in 2024, a rate of 10.3 per lakh women, the highest rape rate among India's large-population States/UTs after Rajasthan.
text.hg: Delhi mein 2024 mein rape ke 1,058 cases darj hue, jinmein 1,089 victims thi; har lakh mahilaon par 10.3 ki yeh rate India ke zyada aabadi wale States/UTs mein Rajasthan ke baad sabse oonchi hai.

facts.caveat: 'Large-population' = projected female population above 100 lakh (compiler's label). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024 (28,597 of 29,536) the offender was known to the victim; family members were the accused in 2,134 cases and friends, online friends, live-in partners or separated husbands in 13,879.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein darj rape ke 96.8% cases (29,536 mein se 28,597) mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha; 2,134 cases mein accused parivaar ke sadasya the aur 13,879 cases mein dost, online dost, live-in partner ya alag reh rahe pati.

facts.value: 96.8% known offender; 2,134 family; 13,879 friends/partners; 12,584 neighbours/employers/other known; 939 unknown
facts.caveat: NCRB's category 'friends/online friends or live-in partners on pretext of marriage/separated husband' includes cases arising from promises of marriage. Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: The share of rape cases with an offender known to the victim exceeded 90% in almost every State/UT in 2024; the lowest shares were in Nagaland (78.6%), Meghalaya (78.9%), West Bengal (84.9%) and Mizoram (85.0%).
text.hg: 2024 mein lagbhag har State/UT mein rape ke 90% se zyada cases mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha; aise cases ka hissa sabse kam Nagaland (78.6%), Meghalaya (78.9%), West Bengal (84.9%) aur Mizoram (85.0%) mein raha.

facts.caveat: Haryana (90.4%) and Assam (93.0%) are also below the national 96.8%. Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: Police registered 266 cases of murder with rape or gang rape in India in 2024 (274 victims); Madhya Pradesh had the most with 50 cases (55 victims), followed by Rajasthan (38), Maharashtra (24) and Uttar Pradesh (23).
text.hg: Police registered 266 cases of murder with rape or gang rape in India in 2024 (274 victims); Madhya Pradesh had the most with 50 cases (55 victims), followed by Rajasthan (38), Maharashtra (24) and Uttar Pradesh (23).

facts.caveat: Murder-with-rape cases are counted under this head, not under rape (Principal Offence Rule). For Madhya Pradesh, 55 is the number of victims, not cases. 2024 counts combine IPC cases (Jan-Jun) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024).

text.en: Only 784 of India's 29,536 registered rape cases in 2024 involved girls under 18, because most child rape is recorded under the POCSO Act: police registered 43,313 POCSO Section 4 & 6 (penetrative and aggravated penetrative sexual assault) cases with girl victims that year.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein darj rape ke 29,536 cases mein se sirf 784 cases 18 saal se kam umar ki ladkiyon se jude the, kyunki bachchon ke saath rape ke zyadatar cases POCSO Act ke tahat darj hote hain: us saal police ne POCSO ki Section 4 aur 6 (penetrative aur aggravated penetrative sexual assault) ke tahat aise 43,313 cases register kiye jinmein victim ladkiyan thi.

facts.value: 784 rape cases (girls <18, IPC/BNS) vs 43,313 POCSO s.4&6 cases (girl victims)
facts.caveat: A fuller count adds the two: 29,536 rape cases + 43,313 POCSO s.4 & 6 cases with girl victims = 72,849 registered cases of rape or penetrative sexual assault against women and girls in 2024 (computed; each FIR is counted once). State practice differs: Himachal Pradesh, Goa and Chandigarh record many child cases under the rape head. Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: Police in India registered 69,191 cases under the POCSO Act in 2024, 36.9% of all crimes against children, at a rate of 15.6 per lakh children.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne POCSO Act ke tahat 69,191 cases register kiye, jo bachchon ke khilaf sabhi crimes ka 36.9% hain; yeh har lakh bachchon par 15.6 ki rate hai.

facts.caveat: Child rates use the 2011 Census child population, which may differ substantially from today's. Of the 44,126 penetrative-assault (s.4 & 6) cases, 43,313 had girl victims and 813 boy victims. Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: The ten states with the most POCSO cases in 2024 were Maharashtra (9,432), Uttar Pradesh (8,087), Tamil Nadu (6,969), Madhya Pradesh (5,861), Kerala (4,513), Karnataka (4,118), Assam (2,920), Telangana (2,902), West Bengal (2,799) and Gujarat (2,699).
text.hg: 2024 mein POCSO ke sabse zyada cases wale das states ye the: Maharashtra (9,432), Uttar Pradesh (8,087), Tamil Nadu (6,969), Madhya Pradesh (5,861), Kerala (4,513), Karnataka (4,118), Assam (2,920), Telangana (2,902), West Bengal (2,799) aur Gujarat (2,699).

facts.caveat: Ranking compiled from NCRB table (all child victims, boys and girls). High counts can reflect stronger registration as well as more abuse (NCRB caution). Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: Among states, Kerala recorded the highest POCSO rate in 2024 at 48.0 cases per lakh children, followed by Sikkim (36.7), Mizoram (36.4), Tamil Nadu (33.7) and Meghalaya (30.7); Uttar Pradesh's rate was 9.5 and Bihar's 5.2.
text.hg: 2024 mein states mein POCSO cases ki sabse oonchi rate Kerala mein darj hui, har lakh bachchon par 48.0 cases; iske baad Sikkim (36.7), Mizoram (36.4), Tamil Nadu (33.7) aur Meghalaya (30.7) rahe; Uttar Pradesh ki rate 9.5 aur Bihar ki 5.2 rahi.

facts.value: Kerala 48.0; Sikkim 36.7; Mizoram 36.4; Tamil Nadu 33.7; Meghalaya 30.7; UP 9.5; Bihar 5.2 per lakh children
facts.caveat: Among UTs, Andaman & Nicobar (82.7, 91 cases) is highest. Rates use 2011 Census child population. Per NCRB's own caution, high registered rates can reflect stronger reporting and registration rather than more abuse. Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: Counting only girl victims, police registered 67,809 POCSO cases in 2024; Maharashtra (9,245), Uttar Pradesh (7,969), Tamil Nadu (6,874) and Madhya Pradesh (5,825) recorded the most.
text.hg: Sirf un cases ko ginein jinmein victim ladkiyan thi, to 2024 mein police ne POCSO ke 67,809 cases register kiye; inmein sabse zyada cases Maharashtra (9,245), Uttar Pradesh (7,969), Tamil Nadu (6,874) aur Madhya Pradesh (5,825) mein darj hue.

facts.value: 67,809 cases (girl victims); MH 9,245; UP 7,969; TN 6,874; MP 5,825
facts.caveat: In the crime-against-women chapter the POCSO rate is per lakh women (all ages), not per lakh girls. Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: India's 19 metropolitan cities with populations above 20 lakh registered 50,584 crimes against women in 2024, down 1.6% from 51,393 in 2023 (48,755 in 2022).
text.hg: 20 lakh se zyada aabadi wale India ke 19 metropolitan cities mein 2024 mein mahilaon ke khilaf 50,584 crime darj hue, jo 2023 ke 51,393 se 1.6% kam hain (2022 mein yeh sankhya 48,755 thi).

facts.caveat: The 19 cities are those with more than 20 lakh population in the 2011 Census. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Delhi registered 13,396 crimes against women in 2024, the most of the 19 metropolitan cities and 26.5% of their combined total; Mumbai was second with 6,358 and Bengaluru third with 4,748.
text.hg: Delhi mein 2024 mein mahilaon ke khilaf 13,396 crime darj hue, jo 19 metropolitan cities mein sabse zyada aur unke kul cases ka 26.5% hain; 6,358 cases ke saath Mumbai doosre aur 4,748 ke saath Bengaluru teesre number par raha.

facts.caveat: Share computed from NCRB counts. Counts reflect population size and registration practice, so they are not a measure of risk on their own (Mumbai's 2011 female population, 85.2 lakh, is larger than Delhi's 75.8 lakh in NCRB's table). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: After Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, the metropolitan cities with the most registered crimes against women in 2024 were Hyderabad (3,255), Jaipur (2,894), Pune (2,631), Lucknow (2,571), Kolkata (1,958), Kanpur (1,950) and Indore (1,884).
text.hg: Delhi, Mumbai aur Bengaluru ke baad 2024 mein mahilaon ke khilaf sabse zyada darj crime wale metropolitan cities ye the: Hyderabad (3,255), Jaipur (2,894), Pune (2,631), Lucknow (2,571), Kolkata (1,958), Kanpur (1,950) aur Indore (1,884).

facts.value: Hyderabad 3,255; Jaipur 2,894; Pune 2,631; Lucknow 2,571; Kolkata 1,958; Kanpur 1,950; Indore 1,884
facts.caveat: NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Jaipur had the highest rate of registered crime against women among the 19 metropolitan cities in 2024 at 199.0 per lakh women, followed by Lucknow (186.0), Indore (181.5), Delhi (176.8), Kanpur (146.1), Patna (129.2) and Nagpur (123.8); Chennai (25.4) and Kolkata (28.8) had the lowest.
text.hg: 2024 mein 19 metropolitan cities mein mahilaon ke khilaf darj crime ki sabse oonchi rate Jaipur mein rahi, har lakh mahilaon par 199.0; iske baad Lucknow (186.0), Indore (181.5), Delhi (176.8), Kanpur (146.1), Patna (129.2) aur Nagpur (123.8) rahe; sabse kam rate Chennai (25.4) aur Kolkata (28.8) mein rahi.

facts.value: Jaipur 199.0; Lucknow 186.0; Indore 181.5; Delhi 176.8; Kanpur 146.1; Patna 129.2; Nagpur 123.8; Chennai 25.4; Kolkata 28.8
facts.caveat: City rates divide 2024 cases by the 2011 Census female population, so they overstate the rate in any city whose population has grown since 2011, and they are not comparable with state rates (NCRB disclaimer). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: The 19 metropolitan cities registered 3,886 rape cases in 2024; Delhi accounted for 1,058 (27.2%), followed by Jaipur (497), Mumbai (411), Hyderabad (358), Pune (244), Indore (195), Bengaluru (168) and Lucknow (161).
text.hg: 2024 mein 19 metropolitan cities mein rape ke 3,886 cases darj hue; inmein se 1,058 (27.2%) Delhi mein the, iske baad Jaipur (497), Mumbai (411), Hyderabad (358), Pune (244), Indore (195), Bengaluru (168) aur Lucknow (161) rahe.

facts.value: 3,886 cases (19 cities); Delhi 1,058; Jaipur 497; Mumbai 411; Hyderabad 358; Pune 244; Indore 195; Bengaluru 168; Lucknow 161
facts.caveat: Share computed from NCRB counts. 2024 counts combine IPC cases (Jan-Jun) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Jaipur recorded the highest registered rape rate among the 19 metropolitan cities in 2024 at 34.2 per lakh women (497 cases), followed by Indore (18.8), Delhi (14.0), Lucknow (11.6) and Nagpur (11.1); Kolkata recorded the lowest at 0.2 (12 cases), followed by Chennai at 1.0 (44 cases).
text.hg: 2024 mein 19 metropolitan cities mein rape ke darj cases ki sabse oonchi rate Jaipur mein rahi, har lakh mahilaon par 34.2 (497 cases); iske baad Indore (18.8), Delhi (14.0), Lucknow (11.6) aur Nagpur (11.1) rahe; sabse kam rate Kolkata mein 0.2 (12 cases) aur uske baad Chennai mein 1.0 (44 cases) rahi.

facts.value: Jaipur 34.2; Indore 18.8; Delhi 14.0; Lucknow 11.6; Nagpur 11.1; Kolkata 0.2; Chennai 1.0
facts.caveat: City rates use 2011 Census female population. Kolkata's 12 rape cases sit beside 194 POCSO cases with girl victims and 1,958 total crimes against women in the same table. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: The 19 metropolitan cities registered 7,508 POCSO cases with girl victims in 2024; Delhi (1,489) and Mumbai (1,331) together accounted for 37.6%, followed by Bengaluru (588), Pune (575) and Chennai (437).
text.hg: 2024 mein 19 metropolitan cities mein POCSO ke aise 7,508 cases darj hue jinmein victim ladkiyan thi; inmein se 37.6% cases Delhi (1,489) aur Mumbai (1,331) mein the, iske baad Bengaluru (588), Pune (575) aur Chennai (437) rahe.

facts.value: 7,508 cases; Delhi 1,489; Mumbai 1,331; Bengaluru 588; Pune 575; Chennai 437
facts.caveat: Share computed from NCRB counts. Rate column is per lakh women (2011 Census). Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence.

text.en: Courts convicted the accused in only 25.7% of crime-against-women cases decided at trial in India in 2024, and 24,32,527 such cases (92.1% of those before courts) were still pending trial at the end of the year.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein mahilaon ke khilaf crime ke jin cases mein trial poora hokar faisla aaya, unmein se sirf 25.7% mein courts ne accused ko doshi thehraya; saal ke ant mein aise 24,32,527 cases (courts ke saamne maujood cases ka 92.1%) mein trial ab bhi pending tha.

facts.value: 25.7% conviction rate; 24,32,527 cases pending trial; 92.1% pendency
facts.caveat: Conviction rate = convictions / trials completed. Acquittals can reflect weak investigation, hostile witnesses, compromise or false complaints; the data do not say which.

text.en: The conviction rate in rape trials completed in India in 2024 was 24.4% (5,032 convictions), and 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial at the end of the year, a pendency of 89.8%.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein rape ke jin cases mein trial poora hua, unmein conviction rate 24.4% rahi (5,032 cases mein saza); saal ke ant mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases mein trial pending tha, yaani pendency 89.8% rahi.

facts.caveat: Conviction rate = convictions / trials completed (20,587).

text.en: West Bengal had the lowest conviction rate for crimes against women of any state in 2024 at 1.6% (203 convictions against 12,301 acquittals), and the largest trial backlog in India with 3,84,388 cases pending at year-end.
text.hg: 2024 mein mahilaon ke khilaf crime mein conviction rate kisi bhi state ke mukable West Bengal mein sabse kam rahi, 1.6% (203 cases mein saza, jabki 12,301 cases mein accused bari hue); saal ke ant mein 3,84,388 pending cases ke saath desh ka sabse bada trial backlog bhi yahin tha.

facts.caveat: West Bengal's backlog is 15.8% of the national pending total (computed). State-level conviction rates depend on how many trials finish and how cases are classified.

text.en: Among large states, conviction rates for crimes against women in 2024 ranged from 76.6% in Uttar Pradesh (21,169 convictions, nearly half of India's 45,832) to 1.6% in West Bengal; Karnataka (4.8%), Andhra Pradesh (5.4%), Odisha (6.3%), Assam (8.1%), Maharashtra (8.7%) and Gujarat (9.9%) also convicted in fewer than one in ten trials.
text.hg: 2024 mein bade states mein mahilaon ke khilaf crime mein conviction rate Uttar Pradesh ke 76.6% (21,169 cases mein saza, jo desh ke kul 45,832 ka lagbhag aadha hai) se lekar West Bengal ke 1.6% tak rahi; Karnataka (4.8%), Andhra Pradesh (5.4%), Odisha (6.3%), Assam (8.1%), Maharashtra (8.7%) aur Gujarat (9.9%) mein bhi das mein se ek se kam trial mein saza hui.

facts.value: UP 76.6%; West Bengal 1.6%; Karnataka 4.8%; Andhra Pradesh 5.4%; Odisha 6.3%; Assam 8.1%; Maharashtra 8.7%; Gujarat 9.9%; India 25.7%
facts.caveat: Uttar Pradesh's share of convictions computed from NCRB counts (46.2%). Smaller states such as Mizoram (87.8%) and Nagaland (61.9%) post higher rates on very few trials; 'large state' = projected female population above 100 lakh (compiler's label). Conviction rates depend on which trials finish in a year and how cases are classified, so they are not directly comparable across states.

text.en: Rajasthan police closed 12,217 crime-against-women cases in 2024 with a 'final report false', a third of the 36,895 such closures in India, and the state's chargesheeting rate of 54.1% was the lowest of all States/UTs.
text.hg: 2024 mein Rajasthan police ne mahilaon ke khilaf crime ke 12,217 cases 'final report false' lagakar (yaani shikayat ko jhootha batakar) band kiye, jo desh bhar mein is tarah band hue 36,895 cases ka ek-tihai hai; state ki chargesheeting rate 54.1% rahi, jo sabhi States/UTs mein sabse kam thi.

facts.caveat: 'Final report false' is a police classification after investigation, not a court finding, and may include cases registered in earlier years. It is not proof that complaints were fabricated, and NCRB does not report why cases were classified this way. Share computed from NCRB counts.

text.en: NCRB's own guidance in Crime in India 2024 states that 'rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are two different things, and that higher numbers may result from citizen-centric initiatives such as e-FIR facilities or women's helpdesks.
text.hg: NCRB ne 'Crime in India 2024' mein apni hi guidance mein kaha hai ki 'rise in crime' aur 'increase in registration of crime by police' do alag-alag baatein hain, aur zyada aankde e-FIR suvidha ya women's helpdesk jaisi citizen-centric pehal ka nateeja bhi ho sakte hain.

facts.caveat: Applies to all states and years; NCRB also says comparing states on these data alone 'will be too simplistic and is best avoided'.

text.en: NCRB warns that more crime registered in a city 'is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe' than a city with fewer recorded crimes, because all offences are counted equally and procedures differ across regions.
text.hg: NCRB chetavni deta hai ki kisi city mein zyada crime darj hona, kam darj crime wale city ke mukable, 'uske comparatively unsafe hone ka indicator nahin hai', kyunki sabhi offences ko barabar gina jaata hai aur alag-alag ilakon mein procedures alag hote hain.

text.en: NCRB counts each FIR only once, under its most serious offence (the 'Principal Offence Rule'), so a case of rape and murder appears only as murder with rape and the true number of each offence may be higher than published.
text.hg: NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar, uske sabse serious offence ke tahat ginta hai ('Principal Offence Rule'), isliye rape aur murder ka koi case sirf 'murder with rape' ke roop mein dikhta hai aur har offence ki asli sankhya published aankdon se zyada ho sakti hai.

text.en: NCRB calculates metropolitan-city crime rates using 2011 Census population because projections are not available for cities, and states that city and state crime rates are therefore not comparable.
text.hg: NCRB metropolitan cities ki crime rate 2011 Census ki aabadi ke aadhaar par nikalta hai, kyunki cities ke liye population projections uplabdh nahin hain, aur kehta hai ki isliye city aur state ki crime rates ki tulna nahin ki ja sakti.

facts.caveat: Same 13,396 Delhi cases give a UT rate of 130.7 (2024 projected population) and a city rate of 176.8 (2011 Census).

text.en: NCRB only compiles crime data furnished by State/UT police and says it is not responsible for the authenticity of the information.
text.hg: NCRB sirf States/UTs ki police se mile crime data ko compile karta hai, aur kehta hai ki is jaankari ki authenticity ke liye woh zimmedar nahin hai.

text.en: As of 20 November 2026, Crime in India 2024 is NCRB's latest published edition: the year selector on NCRB's Crime in India page goes up to 2024 and a query for 2025 returns no records.
text.hg: 20 November 2026 tak 'Crime in India 2024' NCRB ka sabse latest published edition hai: NCRB ke 'Crime in India' page par year selector 2024 tak hi jaata hai aur 2025 ke liye query karne par koi record nahin milta.

facts.caveat: Check again before publishing: NCRB usually releases a new edition once a year.

text.en: NCRB collects crime data for 53 metropolitan cities with populations above 10 lakh (2011 Census) but prints tables only for the 19 cities above 20 lakh; the other 34 cities' data are posted on its website; NCRB also notes that Delhi UT comprises both Delhi City and rural Delhi.
text.hg: NCRB 10 lakh se zyada aabadi (2011 Census) wale 53 metropolitan cities ka crime data collect karta hai, lekin tables sirf 20 lakh se zyada aabadi wale 19 cities ki print karta hai; baaki 34 cities ka data uski website par daala jaata hai; NCRB yeh bhi batata hai ki Delhi UT mein Delhi City aur rural Delhi, dono shaamil hain.

facts.caveat: Delhi City and Delhi UT totals were identical in 2024 (13,396) but differed slightly in 2022 (14,158 vs 14,247) and 2023 (13,366 vs 13,439).

text.en: NCRB's Crime in India 2024, the latest edition of India's official crime statistics, was released on Wednesday, 6 May 2026.
text.hg: India ke official crime statistics ka sabse latest edition, NCRB ki 'Crime in India 2024' report, Wednesday, 6 May 2026 ko jaari hui.

facts.caveat: Two Indian Express reports (7 and 8 May 2026) independently date the release to Wednesday, 6 May 2026.

text.en: NCRB recorded 3,71,503 crimes against women in 2020 and 4,28,278 in 2021, before registrations climbed to 4,45,256 in 2022.
text.hg: NCRB ke records mein 2020 mein mahilaon ke khilaf 3,71,503 aur 2021 mein 4,28,278 crime darj hue; iske baad 2022 mein darj cases badhkar 4,45,256 ho gaye.

facts.caveat: NCRB's tables do not explain year-to-year changes. Rate for 2022 was 66.4 per lakh women. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Delhi also had the highest rate of registered crime against women among States/UTs in 2023 at 133.6 per lakh women, ahead of Telangana (124.9), Rajasthan (114.8), Odisha (112.4) and Haryana (110.3).
text.hg: 2023 mein bhi States/UTs mein mahilaon ke khilaf darj crime ki sabse oonchi rate Delhi mein hi thi, har lakh mahilaon par 133.6; Delhi ke baad Telangana (124.9), Rajasthan (114.8), Odisha (112.4) aur Haryana (110.3) the.

facts.value: Delhi 133.6; Telangana 124.9; Rajasthan 114.8; Odisha 112.4; Haryana 110.3 per lakh women
facts.caveat: Andaman & Nicobar Islands (107.3, 205 cases) was next. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Assam's registered crimes against women fell from 29,046 in 2021 to 14,148 in 2022, 12,070 in 2023 and 10,546 in 2024, a drop of almost two-thirds in three years.
text.hg: Assam mein mahilaon ke khilaf darj crime 2021 ke 29,046 se ghatkar 2022 mein 14,148, 2023 mein 12,070 aur 2024 mein 10,546 reh gaye, yaani teen saal mein lagbhag do-tihai ki girawat.

facts.caveat: Percentage drop (-63.7%) computed from NCRB counts. NCRB does not explain state trends; a fall in registrations can reflect changes in policing or reporting rather than in violence. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: In 2023 India registered 29,670 rape cases (4.4 per lakh women); Rajasthan had the most with 5,078 (12.8 per lakh), followed by Uttar Pradesh (3,516), Madhya Pradesh (2,979), Maharashtra (2,930) and Haryana (1,772, a rate of 12.4).
text.hg: 2023 mein India mein rape ke 29,670 cases darj hue (har lakh mahilaon par 4.4); sabse zyada 5,078 cases Rajasthan mein the (har lakh par 12.8), iske baad Uttar Pradesh (3,516), Madhya Pradesh (2,979), Maharashtra (2,930) aur Haryana (1,772; rate 12.4) rahe.

facts.value: India 29,670; Rajasthan 5,078; UP 3,516; MP 2,979; Maharashtra 2,930; Haryana 1,772
facts.caveat: Columns: cases, victims, rate (preceded by Sec.373 IPC columns). Chandigarh had the highest rate (17.9). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: In 2022 India registered 31,516 rape cases (4.7 per lakh women); Rajasthan had the most with 5,399 (13.8 per lakh), followed by Uttar Pradesh (3,690), Madhya Pradesh (3,029), Maharashtra (2,904) and Haryana (1,787).
text.hg: 2022 mein India mein rape ke 31,516 cases darj hue (har lakh mahilaon par 4.7); sabse zyada 5,399 cases Rajasthan mein the (har lakh par 13.8), iske baad Uttar Pradesh (3,690), Madhya Pradesh (3,029), Maharashtra (2,904) aur Haryana (1,787) rahe.

facts.value: India 31,516; Rajasthan 5,399; UP 3,690; MP 3,029; Maharashtra 2,904; Haryana 1,787
facts.caveat: With the 2023 and 2024 editions, Rajasthan recorded the most rape cases in each of 2022, 2023 and 2024. Uttarakhand had the highest state rate in 2022 (15.4). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.hg: 2023 mein 19 metropolitan cities mein mahilaon ke khilaf 51,393 crime darj hue; Delhi mein 13,366 cases the, aur sabse oonchi rate Jaipur ki thi, har lakh mahilaon par 266.3; iske baad Lucknow (209.9), Indore (184.9) aur Delhi (176.4) rahe.

facts.value: 51,393 (19 cities); Delhi 13,366; Jaipur 266.3; Lucknow 209.9; Indore 184.9 per lakh women
facts.caveat: The 19-city total was 43,414 in 2021 and 48,755 in 2022 (same table). City rates use 2011 Census population. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

facts.value: 3,633 (19 cities); Delhi 1,204; Jaipur 497; Mumbai 370; Hyderabad 104; Kolkata 11

Across the 2022, 2023 and 2024 editions, Hyderabad's registered rape cases rose from 104 to 173 to 358, while Kolkata's stayed at 11, 10 and 12.
