text.en: Police registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by husband or relatives (Section 85 BNS/498A IPC) in 2024; Uttar Pradesh (21,266) and West Bengal (19,330) had the most, while Telangana had the highest rate at 52.8 per lakh women, against 3.0 in Bihar and 2.2 in Tamil Nadu.
text.hg: 2024 mein police ne pati ya rishtedaron dwara cruelty (Section 85 BNS/498A IPC) ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye; sabse zyada cases Uttar Pradesh (21,266) aur West Bengal (19,330) mein the, jabki sabse oonchi rate Telangana mein rahi, har lakh mahilaon par 52.8; iske mukable Bihar mein yeh rate 3.0 aur Tamil Nadu mein 2.2 thi.

facts.value: India 1,20,227 (17.6 per lakh women); UP 21,266; WB 19,330; Telangana 52.8; Bihar 3.0; Tamil Nadu 2.2
facts.caveat: Delhi's rate was 45.3 (4,647 cases). Registered cruelty cases capture only a fraction of domestic violence; compare NFHS-5 survey prevalence (st-nfhs5-spousal-states). 2024 counts combine IPC cases (Jan-Jun) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024).

text.en: India recorded 5,737 dowry deaths in 2024; Uttar Pradesh accounted for 2,038 (35.5%), followed by Bihar (1,078), Madhya Pradesh (450), Rajasthan (386) and West Bengal (337).
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein dowry death ke 5,737 cases darj hue; inmein se 2,038 (35.5%) Uttar Pradesh mein the, iske baad Bihar (1,078), Madhya Pradesh (450), Rajasthan (386) aur West Bengal (337) rahe.

facts.value: India 5,737; UP 2,038; Bihar 1,078; MP 450; Rajasthan 386; WB 337
facts.caveat: Share computed from NCRB counts. 2024 counts combine IPC cases (Jan-Jun) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Nationally, 29.2% of ever-married women aged 18-49 reported physical or sexual violence by their husband in NFHS-5 (2019-21); the highest shares were in Karnataka (44.4%), Bihar (40.1%), Manipur (39.6%), Tamil Nadu (38.1%) and Telangana (37.2%), and the lowest in Lakshadweep (1.3%) and Nagaland (6.5%).
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein desh bhar mein 18-49 saal ki un mahilaon mein se, jinki kabhi bhi shaadi hui ho, 29.2% ne bataya ki unke pati ne unke saath physical ya sexual violence ki; yeh hissa sabse zyada Karnataka (44.4%), Bihar (40.1%), Manipur (39.6%), Tamil Nadu (38.1%) aur Telangana (37.2%) mein, aur sabse kam Lakshadweep (1.3%) aur Nagaland (6.5%) mein raha.

facts.value: India 29.2%; Karnataka 44.4%; Bihar 40.1%; Manipur 39.6%; Tamil Nadu 38.1%; Telangana 37.2%; Lakshadweep 1.3%; Nagaland 6.5%
facts.caveat: Survey data (lifetime experience, ever-married women 18-49, 2019-21) are not comparable one-to-one with police FIR counts per lakh women in a calendar year; the contrast is indicative of under-registration, not a precise measure. Also: Uttar Pradesh 34.9%, Rajasthan 24.1%, Delhi 22.5%, Kerala 9.8%, Goa 8.3%.

text.en: Only 14% of Indian women who had experienced physical or sexual violence had ever sought help to stop it and 77% had never sought help or told anyone, according to NFHS-5 (2019-21); among those who did seek help, only 6% went to the police.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) ke mutabik physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki Indian mahilaon mein se sirf 14% ne use rokne ke liye kabhi madad maangi thi, aur 77% ne na kabhi madad maangi, na kisi ko bataya; jinhone madad maangi, unmein se sirf 6% police ke paas gayin.

facts.value: 14% sought help; 77% told no one; 6% of help-seekers approached police
facts.caveat: The 6% is a share of women who sought help, so fewer than 1 in 100 women who experienced violence went to the police (computed: 14% x 6% = about 0.8%). Covers women 18-49.

text.en: In Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh (12 November 2013), a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court held that registering an FIR is mandatory when information discloses a cognizable offence, that no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such a case, and that action must be taken against officers who refuse.
text.hg: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh case (12 November 2013) mein Supreme Court ki paanch judges ki Constitution Bench ne kaha ki jab information se kisi cognizable offence ka pata chalta ho, to FIR register karna mandatory hai, aise case mein koi preliminary inquiry nahin ho sakti, aur FIR darj karne se inkaar karne wale officers ke khilaf action hona chahiye.

facts.value: FIR registration mandatory for cognizable offences (12 Nov 2013)
facts.caveat: The judgment allowed preliminary inquiries (max. 7 days) in categories such as matrimonial/family disputes. Since 1 July 2024, Section 173(3) BNSS separately permits a 14-day preliminary enquiry for offences punishable with 3 to under 7 years.

text.en: Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, police must record information about a cognizable offence irrespective of where it was committed ('zero FIR'), may receive it electronically (signed within three days), must give a free copy to the informant or victim, and must have information from a woman about rape and other sexual offences recorded by a woman officer.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 173 ke tahat police ko kisi cognizable offence ki information darj karni hi hogi, chahe crime kahin bhi hua ho ('zero FIR'); police yeh information electronically bhi le sakti hai (jis par teen din ke andar signature zaroori hai), use informant ya victim ko iski free copy deni hogi, aur rape va doosre sexual offences ke baare mein kisi mahila ki di hui information mahila officer se hi record karani hogi.

facts.value: Section 173 BNSS: zero FIR, e-FIR, woman officer to record
facts.caveat: In force from 1 July 2024 (see st-law-new-laws-2024). If a station refuses, Section 173(4) lets the complainant write to the Superintendent of Police and then approach a Magistrate.

text.en: Section 173(3) BNSS lets police, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering offences punishable with three to under seven years; rape, punishable with at least ten years under Section 64 BNS, falls outside this window.
text.hg: BNSS ka Section 173(3) police ko yeh chhoot deta hai ki teen saal ya usse zyada, lekin saat saal se kam ki saza wale offences mein FIR darj karne se pehle woh Deputy SP ki permission se 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sake; rape, jismein BNS ke Section 64 ke tahat kam se kam das saal ki saza hai, is daayre se bahar hai.

facts.value: 14-day preliminary enquiry only for 3-7 year offences; rape minimum 10 years
facts.caveat: Offences such as stalking, voyeurism or sexual harassment with lower maximum punishments may fall inside the enquiry window; the conclusion about rape is the compiler's reading of the two sections.

text.en: Section 199(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 makes it a crime for a public servant to fail to record information about rape, gang rape, sexual assault, acid attack or trafficking, punishable with rigorous imprisonment of six months to two years and a fine.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 199(c) ke tahat kisi public servant ka rape, gang rape, sexual assault, acid attack ya trafficking ki information record na karna crime hai, jiski saza chhah mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment (kathor kaid) aur jurmana hai.

facts.value: 6 months to 2 years rigorous imprisonment + fine
facts.caveat: Sections listed cover rape (64-68, 70-71), assault/disrobing/voyeurism/insult to modesty (74, 76, 77, 79), acid attack (124) and trafficking (143-144). In force from 1 July 2024.

text.en: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam came into force across India on 1 July 2024, replacing the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act, which is why NCRB's 2024 tables split cases into IPC and BNS columns.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) aur Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) 1 July 2024 se poore India mein laagu hue aur inhone IPC, CrPC aur Evidence Act ki jagah li; isi wajah se NCRB ki 2024 ki tables mein cases ko IPC aur BNS ke alag-alag columns mein baanta gaya hai.

facts.caveat: NCRB's 2024 crime-head tables report IPC and BNS counts separately and as a total (e.g. Table 3A.2).

text.en: In December 2019 the Ministry of Home Affairs sanctioned Rs 100 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund to set up or strengthen Women Help Desks in police stations, staffed mainly by women officers, to make stations more approachable for women.
text.hg: December 2019 mein Ministry of Home Affairs ne Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 100 crore manzoor kiye, taaki police stations mein Women Help Desks banaye ya mazboot kiye ja sakein, jin par mukhya roop se mahila officers tainaat hon, aur thane mahilaon ke liye zyada approachable banein.

facts.caveat: NCRB cites women's helpdesks and e-FIR as initiatives that can raise registered crime (st-ncrb-caution-registration). State-wise numbers of functioning help desks were not verified.

text.en: A study in the American Economic Journal: Applied Economics (2012) found that after Indian states reserved one-third of local council seats for women, documented crimes against women rose 46% and recorded rapes 23%, driven mainly by greater reporting rather than more crime.
text.hg: 'American Economic Journal: Applied Economics' (2012) mein chhape ek study mein paaya gaya ki Indian states ne jab local councils ki ek-tihai seats mahilaon ke liye reserve ki, to uske baad mahilaon ke khilaf documented crime 46% aur recorded rape 23% badhe, aur iski mukhya wajah crime badhna nahin, balki zyada reporting thi.

facts.caveat: Based on NCRB data 1985-2007 and staggered state implementation of the 73rd Amendment reservations; percentages are from the authors' final version.

text.en: Researchers found that opening all-women police stations in Indian cities was associated with a 29% increase in police reports of crimes against women, mainly domestic violence, with no change in femicide, suggesting more reporting rather than more violence.
text.hg: Researchers ne paaya ki Indian cities mein all-women police stations khulne ke saath mahilaon ke khilaf crimes ki police reports mein 29% ki badhotri dekhi gayi, jinmein zyadatar domestic violence ke cases the, jabki femicide (mahilaon ki hatya) mein koi badlaav nahin aaya; isse sanket milta hai ki violence nahin, balki reporting badhi.

facts.value: +29% police reports of crimes against women
facts.caveat: Working paper (Amaral, Bhalotra, Prakash, April 2021); an earlier 2019 version reported a smaller effect.

text.en: In 2005, 12% of Indian households told the India Human Development Survey that unmarried girls were 'sometimes' or 'often' harassed in their neighbourhood, while NCRB records implied a figure of only 0.06% of households, a gap of about 200 times.
text.hg: 2005 mein India Human Development Survey mein 12% Indian households ne bataya ki unke mohalle mein unmarried ladkiyon ko 'sometimes' ya 'often' harass kiya jaata hai, jabki NCRB ke records se yeh aankda sirf 0.06% households ka banta tha, yaani lagbhag 200 guna ka fark.

facts.caveat: Old (2005) comparison quoted by Iyer et al.; the 'about 200 times' ratio is computed. The same passage notes 3.9% of IHDS households reported a theft versus 0.12% in NCRB data.

text.en: Of the 4,41,534 crimes against women registered in India in 2024, the largest categories were cruelty by husband or relatives (1,20,227 cases, 27.2%), kidnapping and abduction of women (67,829, 15.4%), POCSO cases with girl victims (67,809, 15.4%) and assault on women with intent to outrage their modesty (48,303, 10.9%); rape (29,536 cases) made up 6.7%.
text.hg: Of the 4,41,534 crimes against women registered in India in 2024, the largest categories were cruelty by husband or relatives (1,20,227 cases, 27.2%), kidnapping and abduction of women (67,829, 15.4%), POCSO cases with girl victims (67,809, 15.4%) and assault on women with intent to outrage their modesty (48,303, 10.9%); rape (29,536 cases) made up 6.7%.

facts.value: Cruelty 1,20,227 (27.2%); kidnapping/abduction of women 67,829 (15.4%); POCSO, girl victims 67,809 (15.4%); assault on modesty 48,303 (10.9%); rape 29,536 (6.7%)
facts.caveat: The rape share (29,536 / 4,41,534) is computed. POCSO here counts only cases with girl victims. Principal Offence Rule: one FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Police registered 48,303 cases of assault on women with intent to outrage their modesty (Section 74 BNS/354 IPC) in 2024, a rate of 7.1 per lakh women; Rajasthan (8,276) and Odisha (7,299) recorded the most, followed by Maharashtra (5,857), Karnataka (4,427) and Uttar Pradesh (4,418), and Odisha had the highest rate at 31.5 per lakh women, ahead of Rajasthan (20.7) and Jammu & Kashmir (20.5).
text.hg: Police registered 48,303 cases of assault on women with intent to outrage their modesty (Section 74 BNS/354 IPC) in 2024, a rate of 7.1 per lakh women; Rajasthan (8,276) and Odisha (7,299) recorded the most, followed by Maharashtra (5,857), Karnataka (4,427) and Uttar Pradesh (4,418), and Odisha had the highest rate at 31.5 per lakh women, ahead of Rajasthan (20.7) and Jammu & Kashmir (20.5).

facts.value: India 48,303 (7.1); Rajasthan 8,276; Odisha 7,299; Maharashtra 5,857; Karnataka 4,427; UP 4,418; rates: Odisha 31.5, Rajasthan 20.7, J&K 20.5 per lakh women
facts.caveat: Ranking compiled from the NCRB table (next by count: Madhya Pradesh 2,714; next by rate: Lakshadweep 16.7 on 5 cases, Karnataka 13.2). 2024 counts combine IPC cases (Jan-Jun) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Police registered 2,561 cases of attempt to commit rape in India in 2024; West Bengal (809) and Rajasthan (778) together accounted for 62% of them, far ahead of Assam (155) and Odisha (118).
text.hg: Police registered 2,561 cases of attempt to commit rape in India in 2024; West Bengal (809) and Rajasthan (778) together accounted for 62% of them, far ahead of Assam (155) and Odisha (118).

facts.value: India 2,561; West Bengal 809; Rajasthan 778; Assam 155; Odisha 118
facts.caveat: Share (1,587 / 2,561 = 62.0%) computed from NCRB counts. How states split cases between rape and attempt to rape varies; West Bengal registered 1,118 rape cases and 809 attempts. 2024 counts combine IPC cases (Jan-Jun) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: Police in India's 19 largest metropolitan cities charge-sheeted 76.8% of the crime-against-women cases they disposed of in 2024; the rate was lowest in Jaipur (55.7%) and Ghaziabad (65.8%) and highest in Kolkata (98.5%).
text.hg: Police in India's 19 largest metropolitan cities charge-sheeted 76.8% of the crime-against-women cases they disposed of in 2024; the rate was lowest in Jaipur (55.7%) and Ghaziabad (65.8%) and highest in Kolkata (98.5%).

facts.caveat: Chargesheeting rate = charge-sheeted cases as a share of cases disposed of by police. A high rate means more cases reached court, not that more cases ended in conviction. NCRB data are police-registered FIRs, not incidence; NCRB warns States/UTs should not be compared purely on crime figures. Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: India's three new criminal laws, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, came into force on 1 July 2024.
text.hg: India ke teen naye criminal laws, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) aur Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 1 July 2024 se lagu hue.

facts.caveat: The BNS repeals the Indian Penal Code (BNS s.358) and the BNSS repeals the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (BNSS s.531); the BSA replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Crimes committed before 1 July 2024 are still prosecuted under the IPC. PIB notes that BNS Section 106(2) (hit-and-run) was not brought into force.

text.en: Under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, rape covers penetration of the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus by the penis, insertion of any object or body part, manipulation to cause penetration and oral contact, when done against a woman's will, without her consent, with consent obtained through fear of death or hurt or by a man posing as her husband, with consent given while she was intoxicated or of unsound mind, when she cannot communicate consent, or with any girl under 18 whatever she says.
text.hg: Under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, rape covers penetration of the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus by the penis, insertion of any object or body part, manipulation to cause penetration and oral contact, when done against a woman's will, without her consent, with consent obtained through fear of death or hurt or by a man posing as her husband, with consent given while she was intoxicated or of unsound mind, when she cannot communicate consent, or with any girl under 18 whatever she says.

facts.caveat: Only a man can commit the offence and only a woman can be its victim.

text.en: Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 defines consent as an 'unequivocal voluntary agreement' communicated by words, gestures or other communication, and says a woman who does not physically resist penetration is not, for that reason alone, to be treated as consenting.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ka Section 63 consent ko 'unequivocal voluntary agreement', yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi razamandi, ke roop mein define karta hai, jo words, gestures ya kisi aur communication se batayi gayi ho, aur kehta hai ki agar kisi aurat ne penetration ka physically virodh nahi kiya, to sirf isi wajah se use consent nahi maana jayega.

facts.value: Consent must be unequivocal; not resisting is not consent

text.en: Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 says sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape, so forced sex by a husband on an adult wife is still not legally rape in India.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar wife 18 saal ya usse zyada umr ki hai, to aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sexual intercourse ya sexual acts rape nahi hai, yaani India mein pati ka adult wife ke saath zabardasti sex ab bhi legally rape nahi hai.

facts.caveat: The constitutional challenge is pending in the Supreme Court (final hearing listed for 9 or 10 December 2026); re-check before publishing.

text.en: Rape is punishable under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 with at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life; 13 aggravated forms, including rape by police, public servants, armed forces, jail or hospital staff, relatives, guardians or teachers, rape during communal violence, of a pregnant or disabled woman, or repeated rape, carry 10 years to imprisonment for the rest of natural life.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 64 ke tahat rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo umrqaid tak ho sakti hai; iske 13 aggravated (gambhir) roopon mein, jinmein police, public servants, armed forces, jail ya hospital staff, rishtedaron, guardians ya teachers dwara rape, communal violence ke dauran rape, pregnant ya disabled aurat ka rape, ya baar-baar rape shamil hain, 10 saal se lekar baaki natural life tak jail ki saza hai.

facts.value: Minimum 10 years; aggravated: 10 years to remainder of natural life

text.en: Under Section 65 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, raping a girl under 16 carries at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, and raping a girl under 12 carries the same or death; any fine must be paid to the victim.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 65 ke tahat 16 saal se kam umr ki ladki ke rape par kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo baaki natural life tak jail tak ho sakti hai, aur 12 saal se kam umr ki ladki ke rape par yahi saza ya maut ki saza hai; koi bhi jurmana lage to woh victim ko dena zaroori hai.

facts.value: Under 16: 20 years to natural life; under 12: 20 years to natural life or death

text.en: Under Section 66 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, a rapist who causes the woman's death or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state faces at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 66 ke tahat jis rapist ki wajah se aurat ki maut ho jaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaye, use kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment, jo baaki natural life tak jail tak ho sakti hai, ya maut ki saza ho sakti hai.

facts.value: 20 years to natural life, or death

text.en: Section 67 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes a husband who has sex with his wife without her consent while they live separately with 2 to 7 years in prison, far below the 10-year minimum for raping any other woman.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 67 ke tahat alag rehne ke dauran wife ki consent ke bina uske saath sex karne wale pati ko 2 se 7 saal jail ki saza hai, jo kisi bhi doosri aurat ke rape ke liye tay minimum 10 saal ki saza se bahut kam hai.

text.en: Section 68 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes a person in authority, a public servant, or jail, institution or hospital staff who abuses that position to get a woman in his custody or care to have sex with him, short of rape, with 5 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 68 ke tahat authority wale pad par baitha vyakti, public servant, ya jail, institution ya hospital ka staff agar apne pad ka galat istemal karke apni custody ya dekhrekh mein reh rahi aurat ko apne saath sex ke liye raazi karta hai, aur yeh rape ki category tak nahi pahunchta, to use 5 se 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ki saza hai.

text.en: Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 created a new offence of sex obtained by 'deceitful means' or by a promise of marriage made with no intention of keeping it, including false promises of a job or promotion or marrying while hiding one's identity, punishable with up to 10 years in prison.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 69 ne ek naya offence banaya: 'deceitful means' (dhokhe ke tareekon) se ya shaadi ka aisa vaada karke sex karna jise nibhane ka iraada hi na ho, jismein naukri ya promotion ka jhootha vaada ya apni pehchaan chhipakar shaadi karna bhi shamil hai; iski saza 10 saal tak ki jail hai.

facts.caveat: Section 69 is not among the offences that BNSS Sections 193(2) and 346 require to be investigated and tried within two months.

text.en: Under Section 70 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, every member of a group that rapes a woman is guilty of rape and faces at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life; if she is under 18, the punishment is imprisonment for the rest of natural life or death.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 70 ke tahat kisi aurat ka rape karne wale group ka har member rape ka doshi hai aur use kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai, jo baaki natural life tak jail tak ja sakti hai; agar woh 18 saal se kam umr ki hai, to saza baaki natural life tak jail ya maut hai.

facts.value: Adult: 20 years to natural life; under 18: natural life or death

text.en: Section 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes anyone convicted a second time of rape under Sections 64, 65, 66 or 70 with imprisonment for the rest of natural life or death.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 71 ke tahat Sections 64, 65, 66 ya 70 ke under rape mein doosri baar convict hue kisi bhi vyakti ko baaki natural life tak jail ya maut ki saza hai.

text.en: Publishing the name or any detail that could identify a rape survivor is a crime under Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, punishable with up to 2 years in prison and a fine unless the survivor authorises it in writing, and Section 73 punishes publishing anything about rape-case court proceedings without the court's permission with up to 2 years.
text.hg: Rape survivor ka naam ya koi bhi aisi detail publish karna jisse uski pehchaan ho sake, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 72 ke tahat crime hai, jiski saza 2 saal tak ki jail aur jurmana hai, jab tak survivor khud likhit mein iski ijaazat na de; aur Section 73 ke tahat court ki permission ke bina rape case ki court proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi publish karne par 2 saal tak ki saza hai.

facts.caveat: Publishing High Court or Supreme Court judgments is exempt under Section 73.

text.en: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes assault to outrage a woman's modesty with 1 to 5 years (s.74), sexual harassment with up to 3 years (s.75), assault to disrobe with 3 to 7 years (s.76), voyeurism with 1 to 3 years on first conviction and 3 to 7 years on a repeat (s.77), stalking with up to 3 years, rising to 5 on a repeat (s.78), and words or gestures insulting a woman's modesty with up to 3 years (s.79).
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 mein sazaayein is tarah hain: aurat ki modesty bhang karne (outrage) ke iraade se assault, 1 se 5 saal (s.74); sexual harassment, 3 saal tak (s.75); kapde utaarne (disrobe) ke iraade se assault, 3 se 7 saal (s.76); voyeurism (taak-jhaank), pehli conviction par 1 se 3 saal aur dobara hone par 3 se 7 saal (s.77); stalking, 3 saal tak, jo dobara hone par 5 saal tak ho jaati hai (s.78); aur aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabd ya ishaare, 3 saal tak (s.79).

facts.value: s.74: 1-5 yrs; s.75: up to 3 yrs; s.76: 3-7 yrs; s.77: 1-3 / 3-7 yrs; s.78: up to 3 / 5 yrs; s.79: up to 3 yrs
facts.caveat: Sexually coloured remarks (s.75(1)(iv)) carry up to 1 year. Sexual harassment and stalking can, by their wording, only be committed by a man.

text.en: Under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sharing a private image of a woman without her consent is voyeurism even if she agreed to the image being taken, punishable with 1 to 3 years in prison on first conviction.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 77 ke tahat kisi aurat ki private image uski consent ke bina share karna voyeurism hai, chahe usne image khinchne ke liye consent di ho; pehli conviction par iski saza 1 se 3 saal ki jail hai.

facts.value: Consent to capture is not consent to share

text.en: Under Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, when a woman dies of burns, injuries or in abnormal circumstances within 7 years of marriage after dowry-related cruelty soon before her death, it is a 'dowry death', the husband or in-laws are deemed to have caused it, and the punishment is 7 years to life imprisonment.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 80 ke tahat agar kisi aurat ki shaadi ke 7 saal ke andar jalne, chot lagne ya abnormal halaat mein maut hoti hai, aur maut se kuch samay pehle uske saath dahej se judi cruelty hui thi, to yeh 'dowry death' (dahej mrityu) hai, pati ya sasuraal walon ko hi uski maut ka kaaran maana jaata hai, aur saza 7 saal se lekar umrqaid tak hai.

facts.value: Within 7 years of marriage; 7 years to life

text.en: Cruelty to a woman by her husband or his relatives, defined as wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to force her or her family to meet unlawful demands for property, is punishable under Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 with up to 3 years in prison and a fine.
text.hg: Pati ya uske rishtedaron dwara aurat ke saath cruelty, yaani jaan-boojhkar kiya gaya aisa bartaav jo use suicide ke liye majboor kar sakta ho ya gambhir chot pahuncha sakta ho, ya use ya uske parivaar ko property ki gair-kanooni maangein poori karne ke liye majboor karne ke liye kiya gaya harassment, par Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Sections 85 aur 86 ke tahat 3 saal tak ki jail aur jurmana ho sakta hai.

facts.caveat: Replaces IPC Section 498A.

text.en: An acid attack causing permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns or disability is punishable under Section 124(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 with at least 10 years up to life imprisonment and a fine paid to the victim for treatment, and throwing or attempting to throw acid carries 5 to 7 years under Section 124(2).
text.hg: Permanent ya partial damage, deformity, burns ya disability karne wale acid attack par Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 124(1) ke tahat kam se kam 10 saal se lekar umrqaid tak ki saza aur jurmana hai, jo ilaaj ke liye victim ko diya jaata hai; aur acid phenkne ya phenkne ki koshish karne par Section 124(2) ke tahat 5 se 7 saal ki saza hai.

facts.value: Attack: 10 years to life; attempt: 5 to 7 years

text.en: Trafficking a person for exploitation, including sexual exploitation, is punishable under Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 with 7 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, at least 10 years for trafficking a child and imprisonment for the rest of natural life for a police officer or public servant involved, the victim's consent being immaterial; under Section 144, knowingly sexually exploiting a trafficked child carries 5 to 10 years and a trafficked adult 3 to 7 years.
text.hg: Sexual exploitation samet kisi bhi tarah ke exploitation ke liye kisi vyakti ki trafficking par Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 143 ke tahat 7 se 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, bachche ki trafficking par kam se kam 10 saal, aur ismein shamil police officer ya public servant ke liye baaki natural life tak jail; ismein victim ki consent maayne nahi rakhti. Section 144 ke tahat trafficking ke shikaar vyakti ka jaan-boojhkar sexual exploitation karne par, bachcha ho to 5 se 10 saal aur adult ho to 3 se 7 saal ki saza hai.

facts.value: s.143: 7-10 yrs; child 10 yrs-life; >1 child 14 yrs-life; s.144: child 5-10 yrs, adult 3-7 yrs

text.en: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which repealed the Indian Penal Code, has no counterpart to IPC Section 377, so non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the new code and no specific offence replaced it.
text.hg: Indian Penal Code (IPC) ko repeal karne wali Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 mein IPC Section 377 jaisa koi provision nahi hai, isliye naye code ke tahat kisi adult aadmi ya transgender vyakti ke saath bina consent ke penetrative sex rape nahi hai, aur iski jagah koi specific offence bhi nahi laaya gaya.

facts.caveat: Absence checked by searching the full Act text; NCRB's Crime in India 2024 also marks 'Unnatural Offences' as a section 'deleted in BNS'. Boys under 18 remain protected by POCSO.

text.en: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 defines the pronoun 'he' to cover any person 'whether male, female or transgender', and defines 'man' as a male and 'woman' as a female human being of any age, which keeps rape (Section 63) limited to a man assaulting a woman.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 pronoun 'he' ke daayre mein har vyakti ko shamil karti hai, 'whether male, female or transgender', aur 'man' ko kisi bhi umr ka male aur 'woman' ko kisi bhi umr ki female human being define karti hai, jisse rape (Section 63) sirf aadmi dwara aurat par assault tak simit rehta hai.

text.en: In a July 2024 note on the new criminal laws, the Home Ministry said 'various offences against women and children have been made gender-neutral in BNS, covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender' and that the definition of gender 'now includes transgender individuals'.
text.hg: Naye criminal laws par July 2024 ke ek note mein Home Ministry ne kaha ki 'various offences against women and children have been made gender-neutral in BNS, covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender' aur gender ki definition 'now includes transgender individuals'.

facts.caveat: The rape provision (s.63) itself remains gender-specific; compare with law-bns-rape-definition-s63.

text.en: Voluntarily causing hurt is punishable under Section 115(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 with at most 1 year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both.
text.hg: Jaan-boojhkar chot pahunchane (voluntarily causing hurt) par Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 115(2) ke tahat zyada se zyada 1 saal ki jail, Rs 10,000 tak ka jurmana, ya dono ho sakte hain.

facts.value: Up to 1 year or Rs 10,000 fine
facts.caveat: With no counterpart to IPC Section 377, the BNS has no specific offence for non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man, so only general offences such as hurt, grievous hurt or wrongful confinement may apply, depending on the facts.

text.en: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, a police officer who fails to record an FIR for rape, sexual assault, acid attack or trafficking faces 6 months to 2 years' rigorous imprisonment (s.199), and a hospital in-charge who refuses free treatment to a rape or acid-attack survivor faces up to 1 year (s.200).
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke tahat rape, sexual assault, acid attack ya trafficking ki FIR darj na karne wale police officer ko 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment (s.199) ho sakti hai, aur rape ya acid-attack survivor ko free ilaaj dene se inkaar karne wale hospital in-charge ko 1 saal tak ki saza (s.200) ho sakti hai.

facts.value: FIR refusal: 6 months-2 years; hospital refusal: up to 1 year

text.en: Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 lets anyone report a cognizable offence at any police station 'irrespective of the area where the offence is committed' (Zero FIR) or by electronic communication (e-FIR), which must be signed within 3 days, and the victim must get a copy of the FIR free of cost.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 173 ke tahat koi bhi vyakti kisi cognizable offence ki shikayat kisi bhi police station mein 'irrespective of the area where the offence is committed', yaani crime chahe kisi bhi ilaake mein hua ho (Zero FIR), ya electronic communication se (e-FIR) darj kara sakta hai, jis par 3 din ke andar sign karna zaroori hai, aur victim ko FIR ki copy free milni chahiye.

facts.value: Zero FIR and e-FIR in statute; free FIR copy

text.en: Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a woman's complaint of rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism or acid attack must be recorded by a woman police officer or woman officer (s.173), and a rape survivor's statement must be taken at her home or a place of her choice, as far as practicable by a woman officer, and may be recorded on video including a mobile phone (s.176).
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke tahat rape, sexual harassment, stalking, voyeurism ya acid attack ki kisi aurat ki complaint woman police officer ya kisi woman officer ko hi record karni hogi (s.173), aur rape survivor ka bayaan uske ghar par ya uski pasand ki jagah par, jahan tak mumkin ho kisi woman officer dwara, liya jaana chahiye, aur ise mobile phone samet video par record kiya ja sakta hai (s.176).

facts.value: Woman officer; statement at home or place of choice; audio-video
facts.caveat: For a survivor with a disability, the FIR must be recorded at her home or a place of her choice with an interpreter or special educator, and videographed.

text.en: Under Section 183(6) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a magistrate, as far as practicable a woman magistrate, must record the survivor's statement in rape, sexual harassment, stalking and acid-attack cases as soon as police learn of the offence, with an interpreter or special educator and video recording if the survivor has a disability.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 183(6) ke tahat rape, sexual harassment, stalking aur acid-attack cases mein police ko crime ka pata chalte hi kisi magistrate ko, jahan tak mumkin ho woman magistrate ko, survivor ka bayaan record karna hoga; agar survivor ko koi disability hai, to interpreter ya special educator ki madad li jayegi aur video recording hogi.

facts.value: Statement before magistrate, preferably a woman

text.en: Section 184 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 requires a rape survivor to be sent for medical examination, preferably by a government doctor, within 24 hours of police receiving information, only with her consent, and the doctor must send the report to the investigating officer within 7 days.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 184 ke mutabik police ko information milne ke 24 ghante ke andar rape survivor ko, sirf uski consent se, medical examination ke liye bhejna zaroori hai, preferably kisi government doctor ke paas, aur doctor ko 7 din ke andar report investigating officer ko bhejni hogi.

facts.value: Exam within 24 hours; report within 7 days; consent mandatory

text.en: Under Section 193(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, police must complete the investigation of rape (BNS ss.64-68, 70, 71) and of penetrative and other sexual assault on children under POCSO (ss.4, 6, 8, 10) within two months of recording the information.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 193(2) ke tahat police ko rape (BNS ss.64-68, 70, 71) aur POCSO ke tahat bachchon par penetrative aur doosre sexual assault (ss.4, 6, 8, 10) ki investigation information record karne ke do mahine ke andar poori karni hogi.

facts.caveat: The law sets no consequence for missing the deadline. The two-month rule first entered the CrPC in 2018.

text.en: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 requires rape trials under BNS Sections 64 to 68, 70 and 71 to be completed within two months of the chargesheet (s.346) and appeals against rape sentences to be decided within six months (s.415(4)).
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke mutabik BNS Sections 64 se 68, 70 aur 71 ke tahat rape trials chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar poore hone chahiye (s.346), aur rape ki saza ke khilaf appeals par faisla chhah mahine ke andar hona chahiye (s.415(4)).

facts.value: Trial: 2 months from chargesheet; appeal: 6 months
facts.caveat: Directory deadlines with no consequence for breach; compare with Fast Track Special Court pendency.

text.en: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 entitles a victim to an update on the investigation within 90 days (s.193(3)), free copies of the police report, FIR and statements within 14 days of the accused's first appearance if she has a lawyer (s.230), and a hearing before any prosecution is withdrawn (s.360).
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke tahat victim ko yeh haq hain: 90 din ke andar investigation par update (s.193(3)); agar uska vakeel hai, to accused ki pehli peshi ke 14 din ke andar police report, FIR aur bayaanon ki free copies (s.230); aur kisi bhi prosecution ko wapas lene se pehle sunwai ka mauka (s.360).

facts.value: Update in 90 days; documents in 14 days; heard before withdrawal

text.en: Under Section 366(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, rape and POCSO trials must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge or magistrate, and nothing about the proceedings may be published without the court's permission.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 366(2) ke tahat rape aur POCSO trials in camera, yaani band kamre mein, hone chahiye, jahan tak mumkin ho kisi woman judge ya magistrate ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi publish nahi kiya ja sakta.

facts.value: In-camera trial; woman judge where practicable

text.en: Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 obliges every hospital, public or private, to give immediate free first aid or medical treatment to survivors of rape, acid attack and POCSO offences and to inform the police.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 397 ke tahat har hospital, chahe government ho ya private, rape, acid attack aur POCSO offences ke survivors ko turant free first aid ya medical treatment dene aur police ko inform karne ke liye baadhya hai.

text.en: Under Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (formerly CrPC Section 357A), every state must run a victim compensation scheme; a victim can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, and the authority must finish its inquiry within two months.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 396 (pehle CrPC Section 357A) ke tahat har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hogi; victim seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakta hai, chahe offender ka kabhi pata na chale aur koi trial na ho, aur authority ko do mahine ke andar apni inquiry poori karni hogi.

facts.value: Compensation without a trial; decision within 2 months
facts.caveat: Compensation is also available when the trial ends in acquittal (s.396(3)) and is in addition to any fine paid to the victim (s.396(7)).

text.en: Section 482(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 bars anticipatory bail for anyone accused of raping a girl under 16 (BNS s.65) or of gang rape of a girl under 18 (BNS s.70(2)).
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ke Section 482(4) ke tahat 16 saal se kam umr ki ladki ke rape (BNS s.65) ya 18 saal se kam umr ki ladki ke gang rape (BNS s.70(2)) ke kisi bhi accused ko anticipatory bail nahi mil sakti.

text.en: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, in force since 14 November 2012, defines a child as anyone under 18 and protects boys and girls alike.
text.hg: 14 November 2012 se lagu Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, 18 saal se kam umr ke har vyakti ko child maanta hai aur ladkon aur ladkiyon ko barabar protection deta hai.

text.en: The POCSO Amendment Act, 2019 (in force 16 August 2019) made aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child punishable with at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death, raised the minimum for penetrative sexual assault from 7 to 10 years, and set a 20-year minimum when the child is under 16.
text.hg: POCSO Amendment Act, 2019 (16 August 2019 se lagu) ne bachche par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ki saza kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment, jo baaki natural life tak jail tak ho sakti hai, ya maut kar di, penetrative sexual assault ki minimum saza 7 se badhakar 10 saal kar di, aur bachche ki umr 16 saal se kam hone par minimum saza 20 saal tay ki.

facts.value: Death penalty added; minimum raised 7 to 10 years; under 16: 20 years

text.en: POCSO Sections 19 and 21 make reporting child sexual abuse mandatory for anyone who knows of it; failing to report or record a case is punishable with up to 6 months in prison or a fine, and the head of a company or institution who fails to report abuse by a subordinate faces up to 1 year and a fine.
text.hg: POCSO ke Sections 19 aur 21 ke tahat child sexual abuse ki jaankari rakhne wale har vyakti ke liye uski report karna mandatory hai; case report na karne ya record na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya jurmana ho sakta hai, aur apne subordinate dwara kiye gaye abuse ki report na karne wale kisi company ya institution ke head ko 1 saal tak ki saza aur jurmana ho sakta hai.

facts.value: Up to 6 months; institution heads up to 1 year
facts.caveat: Section 19(1) puts the duty to report on 'any person (including the child)', but a child cannot be punished for not reporting (s.21(3)). Police must also report the case to the Child Welfare Committee and Special Court within 24 hours (s.19(6)).

text.en: Section 23 of the POCSO Act bars any media report from revealing a child victim's name, address, photograph, family details, school or neighbourhood unless the Special Court permits it in the child's interest; a violation is punishable with 6 months to 1 year in prison, a fine, or both, and the publisher or owner is jointly liable.
text.hg: Section 23 of the POCSO Act bars any media report from revealing a child victim's name, address, photograph, family details, school or neighbourhood unless the Special Court permits it in the child's interest; a violation is punishable with 6 months to 1 year in prison, a fine, or both, and the publisher or owner is jointly liable.

facts.value: 6 months to 1 year, or fine, or both

text.en: The POCSO Act requires a designated Special Court in each district (s.28), the child's evidence to be recorded within 30 days of the court taking cognizance, and the trial to be completed, as far as possible, within one year (s.35).
text.hg: POCSO Act ke mutabik har district mein ek designated Special Court hona chahiye (s.28), court ke cognizance lene ke 30 din ke andar bachche ki gawahi record honi chahiye, aur jahan tak mumkin ho, trial ek saal ke andar poora hona chahiye (s.35).

facts.value: Evidence within 30 days; trial within 1 year

text.en: Under Section 29 of the POCSO Act, a Special Court must presume that a person prosecuted for penetrative or sexual assault on a child committed the offence unless the contrary is proved, reversing the usual burden of proof.
text.hg: POCSO Act ke Section 29 ke tahat, bachche par penetrative ya sexual assault ke liye jis vyakti par case chal raha hai, Special Court ko yeh maankar chalna hoga ki offence usi ne kiya hai, jab tak iske ulat saabit na ho jaye; isse burden of proof ka aam niyam ulat jaata hai.

text.en: The Criminal Law Amendment Act 43 of 1983, in force from 25 December 1983, made it a crime to disclose a rape victim's identity (IPC Section 228A) and required rape trials to be held in camera (CrPC Section 327(2)), according to the Supreme Court.
text.hg: Supreme Court ke mutabik, 25 December 1983 se lagu Criminal Law Amendment Act 43 of 1983 ne rape victim ki pehchaan disclose karne ko crime banaya (IPC Section 228A) aur rape trials ko in camera, yaani band kamre mein, chalana zaroori kiya (CrPC Section 327(2)).

facts.value: Identity ban and in-camera trials since 25 Dec 1983
facts.caveat: The 1983 Act's other changes (custodial rape provisions, presumption of absence of consent) and the protests that preceded it were not verified from a primary source in this session.

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, deemed in force from 3 February 2013, rewrote the definition of rape to cover penetration of the mouth, urethra or anus and insertion of objects, fixed the age of consent at 18, set a 20-year minimum for gang rape, created the offences of sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism, stalking and acid attack, and rewrote the trafficking offence.
text.hg: 3 February 2013 se lagu maane gaye Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne rape ki definition naye sire se likhi taaki usmein munh, urethra ya anus mein penetration aur objects daalna bhi shamil ho, age of consent 18 saal tay ki, gang rape ke liye minimum 20 saal ki saza tay ki, sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism, stalking aur acid attack ko offence banaya, aur trafficking ke offence ko naye sire se likha.

facts.value: In force 3 Feb 2013; consent age 18; gang rape min 20 years
facts.caveat: The 2013 Act kept the minimum sentence for rape at 7 years (s.376(1)); it was raised to 10 years in 2018.

text.en: When the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 raised the age of consent to 18, it kept the marital exception for wives aged 15 and above, so from 2013 until 2017 a husband's sex with a 15-to-17-year-old wife was not legally rape.
text.hg: Jab Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne age of consent badhakar 18 saal ki, tab bhi usne 15 saal aur usse zyada umr ki wives ke liye marital exception banaye rakha, isliye 2013 se 2017 tak 15 se 17 saal ki wife ke saath pati ka sex legally rape nahi tha.

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 made it a crime for police to refuse to record an FIR for rape or acid attack (6 months to 2 years), required all hospitals to treat rape and acid-attack survivors free of cost, and barred evidence of a survivor's character or past sexual experience on the question of consent.
text.hg: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne rape ya acid attack ki FIR darj karne se police ke inkaar ko crime banaya (6 mahine se 2 saal), sabhi hospitals ke liye rape aur acid-attack survivors ka free ilaaj karna zaroori kiya, aur consent ke sawaal par survivor ke character ya pichhle sexual experience se jude evidence par rok lagayi.

facts.value: FIR refusal 6 months-2 years; free treatment; sexual history irrelevant

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, deemed in force from 21 April 2018, raised the minimum sentence for rape from 7 to 10 years, introduced the death penalty for raping a girl under 12, set a 20-year minimum for raping a girl under 16, required every rape investigation to be completed within two months (earlier only child-rape cases had a three-month target), required rape appeals to be decided within six months and barred anticipatory bail for rape of girls under 16.
text.hg: 21 April 2018 se lagu maane gaye Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 ne rape ki minimum saza 7 se badhakar 10 saal ki, 12 saal se kam umr ki ladki ke rape ke liye maut ki saza ka provision kiya, 16 saal se kam umr ki ladki ke rape par minimum 20 saal ki saza tay ki, har rape investigation do mahine ke andar poori karna zaroori kiya (pehle sirf child-rape cases mein teen mahine ka target tha), rape appeals par chhah mahine ke andar faisla zaroori kiya, aur 16 saal se kam umr ki ladkiyon ke rape mein anticipatory bail par rok lagayi.

facts.value: Minimum 7 to 10 years; death for rape of girls under 12
facts.caveat: Act No. 22 of 2018 received assent on 11 August 2018; it replaced an ordinance of April 2018.

text.en: In Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (11 December 2018), the Supreme Court ruled that no one may publish a rape survivor's name in print, electronic or social media 'or even in a remote manner' disclose facts that could identify her, and that FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain.
text.hg: Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (11 December 2018) case mein Supreme Court ne faisla diya ki koi bhi print, electronic ya social media mein rape survivor ka naam publish nahi kar sakta, 'or even in a remote manner', yaani ghuma-phira kar bhi, aise facts disclose nahi kar sakta jinse uski pehchaan ho sake, aur rape aur POCSO cases ki FIRs public domain mein nahi daali jaani chahiye.

facts.value: Total bar on direct or indirect identification
facts.caveat: The bar applies even when the victim has died, unless a Sessions Judge permits disclosure.

text.en: In December 2018 the Supreme Court asked every state and union territory to set up at least one One Stop Centre for survivors of sexual violence in every district within one year.
text.hg: December 2018 mein Supreme Court ne har state aur union territory se kaha ki woh ek saal ke andar har district mein sexual violence ke survivors ke liye kam se kam ek One Stop Centre banayein.

facts.value: At least one OSC per district by December 2019

text.en: On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read down the marital rape exception so that sex with a wife under 18 is rape, noting that Parliament had raised the age of consent to 18 in 2013 but left the exception at 15.
text.hg: 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne marital rape exception ko read down kar diya, jisse 18 saal se kam umr ki wife ke saath sex rape hai; court ne note kiya ki Parliament ne 2013 mein age of consent badhakar 18 saal kar di thi, lekin exception ko 15 saal par hi chhod diya tha.

facts.value: Marital exception read down to wives aged 18+
facts.caveat: The court expressly did not decide the marital rape of adult women (para 106).

text.en: On 31 October 2022, in State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai, the Supreme Court held that anyone who conducts the 'two-finger test' on a rape survivor is guilty of misconduct, calling it a practice with 'no scientific basis' that 're-victimizes and re-traumatizes' women, and ordered it removed from medical curricula.
text.hg: 31 October 2022 ko State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai case mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki rape survivor par 'two-finger test' karne wala koi bhi vyakti misconduct ka doshi hai; court ne ise aisi practice bataya jiska 'koi scientific aadhaar nahi' hai aur jo aurton ko 'dobara victim banati aur dobara trauma deti hai', aur ise medical curricula se hatane ka order diya.

facts.caveat: The Court also directed that Health Ministry guidelines banning the test be circulated to all government and private hospitals; it restored the trial court's conviction of the accused for rape and murder.

text.en: On 11 May 2022 the Delhi High Court delivered a split verdict on the marital rape exception in RIT Foundation v. Union of India: Justice Rajiv Shakdher held it unconstitutional, while Justice C. Hari Shankar upheld it, sending the question to the Supreme Court.
text.hg: 11 May 2022 ko Delhi High Court ne RIT Foundation v. Union of India case mein marital rape exception par split verdict diya: Justice Rajiv Shakdher ne ise unconstitutional thehraya, jabki Justice C. Hari Shankar ne ise barkaraar rakha, jisse yeh sawaal Supreme Court ke paas pahunch gaya.

text.en: In an October 2024 affidavit to the Supreme Court, the Union government opposed striking down the marital rape exception, arguing that treating non-consensual sex within marriage as rape could be 'excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate' and that other laws, including the domestic violence law, already give remedies.
text.hg: October 2024 mein Supreme Court mein diye gaye ek affidavit mein Union government ne marital rape exception ko radd karne ka virodh kiya aur dalil di ki shaadi ke andar bina consent ke sex ko rape maanna 'excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate' ho sakta hai, aur domestic violence law samet doosre kanoon pehle se hi remedies dete hain.

text.en: As of 19 November 2026, the Supreme Court had still not ruled on the marital rape exception; a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026, before the winter break.
text.hg: 19 November 2026 tak bhi Supreme Court ne marital rape exception par faisla nahi diya tha; Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur V. Mohana ki bench ne kaha ki woh winter break se pehle, 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko, final hearing rakhegi.

facts.caveat: Fast-moving: check for a verdict before publishing.

text.en: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs, in its report on the BNS Bill submitted on 10 November 2023, said it was 'mandatory to reintroduce and retain Section 377 of the IPC' for non-consensual acts, but the government did not accept the recommendation.
text.hg: Home Affairs par Parliamentary Standing Committee ne 10 November 2023 ko submit ki gayi BNS Bill par apni report mein kaha ki non-consensual acts ke liye IPC ke Section 377 ko wapas laana aur banaye rakhna 'mandatory' hai, lekin sarkar ne yeh recommendation nahi maani.

facts.caveat: The enacted BNS (Act 45 of 2023) contains no such provision.

text.en: Under Section 66E of the Information Technology Act, 2000, capturing, publishing or transmitting an image of a person's private area without consent is punishable with up to 3 years in prison, a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh, or both.
text.hg: Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 ke Section 66E ke tahat kisi vyakti ke private area ki image bina consent ke capture, publish ya transmit karne par 3 saal tak ki jail, Rs 2 lakh tak ka jurmana, ya dono ho sakte hain.

facts.value: Up to 3 years or Rs 2 lakh

text.en: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000, publishing obscene material online carries up to 3 years and a Rs 5 lakh fine on first conviction (s.67), sexually explicit material up to 5 years and Rs 10 lakh (s.67A), and child sexual abuse material, including creating, browsing or downloading it, up to 5 years and Rs 10 lakh (s.67B), with repeat convictions punishable by up to 5 years (s.67) or 7 years (ss.67A and 67B).
text.hg: Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 ke tahat online obscene material publish karne par pehli conviction par 3 saal tak ki jail aur Rs 5 lakh jurmana (s.67), sexually explicit material par 5 saal tak aur Rs 10 lakh (s.67A), aur child sexual abuse material par, jismein use banana, browse karna ya download karna bhi shamil hai, 5 saal tak aur Rs 10 lakh (s.67B) ki saza hai; dobara conviction par 5 saal (s.67) ya 7 saal (ss.67A aur 67B) tak ki saza ho sakti hai.

facts.value: s.67: 3 yrs/Rs 5 lakh; s.67A and 67B: 5 yrs/Rs 10 lakh; repeat 5-7 yrs
facts.caveat: POCSO Special Courts can try s.67B offences (POCSO s.28(3)).

text.en: Under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, giving, taking or abetting dowry is punishable with at least 5 years in prison and a fine of at least Rs 15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more, and demanding dowry with 6 months to 2 years and a fine of up to Rs 10,000; the offences are non-bailable.
text.hg: Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ke tahat dahej dene, lene ya iske liye uksane par kam se kam 5 saal ki jail aur kam se kam Rs 15,000 ya dahej ki value, jo bhi zyada ho, ka jurmana hai, aur dahej maangne par 6 mahine se 2 saal ki jail aur Rs 10,000 tak ka jurmana; yeh offences non-bailable hain.

facts.value: Giving/taking: min 5 years + Rs 15,000; demanding: 6 months-2 years
facts.caveat: Courts may impose less than the minimum for 'adequate and special reasons' recorded in the judgment.

text.en: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts 'sexual abuse', defined as any sexual conduct that abuses, humiliates, degrades or violates a woman's dignity, as domestic violence, but breaching a protection order is punishable with at most 1 year in prison or a Rs 20,000 fine.
text.hg: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 'sexual abuse' ko, yaani aise kisi bhi sexual conduct ko jo aurat ki dignity ko thes pahunchaye, use humiliate kare, neecha dikhaye ya uska ullanghan kare, domestic violence maanta hai, lekin protection order todne par zyada se zyada 1 saal ki jail ya Rs 20,000 ka jurmana hai.

facts.value: Breach of protection order: up to 1 year or Rs 20,000
facts.caveat: PWDVA is mainly a civil law (protection, residence, maintenance orders); its only offences are breach of a protection order (s.31) and a Protection Officer's failure to do his duty (s.33), each punishable with up to 1 year or Rs 20,000.

text.en: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, every employer must set up an Internal Complaints Committee, districts must run Local Committees for workplaces with fewer than 10 workers, a complaint must be filed within 3 months of the incident (extendable by up to 3 more months if circumstances prevented it), the inquiry must finish within 90 days, and an employer who fails to comply can be fined up to Rs 50,000, doubled on repeat.
text.hg: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, every employer must set up an Internal Complaints Committee, districts must run Local Committees for workplaces with fewer than 10 workers, a complaint must be filed within 3 months of the incident (extendable by up to 3 more months if circumstances prevented it), the inquiry must finish within 90 days, and an employer who fails to comply can be fined up to Rs 50,000, doubled on repeat.

facts.value: Complaint in 3 months (extendable by 3); inquiry in 90 days; Rs 50,000 fine
facts.caveat: Repeat violations can also lead to cancellation of the employer's licence or registration.

text.en: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a marriage is a child marriage if the bride is under 18 or the groom under 21; it is voidable at the child's option until two years after reaching majority, and an adult man who marries a child, or anyone who performs or abets a child marriage, faces up to 2 years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh, the offences being cognizable and non-bailable.
text.hg: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke tahat agar dulhan 18 saal se kam ya dulha 21 saal se kam umr ka hai, to woh child marriage hai; balig hone ke do saal baad tak woh bachcha chahe to is shaadi ko radd karwa sakta hai, aur kisi bachche se shaadi karne wale adult aadmi ko, ya child marriage karwane ya uske liye uksane wale kisi bhi vyakti ko 2 saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment aur Rs 1 lakh tak ka jurmana ho sakta hai; yeh offences cognizable aur non-bailable hain.

facts.value: Girls <18, boys <21; up to 2 years and Rs 1 lakh
facts.caveat: A child marriage is void, not merely voidable, if solemnised in breach of an injunction (s.14).

text.en: Under the PC-PNDT Act, 1994, a doctor or clinic that conducts sex determination faces up to 3 years in prison and a Rs 10,000 fine, rising to 5 years and Rs 50,000 for a repeat offence, with the doctor's registration suspended once charges are framed and cancelled for 5 years on a first conviction and permanently on a second; anyone seeking sex selection faces up to 3 years and Rs 50,000.
text.hg: PC-PNDT Act, 1994 ke tahat sex determination karne wale doctor ya clinic ko 3 saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10,000 jurmana ho sakta hai, jo dobara offence par 5 saal aur Rs 50,000 tak ho jaata hai; charges frame hote hi doctor ka registration suspend ho jaata hai, aur pehli conviction par 5 saal ke liye aur doosri par hamesha ke liye cancel ho jaata hai; sex selection karwana chahne wale kisi bhi vyakti ko 3 saal tak ki jail aur Rs 50,000 jurmana ho sakta hai.

facts.value: 3 yrs + Rs 10,000; repeat 5 yrs + Rs 50,000; licence loss
facts.caveat: A woman compelled to undergo sex selection is not punishable. The PDF text is font-encoded and was decoded for reading.

text.en: Under Section 18 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, sexual abuse of a transgender person is punishable with 6 months to 2 years in prison and a fine.
text.hg: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 ke Section 18 ke tahat kisi transgender vyakti ke sexual abuse par 6 mahine se 2 saal tak ki jail aur jurmana hai.

facts.caveat: The same penalty covers forced labour, denial of access to public places and eviction from home; the 10-year rape minimum is in BNS s.64. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026 rewrote s.18 but kept this 6-month-to-2-year penalty for sexual abuse (new s.18(d)); see law-transgender-amendment-2026.

text.en: Under NALSA's Compensation Scheme for Women Victims/Survivors of Sexual Assault/other Crimes, 2018, a rape survivor is entitled to Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh, a gang-rape survivor to Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh, and the family of a woman killed to Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh.
text.hg: NALSA ki Compensation Scheme for Women Victims/Survivors of Sexual Assault/other Crimes, 2018 ke tahat rape survivor Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh, gang-rape survivor Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh, aur maari gayi aurat ka parivaar Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh ke compensation ka haqdaar hai.

facts.value: Rape: Rs 4-7 lakh; gang rape: Rs 5-10 lakh; death: Rs 5-10 lakh
facts.caveat: Model scheme framed on Supreme Court directions in Nipun Saxena; payouts depend on state and district legal services authorities.

text.en: NALSA's 2018 scheme sets compensation of Rs 3 lakh to Rs 4 lakh for pregnancy resulting from rape, Rs 2 lakh to Rs 3 lakh for loss of a foetus or fertility due to assault, and Rs 7 lakh to Rs 8 lakh for an acid attack that disfigures the face.
text.hg: NALSA ki 2018 ki scheme mein rape ki wajah se pregnancy par Rs 3 lakh se Rs 4 lakh, assault ki wajah se foetus ya fertility kho dene par Rs 2 lakh se Rs 3 lakh, aur chehra bigaad dene wale acid attack ke liye Rs 7 lakh se Rs 8 lakh ka compensation tay hai.

facts.value: Pregnancy from rape: Rs 3-4 lakh; foetus loss: Rs 2-3 lakh; facial acid injury: Rs 7-8 lakh

text.en: Under the 2018 NALSA scheme, compensation limits are 50% higher when the victim is a minor, the inquiry must finish within 60 days, and an acid-attack survivor must receive Rs 1 lakh within 15 days of the case reaching the District Legal Services Authority and a further Rs 2 lakh within two months.
text.hg: 2018 ki NALSA scheme ke tahat victim minor ho to compensation ki limits 50% zyada hoti hain, inquiry 60 din ke andar poori honi chahiye, aur acid-attack survivor ko case District Legal Services Authority tak pahunchne ke 15 din ke andar Rs 1 lakh aur do mahine ke andar Rs 2 lakh aur milne chahiye.

facts.value: Minors +50%; 60-day inquiry; acid: Rs 1 lakh in 15 days + Rs 2 lakh

text.en: The Centre released Rs 200 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund as a one-time grant to states and union territories under the Central Victim Compensation Fund to support compensation for survivors of rape, acid attacks, crimes against children and trafficking.
text.hg: Centre ne Central Victim Compensation Fund ke tahat states aur union territories ko Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 200 crore one-time grant ke roop mein jaari kiye, taaki rape, acid attacks, bachchon ke khilaf crimes aur trafficking ke survivors ko compensation dene mein madad mile.

facts.caveat: Release date of the grant not stated in the reply.

text.en: As of November 2026, 779 Fast Track Special Courts, including 399 exclusive POCSO courts, were functioning in 29 states and union territories under the central scheme launched on 2 October 2019, and they had disposed of 4,02,457 rape and POCSO cases since inception.
text.hg: November 2026 tak, 2 October 2019 ko shuru hui central scheme ke tahat 29 states aur union territories mein 779 Fast Track Special Courts chal rahe the, jinmein 399 exclusive POCSO courts shamil the, aur shuruaat se ab tak yeh rape aur POCSO ke 4,02,457 cases ka nipataara kar chuke the.

facts.value: 779 FTSCs incl. 399 POCSO courts; 4,02,457 cases disposed
facts.caveat: Earlier counts: 745 FTSCs incl. 404 POCSO courts in 30 states/UTs (March 2025); 774 functional on 31 December 2025.

text.en: On 4 November 2026 the Union Cabinet extended the Fast Track Special Courts scheme for five years, from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, with an outlay of Rs 3,788.04 crore (central share Rs 2,353.15 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund) and provision for up to 850 courts.
text.hg: 4 November 2026 ko Union Cabinet ne Fast Track Special Courts scheme ko paanch saal ke liye, 1 April 2026 se 31 March 2031 tak, badha diya, jiska outlay Rs 3,788.04 crore hai (central share Rs 2,353.15 crore, Nirbhaya Fund se) aur jismein 850 tak courts ka provision hai.

text.en: India's Fast Track Special Courts disposed of 76,319 rape and POCSO cases in 2023, 85,595 in 2024 and 66,500 in 2025, a 22% fall in the last year, according to High Court data given to the Rajya Sabha in February 2026.
text.hg: Rajya Sabha ko February 2026 mein diye gaye High Court data ke mutabik, India ke Fast Track Special Courts ne 2023 mein rape aur POCSO ke 76,319 cases ka nipataara kiya, 2024 mein 85,595 aur 2025 mein 66,500 ka, yaani aakhri saal mein 22% ki girawat.

facts.caveat: 774 FTSCs were functional on 31 December 2025; Jharkhand left the scheme in July 2025.

text.en: About 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases were pending before India's Fast Track Special Courts on 31 December 2025, according to a Law Ministry reply in the Rajya Sabha reported in July 2026.
text.hg: Rajya Sabha mein Law Ministry ke ek jawab ke mutabik, jiski khabar July 2026 mein aayi, 31 December 2025 ko India ke Fast Track Special Courts mein rape aur POCSO ke lagbhag 2,45,579 cases pending the.

facts.caveat: PIB's table prints the figure as '2,45.579', a typing slip for 2,45,579 (the figure Business Today also reports). At the 2025 disposal rate (66,500 a year) the backlog would take about 3.7 years to clear even with no new cases.

text.en: Up to financial year 2024-25, Rs 7,712.85 crore had been allocated to India's Nirbhaya Fund for women's safety, of which Rs 5,846.08 crore, about 76%, had been released and utilised.
text.hg: Financial year 2024-25 tak aurton ki suraksha ke liye India ke Nirbhaya Fund ko Rs 7,712.85 crore allocate kiye gaye the, jinmein se Rs 5,846.08 crore, yaani lagbhag 76%, release aur use kiye ja chuke the.

facts.value: Rs 7,712.85 crore allocated; Rs 5,846.08 crore (76%) used
facts.caveat: 'Released and utilised' is reported as one figure, so it does not show how much was actually spent on the ground.

text.en: As of March 2025, 802 One Stop Centres were functional in 36 states and union territories and had assisted over 10.80 lakh women, and 14,658 women help desks had been set up in police stations, 13,743 of them headed by women officers.
text.hg: March 2025 tak 36 states aur union territories mein 802 One Stop Centres kaam kar rahe the aur 10.80 lakh se zyada aurton ki madad kar chuke the, aur police stations mein 14,658 women help desks banaye ja chuke the, jinmein se 13,743 ko women officers head kar rahi thin.

text.en: As of March 2026, 926 One Stop Centres (Sakhi) were operational across India and had assisted more than 13 lakh women, according to the Minister of State for Women and Child Development in the Lok Sabha.
text.hg: Lok Sabha mein Women and Child Development ke Minister of State ke mutabik, March 2026 tak poore India mein 926 One Stop Centres (Sakhi) chal rahe the aur 13 lakh se zyada aurton ki madad kar chuke the.

text.en: As of July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 One Stop Centres approved across India were operational, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women between April 2015 and June 2026.

text.en: Police in India registered 31,516 rape cases in 2022, 29,670 in 2023 and 29,536 in 2024 (19,683 under the IPC and 9,853 under the BNS), according to the NCRB.
text.hg: NCRB ke mutabik, India mein police ne 2022 mein rape ke 31,516 cases register kiye, 2023 mein 29,670 aur 2024 mein 29,536 (19,683 IPC ke tahat aur 9,853 BNS ke tahat).

facts.caveat: NCRB counts only the most serious offence in each FIR (Principal Offence Rule) and records reported cases, not incidence; sexual violence is heavily under-reported. In 2024, offences committed before 1 July 2024 were registered under the IPC and later ones under the BNS, so the IPC/BNS split is not a half-year split.

text.en: In 2024, the first year of the new code, police registered 1,325 cases under BNS Section 69 (sex by deceit or false promise of marriage) and just 11 cases under Section 72 (disclosing a rape victim's identity), all in the July-December period after the BNS took effect.
text.hg: Naye code ke pehle saal, 2024 mein police ne BNS Section 69 (dhokhe se ya shaadi ka jhootha vaada karke sex) ke tahat 1,325 cases aur Section 72 (rape victim ki pehchaan disclose karna) ke tahat sirf 11 cases register kiye; yeh sab BNS lagu hone ke baad July-December ke dauran ke hain.

text.en: Police in India registered 987 cases of 'unnatural offences' under IPC Section 377 in 2022 and 888 in 2023; in the 2024 data the head disappears, with the NCRB noting the section was 'deleted in BNS'.
text.hg: India mein police ne IPC Section 377 ke tahat 'unnatural offences' ke 2022 mein 987 aur 2023 mein 888 cases register kiye; 2024 ke data mein yeh head gayab ho jaata hai, aur NCRB ne note kiya ki yeh section 'deleted in BNS' hai.

facts.caveat: After the Supreme Court's 2018 Navtej Singh Johar ruling decriminalised consensual same-sex acts, Section 377 applied to non-consensual acts and bestiality; the NCRB figure does not separate victims by gender or type.

text.en: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which replaced the Indian Evidence Act, a survivor's character or previous sexual experience is irrelevant to the question of consent in prosecutions for rape, sexual harassment, voyeurism, stalking and related offences (s.48), and in rape cases she may not be asked in cross-examination about her 'general immoral character' or previous sexual experience to prove consent (s.149).
text.hg: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which replaced the Indian Evidence Act, a survivor's character or previous sexual experience is irrelevant to the question of consent in prosecutions for rape, sexual harassment, voyeurism, stalking and related offences (s.48), and in rape cases she may not be asked in cross-examination about her 'general immoral character' or previous sexual experience to prove consent (s.149).

facts.value: Sexual history irrelevant to consent; barred in cross-examination
facts.caveat: Carries forward Evidence Act s.53A and the proviso to s.146, both introduced by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013. The s.48 rule covers BNS ss.64-71 and 74-78; the s.149 bar covers ss.64-71. BSA s.170 repeals the Evidence Act.

text.en: Under Section 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, in a prosecution for aggravated rape under BNS Section 64(2), such as rape by a police officer, public servant, relative, guardian or hospital staff, once sexual intercourse is proved and the woman testifies that she did not consent, the court must presume that she did not consent.
text.hg: Under Section 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, in a prosecution for aggravated rape under BNS Section 64(2), such as rape by a police officer, public servant, relative, guardian or hospital staff, once sexual intercourse is proved and the woman testifies that she did not consent, the court must presume that she did not consent.

facts.value: Presumption of no consent in aggravated rape cases
facts.caveat: Successor to Evidence Act s.114A as substituted in 2013. 'Shall presume' means the fact is treated as proved unless disproved (BSA s.2), and it applies only to the aggravated forms in BNS s.64(2), not to every rape prosecution.

text.en: Under Section 24 of the POCSO Act, police must record a child's statement at the child's home or a place of the child's choice, as far as practicable through a woman officer not below sub-inspector rank who is not in uniform, must make sure the child never comes into contact with the accused, and may not keep a child at a police station at night for any reason.
text.hg: Under Section 24 of the POCSO Act, police must record a child's statement at the child's home or a place of the child's choice, as far as practicable through a woman officer not below sub-inspector rank who is not in uniform, must make sure the child never comes into contact with the accused, and may not keep a child at a police station at night for any reason.

facts.value: Statement at home; woman officer out of uniform; no night detention

text.en: In a POCSO trial, lawyers must put their questions to the child through the judge (s.33(2)); the Special Court must not allow aggressive questioning or character assassination of the child or call the child to testify repeatedly (s.33(5)-(6)), must keep the child from being exposed to the accused while testifying, using video links, one-way mirrors or curtains if needed (s.36), and must hold the trial in camera with a parent or trusted person present (s.37).
text.hg: In a POCSO trial, lawyers must put their questions to the child through the judge (s.33(2)); the Special Court must not allow aggressive questioning or character assassination of the child or call the child to testify repeatedly (s.33(5)-(6)), must keep the child from being exposed to the accused while testifying, using video links, one-way mirrors or curtains if needed (s.36), and must hold the trial in camera with a parent or trusted person present (s.37).

facts.value: Questions via the judge; no aggressive questioning; child shielded from accused; in camera

text.en: Cases pending before India's Fast Track Special Courts rose from 2,02,175 at the end of 2023 to 2,04,122 at the end of 2024 and 2,45,579 at the end of 2025, as new cases registered in these courts jumped to 1,43,936 in 2025 while disposals fell to 66,500, according to a Law Ministry reply in the Rajya Sabha on 23 July 2026.
text.hg: Cases pending before India's Fast Track Special Courts rose from 2,02,175 at the end of 2023 to 2,04,122 at the end of 2024 and 2,45,579 at the end of 2025, as new cases registered in these courts jumped to 1,43,936 in 2025 while disposals fell to 66,500, according to a Law Ministry reply in the Rajya Sabha on 23 July 2026.

facts.caveat: Pending counts are as on 31 December of each year; PIB prints the 2025 figure as '2,45.579'. As of 30 April 2026, 775 FTSCs including 398 exclusive POCSO courts were functional in 29 states/UTs, and the scheme had been temporarily extended to 30 September 2026 before the November 2026 five-year extension.

text.en: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, which received presidential assent on 30 March 2026, rewrote Section 18 but kept sexual abuse of a transgender person punishable with only 6 months to 2 years in prison and a fine, while adding new offences carrying 10 years to life imprisonment for kidnapping a person and causing grievous hurt to force them to present as transgender.
text.hg: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, which received presidential assent on 30 March 2026, rewrote Section 18 but kept sexual abuse of a transgender person punishable with only 6 months to 2 years in prison and a fine, while adding new offences carrying 10 years to life imprisonment for kidnapping a person and causing grievous hurt to force them to present as transgender.

facts.value: Sexual abuse still 6 months-2 years; new forced-transition offences 10 years to life
facts.caveat: The Act comes into force on a date the Centre notifies, and its validity is under challenge in the Supreme Court (W.P.(C) 548/2026, per Supreme Court Observer, last updated 31 October 2026). For a child, the new kidnapping offence (s.18(f)) carries rigorous imprisonment for life.

text.en: In a judgment dated 15 September 1978 (reported as AIR 1979 SC 185; (1979) 2 SCC 143), a three-judge Supreme Court bench acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra in 1972, reversing the Bombay High Court, which had sentenced one to five years for rape and the other to one year for outraging modesty.
text.hg: In a judgment dated 15 September 1978 (reported as AIR 1979 SC 185; (1979) 2 SCC 143), a three-judge Supreme Court bench acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra in 1972, reversing the Bombay High Court, which had sentenced one to five years for rape and the other to one year for outraging modesty.

facts.value: Acquittal by 3-judge bench (A.D. Koshal, Jaswant Singh, P.S. Kailasam JJ.)
facts.caveat: Many secondary sources date the judgment to 1979 (year of the law report and of the protest letter). The Supreme Court's 2026 publication 'Judgments and Gender' describes it as 'Rape of a minor girl in police custody; accused acquitted due to restrictive reasoning on consent'. The case is popularly known by the survivor's first name and its formal title names one of the acquitted policemen; use neither in published text - cite it as AIR 1979 SC 185.
