Add no identifying detail about the survivor.

text.en: In that 1978 judgment the Supreme Court noted that no marks of injury were found on the girl, described the alleged intercourse as 'a peaceful affair', and concluded that the sexual intercourse was 'not proved to amount to rape'.
text.hg: In that 1978 judgment the Supreme Court noted that no marks of injury were found on the girl, described the alleged intercourse as 'a peaceful affair', and concluded that the sexual intercourse was 'not proved to amount to rape'.

facts.caveat: Quoted words are the Supreme Court's own. The Supreme Court's 2026 publication 'Judgments and Gender' lists the case as an acquittal 'due to restrictive reasoning on consent'.

text.en: In September 1979 four law teachers - Upendra Baxi, Raghunath Kelkar, Lotika Sarkar and Vasudha Dhagamwar - wrote an open letter to the Chief Justice of India protesting the 1978 judgment's view of consent, a letter widely credited with starting India's anti-rape law reform movement.
text.hg: In September 1979 four law teachers - Upendra Baxi, Raghunath Kelkar, Lotika Sarkar and Vasudha Dhagamwar - wrote an open letter to the Chief Justice of India protesting the 1978 judgment's view of consent, a letter widely credited with starting India's anti-rape law reform movement.

facts.value: Open letter by 4 law professors, September 1979
facts.caveat: Secondary source (Wikipedia, citing 'An Open Letter to the Chief Justice of India', (1979) 4 SCC (Jour) 17). 'Widely credited' is a characterisation, not a statistic.

text.en: Protests over the 1978 acquittal led Parliament to pass the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 (Act No. 43 of 1983, in force from 25 December 1983), which made custodial rape a separate aggravated offence, introduced a presumption of absence of consent in custodial rape trials (Section 114A, Indian Evidence Act), provided for in-camera rape trials and made it an offence to disclose a rape victim's identity (Section 228A IPC).
text.hg: Protests over the 1978 acquittal led Parliament to pass the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 (Act No. 43 of 1983, in force from 25 December 1983), which made custodial rape a separate aggravated offence, introduced a presumption of absence of consent in custodial rape trials (Section 114A, Indian Evidence Act), provided for in-camera rape trials and made it an offence to disclose a rape victim's identity (Section 228A IPC).

facts.value: Act No. 43 of 1983 (in force 25 Dec 1983): custodial rape offences; s.114A presumption; in-camera trials; s.228A identity bar
facts.caveat: The Supreme Court's own text (Nipun Saxena, 2018) settles the Act number as 43 of 1983 for s.228A IPC and s.327(2) CrPC. A Law Commission reference cited on Wikipedia attaches ss.113A/114A to 'Criminal Law (Second Amendment) Act, 46 of 1983'; the attribution of s.114A to Act 43 rests on Wikipedia and CNN, not on the Act text, which India Code could not serve (HTTP 504). s.114A was substituted in 2013; the identity bar (s.228A IPC) is now Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 wrote into Section 375 IPC that a woman who does not physically resist penetration shall not, for that reason alone, be regarded as consenting - reversing the logic of the Supreme Court's 1978 custodial rape judgment - and defined consent as 'an unequivocal voluntary agreement'.
text.hg: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 wrote into Section 375 IPC that a woman who does not physically resist penetration shall not, for that reason alone, be regarded as consenting - reversing the logic of the Supreme Court's 1978 custodial rape judgment - and defined consent as 'an unequivocal voluntary agreement'.

facts.caveat: The link to the 1978 judgment is editorial interpretation. The same definition and proviso are carried into Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (checked in the text of the Bharatiya Nyaya (Second) Sanhita Bill, 2023 as passed by Parliament, PRS copy).

text.en: In the case that prompted the Vishaka guidelines, a 'saathin' (village-level worker) of the Rajasthan government's Women's Development Programme who had campaigned against child marriages was gang-raped in her village near Jaipur on 22 September 1992; in November 1995 a district and sessions court in Jaipur acquitted all five accused of rape.
text.hg: In the case that prompted the Vishaka guidelines, a 'saathin' (village-level worker) of the Rajasthan government's Women's Development Programme who had campaigned against child marriages was gang-raped in her village near Jaipur on 22 September 1992; in November 1995 a district and sessions court in Jaipur acquitted all five accused of rape.

facts.value: Gang rape 22 Sep 1992; all 5 accused acquitted of rape, Nov 1995
facts.caveat: The exact verdict date (15 November 1995) appears only on Wikipedia; the month is confirmed by BBC and India Today. BBC reports convictions for lesser offences (assault, conspiracy; nine months) while India Today (1995) says all five were acquitted - hence 'acquitted of rape'. The survivor has campaigned publicly under her own name for three decades; this bank still does not print it (editors may use it only with her consent). Never name the five men. Rajasthan High Court appeal: one hearing in 22 years as of 2017 (BBC); current status not confirmed.

text.en: On 13 August 1997, in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan - a petition prompted by the 'brutal gang rape of a social worker in a village of Rajasthan' - a Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice J.S. Verma laid down binding guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace, to be treated as law under Article 141 until Parliament legislated.
text.hg: 13 August 1997 ko Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan case mein - yeh petition 'brutal gang rape of a social worker in a village of Rajasthan' ke chalte daayar hui thi - Chief Justice J.S. Verma ki adhyakshata wali Supreme Court bench ne workplace par sexual harassment ke khilaf binding guidelines tay kin. Parliament ke kanoon banane tak inhe Article 141 ke tahat law maana jaana tha.

facts.caveat: Justice J.S. Verma later chaired the 2012-13 Verma Committee on rape law.

text.en: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, which turned the Vishaka guidelines into statute, was published in the Gazette of India as Act No. 14 of 2013 on 23 April 2013 - nearly 16 years after Vishaka.
text.hg: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, jisne Vishaka guidelines ko kanoon ka roop diya, 23 April 2013 ko Gazette of India mein Act No. 14 of 2013 ke roop mein publish hua - Vishaka ke lagbhag 16 saal baad.

facts.caveat: Per Wikipedia (secondary): Lok Sabha passed it on 3 September 2012 and Rajya Sabha on 26 February 2013; in force from 9 December 2013; employers with 10 or more employees must set up an Internal Complaints Committee, a Local Committee is formed in every district, and non-compliance draws a fine of up to Rs 50,000.

text.en: The three-member Justice J.S. Verma Committee (with Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium), set up in December 2012 after the Delhi gang rape, submitted its report on 23 January 2013; it advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it 'may not have a deterrent effect', and recommended deleting the marital rape exception in Section 375 IPC.
text.hg: The three-member Justice J.S. Verma Committee (with Justice Leila Seth and Gopal Subramanium), set up in December 2012 after the Delhi gang rape, submitted its report on 23 January 2013; it advised against the death penalty for rape, noting that it 'may not have a deterrent effect', and recommended deleting the marital rape exception in Section 375 IPC.

facts.value: Report 23 Jan 2013; against death penalty for rape; delete marital rape exception
facts.caveat: The phrases 'death penalty was not a deterrence to serious crimes' and 'Marriage should not be considered as an irrevocable consent to sexual acts' are PRS's summary wording - quote them only as PRS's. The full report link on PRS returns 404. Some sources give 22 December 2012 for the panel's announcement (PRS: constituted 23 December). Parliament followed neither recommendation in 2013. AFSPA in conflict areas 'needs to be revisited' (PRS).

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 (No. 13 of 2013), assented to on 2 April 2013 and in force from 3 February 2013, made sexual intercourse with a girl under 18 rape whether or not she consented, raising the statutory age of consent to 18.
text.hg: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 (No. 13 of 2013), jise 2 April 2013 ko assent mila aur jo 3 February 2013 se laagu hua, ne 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sexual intercourse ko rape bana diya, chahe usne consent di ho ya nahi. Isse consent ki kanooni umar (statutory age of consent) badh kar 18 ho gayi.

facts.value: Age of consent 18; Act No. 13 of 2013
facts.caveat: 3 February 2013 is the date of the ordinance that followed the Verma report. The previous age of consent was 16 (Supreme Court, Independent Thought, 2017: Parliament 'decided to increase the age of consent to 18 years under clause Sixthly').

text.en: The 2013 amendment kept the marital rape exception: Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC said sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under 15 years of age, is not rape.
text.hg: 2013 ke amendment ne marital rape exception ko bana rehne diya: Section 375 IPC ke Exception 2 mein kaha gaya tha ki koi aadmi apni hi wife ke saath, jiski umar 15 saal se kam na ho, sexual intercourse ya sexual acts kare toh woh rape nahi hai.

facts.caveat: Read up to 18 by the Supreme Court in Independent Thought (2017).

text.en: The 2013 amendment set a minimum of 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, extendable to imprisonment for the remainder of natural life, for gang rape (Section 376D IPC), and made rape causing death or a persistent vegetative state punishable with at least 20 years, natural-life imprisonment or death (Section 376A).
text.hg: 2013 ke amendment ne gang rape (Section 376D IPC) ke liye kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment tay ki, jise baaki natural life tak ki jail tak badhaya ja sakta hai. Aur aise rape ke liye, jisse victim ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye, kam se kam 20 saal, natural-life imprisonment ya death penalty ki saza rakhi gayi (Section 376A).

facts.value: Min 20 years for gang rape; death possible where victim dies or is left vegetative
facts.caveat: The death/vegetative-state offence is now Section 66 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita - one of the sections in the 2025 RG Kar conviction. The basic minimum for rape in 2013 was seven years (raised to ten in 2018).

text.en: The 2013 amendment's Section 376E IPC made repeat rape offenders liable to imprisonment for the remainder of their natural life or death.
text.hg: 2013 ke amendment se judi Section 376E IPC ne repeat rape offenders ke liye baaki natural life tak ki jail ya death penalty ka provision kiya.

facts.value: Natural-life imprisonment or death for repeat offenders
facts.caveat: First applied in the 2014 Shakti Mills sentencing.

text.en: The 2013 amendment created new offences in the Indian Penal Code for acid attack (Sections 326A and 326B), sexual harassment (354A), disrobing (354B), voyeurism (354C) and stalking (354D).
text.hg: 2013 ke amendment ne Indian Penal Code mein naye offences banaye: acid attack (Sections 326A aur 326B), sexual harassment (354A), disrobing (354B), voyeurism (354C) aur stalking (354D).

facts.value: New offences: acid attack, sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism, stalking
facts.caveat: s.354B in the gazette: 'Any man who assaults or uses criminal force to any woman or abets such act with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked'.

text.en: Since 2013, Section 357C of the Code of Criminal Procedure has required every hospital, public or private, to immediately give rape and acid-attack victims first aid or medical treatment free of cost and inform the police, and refusing treatment became an offence (Section 166B IPC).
text.hg: 2013 se Code of Criminal Procedure ki Section 357C ke tahat har hospital ke liye - chahe sarkari ho ya private - zaroori raha hai ki woh rape aur acid attack victims ko turant free first aid ya medical treatment de aur police ko inform kare; aur treatment se inkaar karna offence bana diya gaya (Section 166B IPC).

facts.value: Free immediate treatment mandatory in all hospitals
facts.caveat: Now carried in the BNSS, 2023 (not re-verified in this session).

text.en: Since 2013, Section 53A of the Indian Evidence Act has made a victim's character or previous sexual experience irrelevant to the question of consent in trials for rape and other sexual offences.
text.hg: 2013 se Indian Evidence Act ki Section 53A ne rape aur doosre sexual offences ke trials mein victim ke character ya pichhle sexual experience ko consent ke sawaal ke liye irrelevant bana diya hai.

facts.value: Past sexual history irrelevant to consent
facts.caveat: In 2022 the Supreme Court (Shailendra Kumar Rai) again called it patriarchal and sexist to doubt a rape claim because a woman is sexually active.

text.en: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (No. 2 of 2016), assented to on 31 December 2015, requires Juvenile Justice Boards to make a 'preliminary assessment' of any child aged 16 or above accused of a heinous offence - one with a minimum punishment of seven years or more - which can send the case to a Children's Court for trial as an adult.
text.hg: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (No. 2 of 2016), jise 31 December 2015 ko assent mila, Juvenile Justice Boards ke liye zaroori banata hai ki woh kisi heinous offence - yaani aisa offence jiski minimum saza saat saal ya usse zyada ho - ke accused, 16 saal ya usse zyada umar ke kisi bhi bachche ka 'preliminary assessment' karein. Is assessment ke baad case Children's Court ko bheja ja sakta hai, taaki us par adult ki tarah trial chale.

facts.value: Children aged 16-18 accused of heinous offences can be tried as adults
facts.caveat: In force from 15 January 2016 (secondary sources). Section 21 bars death or life imprisonment without possibility of release for such children (Supreme Court Handbook on Child Rights, 2025). The Act followed the 2015 release of the juvenile convicted in the 2012 Delhi case after three years in a correctional home (context; see case-nirbhaya-execution-2020).

text.en: On 5 May 2017 the Supreme Court (Justices Dipak Misra, R. Banumathi and Ashok Bhushan) dismissed the appeals of the four adult convicts in the 16 December 2012 Delhi gang rape and murder and confirmed their death sentences, holding that the aggravating circumstances outweighed the mitigating ones.
text.hg: 5 May 2017 ko Supreme Court (Justices Dipak Misra, R. Banumathi aur Ashok Bhushan) ne 16 December 2012 ke Delhi gang rape aur murder ke chaar adult convicts ki appeals khaarij kar di aur unki death sentences barkarar rakhin. Court ne maana ki aggravating circumstances, mitigating circumstances par bhaari hain.

facts.caveat: The judgment contains graphic detail; do not reproduce it. The victim was a 23-year-old paramedical student; 'Nirbhaya' is a media pseudonym and her real name must not be used.

text.en: The four adult convicts in the 2012 Delhi gang rape and murder were hanged together at Tihar Jail at 5:30 am on 20 March 2020; of the other two accused, one was found dead in jail in March 2013 and the juvenile was released in 2015 after three years in a correctional home.
text.hg: The four adult convicts in the 2012 Delhi gang rape and murder were hanged together at Tihar Jail at 5:30 am on 20 March 2020; of the other two accused, one was found dead in jail in March 2013 and the juvenile was released in 2015 after three years in a correctional home.

facts.value: 4 executed at 5:30 am, 20 March 2020; juvenile freed 2015 after 3 years
facts.caveat: The death in custody was reported as an apparent suicide; no court finding seen. Do not name the juvenile. The Tribune (PTI) adds that this was the first time four men were hanged together at Tihar; BBC and India Today do not say so, so it is not printed.

text.en: In his Budget 2013-14 speech, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram proposed a 'Nirbhaya Fund' with a government contribution of Rs 1,000 crore, saying recent incidents had 'cast a long, dark shadow' on India's liberal and progressive credentials.
text.hg: Budget 2013-14 ki apni speech mein Finance Minister P. Chidambaram ne Rs 1,000 crore ke sarkari contribution wale 'Nirbhaya Fund' ka prastaav rakha, aur kaha ki haal ki ghatnaon ne India ki liberal aur progressive saakh par ek lambi, kaali parchhai daal di hai ('cast a long, dark shadow').

facts.caveat: The Budget was presented on 28 February 2013 (date printed on the speech).

text.en: By March 2025 the Centre had allocated Rs 7,712.85 crore under the Nirbhaya Fund and used Rs 5,846.08 crore (nearly 76%), funding 14,658 Women Help Desks in police stations (13,743 headed by women officers), 827 Anti-Human Trafficking Units and 802 One Stop Centres that had assisted over 10.80 lakh women.
text.hg: March 2025 tak Centre ne Nirbhaya Fund ke tahat Rs 7,712.85 crore allocate kiye the aur Rs 5,846.08 crore (lagbhag 76%) use kiye the. Is paise se police stations mein 14,658 Women Help Desks (jinme se 13,743 ko women officers head karti thin), 827 Anti-Human Trafficking Units aur 802 One Stop Centres ko funding mili; in One Stop Centres ne 10.80 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad ki thi.

facts.value: Rs 7,712.85 crore allocated; Rs 5,846.08 crore (about 76%) used; 802 One Stop Centres
facts.caveat: Ministry says actual use may be higher because states have not sent utilisation certificates. Outputs are government-reported.

text.en: A Rajya Sabha written reply reported in July 2026 put total Nirbhaya Fund allocations since 2013-14 at Rs 7,990.85 crore - the Rs 7,712.85 crore allocated up to 2024-25 plus Rs 278 crore for 2025-26 - of which Rs 6,703.02 crore (83.9%) had been released and used, leaving about Rs 1,288 crore unspent.
text.hg: A Rajya Sabha written reply reported in July 2026 put total Nirbhaya Fund allocations since 2013-14 at Rs 7,990.85 crore - the Rs 7,712.85 crore allocated up to 2024-25 plus Rs 278 crore for 2025-26 - of which Rs 6,703.02 crore (83.9%) had been released and used, leaving about Rs 1,288 crore unspent.

facts.value: Rs 7,990.85 crore allocated; Rs 6,703.02 crore (83.9%) used; Rs 1,287.83 crore unspent; 2025-26: Rs 278 crore
facts.caveat: News report of a written reply by MoS Savitri Thakur; the reply itself was not retrieved. ThePrint also calls the 2025-26 allocation the lowest in the fund's history - not checkable, not printed.

text.en: On 4 April 2014 a Mumbai sessions court sentenced three repeat offenders in the 2013 Shakti Mills gang rape cases to death under Section 376E IPC - the first time any court applied the repeat-offender provision added after the 2012 Delhi gang rape.
text.hg: 4 April 2014 ko Mumbai ki ek sessions court ne 2013 ke Shakti Mills gang rape cases ke teen repeat offenders ko Section 376E IPC ke tahat death sentence sunayi - pehli baar kisi court ne 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad jode gaye repeat-offender provision ko laagu kiya.

facts.value: 3 death sentences; first use of s.376E
facts.caveat: Scroll (2021) gives 24 March 2014, but contemporaneous TOI and Hindustan Times reports (4 April 2014) and Indian Express (5 April 2014) support 4 April 2014. The survivor in the main case was a photojournalist (per news headlines); add no other details.

text.en: On 25 November 2021 the Bombay High Court (Justices S.S. Jadhav and P.K. Chavan) commuted the three Shakti Mills death sentences to life imprisonment, holding that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion.
text.hg: 25 November 2021 ko Bombay High Court (Justices S.S. Jadhav aur P.K. Chavan) ne Shakti Mills case ki teenon death sentences ko life imprisonment mein badal diya, yeh kehte hue ki ek constitutional court public opinion ke aadhaar par saza nahi de sakti.

facts.caveat: LiveLaw: 'imprisonment for the remainder of their natural lives' and the 376E conviction 'would not sustain'; Scroll: no entitlement to parole or furlough (https://scroll.in/latest/1011379/).

text.en: On 7 May 2018 a Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice Dipak Misra moved the Kathua rape and murder trial out of Jammu and Kashmir to Pathankot in Punjab and ordered it held in camera, day to day.
text.hg: 7 May 2018 ko Chief Justice Dipak Misra ki adhyakshata wali Supreme Court bench ne Kathua rape aur murder trial ko Jammu and Kashmir se bahar Punjab ke Pathankot shift kar diya, aur order diya ki trial in camera aur day to day chale.

facts.value: Trial moved to Pathankot; in-camera, day-to-day

text.en: On 10 June 2019 a Pathankot court convicted six of the seven accused tried for the rape and murder of an eight-year-old girl in Kathua: three got life imprisonment for murder (and 25 years for gang rape) and three policemen got five years for destroying evidence; one accused was acquitted.
text.hg: 10 June 2019 ko Pathankot ki ek court ne Kathua mein aath saal ki ek bachchi ke rape aur murder ke case mein jin saat accused par trial chala tha, unme se chhah ko convict kiya: teen ko murder ke liye life imprisonment (aur gang rape ke liye 25 saal) mili, aur teen policewalon ko saboot mitaane ke liye paanch saal ki saza mili; ek accused bari hua.

facts.value: 6 of 7 convicted: 3 life terms, 3 policemen 5 years, 1 acquitted
facts.caveat: Do not name the child. Appeals to the Punjab and Haryana High Court were expected; their outcome was not verified. The acquitted accused must not be named.

text.en: On 16 November 2022 the Supreme Court (Justices Ajay Rastogi and J.B. Pardiwala) ruled that a Kathua accused earlier declared a juvenile must be tried as an adult, setting aside a Kathua court order and its affirmation by the Jammu and Kashmir High Court.
text.hg: 16 November 2022 ko Supreme Court (Justices Ajay Rastogi aur J.B. Pardiwala) ne faisla diya ki Kathua case ke jis accused ko pehle juvenile ghoshit kiya gaya tha, us par adult ki tarah trial chalna chahiye. Court ne Kathua ki ek court ka order aur use sahi thehraane wala Jammu and Kashmir High Court ka faisla radd kar diya.

facts.value: Accused to be tried as adult
facts.caveat: Outcome of his separate trial not verified. He is an accused, not a convict: do not name him.

text.en: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 (No. 22 of 2018), assented to on 11 August 2018 and in force from 21 April 2018 (the date of the ordinance), made rape of a girl under 12 punishable with at least 20 years, natural-life imprisonment or death (Section 376AB IPC), and gang rape of a girl under 12 punishable with natural-life imprisonment or death (Section 376DB).
text.hg: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 (No. 22 of 2018), jise 11 August 2018 ko assent mila aur jo 21 April 2018 (ordinance ki date) se laagu hua, ne 12 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ke liye kam se kam 20 saal, natural-life imprisonment ya death penalty ki saza rakhi (Section 376AB IPC), aur 12 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke gang rape ke liye natural-life imprisonment ya death penalty (Section 376DB).

facts.value: Death penalty for rape of a girl under 12
facts.caveat: PRS: the Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance was promulgated on 21 April 2018; it came amid national protests over the Kathua and Unnao cases (context widely reported, not stated by PRS).

text.en: The 2018 amendment raised the minimum punishment for rape from seven to ten years, set a 20-year minimum for rape of a girl under 16, and required police to finish rape investigations within two months and appeals to be decided within six months.
text.hg: 2018 ke amendment ne rape ki minimum saza saat saal se badha kar das saal kar di, 16 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ke liye 20 saal ki minimum saza tay ki, aur zaroori kiya ki police rape investigation do mahine ke andar poori kare aur appeals ka faisla chhah mahine ke andar ho.

facts.value: Rape minimum 10 years; under-16: min 20 years; probe 2 months; appeal 6 months
facts.caveat: PRS also notes the 2018 law bars anticipatory bail for rape of girls under 16. Compliance with the timelines was not verified.

text.en: The POCSO Act now punishes aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child with 20 years to life imprisonment or death, after a 2019 amendment raised the minimum from 10 to 20 years and added the death penalty; penetrative sexual assault carries 10 years to life.
text.hg: POCSO Act ab kisi bachche par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke liye 20 saal se lekar life imprisonment tak, ya death penalty ki saza deta hai. Aisa 2019 ke ek amendment ke baad hua, jisne minimum saza 10 se badha kar 20 saal ki aur death penalty jodi; penetrative sexual assault ke liye 10 saal se lekar life tak ki saza hai.

facts.value: Aggravated penetrative sexual assault: 20 years to life or death
facts.caveat: The PRS page covers the January 2019 Bill; the enacted 2019 amendment (Act number and dates) was not retrieved, but the Supreme Court's 2025 handbook confirms the resulting penalties.

text.en: On 20 December 2019 a Delhi court sentenced former BJP MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar to imprisonment for the remainder of his life and a Rs 25 lakh fine for the 2017 rape of a minor girl in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, after the Supreme Court had moved all Unnao trials from Lucknow to Delhi.
text.hg: 20 December 2019 ko Delhi ki ek court ne former BJP MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar ko Unnao, Uttar Pradesh mein 2017 mein ek naabalig ladki ke rape ke liye baaki poori zindagi ki jail aur Rs 25 lakh jurmaane ki saza sunayi. Isse pehle Supreme Court ne Unnao ke saare trials Lucknow se Delhi transfer kar diye the.

facts.value: Life imprisonment (remainder of life) + Rs 25 lakh fine
facts.caveat: Sengar is convicted and widely reported, so naming him is allowed; never name the survivor. On 13 March 2020 he and six others were also sentenced to 10 years over the death of the survivor's father (Bar and Bench, https://www.barandbench.com/news/unnao-delhi-court-sentences-kuldeep-singh-sengar-six-others-to-10-years-imprisonment-for-role-in-death-of-rape-victims-father).

text.en: In December 2025 the Delhi High Court suspended Sengar's life sentence pending appeal, reasoning at the interim stage that an MLA was not a 'public servant' for aggravated POCSO purposes and that he had already served more than seven years; on 29 December 2025 a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant stayed that order.
text.hg: December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ne appeal pending rehne tak Sengar ki life sentence suspend kar di. Interim stage par court ka tark tha ki aggravated POCSO provisions ke liye ek MLA 'public servant' nahi hai, aur woh pehle hi saat saal se zyada ki saza kaat chuka hai. 29 December 2025 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ki aguwai wali Supreme Court bench ne us order par rok laga di.

facts.value: HC suspension (Dec 2025) stayed by SC on 29 Dec 2025
facts.caveat: The High Court order was passed on 23 December 2025 (LiveLaw listing 'Delhi High Court Suspends Life Sentence Of Kuldeep Singh Sengar In Unnao Rape Case', 23 Dec 2025; Wikipedia citing NDTV). He remained in jail because of the separate custodial-death conviction (BBC).

text.en: On 15 May 2026 the Supreme Court (Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi) set aside the Delhi High Court order suspending Sengar's sentence and sent the matter back, asking the High Court either to decide his main appeal quickly or to pass a fresh order on suspending the sentence.
text.hg: On 15 May 2026 the Supreme Court (Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi) set aside the Delhi High Court order suspending Sengar's sentence and sent the matter back, asking the High Court either to decide his main appeal quickly or to pass a fresh order on suspending the sentence.

facts.value: Suspension set aside and matter remitted, 15 May 2026
facts.caveat: Timeframe conflict (two months in the order extract quoted by The Wire; three months per LiveLaw and The Wire's own summary) - not printed. LiveLaw lists Sengar's arguments against his conviction before the Delhi High Court on 26 May 2026; no decision on the appeal found as of 20 November 2026.

text.en: The 19-year-old Dalit woman at the centre of the Hathras case was assaulted on 14 September 2020, died on 29 September 2020 and was cremated by police in the middle of the night without her family's consent; in December 2020 the CBI charged four men with rape, gang rape and murder.
text.hg: Hathras case ke kendra mein rahi 19 saal ki Dalit yuvati par 14 September 2020 ko hamla hua, 29 September 2020 ko uski maut ho gayi, aur police ne uske parivaar ki consent ke bina aadhi raat ko uska antim sanskar kar diya; December 2020 mein CBI ne chaar aadmiyon par rape, gang rape aur murder ke charges lagaye.

facts.value: Assaulted 14 Sep 2020; died 29 Sep 2020; night cremation; CBI chargesheet Dec 2020
facts.caveat: Never name the victim or her village details beyond the district.

text.en: On 2 March 2023 a special SC/ST court in Hathras acquitted three of the four accused and convicted one of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and offences under the SC/ST Act; none was found guilty of gang rape or murder.
text.hg: 2 March 2023 ko Hathras ki ek special SC/ST court ne chaar mein se teen accused ko bari kar diya aur ek ko culpable homicide not amounting to murder aur SC/ST Act ke tahat offences ka doshi thehraaya; kisi ko bhi gang rape ya murder ka doshi nahi paaya gaya.

facts.value: 3 acquitted, 1 convicted (s.304 IPC + SC/ST Act); no rape conviction
facts.caveat: The three acquitted men must not be named. The family said it would appeal; appeal status not verified.

text.en: The one man convicted in the Hathras case was sentenced to life imprisonment and a Rs 50,000 fine, Rs 40,000 of it for the victim's mother; the court held the prosecution had failed to prove rape and said the other accused were named later 'after being coached by her relatives'.
text.hg: Hathras case mein convict hue ekmaatra aadmi ko life imprisonment aur Rs 50,000 jurmaane ki saza mili, jisme se Rs 40,000 victim ki maa ke liye the; court ne maana ki prosecution rape saabit nahi kar paaya, aur kaha ki baaki accused ke naam baad mein 'after being coached by her relatives' liye gaye.

facts.value: Life imprisonment + Rs 50,000 fine; rape not proved
facts.caveat: This is the trial court's reasoning; it remains open to appeal. The order is in Hindi: LiveLaw renders the phrase as 'tutored by her family members', ThePrint as 'coached by her relatives'. Never name the victim or her family.

text.en: The Supreme Court-appointed Sirpurkar Commission found that the four men accused of a 2019 rape and murder near Hyderabad were 'deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death' by police, that three of the four were minors, and recommended that all ten police officers involved be tried for murder.
text.hg: Supreme Court dwara appoint kiye gaye Sirpurkar Commission ne paaya ki Hyderabad ke paas 2019 mein hue ek rape aur murder ke chaar accused par police ne jaan-boojh kar, unki maut ke iraade se goli chalayi ('deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death'), aur yeh ki chaar mein se teen minor the; commission ne sifarish ki ki is mein shaamil sabhi das police officers par murder ka trial chalaya jaaye.

facts.value: Encounter staged; 3 of 4 killed were minors; 10 officers to be tried for murder
facts.caveat: The four were accused, never tried. The victim was a young veterinarian (widely reported); never use her name or the police pseudonym. Whether any officer has been prosecuted was not confirmed.

text.en: The Supreme Court set up the inquiry commission on 12 December 2019 under former Supreme Court judge V.S. Sirpurkar, with former Bombay High Court judge Rekha Baldota and former CBI Director D.R. Karthikeyan; on 20 May 2022 a bench of Chief Justice N.V. Ramana and Justice Hima Kohli refused Telangana's request to keep its report sealed and sent the matter to the Telangana High Court.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne 12 December 2019 ko former Supreme Court judge V.S. Sirpurkar ki adhyakshata mein inquiry commission banaya, jisme former Bombay High Court judge Rekha Baldota aur former CBI Director D.R. Karthikeyan the; 20 May 2022 ko Chief Justice N.V. Ramana aur Justice Hima Kohli ki bench ne commission ki report sealed rakhne ki Telangana ki request thukra di aur maamla Telangana High Court ko bhej diya.

facts.value: Commission formed 12 Dec 2019; report made public and remitted 20 May 2022
facts.caveat: Status of Telangana High Court proceedings in 2025-26 not confirmed (search-result snippets said a single judge stayed action on the report; not verified).

text.en: On 20 August 2024, in a suo motu case taken up after the 9 August 2024 rape and murder of a doctor at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata, the Supreme Court set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals, headed by Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin, declaring that 'the nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground'.
text.hg: On 20 August 2024, in a suo motu case taken up after the 9 August 2024 rape and murder of a doctor at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata, the Supreme Court set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals, headed by Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin, declaring that 'the nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground'.

facts.value: National Task Force set up, 20 Aug 2024
facts.caveat: LiveLaw calls it a 'ten-member' task force; Wikipedia calls it a '9-member task force' and lists nine named members plus ex-officio officials - count not printed. Never name the victim.

text.en: On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court in Kolkata sentenced the man convicted of the RG Kar rape and murder to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life and a Rs 50,000 fine under Sections 64, 66 and 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, rejecting the CBI's plea for death because the crime was not 'rarest of the rare', and ordered the state to pay Rs 17 lakh to the family.
text.hg: 20 January 2025 ko Kolkata mein Sealdah ki ek court ne RG Kar rape aur murder ke convict ko Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ki Sections 64, 66 aur 103(1) ke tahat baaki poori natural life ke liye life imprisonment aur Rs 50,000 jurmaane ki saza sunayi. Court ne CBI ki death penalty ki maang yeh keh kar thukra di ki crime 'rarest of the rare' nahi tha, aur state ko family ko Rs 17 lakh dene ka order diya.

facts.value: Natural-life imprisonment + Rs 50,000 fine; Rs 17 lakh compensation
facts.caveat: Conviction on Saturday 18 January 2025 is confirmed (TOI; AP via Wikipedia). The convict was a Kolkata Police civic volunteer (Wikipedia). The Calcutta High Court admitted the CBI's appeal for death on 7 Feb 2025 (LiveLaw); its outcome was not found as of 20 Nov 2026. The family said it would move a higher court (Tribune); other reports say the parents declined the compensation.

text.en: On 7 February 2025 the Calcutta High Court dismissed the West Bengal government's appeal seeking the death penalty for the RG Kar convict, leaving the CBI - which investigated and prosecuted the case - to pursue its own appeal.
text.hg: 7 February 2025 ko Calcutta High Court ne RG Kar convict ke liye death penalty maangne wali West Bengal sarkar ki appeal khaarij kar di. Isse apni appeal aage badhaane ka kaam CBI ke zimme raha, jisne is case ki investigation aur prosecution ki thi.

facts.value: State appeal dismissed; CBI appeal to proceed

text.en: On 3 September 2024 the West Bengal Assembly unanimously passed the Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024, which makes the death penalty mandatory for rape where the victim dies or is left in a vegetative state.
text.hg: 3 September 2024 ko West Bengal Assembly ne sarvsammati se Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024 paas kiya, jo aise rape ke liye death penalty ko mandatory banata hai jisme victim ki maut ho jaaye ya woh vegetative state mein chali jaaye.

facts.caveat: A state amendment to central criminal law (BNS, BNSS, POCSO) needs presidential assent.

text.en: The Aparajita Bill would make life imprisonment the minimum and death the maximum punishment for rape under Section 64 BNS and cut the deadline for rape investigations from two months to 21 days (extendable by 15 days); the Governor reserved it for the President on 6 September 2024.
text.hg: Aparajita Bill Section 64 BNS ke tahat rape ke liye life imprisonment ko minimum aur death ko maximum saza bana dega, aur rape investigation ki deadline do mahine se ghata kar 21 din kar dega (jise 15 din aur badhaya ja sakta hai); Governor ne 6 September 2024 ko ise President ke liye reserve kar diya.

facts.value: Rape: life to death; investigation in 21 days
facts.caveat: The explainer's statement that the Assembly passed the Bill on 6 September is wrong - India Today and Bar and Bench confirm passage on Tuesday 3 September 2024; 6 September is the date the explainer gives for the Governor's reservation. ThePrint (25 July 2025) confirms the Bill had been reserved for the President but gives no date. A state amendment to central criminal law needs presidential assent; its status after July 2025 was not confirmed.

text.en: On 21 January 2008 a special court in Mumbai sentenced 11 men to life imprisonment for the gang rape of a pregnant woman and the murder of 14 of her relatives during the 2002 Gujarat riots, convicted a police officer of deliberately recording the FIR incorrectly, and acquitted five police personnel and two doctors; on 4 May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld the 11 convictions and also convicted the seven who had been acquitted.
text.hg: On 21 January 2008 a special court in Mumbai sentenced 11 men to life imprisonment for the gang rape of a pregnant woman and the murder of 14 of her relatives during the 2002 Gujarat riots, convicted a police officer of deliberately recording the FIR incorrectly, and acquitted five police personnel and two doctors; on 4 May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld the 11 convictions and also convicted the seven who had been acquitted.

facts.value: 2008: 11 life sentences + 1 police officer convicted, 7 acquitted; 4 May 2017: HC upheld and convicted the 7
facts.caveat: SC Observer's '13 of 20 accused convicted' count conflicts with the Supreme Court's own account (11 + 1 convicted, 7 acquitted) and is not used. The survivor has publicly identified herself and the case is widely known by her name; this bank does not print it. The trial was moved to Mumbai, which is why Maharashtra was later held to be the 'appropriate government'. Do not reproduce the judgment's graphic descriptions.

text.en: On 23 April 2019 the Supreme Court (Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi, Justices Deepak Gupta and Sanjiv Khanna) ordered the Gujarat government to pay the survivor of the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case Rs 50 lakh in compensation and give her a government job and housing.
text.hg: On 23 April 2019 the Supreme Court (Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi, Justices Deepak Gupta and Sanjiv Khanna) ordered the Gujarat government to pay the survivor of the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case Rs 50 lakh in compensation and give her a government job and housing.

text.en: On 15 August 2022 all 11 men serving life sentences in the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case - convicted of gang rape and of murdering 14 of the survivor's relatives - walked out of Godhra jail after the Gujarat government granted them remission (orders dated 10 August 2022) under its 1992 remission policy.
text.hg: On 15 August 2022 all 11 men serving life sentences in the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case - convicted of gang rape and of murdering 14 of the survivor's relatives - walked out of Godhra jail after the Gujarat government granted them remission (orders dated 10 August 2022) under its 1992 remission policy.

facts.value: 11 life convicts released, 15 Aug 2022 (remission orders dated 10 Aug 2022)
facts.caveat: The Leaflet gives 11 August 2022, and some reports (The Hindu, 2019; a tweet quoted by Scroll) say seven family members were killed; the Supreme Court's 2024 judgment lists 14 relatives. Survivor's name not printed.

text.en: On 8 January 2024 a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan quashed the remission of the 11 convicts in the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case, holding that Gujarat had no power to grant it because Maharashtra, where the trial was held, was the appropriate government, and that the court's May 2022 order directing Gujarat to decide remission had been obtained by suppressing facts and fraud.
text.hg: On 8 January 2024 a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan quashed the remission of the 11 convicts in the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case, holding that Gujarat had no power to grant it because Maharashtra, where the trial was held, was the appropriate government, and that the court's May 2022 order directing Gujarat to decide remission had been obtained by suppressing facts and fraud.

facts.value: Remission quashed; convicts ordered back to jail
facts.caveat: Cited as W.P. (Crl.) No. 491 of 2022 (2024 INSC 24 per search results); the official cause title carries the survivor's name. The Supreme Court dismissed Gujarat's review petition on 26 September 2024 (SC Observer; not re-verified).

text.en: All 11 convicts in the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case surrendered at Godhra sub-jail in Gujarat's Panchmahal district late on the night of 21 January 2024, the Supreme Court's deadline, after the court refused their pleas for more time.
text.hg: All 11 convicts in the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case surrendered at Godhra sub-jail in Gujarat's Panchmahal district late on the night of 21 January 2024, the Supreme Court's deadline, after the court refused their pleas for more time.

text.en: A social audit of Bihar's children's homes by the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), done for the state government and submitted in April 2018, flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur.
text.hg: A social audit of Bihar's children's homes by the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), done for the state government and submitted in April 2018, flagged sexual abuse at several institutions, including a state-funded girls' shelter home in Muzaffarpur.

facts.value: TISS audit submitted April 2018; Muzaffarpur home flagged
facts.caveat: The counts (110 homes, 38 districts, 15 institutions) come from Newslaundry alone; other reports say 35 districts and the CBI later investigated 17 homes - not printed. The audit itself was not retrieved.

text.en: The TISS audit revealed the sexual abuse of 34 minor girls at the state-run shelter home in Muzaffarpur, according to the Supreme Court's 2025 Handbook on Child Rights and the Law.
text.hg: Supreme Court ki 2025 ki Handbook on Child Rights and the Law ke mutabik, TISS audit se Muzaffarpur ke state-run shelter home mein 34 naabalig ladkiyon ke sexual abuse ka khulasa hua tha.

facts.caveat: An early figure from audit-team members (June 2018 medical examinations) was 29 of 42 girls (Newslaundry); later medical findings put it at 34 of 42 (Wikipedia, citing Indian Express, 5 Aug 2018). The handbook also notes that in Nivedita Jha v. State of Bihar (order dated 20 September 2018) the Supreme Court found the Patna High Court's blanket ban on media reporting of the case an excessive restriction.

text.en: On 20 January 2020 a POCSO court at Saket, Delhi - to which the Supreme Court had transferred the trial on 7 February 2019 - convicted 19 of the 20 accused in the Muzaffarpur shelter home case; 11 were later sentenced to life imprisonment.
text.hg: 20 January 2020 ko Saket, Delhi ki ek POCSO court ne - jise Supreme Court ne 7 February 2019 ko yeh trial transfer kiya tha - Muzaffarpur shelter home case ke 20 mein se 19 accused ko convict kiya; baad mein 11 ko life imprisonment ki saza mili.

facts.caveat: Hindustan Times' headline ('Brajesh Thakur, 11 others sentenced to life') implies 12 life terms, but the CBI's itemised list and LiveLaw ('Brajesh Thakur and 10 others') give 11.

text.en: On 11 February 2020 the shelter home's operator, Brajesh Thakur, was sentenced by a Saket court to life imprisonment for the remainder of his life and fined about Rs 32 lakh.
text.hg: 11 February 2020 ko Saket ki ek court ne shelter home ke operator Brajesh Thakur ko baaki poori zindagi ke liye life imprisonment ki saza sunayi aur us par lagbhag Rs 32 lakh ka jurmaana lagaya.

facts.value: Life imprisonment till remainder of life; fine about Rs 32 lakh
facts.caveat: Convicted and widely reported, so naming is allowed.

text.en: In Lillu @ Rajesh v. State of Haryana ((2013) 14 SCC 643), decided in April 2013, a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.S. Chauhan and F.M. Ibrahim Kalifulla held that the 'two-finger test' violates the right of rape survivors to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity.
text.hg: In Lillu @ Rajesh v. State of Haryana ((2013) 14 SCC 643), decided in April 2013, a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.S. Chauhan and F.M. Ibrahim Kalifulla held that the 'two-finger test' violates the right of rape survivors to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity.

facts.caveat: Reported in the press in May 2013. Bar and Bench gives 9 April 2013; the exact day was not independently confirmed. The appellant had been convicted of rape (Bar and Bench).

text.en: On 31 October 2022, in State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai, the Supreme Court (Justices D.Y. Chandrachud and Hima Kohli) said the two-finger test 'has no scientific basis', ruled that anyone conducting it in breach of its directions 'shall be guilty of misconduct', and directed governments to circulate the Health Ministry's 2014 guidelines to all government and private hospitals and to review medical curricula so that the test is not prescribed.
text.hg: On 31 October 2022, in State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai, the Supreme Court (Justices D.Y. Chandrachud and Hima Kohli) said the two-finger test 'has no scientific basis', ruled that anyone conducting it in breach of its directions 'shall be guilty of misconduct', and directed governments to circulate the Health Ministry's 2014 guidelines to all government and private hospitals and to review medical curricula so that the test is not prescribed.

facts.value: Two-finger test = misconduct; guidelines circulated; curricula reviewed
facts.caveat: In this case a medical board at Sadar hospital, Deoghar had performed the test; the trial judgment dates to 2006, so the examination likely predates Lillu.

text.en: On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, a Supreme Court bench of Justices Madan B. Lokur and Deepak Gupta read down the marital rape exception in Section 375 IPC so that sexual intercourse by a man with his wife aged between 15 and 18 is rape.
text.hg: 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein Justices Madan B. Lokur aur Deepak Gupta ki Supreme Court bench ne Section 375 IPC ke marital rape exception ko read down kiya, jisse 15 se 18 saal ki umar ki wife ke saath pati ka sexual intercourse rape hai.

facts.value: Marital exception read down to wives 18+
facts.caveat: SC Observer's 12 October date is wrong; the judgment is dated 11 October 2017. The ruling did not touch the exception for wives aged 18 and above.

text.en: On 29 September 2022, in X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, the Supreme Court (Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, A.S. Bopanna and J.B. Pardiwala) held that 'rape' under the abortion law includes marital rape, so a woman pregnant through rape by her husband can seek termination up to 24 weeks, while leaving the validity of the criminal-law marital rape exception to a separate pending case.
text.hg: 29 September 2022 ko X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department case mein Supreme Court (Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, A.S. Bopanna aur J.B. Pardiwala) ne kaha ki abortion law ke tahat 'rape' mein marital rape bhi shaamil hai, isliye pati dwara kiye gaye rape se pregnant hui aurat 24 hafte tak termination maang sakti hai; lekin criminal law ke marital rape exception ki validity ka sawaal court ne ek alag pending case ke liye chhod diya.

facts.value: Marital rape counts as rape for abortion law (MTP Act)
facts.caveat: Applies only to the MTP Act; it does not make marital rape a crime.

text.en: The same 29 September 2022 judgment held that unmarried and single women are entitled to abortion between 20 and 24 weeks on the same footing as married women, calling the distinction 'artificial' and 'not constitutionally sustainable'.
text.hg: 29 September 2022 ke isi judgment mein kaha gaya ki unmarried aur single auraton ko bhi married auraton ki tarah 20 se 24 hafte ke beech abortion ka haq hai; court ne is farq ko 'artificial' aur 'not constitutionally sustainable' bataya.

facts.value: Unmarried women: abortion up to 24 weeks
facts.caveat: Relevant to rape survivors because many do not report rape; the court held a woman need not prove rape through formal legal proceedings to use Rule 3B(a).

text.en: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the Indian Penal Code, keeps the marital rape exception: Exception 2 to Section 63 says sexual intercourse by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under 18, is not rape.
text.hg: Indian Penal Code ki jagah lene wali Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 mein marital rape exception barkarar hai: Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke mutabik koi aadmi apni hi wife ke saath, jiski umar 18 se kam na ho, sexual intercourse kare toh woh rape nahi hai.

facts.value: Marital rape exception retained in BNS s.63 (wife 18+)
facts.caveat: Text checked in the Bill as passed by Parliament; India Code's copy of the enacted Act could not be retrieved (HTTP 504). The 18-year age follows Independent Thought (2017).

text.en: On 11 May 2022 a two-judge Delhi High Court bench delivered a split verdict on the marital rape exception in RIT Foundation v. Union of India: Justice Rajiv Shakdher held it unconstitutional, Justice C. Hari Shankar upheld it, and the case went to the Supreme Court.
text.hg: On 11 May 2022 a two-judge Delhi High Court bench delivered a split verdict on the marital rape exception in RIT Foundation v. Union of India: Justice Rajiv Shakdher held it unconstitutional, Justice C. Hari Shankar upheld it, and the case went to the Supreme Court.

facts.caveat: The petitioners included the NGOs RIT Foundation and All India Democratic Women's Association (per LiveLaw).

text.en: As of 20 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on the petitions challenging the marital rape exception (now Exception 2 to Section 63 of the BNS): on 9 September 2026 a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana posted the batch for final hearing. The Union government had opposed criminalising marital rape in a preliminary affidavit filed in October 2024.
text.hg: As of 20 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on the petitions challenging the marital rape exception (now Exception 2 to Section 63 of the BNS): on 9 September 2026 a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana posted the batch for final hearing. The Union government had opposed criminalising marital rape in a preliminary affidavit filed in October 2024.

facts.value: Pending (posted for final hearing, 9 Sep 2026); Centre opposed (Oct 2024)
facts.caveat: Status as of 20 November 2026, from LiveLaw's coverage; re-check before publication.

text.en: On 18 November 2021, in Attorney General for India v. Satish, the Supreme Court set aside the Bombay High Court's January 2021 'skin-to-skin' ruling, holding that 'the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child'.
text.hg: 18 November 2021 ko Attorney General for India v. Satish case mein Supreme Court ne Bombay High Court ka January 2021 ka 'skin-to-skin' ruling radd kar diya, aur kaha ki 'the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child'.

facts.caveat: The Supreme Court's 2025 Handbook on Child Rights describes the HC ruling as the best-known example of courts narrowly interpreting sexual assault.

text.en: On 18 March 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the Supreme Court (Justices A.M. Khanwilkar and S. Ravindra Bhat) struck down a High Court bail condition requiring a man accused of sexual assault to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him, and ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact with the victim, that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage, and that every judge must receive gender-sensitisation training.
text.hg: 18 March 2021 ko Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh case mein Supreme Court (Justices A.M. Khanwilkar aur S. Ravindra Bhat) ne High Court ki woh bail condition radd kar di jisme sexual assault ke accused se kaha gaya tha ki woh complainant se rakhi bandhwane ki request kare. Court ne rule kiya ki bail conditions victim se contact ko na zaroori banayein na allow karein, courts compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav na dein, aur har judge ko gender-sensitisation training milni chahiye.

facts.value: Rakhi-for-bail set aside; no-contact rule; no compromise/marriage; judge training
facts.caveat: Date from the LiveLaw timestamp (2021-03-18); neutral citation 2021 INSC 192 per search results.

text.en: On 11 December 2018, in Nipun Saxena v. Union of India, the Supreme Court (Justices Madan B. Lokur and Deepak Gupta) directed that no person may print or publish in print, electronic or social media the name of a rape victim 'or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified'.
text.hg: 11 December 2018 ko Nipun Saxena v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court (Justices Madan B. Lokur aur Deepak Gupta) ne nirdesh diya ki koi bhi vyakti print, electronic ya social media mein rape victim ka naam print ya publish nahi kar sakta, 'or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified' - yaani door-door tak bhi aisa koi fact nahi bata sakta jisse victim ki pehchaan ho sake.

facts.value: No disclosure of victim identity, even remotely
facts.caveat: Direction 2: even for a dead victim, next of kin cannot authorise disclosure unless the Sessions Judge finds justifying circumstances. The statutory bar is now Section 72 BNS (formerly s.228A IPC), which the Supreme Court's 2025 child-rights handbook notes allows disclosure with written authorisation in some situations.

text.en: The Nipun Saxena judgment also ordered that FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain and asked every state and union territory to set up at least one 'one stop centre' in every district within a year.
text.hg: Nipun Saxena judgment ne yeh order bhi diya ki rape aur POCSO cases ki FIRs public domain mein na daali jaayein, aur har state aur union territory se kaha ki ek saal ke andar har district mein kam se kam ek 'one stop centre' banayein.

facts.value: FIRs not public; one stop centre in every district
facts.caveat: By March 2025 there were 802 One Stop Centres (PIB).

text.en: On 16 August 2023 the Supreme Court released a Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, with a foreword by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, telling judges to replace terms such as 'eve teasing' with 'street sexual harassment', 'forcible rape' with 'rape', 'ravished' with 'sexually assaulted or raped', and 'chaste woman', 'fallen woman' and 'seductress' with 'woman'.
text.hg: 16 August 2023 ko Supreme Court ne Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ke foreword ke saath Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes jaari ki, jisme judges se kaha gaya ki woh 'eve teasing' ki jagah 'street sexual harassment', 'forcible rape' ki jagah 'rape', 'ravished' ki jagah 'sexually assaulted or raped', aur 'chaste woman', 'fallen woman' aur 'seductress' ki jagah 'woman' jaise terms use karein.

facts.caveat: The 'prostitute' entry was amended on 13 November 2023.

text.en: The Supreme Court handbook lists as false stereotypes that a woman's clothing, drinking or smoking invites sexual contact, that rapists are usually strangers, and that a genuine survivor cries incessantly or never speaks to the accused again - and quotes a 2022 Kerala sessions court bail order which said the complainant was 'exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one'.
text.hg: The Supreme Court handbook lists as false stereotypes that a woman's clothing, drinking or smoking invites sexual contact, that rapists are usually strangers, and that a genuine survivor cries incessantly or never speaks to the accused again - and quotes a 2022 Kerala sessions court bail order which said the complainant was 'exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one'.

facts.value: Rape myths named by the Supreme Court
facts.caveat: The Kozhikode accused was not convicted in that order; do not name him.

text.en: On 23 September 2024, on an appeal by Just Rights for Children Alliance (2024 INSC 716), the Supreme Court overturned a Madras High Court ruling that privately viewing or storing child sexual abuse material was not a crime, held that viewing, possessing and storing such material is punishable under Section 15 of the POCSO Act and Section 67B of the IT Act, and told courts to use the term 'Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material' (CSEAM) instead of 'child pornography'.
text.hg: On 23 September 2024, on an appeal by Just Rights for Children Alliance (2024 INSC 716), the Supreme Court overturned a Madras High Court ruling that privately viewing or storing child sexual abuse material was not a crime, held that viewing, possessing and storing such material is punishable under Section 15 of the POCSO Act and Section 67B of the IT Act, and told courts to use the term 'Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material' (CSEAM) instead of 'child pornography'.

facts.value: Possessing/viewing CSEAM is a crime; term 'child pornography' dropped
facts.caveat: Neutral citation 2024 INSC 716. The respondent named in the case title is an accused whose prosecution was revived, not a convict, so he is not named. The handbook cites NCRB data showing CSEAM-related cybercrimes against children rose from 44 cases in 2018 to 1,171 in 2022 (PIB, 29 July 2025; not re-verified).

text.en: On 10 February 2026, in a suo motu case over a High Court order that had reduced charges in a child sexual assault case from attempt to rape to lesser offences, a Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and N.V. Anjaria said efforts to sensitise judges 'have not borne the fruit that was expected' and asked a National Judicial Academy expert committee headed by former judge Aniruddha Bose to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases.
text.hg: 10 February 2026 ko, ek High Court order par suo motu liye gaye case mein - us order ne ek child sexual assault case mein charges ko attempt to rape se ghata kar kam gambhir offences mein badal diya tha - Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur N.V. Anjaria ki Supreme Court bench ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishein 'have not borne the fruit that was expected', yaani unse ummeed ke mutabik nateeje nahi mile. Bench ne former judge Aniruddha Bose ki adhyakshata wali National Judicial Academy expert committee se sexual-offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines draft karne ko kaha.

facts.value: Expert committee on judicial sensitivity ordered, 10 Feb 2026
facts.caveat: LiveLaw (14 Jul 2026) identifies the High Court as the Allahabad High Court. On 14 July 2026 a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana approved the NJA expert committee's guidelines and directed all courts to follow them (LiveLaw; single source, not added as a separate fact). Avoid the High Court order's graphic descriptions.

text.en: In October 2020 the Allahabad High Court (Justices Pankaj Mithal and Rajan Roy) observed that the Hathras victim's hurried night cremation was 'prima facie an infringement upon the human rights of the victim and her family'.
text.hg: In October 2020 the Allahabad High Court (Justices Pankaj Mithal and Rajan Roy) observed that the Hathras victim's hurried night cremation was 'prima facie an infringement upon the human rights of the victim and her family'.

facts.value: 'prima facie an infringement upon the human rights' (Oct 2020)
facts.caveat: Mint dates the observation to 13 October 2020. The finding that the cremation was carried out on the District Magistrate's orders is in LiveLaw only. Never name the victim.

text.en: On 13 March 2020 a Delhi court sentenced Kuldeep Singh Sengar and six others to 10 years' imprisonment for culpable homicide over the death of the Unnao survivor's father, who had been arrested on an illegal-firearms charge after an assault in April 2018 and died in custody.
text.hg: On 13 March 2020 a Delhi court sentenced Kuldeep Singh Sengar and six others to 10 years' imprisonment for culpable homicide over the death of the Unnao survivor's father, who had been arrested on an illegal-firearms charge after an assault in April 2018 and died in custody.

facts.caveat: Sengar is convicted and widely reported, so naming him is allowed; never name the survivor or her family, and the six co-convicts are not named here. This conviction kept him in jail when his rape sentence was suspended in December 2025. LiveLaw lists a 19 Jan 2026 Delhi High Court refusal to suspend this sentence (listing only, not verified).

text.en: The law that legalised abortion in India grew out of a government committee constituted in 1964 and headed by Shantilal Shah, which reported in 1966 that the existing abortion law was too restrictive and should be liberalised.
text.hg: India mein abortion ko legal banane wala kanoon ek sarkari committee se nikla tha, jo 1964 mein bani thi aur jiske head Shantilal Shah the. Is committee ne 1966 ki apni report mein kaha ki us waqt ka abortion kanoon bahut zyada sakht hai aur use liberal banaya jana chahiye.

facts.caveat: India Code's legislative history for the MTP Act confirms the 1964 committee; the 1966 report date and the quoted recommendation come from ThePrint's news history piece. Some accounts give 1965 for the committee's formation. ThePrint also reports that the committee considered abortion unviable as a method of population control.

text.en: India's Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, passed in 1971, came into force on 1 April 1972.
text.hg: India's Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, passed in 1971, came into force on 1 April 1972.

facts.caveat: Brought into force by notification G.S.R. 285 of 19 February 1972. ThePrint (29 June 2022) also reports that the Act "was implemented in the month of April, 1972".

text.en: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (Act No. 34 of 1971), which received the President's assent on 10 August 1971, allowed abortion up to 12 weeks on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner and between 12 and 20 weeks only if two registered medical practitioners agreed.
text.hg: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971 (Act No. 34 of 1971), jise 10 August 1971 ko President ki manzoori mili thi, 12 hafte tak abortion ki ijazat ek registered doctor ki raay par deta tha, aur 12 se 20 hafte ke beech abortion sirf tab ho sakta tha jab do registered doctors sehmat hon.

facts.value: Assent 10 August 1971; 12 weeks / 1 doctor; 12-20 weeks / 2 doctors
facts.caveat: The Act originally extended to the whole of India except Jammu and Kashmir. These limits stood for 50 years, until the 2021 amendment took effect on 24 September 2021.

text.en: The 1971 MTP Act presumed grave injury to mental health from contraceptive failure only when the device or method was used by "any married woman or her husband", leaving unmarried women outside that ground until 2021.
text.hg: 1971 ka MTP Act yeh maan kar chalta tha ki contraceptive fail hone se mental health ko gambhir nuksaan pahunchta hai, lekin sirf tab jab woh device ya method "any married woman or her husband" ne use kiya ho. Isliye 2021 tak unmarried auratein is ground ke daayre se bahar rahin.

text.en: Under the MTP Act, an adult woman's own consent is the only consent needed for an abortion; written consent of a guardian is required only if she is under 18 or a mentally ill person. The law does not require a husband's consent.
text.hg: MTP Act ke tahat abortion ke liye adult aurat ki sirf apni consent chahiye; guardian ki likhit consent tabhi zaroori hai jab woh 18 saal se kam ki ho ya mentally ill ho. Kanoon pati ki consent nahi maangta.

facts.value: Woman's consent only; guardian consent if under 18
facts.caveat: The 2002 amendment replaced "lunatic" with "mentally ill person". The statement that no husband's consent is required is an inference from the text, which names no such requirement.

text.en: Since the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2002 (Act 64 of 2002), an abortion performed by anyone who is not a registered medical practitioner, or at a place not approved under the Act, is punishable with two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment; the same amendment let District Level Committees of three to five members, chaired by the Chief Medical Officer or District Health Officer, approve private abortion facilities.
text.hg: MTP (Amendment) Act, 2002 (Act 64 of 2002) ke baad se, registered doctor ke alawa kisi aur ke dwara, ya is Act ke tahat approved na ki gayi jagah par kiye gaye abortion ke liye do se saat saal ki rigorous imprisonment (kathor kaid) ho sakti hai; isi amendment ne Chief Medical Officer ya District Health Officer ki adhyakshata wali teen se paanch members ki District Level Committees ko private abortion facilities ko approve karne ka adhikaar diya.

facts.value: 2 to 7 years rigorous imprisonment; district-level approval of facilities
facts.caveat: Attribution to 2002 is by comparison with the 1971 Gazette text, which only made such abortions punishable under the IPC and allowed approval of places only "by Government"; the 2021 amendment did not change Sections 4 and 5(2)-(3). The 2002 amendment also replaced the word "lunatic" with "mentally ill person".

text.en: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 (Act No. 8 of 2021) received the assent of the President of India on 25 March 2021.
text.hg: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 (Act No. 8 of 2021) ko 25 March 2021 ko India ke President ki manzoori mili.

text.en: The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 came into force on 24 September 2021.
text.hg: 24 September 2021 ko Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 lagu hua.

facts.caveat: Parliament passed the Bill in the Lok Sabha on 17 March 2020 and the Rajya Sabha on 16 March 2021 (PIB, 17 March 2021).

text.en: The Lok Sabha passed the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Bill on 17 March 2020, but the Rajya Sabha approved it only on 16 March 2021, almost a year later; the government said the changes would ensure "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" for women.
text.hg: Lok Sabha ne Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Bill 17 March 2020 ko paas kiya, lekin Rajya Sabha ne ise lagbhag ek saal baad, 16 March 2021 ko jaakar manzoori di; sarkar ne kaha ki yeh badlaav auraton ke liye "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" ensure karenge.

facts.value: Lok Sabha 17 March 2020; Rajya Sabha 16 March 2021
facts.caveat: PIB noted that courts had received several petitions seeking abortion beyond the 20-week limit because of foetal abnormalities or sexual violence, which drove the change.

text.en: Since the 2021 amendment, a pregnancy of up to 20 weeks can be terminated in India on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner, if continuing it would risk the woman's life or gravely injure her physical or mental health, or if there is a substantial risk of serious foetal abnormality.
text.hg: 2021 ke amendment ke baad se India mein 20 hafte tak ki pregnancy ek registered doctor ki raay par terminate ki ja sakti hai, agar pregnancy jaari rakhne se aurat ki jaan ko khatra ho ya uski physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan pahunche, ya agar foetus mein serious abnormality ka kaafi khatra ho.

facts.value: Up to 20 weeks: opinion of 1 doctor
facts.caveat: Abortion is not available on request at any stage in India; it is permitted only on the grounds in Section 3(2), on a doctor's opinion.

text.en: Under the MTP Act as amended in 2021, a pregnancy between 20 and 24 weeks can be terminated only for categories of women prescribed by the rules, and only if at least two registered medical practitioners agree.
text.hg: 2021 mein amend kiye gaye MTP Act ke tahat 20 se 24 hafte ke beech ki pregnancy sirf rules mein tay ki gayi categories ki auraton ke liye terminate ki ja sakti hai, aur woh bhi tabhi jab kam se kam do registered doctors sehmat hon.

text.en: Since 2021 the MTP Act sets no upper gestational limit when an abortion is needed because a Medical Board has diagnosed a substantial foetal abnormality; every state and union territory must set up such a board, with at least a gynaecologist, a paediatrician and a radiologist or sonologist.
text.hg: 2021 se MTP Act mein aise abortion ke liye pregnancy ki avadhi ki koi upper limit nahi hai jiski zaroorat isliye ho ki Medical Board ne foetus mein substantial abnormality diagnose ki hai; har state aur union territory ko aisa board banana zaroori hai, jismein kam se kam ek gynaecologist, ek paediatrician aur ek radiologist ya sonologist ho.

facts.value: No upper limit for substantial foetal abnormality
facts.caveat: The exemption covers only foetal abnormalities. Past 24 weeks, a rape survivor or a minor has no statutory route except a termination immediately necessary to save her life (Section 5), and must otherwise petition a High Court or the Supreme Court.

text.en: Section 5A of the MTP Act, inserted in 2021, bars any registered medical practitioner from revealing the name or other particulars of a woman whose pregnancy was terminated, except to a person authorised by law, on pain of up to one year in prison, a fine, or both.
text.hg: 2021 mein jodi gayi MTP Act ki Section 5A kisi bhi registered doctor ko us aurat ka naam ya koi aur details bataane se rokti hai jiski pregnancy terminate hui ho, siwaay kanoon dwara authorised vyakti ke; aisa karne par ek saal tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain.

facts.value: Up to 1 year imprisonment, fine, or both

text.en: The 2021 amendment extended the contraceptive-failure ground of the MTP Act from "married woman or her husband" to "any woman or her partner", so unmarried women can also rely on it.
text.hg: 2021 ke amendment ne MTP Act ke contraceptive-failure wale ground ko "married woman or her husband" se badha kar "any woman or her partner" kar diya, jisse unmarried auratein bhi iska sahara le sakti hain.

facts.caveat: PIB described it as: "The ground of failure of contraceptive has been extended to women and her partner."

text.en: Under the MTP Act, when a pregnant woman alleges that her pregnancy was caused by rape, the anguish caused by the pregnancy is presumed to be a grave injury to her mental health, which is a legal ground for termination.
text.hg: MTP Act ke tahat, jab koi pregnant aurat yeh aarop lagaati hai ki uski pregnancy rape ki wajah se hui hai, to us pregnancy se hone wali peeda ko uski mental health ke liye gambhir nuksaan maana jaata hai, jo termination ka ek legal ground hai.

facts.value: Rape presumed to cause grave injury to mental health
facts.caveat: The same presumption existed in the 1971 text. The Supreme Court held in 2022 (para 76) that no FIR, court finding or conviction is needed before a woman can rely on it.

text.en: The MTP (Amendment) Rules, notified by the Union Health Ministry on 12 October 2021, list seven categories of women eligible for abortion up to 24 weeks: survivors of sexual assault, rape or incest; minors; women whose marital status changes during the pregnancy (widowhood or divorce); women with major physical disabilities; mentally ill women; cases of serious foetal malformation; and women in humanitarian, disaster or emergency settings.
text.hg: Union Health Ministry ne 12 October 2021 ko jo MTP (Amendment) Rules notify kiye, unmein auraton ki saat categories hain jo 24 hafte tak abortion ke liye eligible hain: sexual assault, rape ya incest ki survivors; minors; woh auratein jinka marital status pregnancy ke dauraan badal jaaye (widow hona ya divorce); badi physical disabilities wali auratein; mentally ill auratein; foetus mein serious malformation ke cases; aur humanitarian, disaster ya emergency halaat mein rehne wali auratein.

facts.caveat: The rule uses the outdated term "mental retardation". In 2022 the Supreme Court read clause (c) to cover unmarried and single women whose circumstances change.

text.en: Under the MTP Rules as amended in 2021, a Medical Board must give its opinion on a request to terminate a pregnancy beyond 24 weeks within three days, and when it approves, the procedure must be carried out within five days of the request.
text.hg: 2021 mein amend kiye gaye MTP Rules ke tahat, 24 hafte se zyada ki pregnancy terminate karne ki request par Medical Board ko teen din ke andar apni raay deni hoti hai, aur agar board manzoori de, to request ke paanch din ke andar procedure karna zaroori hai.

facts.value: Opinion within 3 days; termination within 5 days
facts.caveat: These deadlines apply to requests under Section 3(2B) (substantial foetal abnormality).

text.en: India's Health Ministry guidelines (2023) state that the mifepristone-misoprostol combination is approved for ending a pregnancy up to nine weeks (63 days), succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions, and can be prescribed by a qualified doctor at a clinic linked to an approved abortion facility.
text.hg: India ke Health Ministry ki guidelines (2023) kehti hain ki mifepristone-misoprostol combination nau hafte (63 din) tak ki pregnancy khatam karne ke liye approved hai, early abortions ke 95-99% cases mein kaamyaab rehta hai, aur ise kisi approved abortion facility se jude clinic mein ek qualified doctor prescribe kar sakta hai.

facts.caveat: Selling these drugs without a prescription, and taking them without medical advice, falls outside this framework; that is how most medication abortions in India actually happen (see Lancet 2018 facts).

text.en: An estimated 15.6 million abortions took place in India in 2015 (range 14.1 million to 17.3 million), a rate of 47.0 per 1,000 women aged 15-49, according to a national study by the Guttmacher Institute, IIPS Mumbai and the Population Council published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018.
text.hg: Guttmacher Institute, IIPS Mumbai aur Population Council ki ek national study ke mutabik, jo 2018 mein The Lancet Global Health mein chhapi, India mein 2015 mein andaazan 15.6 million abortions hue (range 14.1 million se 17.3 million), yaani 15-49 saal ki har 1,000 auraton par 47.0 ki rate.

facts.caveat: Modelled estimate built from a 2015 survey of 4,001 health facilities in six states, national medication-abortion drug sales data and NFHS-4. It is the most recent national estimate found in this session.

text.en: About 11.5 million of India's estimated 15.6 million abortions in 2015 (73%) were medication abortions done outside health facilities, while only 3.4 million (22%) took place in health facilities, 73% of them private.
text.hg: 2015 mein India ke andaazan 15.6 million abortions mein se lagbhag 11.5 million (73%) medication abortions the jo health facilities ke bahar hue, jabki sirf 3.4 million (22%) health facilities mein hue, aur unmein se 73% private facilities mein.

facts.value: 11.5 million (73%) outside facilities; 3.4 million (22%) in facilities
facts.caveat: Medication abortion outside facilities is not automatically unsafe; the authors note that little is known about the information women get from chemists and informal vendors and whether they take the pills correctly.

text.en: Of India's estimated 15.6 million abortions in 2015, 12.7 million (81%) were medication abortions, 2.2 million (14%) were surgical, and 0.8 million (5%) used other methods the authors judged probably unsafe.
text.hg: 2015 mein India ke andaazan 15.6 million abortions mein se 12.7 million (81%) medication abortions the, 2.2 million (14%) surgical the, aur 0.8 million (5%) mein doosre tareeke use hue jinhe study ke authors ne shayad unsafe maana.

text.en: Ready-made mifepristone-misoprostol "MA Combipacks" were used in 87% of the estimated 11.5 million medication abortions done outside health facilities in India in 2015.
text.hg: 2015 mein India mein health facilities ke bahar hue andaazan 11.5 million medication abortions mein se 87% mein ready-made mifepristone-misoprostol "MA Combipacks" use hue.

text.en: India had an estimated 48.1 million pregnancies in 2015; one third ended in induced abortion and nearly half were unintended, an unintended pregnancy rate of 70.1 per 1,000 women aged 15-49.
text.hg: 2015 mein India mein andaazan 48.1 million pregnancies huin; inmein se ek-tihaai induced abortion (jaan-boojh kar karaye gaye abortion) se khatam huin aur lagbhag aadhi unintended thin, yaani unintended pregnancy ki rate 15-49 saal ki har 1,000 auraton par 70.1 thi.

facts.caveat: The paper reports 52% of pregnancies as intended.

text.en: Across six Indian states surveyed in 2015 (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh), 4-16% of patients receiving post-abortion care were being treated for serious complications such as uterine infection, perforation, sepsis and shock.
text.hg: 2015 mein jin chhah Indian states (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu aur Uttar Pradesh) mein survey hua, wahan post-abortion care le rahe 4-16% patients ka serious complications ka ilaaj chal raha tha, jaise uterus ka infection, perforation, sepsis aur shock.

facts.caveat: The share is of post-abortion care patients, not of all abortions.

text.en: India's Health Ministry recorded only 701,415 abortions in 2014-15, and between 621,000 and 770,000 a year over the previous 15 years, against a research estimate of 15.6 million abortions in 2015.
text.hg: India ki Health Ministry ne 2014-15 mein sirf 701,415 abortions record kiye, aur usse pehle ke 15 saalon mein har saal 621,000 se 770,000 ke beech, jabki ek research estimate ke mutabik 2015 mein 15.6 million abortions hue.

facts.caveat: Official counts cover only reporting facilities, so they capture under 5% of the estimated total (701,415 / 15.6 million, derived).

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 2.9% of women's last pregnancies in the five years before the survey were reported to have ended in an abortion: 4.0% in urban areas and 2.5% in rural areas.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein, survey se pehle ke paanch saalon mein auraton ki aakhri pregnancies mein se 2.9% ka ant abortion mein hone ki baat report hui: urban areas mein 4.0% aur rural areas mein 2.5%.
