facts.caveat: Abortion is heavily under-reported in household surveys; the Lancet 2018 study estimated that about one third of all pregnancies in 2015 ended in abortion.

text.en: Among women in NFHS-5 (2019-21) whose last pregnancy ended in an abortion, 52.9% had it in the private sector, 20.3% in the public sector and 26.2% at home, and 26.9% said they performed it themselves (30.0% in rural areas); a doctor performed 54.8%.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin auraton ki aakhri pregnancy abortion mein khatam hui, unmein se 52.9% ka abortion private sector mein, 20.3% ka public sector mein aur 26.2% ka ghar par hua; 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone yeh khud kiya (rural areas mein 30.0%), aur 54.8% abortions doctor ne kiye.

facts.caveat: Two in three reported abortions used medicines (67.5%). Self-managed medication abortion can be safe with correct information; this measures who performed it, not whether it was unsafe.

text.en: The main reason women gave for their abortion in NFHS-5 (2019-21) was an unplanned pregnancy (47.6%), followed by health not permitting (11.3%), the last child being too young (9.7%), pregnancy complications (9.1%), the husband or mother-in-law not wanting it (4.1%) and contraceptive failure (3.6%).
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein auraton ne abortion ki sabse badi wajah unplanned pregnancy (47.6%) batayi, uske baad health ka ijazat na dena (11.3%), pichhle bachche ka bahut chhota hona (9.7%), pregnancy complications (9.1%), pati ya saas ka yeh pregnancy na chahna (4.1%) aur contraceptive fail hona (3.6%).

facts.value: Unplanned 47.6%; health 11.3%; last child too young 9.7%

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 2.1% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion openly named a female foetus as the main reason; among the larger states the share was highest in Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) and Punjab (4.2%).
text.hg: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 2.1% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion openly named a female foetus as the main reason; among the larger states the share was highest in Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) and Punjab (4.2%).

facts.value: 2.1% India; larger states: Bihar 5.3%, Jharkhand 4.9%, Punjab 4.2%
facts.caveat: Sex-selective abortion is a crime, so self-reporting is almost certainly a large undercount; state figures rest on small numbers of abortions. Two small states/UTs recorded higher shares on very few cases: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (7.6%) and Goa (7.3%).

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 15.6% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion reported complications; 89.7% of them sought treatment, 70.6% of it in the private sector.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin auraton ki aakhri pregnancy abortion mein khatam hui, unmein se 15.6% ne complications report kiye; inmein se 89.7% ilaaj ke liye gayin, aur us ilaaj ka 70.6% private sector mein hua.

text.en: Unsafe abortions account for about 8% of maternal deaths in India, according to the Union Health Ministry's 2023 Comprehensive Abortion Care guidelines, which rely on Registrar General cause-of-death data for 2001-03.
text.hg: Union Health Ministry ki 2023 ki Comprehensive Abortion Care guidelines ke mutabik India mein lagbhag 8% maternal deaths unsafe abortions ki wajah se hoti hain; yeh guidelines 2001-03 ke Registrar General ke cause-of-death data par based hain.

facts.caveat: The 8% cause breakdown comes from Registrar General verbal-autopsy data for 2001-03, more than 20 years old; deaths from abortion are often misclassified and under-reported because of stigma.

text.en: Unsafe abortion is the third leading cause of maternal deaths in India, close to eight women die every day from causes related to it, and young women aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from abortion complications, according to UNFPA India (2022).
text.hg: UNFPA India (2022) ke mutabik India mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah unsafe abortion hai, isse jude kaaranon se har din kareeb aath auraton ki maut hoti hai, aur abortion complications se marne ka sabse zyada risk 15-19 saal ki young auraton ko hota hai.

facts.caveat: An estimate, not a death count. UNFPA's source is the preface of a 2018 Guttmacher Institute report; the Health Ministry's 2015 guidance handbook gives the same rank and the 8% share (Registrar General data for 2001-03) but put the toll at close to 10 women a day. The finding on 15-19-year-olds comes from a study of nine Annual Health Survey states (2007-2011). The Supreme Court repeated the 'third leading cause' and 'eight women a day' figures in X v. Principal Secretary (29 September 2022).

text.en: In nine poorer states covered by India's Annual Health Survey (Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand), 67% of abortions reported for 2007-2011 were classified as unsafe, ranging from 45.1% in Assam to 78.3% in Chhattisgarh, according to a 2019 BMJ Global Health study of 1.8 million pregnant women.
text.hg: In nine poorer states covered by India's Annual Health Survey (Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand), 67% of abortions reported for 2007-2011 were classified as unsafe, ranging from 45.1% in Assam to 78.3% in Chhattisgarh, according to a 2019 BMJ Global Health study of 1.8 million pregnant women.

facts.caveat: 'Unsafe' meant not done or completed in a health facility, not by a skilled birth attendant, or at 20 weeks or later; the count combines induced and spontaneous abortions. The nine states held about half of India's population. UNFPA India (2022) and the Supreme Court (2022) cite the 67% as if it covered all of India. Data predate the spread of medication abortion and the 2021 law changes.

text.en: India's maternal mortality ratio was 88 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in 2021-23 (95% CI 79-96), down from 130 in 2014-16 but unchanged from 2020-22 and still above the SDG target of below 70; a woman's lifetime risk of maternal death was 0.18%.
text.hg: 2021-23 mein India ka maternal mortality ratio (MMR) har 100,000 live births par 88 maternal deaths tha (95% CI: 79-96). Yeh 2014-16 ke 130 se kam hai, lekin 2020-22 jitna hi raha aur ab bhi 70 se neeche ke SDG target se upar hai; ek aurat ke poore jeevan mein maternal death ka risk 0.18% tha.

facts.caveat: Series: 130 (2014-16), 122, 113, 103, 97, 93 (2019-21), 88 (2020-22), 88 (2021-23). SRS pools three years. A newer bulletin (May 2026) puts 2022-24 at 87 (see abr-mmr-2022-24). A 0.18% lifetime risk is about 1 in 550 women (derived).

text.en: In 2021-23, Odisha had the highest maternal mortality ratio among India's major states at 153 per 100,000 live births, followed by Chhattisgarh (146), Madhya Pradesh (142) and Uttar Pradesh (141), while Kerala and Andhra Pradesh had the lowest at 30; the lifetime risk of maternal death was 0.41% in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
text.hg: In 2021-23, Odisha had the highest maternal mortality ratio among India's major states at 153 per 100,000 live births, followed by Chhattisgarh (146), Madhya Pradesh (142) and Uttar Pradesh (141), while Kerala and Andhra Pradesh had the lowest at 30; the lifetime risk of maternal death was 0.41% in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.

facts.caveat: The bulletin gives separate estimates only for major states; smaller states are pooled. State estimates have wide confidence intervals (e.g. Chhattisgarh 63-229). In the 2022-24 bulletin Uttar Pradesh (154) became the highest and Odisha fell to 124 (see abr-mmr-states-2022-24).

text.en: On 29 September 2022 the Supreme Court of India held, in X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, that excluding unmarried or single women from abortion between 20 and 24 weeks would violate Article 14 of the Constitution, giving them the same access as married women.
text.hg: 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court of India ne X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department case mein faisla diya ki unmarried ya single auraton ko 20 se 24 hafte ke beech abortion se bahar rakhna Constitution ke Article 14 ka ullanghan hoga, aur is tarah unhe shaadishuda auraton jitna hi access diya.

facts.caveat: Bench: Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, A.S. Bopanna and J.B. Pardiwala; Civil Appeal No. 5802 of 2022.

text.en: In its 29 September 2022 judgment the Supreme Court held that "rape" in the MTP Act and Rules includes marital rape, so a married woman pregnant from forced sex by her husband can seek abortion up to 24 weeks as a survivor of rape, without filing an FIR or proving the rape in court.
text.hg: 29 September 2022 ke apne judgment mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki MTP Act aur Rules mein "rape" mein marital rape bhi shaamil hai, isliye pati ke zabardasti kiye gaye sex se pregnant hui shaadishuda aurat rape survivor ke taur par 24 hafte tak abortion maang sakti hai, bina FIR file kiye ya court mein rape saabit kiye.

facts.value: Marital rape recognised for MTP purposes
facts.caveat: Applies only to the MTP Act; the Court left the marital rape exception in criminal law (then Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC) to another bench.

text.en: The Supreme Court ruled in September 2022 that a doctor terminating a minor's pregnancy, who must report it to police under Section 19(1) of the POCSO Act, need not disclose the minor's identity or personal details in that report if the minor and her guardian ask.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne September 2022 mein faisla diya ki kisi minor ki pregnancy terminate karne wale doctor ko, jise POCSO Act ki Section 19(1) ke tahat police ko report karna hota hai, us report mein minor ki identity ya personal details batane ki zaroorat nahi hai, agar minor aur uske guardian aisa kahen.

facts.value: Identity can be withheld from POCSO report on request
facts.caveat: Mandatory reporting itself remains; failing to report is an offence under Section 21 of POCSO. The doctor is also exempt from disclosing the minor's identity in any criminal proceedings that follow.

text.en: The Supreme Court observed in 2022 that because of POCSO's mandatory reporting rule, a pregnant minor and her guardian face a choice between approaching a registered doctor and risking criminal proceedings, or going to an unqualified provider.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki POCSO ke mandatory reporting rule ki wajah se pregnant minor aur uske guardian ke saamne yeh choice hoti hai: ya to registered doctor ke paas jaa kar criminal proceedings ka risk uthayein, ya kisi unqualified provider ke paas jaayein.

facts.value: Mandatory reporting pushes minors to unqualified providers
facts.caveat: Under POCSO any sexual activity with a person under 18 is an offence even if consensual, so every pregnancy in a minor triggers mandatory reporting.

text.en: On 21 July 2022 the Supreme Court modified a Delhi High Court order and allowed an unmarried woman, more than 22 weeks pregnant, to end her pregnancy if a Medical Board at AIIMS Delhi found it safe.
text.hg: 21 July 2022 ko Supreme Court ne Delhi High Court ke ek order ko modify karke 22 hafte se zyada ki pregnant ek unmarried aurat ko pregnancy khatam karne ki ijazat di, agar AIIMS Delhi ka Medical Board ise safe paaye.

facts.caveat: The Delhi High Court had refused interim relief on 15 July 2022, saying it "cannot go beyond the Statute". The woman was about 22 weeks pregnant when she petitioned the High Court, and AIIMS later reported that the termination was carried out safely.

text.en: The Supreme Court's 2022 abortion judgment relied on Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), which recognised a woman's reproductive autonomy, and the nine-judge privacy ruling in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), which tied the statutory right to abortion to the right to make reproductive choices under Article 21.
text.hg: Supreme Court ka 2022 ka abortion judgment Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009) par tika tha, jisne aurat ki reproductive autonomy ko maana tha, aur K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) mein nau judges ke privacy faisle par bhi, jisne abortion ke statutory right ko Article 21 ke tahat reproductive choices karne ke right se joda.

facts.caveat: The 2009 Suchita Srivastava case concerned a woman with an intellectual disability, whose name the Court withheld, who became pregnant after an alleged rape while living in a government-run welfare institution; Suchita Srivastava was one of the appellants, not the woman. Do not add identifying details.

text.en: India's Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act (Act No. 57 of 1994), dated 20 September 1994 and now titled the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, bans sex selection before or after conception and the misuse of prenatal tests to determine the sex of a foetus.
text.hg: India ka Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act (Act No. 57 of 1994), jo 20 September 1994 ka hai aur jiska naam ab Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act (PCPNDT Act) hai, conception se pehle ya baad mein sex selection par, aur foetus ka sex jaanne ke liye prenatal tests ke misuse par rok lagata hai.

facts.caveat: In force since 1 January 1996; the 2003 amendment (Act 14 of 2003, in force from 14 February 2003) renamed it and added pre-conception sex selection (see abr-pcpndt-commencement-amendment). Text read from a consolidated PDF hosted by the Delhi government and checked against the Health Ministry's compilation. The Act also bans advertising sex-determination services, including online (Section 22: up to 3 years and Rs 10,000 fine).

text.en: Under Section 5(2) of the PCPNDT Act, no one, including the person conducting a prenatal test, may tell a pregnant woman, her relatives or anyone else the sex of the foetus "by words, signs or in any other manner".
text.hg: PCPNDT Act ki Section 5(2) ke tahat koi bhi, prenatal test karne wala vyakti bhi, pregnant aurat, uske rishtedaaron ya kisi aur ko foetus ka sex "by words, signs or in any other manner" nahi bata sakta.

facts.caveat: Wording as amended in 2003; the original 1994 text barred only the person conducting the procedure from telling the woman or her relatives.

text.en: Under Section 23 of the PCPNDT Act, a doctor or clinic owner who breaks the law faces up to three years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 10,000, rising to five years and Rs 50,000 for a repeat offence, and on conviction loses medical registration for five years (permanently for a second offence).
text.hg: PCPNDT Act ki Section 23 ke tahat kanoon todne wale doctor ya clinic owner ko teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai, jo repeat offence par paanch saal aur Rs 50,000 tak ho jaata hai, aur conviction par uska medical registration paanch saal ke liye chhin jaata hai (doosre offence par hamesha ke liye).

facts.value: Up to 3 years + Rs 10,000; repeat 5 years + Rs 50,000
facts.caveat: Registration is also to be suspended once a court frames charges, until the case is decided.

text.en: Anyone who seeks sex selection under the PCPNDT Act faces up to three years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 50,000, rising to five years and Rs 1 lakh for a repeat offence, but the law presumes that a pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives and does not punish a woman who was forced.
text.hg: PCPNDT Act ke tahat sex selection maangne wale kisi bhi vyakti ko teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 50,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai, jo repeat offence par paanch saal aur Rs 1 lakh tak ho jaata hai, lekin kanoon yeh maan kar chalta hai ki pregnant aurat ko uske pati ya rishtedaaron ne majboor kiya tha, aur majboor ki gayi aurat ko saza nahi deta.

facts.value: Up to 3 years + Rs 50,000; repeat 5 years + Rs 1 lakh
facts.caveat: Under Section 24 the husband or relative is liable for abetment.

text.en: Every offence under the PCPNDT Act is cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable, yet a court can take up a case only on a complaint by the Appropriate Authority, an authorised officer, or a person or social organisation that has given the authority at least 15 days' notice.
text.hg: PCPNDT Act ke tahat har offence cognisable, non-bailable aur non-compoundable hai, phir bhi court kisi case ko sirf tab utha sakti hai jab complaint Appropriate Authority, kisi authorised officer, ya aise vyakti ya social organisation ne ki ho jisne authority ko kam se kam 15 din ka notice diya ho.

facts.caveat: Enforcement therefore depends on district Appropriate Authorities (health officials) filing complaints. The 2003 amendment cut the notice period for private complainants from 30 to 15 days.

text.en: India's sex ratio at birth was 917 girls per 1,000 boys in 2021-23 according to the Sample Registration System (914 rural, 925 urban), having crept up from 904 in 2017-19 through 907, 913 and 914.
text.hg: Sample Registration System (SRS) ke mutabik 2021-23 mein India ka sex ratio at birth har 1,000 ladkon par 917 ladkiyan tha (rural 914, urban 925); yeh 2017-19 ke 904 se dheere-dheere badh kar 907, 913 aur 914 hote hue yahan tak pahuncha.

facts.caveat: The natural ratio is about 950 girls per 1,000 boys (105 boys per 100 girls, per Pew Research Center). SRS figures are three-year averages. The SRS Statistical Report 2024 (May 2026) puts 2022-24 at 918 (see abr-srb-srs-2022-24).

text.en: In 2021-23, Uttarakhand had India's lowest sex ratio at birth among bigger states at 868 girls per 1,000 boys, followed by Delhi (872), Haryana (884), Maharashtra (894) and Bihar (897); Chhattisgarh (974) and Kerala (971) had the highest.
text.hg: 2021-23 mein India ke bade states mein sabse kam sex ratio at birth Uttarakhand mein tha, har 1,000 ladkon par 868 ladkiyan; uske baad Delhi (872), Haryana (884), Maharashtra (894) aur Bihar (897) the, jabki sabse zyada Chhattisgarh (974) aur Kerala (971) mein tha.

facts.caveat: State SRS estimates rest on smaller samples than the national figure. In 2022-24 Uttarakhand (872) was again lowest and Chhattisgarh (978) highest.

text.en: India's sex ratio at birth was reported as 918 girls per 1,000 boys in the SRS Statistical Report 2024 (period 2022-24), with Chhattisgarh highest (978) and Uttarakhand lowest (872).
text.hg: India's sex ratio at birth was reported as 918 girls per 1,000 boys in the SRS Statistical Report 2024 (period 2022-24), with Chhattisgarh highest (978) and Uttarakhand lowest (872).

facts.caveat: Three-year average. Among bigger states Delhi (876) and Haryana (885) were the next lowest after Uttarakhand.

text.en: India's sex ratio at birth for children born in the five years before NFHS-5 (2019-21) was 929 girls per 1,000 boys, up from 919 in NFHS-4 (2015-16).
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) se pehle ke paanch saalon mein paida hue bachchon mein India ka sex ratio at birth har 1,000 ladkon par 929 ladkiyan tha, jo NFHS-4 (2015-16) ke 919 se zyada hai.

facts.caveat: Survey estimate with sampling error; SRS (917 for 2021-23) is the official annual series. Do not mix the two.

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), the sex ratio at birth among larger states was lowest in Himachal Pradesh (875), Tamil Nadu (878), Rajasthan (891) and Haryana (893), but the survey put Uttarakhand at 984 while SRS put it at 868 for 2021-23.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein bade states mein sex ratio at birth sabse kam Himachal Pradesh (875), Tamil Nadu (878), Rajasthan (891) aur Haryana (893) mein tha, lekin is survey ne Uttarakhand ko 984 par rakha, jabki SRS ne 2021-23 ke liye ise 868 bataya.

facts.caveat: State-level survey SRBs swing widely between rounds (Kerala 1047 to 951; Tamil Nadu 954 to 878) because of small samples; treat single-state figures with caution.

text.en: NFHS-5 (2019-21) estimated India's overall population sex ratio at 1,020 females per 1,000 males, even as its sex ratio at birth stayed skewed at 929.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) ne India ki overall population ka sex ratio har 1,000 males par 1,020 females aanka, jabki sex ratio at birth 929 par skewed bana raha.

facts.caveat: A household survey estimate, not a census count; it does not mean sex selection has ended.

text.en: India accounted for 45.8 million of the world's estimated 142.6 million "missing" females in 2020, second only to China (72.3 million), according to UNFPA's State of World Population 2020.
text.hg: UNFPA ki State of World Population 2020 report ke mutabik 2020 mein duniya ki andaazan 142.6 million "missing" females mein se 45.8 million India ki thin; is maamle mein India sirf China (72.3 million) ke baad doosre number par tha.

facts.caveat: Cumulative stock over about 50 years, combining sex-selective abortion and excess deaths of girls after birth. The same table puts India's annual excess female deaths at 0.36 million (2015-2020).

text.en: About 460,000 girls in India went "missing" at birth every year between 2013 and 2017; gender-biased sex selection accounts for about two thirds of India's missing girls and post-birth female mortality for about one third, UNFPA reported in 2020.
text.hg: UNFPA ne 2020 mein report kiya ki 2013 se 2017 ke beech India mein har saal lagbhag 460,000 ladkiyan janm ke samay "missing" huin; India ki missing ladkiyon mein se lagbhag do-tihaai ke peeche gender-biased sex selection hai aur lagbhag ek-tihaai ke peeche janm ke baad ladkiyon ki maut.

facts.caveat: Model-based estimate; UNFPA's Table 3.5 gives 0.59 million annual missing female births for 2015-2020, so figures vary with period and method.

text.en: China and India together account for about 90-95% of the estimated 1.2 million to 1.5 million female births "missing" every year worldwide because of gender-biased sex selection.
text.hg: Gender-biased sex selection ki wajah se duniya bhar mein har saal andaazan 1.2 million se 1.5 million female births "missing" hote hain, aur inmein se lagbhag 90-95% China aur India mein milkar hote hain.

text.en: At least 9.0 million female births went "missing" in India between 2000 and 2019 because of female-selective abortions, and the annual number fell from about 480,000 in 2010 to 410,000 in 2019, according to a 2022 Pew Research Center analysis.
text.hg: Pew Research Center ke 2022 ke ek analysis ke mutabik 2000 se 2019 ke beech India mein female-selective abortions (ladki hone ki wajah se karaye gaye abortions) ke kaaran kam se kam 9.0 million female births "missing" hue, aur saalana sankhya 2010 mein lagbhag 480,000 se ghat kar 2019 mein 410,000 reh gayi.

facts.caveat: Pew notes its estimate is smaller than some other scholars' because NFHS data produce less skewed ratios than SRS.

text.en: India's sex ratio at birth narrowed from about 111 boys per 100 girls in the 2011 census to about 109 in NFHS-4 (2015-16) and 108 in NFHS-5 (2019-21), against a natural level of about 105.
text.hg: India ka sex ratio at birth 2011 census mein har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 111 ladkon se ghat kar NFHS-4 (2015-16) mein lagbhag 109 aur NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 108 par aa gaya, jabki iska natural level lagbhag 105 hota hai.

text.en: Among Sikhs, India's sex ratio at birth fell from 130 boys per 100 girls in the 2001 census to 121 in 2011 and about 110 in NFHS-5 (2019-21), the sharpest decline in son bias among major religious groups.
text.hg: Sikhs mein India ka sex ratio at birth 2001 census mein har 100 ladkiyon par 130 ladkon se ghat kar 2011 mein 121 aur NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein lagbhag 110 reh gaya; bade dharmik groups mein son bias mein yeh sabse tez giraavat hai.

facts.caveat: The NFHS-5 Sikh estimate has a margin of error of plus or minus 8 per 100. Present as a story of change, not as blame on a community.

text.en: 66.7% of currently married women aged 15-49 in India were using a contraceptive method in NFHS-5 (2019-21), and 56.4% were using a modern method, up from 48% for modern methods in 2015-16.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India mein 15-49 saal ki 66.7% currently married auratein koi contraceptive method use kar rahi thin, aur 56.4% modern method, jo 2015-16 mein modern methods ke 48% se zyada hai.

facts.caveat: Value from Table 5.5 of the NFHS-5 India Report; summary documents may round differently.

text.en: Female sterilisation was used by 37.9% of currently married women in India in NFHS-5 (2019-21), about two thirds of all modern contraceptive use, while male sterilisation was used by just 0.3%.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India ki 37.9% currently married auraton ne female sterilisation (nasbandi) apnaya tha, jo modern contraceptive use ka lagbhag do-tihaai hai, jabki male sterilisation sirf 0.3% ne use kiya.

facts.caveat: Share of modern use (37.9/56.4 = 67%) and the ratio of female to male sterilisation (over 100 to 1) are derived.

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 9.5% of currently married women in India reported condom use, 5.1% the pill, 2.1% an IUD and 0.6% injectables, while 10.3% relied on traditional methods.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India ki currently married auraton mein se 9.5% ne condom, 5.1% ne pill, 2.1% ne IUD aur 0.6% ne injectables use karne ki baat batayi, jabki 10.3% traditional methods par nirbhar thin.

text.en: 9.4% of currently married women in India had an unmet need for family planning in NFHS-5 (2019-21), 4.0% for spacing births and 5.4% for limiting them, down from 13% in 2015-16.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India ki 9.4% currently married auraton ki family planning ki zaroorat poori nahi ho rahi thi (unmet need): 4.0% ki bachchon ke beech gap rakhne ke liye aur 5.4% ki bachche limit karne ke liye; yeh 2015-16 ke 13% se kam hai.

text.en: Among currently married women aged 15-19 in India, only 28.1% used any contraceptive method and 17.8% had an unmet need for family planning in NFHS-5 (2019-21), nearly double the national unmet need.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India mein 15-19 saal ki currently married auraton mein se sirf 28.1% koi contraceptive method use kar rahi thin aur 17.8% ki family planning ki unmet need thi, jo national unmet need ka lagbhag double hai.

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 35.1% of Indian men aged 15-49 agreed that "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it", and 19.6% agreed that women who use contraception may become promiscuous.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ke 35.1% Indian mardon ne maana ki "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it", aur 19.6% ne maana ki contraception use karne wali auratein promiscuous (kai logon se sexual relations rakhne wali) ho sakti hain.

facts.caveat: Punjab (77.3%) and Chandigarh (69.1%) had the highest shares agreeing with the first statement.

text.en: 6.8% of women aged 15-19 in India had begun childbearing in NFHS-5 (2019-21), rising to 20.0% by age 19, 17.6% among girls with no schooling and 10.0% in the poorest households, against 2.2% in the richest.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India mein 15-19 saal ki 6.8% auratein bachche paida karna shuru kar chuki thin; 19 saal ki umar tak yeh 20.0% tha, bina schooling wali ladkiyon mein 17.6% aur sabse gareeb gharon mein 10.0%, jabki sabse ameer gharon mein 2.2%.

facts.caveat: 4.5% had given birth and 2.3% were pregnant with their first child. UNFPA India's 2022 note cites 7.9%, which matches the older NFHS-4 level of about 8%; use 6.8% for NFHS-5.

text.en: Teenage childbearing in NFHS-5 (2019-21) was highest in Tripura, where 21.9% of women aged 15-19 had begun childbearing, followed by West Bengal (16.4%), Andhra Pradesh (12.6%), Assam (11.7%) and Bihar (11.0%).
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein teenage childbearing sabse zyada Tripura mein tha, jahan 15-19 saal ki 21.9% auratein bachche paida karna shuru kar chuki thin; uske baad West Bengal (16.4%), Andhra Pradesh (12.6%), Assam (11.7%) aur Bihar (11.0%) the.

text.en: Around 73 million induced abortions take place worldwide each year, and 61% of unintended pregnancies and 29% of all pregnancies end in induced abortion, according to the WHO.
text.hg: WHO ke mutabik duniya bhar mein har saal lagbhag 73 million induced abortions hote hain, aur 61% unintended pregnancies aur saari pregnancies mein se 29% ka ant induced abortion mein hota hai.

facts.caveat: Based on Bearak et al., Lancet Global Health 2020 (model for 1990-2019); WHO fact sheet dated 8 December 2025.

text.en: About 45% of all induced abortions worldwide are unsafe, one third of these are performed in the least safe conditions by untrained people using dangerous methods, and more than half of all unsafe abortions occur in Asia, mostly in south and central Asia, according to the WHO.
text.hg: WHO ke mutabik duniya bhar mein saare induced abortions mein se lagbhag 45% unsafe hote hain; inmein se ek-tihaai sabse kam safe halaat mein untrained logon dwara khatarnaak tareekon se kiye jaate hain, aur saare unsafe abortions mein se aadhe se zyada Asia mein hote hain, zyaadatar South aur Central Asia mein.

text.en: About 8% of maternal deaths worldwide in 2009-2020 were linked to abortion; deaths from safe abortion are negligible at under 1 per 100,000 abortions, but exceed 200 per 100,000 where unsafe abortion is common, the WHO says.
text.hg: WHO ke mutabik 2009-2020 mein duniya bhar mein lagbhag 8% maternal deaths abortion se judi thin; safe abortion se maut na ke barabar hai, har 100,000 abortions par 1 se bhi kam, lekin jahan unsafe abortion aam hai wahan yeh har 100,000 par 200 se zyada hai.

facts.value: 8% of maternal deaths; >200 deaths per 100,000 unsafe abortions
facts.caveat: Cites a WHO systematic analysis (Cresswell et al., Lancet Global Health, 2025). WHO also notes that in developing countries about 7 million women a year (2012) were treated in hospital for unsafe-abortion complications.

text.en: India's maternal mortality ratio was 87 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in 2022-24 (95% CI 78-95), one point below the 88 recorded for both 2020-22 and 2021-23 and still above the SDG target of below 70; a woman's lifetime risk of maternal death was 0.18%, according to the Registrar General's special bulletin of May 2026.
text.hg: India's maternal mortality ratio was 87 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in 2022-24 (95% CI 78-95), one point below the 88 recorded for both 2020-22 and 2021-23 and still above the SDG target of below 70; a woman's lifetime risk of maternal death was 0.18%, according to the Registrar General's special bulletin of May 2026.

facts.caveat: The 95% confidence intervals for 2021-23 (79-96) and 2022-24 (78-95) almost coincide, so the one-point fall is within the margin of error; the ratio has been flat at 88, 88 and 87 over the last three rounds. SRS pools three years of data.

text.en: In 2022-24, Uttar Pradesh had the highest maternal mortality ratio among India's major states at 154 per 100,000 live births, followed by Madhya Pradesh (135), Chhattisgarh (124) and Odisha (124), while Kerala (24) and Tamil Nadu (25) had the lowest; a woman's lifetime risk of maternal death was 0.44% in Uttar Pradesh.
text.hg: In 2022-24, Uttar Pradesh had the highest maternal mortality ratio among India's major states at 154 per 100,000 live births, followed by Madhya Pradesh (135), Chhattisgarh (124) and Odisha (124), while Kerala (24) and Tamil Nadu (25) had the lowest; a woman's lifetime risk of maternal death was 0.44% in Uttar Pradesh.

facts.caveat: The bulletin gives separate estimates only for major states. State estimates have very wide confidence intervals (Chhattisgarh 48-199; Kerala 0-50), so year-to-year rank changes should not be over-read.

text.en: India's Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1994 came into operation on 1 January 1996; an amending Act (No. 14 of 2003, assented to on 17 January 2003 and in force from 14 February 2003) renamed it the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act and extended it to sex selection before conception.
text.hg: India's Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Act, 1994 came into operation on 1 January 1996; an amending Act (No. 14 of 2003, assented to on 17 January 2003 and in force from 14 February 2003) renamed it the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act and extended it to sex selection before conception.

facts.value: In force 1 January 1996; amended and renamed from 14 February 2003
facts.caveat: The amending law is formally titled the Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Regulation and Prevention of Misuse) Amendment Act, 2002, although it is Act No. 14 of 2003. The Health Ministry's note links the amendment to a 2000 Supreme Court petition by CEHAT and others on slow implementation.

text.en: Police in India registered only 31 cases under the PC-PNDT Act in 2024, after 57 in 2022 and 30 in 2023, and 15 cases under the MTP Act in 2024 (32 in 2022 and 30 in 2023), according to the National Crime Records Bureau.
text.hg: Police in India registered only 31 cases under the PC-PNDT Act in 2024, after 57 in 2022 and 30 in 2023, and 15 cases under the MTP Act in 2024 (32 in 2022 and 30 in 2023), according to the National Crime Records Bureau.

facts.caveat: NCRB counts police FIRs. Under Section 28 of the PC-PNDT Act courts act only on complaints by Appropriate Authorities or notified persons, so most PC-PNDT prosecutions start as court complaints that these figures do not capture. NCRB still uses the Act's pre-2003 name.

text.en: Police in India registered 140 foeticide cases in 2024 (59 under the IPC and 81 under Section 91 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita), up from 102 in 2022 and 88 in 2023, and 299 cases of offences of miscarriage in 2024, according to the National Crime Records Bureau.
text.hg: Police in India registered 140 foeticide cases in 2024 (59 under the IPC and 81 under Section 91 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita), up from 102 in 2022 and 88 in 2023, and 299 cases of offences of miscarriage in 2024, according to the National Crime Records Bureau.

facts.caveat: NCRB's 'foeticide' head counts FIRs under Section 91 BNS / Section 315 IPC (an act meant to prevent a child being born alive or to cause its death after birth); it is not a count of sex-selective abortions, which fall under the PC-PNDT Act. NCRB's crime-head key defines 'offences of miscarriage' as Sections 89-90 BNS / 313-314 IPC: miscarriage caused without the woman's consent, and death caused by an act meant to cause miscarriage.

text.en: Of 238 foeticide cases before Indian courts in 2024, trials were completed in only four, and none ended in a conviction (two acquittals, two discharges); 233 cases (97.9%) were still pending at the end of the year, according to the National Crime Records Bureau.
text.hg: Of 238 foeticide cases before Indian courts in 2024, trials were completed in only four, and none ended in a conviction (two acquittals, two discharges); 233 cases (97.9%) were still pending at the end of the year, according to the National Crime Records Bureau.

facts.caveat: Foeticide here means Section 91 BNS / Section 315 IPC; NCRB files it under crimes against children. One more case was disposed of without trial.

text.en: Causing a miscarriage outside the MTP Act is still a crime in India: Section 88 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, in force since 1 July 2024, punishes anyone who voluntarily causes a woman to miscarry, other than in good faith to save her life, with up to three years in prison (up to seven if she is "quick with child"), and expressly covers a woman who causes her own miscarriage; without her consent the punishment rises to up to ten years or life (Section 89).
text.hg: Causing a miscarriage outside the MTP Act is still a crime in India: Section 88 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, in force since 1 July 2024, punishes anyone who voluntarily causes a woman to miscarry, other than in good faith to save her life, with up to three years in prison (up to seven if she is "quick with child"), and expressly covers a woman who causes her own miscarriage; without her consent the punishment rises to up to ten years or life (Section 89).

facts.value: Up to 3 years (7 if quick with child); without consent up to 10 years or life
facts.caveat: Section 88 repeats Section 312 of the Indian Penal Code word for word. The MTP Act (Section 3(1)) protects only registered medical practitioners who end a pregnancy within its conditions. Sections 90-92 BNS cover death caused by an act meant to cause miscarriage, acts to prevent a child being born alive, and causing the death of a quick unborn child.

text.en: Mifepristone (in 2002) and misoprostol (in 2006) were approved in India for ending a pregnancy of up to seven weeks (49 days), and in December 2008 the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation approved a mifepristone-misoprostol combipack for use up to nine weeks (63 days), according to the Health Ministry's 2018 abortion care guidelines.
text.hg: Mifepristone (in 2002) and misoprostol (in 2006) were approved in India for ending a pregnancy of up to seven weeks (49 days), and in December 2008 the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation approved a mifepristone-misoprostol combipack for use up to nine weeks (63 days), according to the Health Ministry's 2018 abortion care guidelines.

facts.caveat: The 2023 guidelines keep the nine-week limit for medical methods (see abr-mma-nine-weeks).

text.en: Police in India registered 1,87,702 cases of crimes against children in 2024, up 5.9% from 1,77,335 in 2023 and 1,62,449 in 2022; the rate rose to 42.3 cases per lakh children from 39.9 in 2023, according to NCRB's Crime in India 2024.
text.hg: NCRB ki report 'Crime in India 2024' ke mutabik, 2024 mein India mein police ne bachchon ke khilaf crime ke 1,87,702 cases register kiye. Yeh 2023 ke 1,77,335 cases se 5.9% zyada hai; 2022 mein 1,62,449 cases register hue the. Har lakh bachchon par cases ka rate 2023 ke 39.9 se badhkar 42.3 ho gaya.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only. NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (Principal Offence Rule). A rise can reflect better reporting and registration, not only more crime. IPC was replaced by BNS from 1 July 2024, so 2024 mixes both codes. The rate uses the 2011 Census child population (4,441.5 lakh).

text.en: Police in India registered 69,191 cases under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in 2024, involving 70,132 child victims (15.6 cases per lakh children); POCSO made up 36.9% of all crimes against children, second only to kidnapping and abduction (40.0%).
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act ke tahat 69,191 cases register kiye, jinme 70,132 child victims the (har lakh bachchon par 15.6 cases). Bachchon ke khilaf saare crimes mein 36.9% cases POCSO ke the; is hisaab se POCSO sirf kidnapping aur abduction (40.0%) se peeche tha.

facts.value: 69191 cases; 70132 victims; 15.6 per lakh children; 36.9% of crimes against children
facts.caveat: Child sexual abuse is heavily under-reported; these are FIRs registered under POCSO as the principal offence. Rate uses the 2011 Census child population.

text.en: Of the 69,191 POCSO cases registered in India in 2024, 44,126 were for penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault (Sections 4 and 6), with 44,567 victims: 43,675 girls and 892 boys.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein register hue POCSO ke 69,191 cases mein se 44,126 cases penetrative ya aggravated penetrative sexual assault (Sections 4 aur 6) ke the, jinme 44,567 victims the: 43,675 ladkiyan aur 892 ladke.

facts.caveat: Boys are far less likely to be reported as victims; the 2% share of boys reflects reporting, not the true distribution of abuse.

text.en: In 96.6% of POCSO penetrative sexual assault cases registered in India in 2024 (42,634 of 44,126), the offender was someone the child knew.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein POCSO ke tahat register hue penetrative sexual assault ke 96.6% cases mein (44,126 mein se 42,634) offender koi aisa insaan tha jise bachcha jaanta tha.

facts.caveat: Covers only Sections 4 and 6 (penetrative assault), not all POCSO cases. A large part of the 'known' group is friends or partners, which includes consensual adolescent relationships prosecuted under POCSO.

text.en: In 2024, among 44,126 POCSO penetrative assault cases in India, the offender was a family member in 3,658 cases (8.3%), a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in 16,668 (37.8%), a friend, online friend or live-in partner 'on pretext of marriage' in 22,308 (50.6%), and unknown or unidentified in only 1,492 (3.4%).
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein POCSO ke tahat penetrative assault ke 44,126 cases mein se 3,658 cases (8.3%) mein offender family member tha, 16,668 (37.8%) mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala, 22,308 (50.6%) mein 'shaadi ke bahane' wala friend, online friend ya live-in partner, aur sirf 1,492 (3.4%) mein koi anjaan ya unidentified insaan.

facts.value: Family 3658; family friends/neighbours/employers 16668; friends/online friends/partners 22308; unknown 1492
facts.caveat: Percentages calculated from the NCRB table. The 'friends/partners' category mixes grooming by online contacts with romantic relationships between adolescents, which POCSO criminalises below 18.

text.en: Of 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault recorded under POCSO in India in 2024, 831 were under 6 years old and 3,438 were aged 6-12 (4,269 under 12 in all), 16,801 were 12-16 and 23,497 (52.7%) were 16-18.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein POCSO ke tahat record hue penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims mein se 831 ki umar 6 saal se kam thi aur 3,438 ki 6-12 saal (yaani kul 4,269 bachche 12 saal se kam umar ke the), 16,801 ki umar 12-16 saal thi aur 23,497 (52.7%) ki 16-18 saal.

facts.caveat: Section 4 and 6 victims only. Young children rarely disclose, so the under-12 counts are minimums. The concentration at 16-18 may partly reflect cases arising from adolescent relationships and elopements, which NCRB does not count separately.

text.en: Maharashtra registered the most POCSO cases in India in 2024 (9,432), followed by Uttar Pradesh (8,087), Tamil Nadu (6,969), Madhya Pradesh (5,861), Kerala (4,513) and Karnataka (4,118).
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein POCSO ke sabse zyada cases Maharashtra mein register hue (9,432), uske baad Uttar Pradesh (8,087), Tamil Nadu (6,969), Madhya Pradesh (5,861), Kerala (4,513) aur Karnataka (4,118) ka number tha.

facts.value: Maharashtra 9432; UP 8087; TN 6969; MP 5861; Kerala 4513; Karnataka 4118
facts.caveat: NCRB warns that states may not be compared purely on crime figures; high counts can reflect better registration. By rate, Kerala (48.0 per lakh children) far exceeds Uttar Pradesh (9.5).

text.en: Police filed chargesheets in 95.3% of the POCSO cases they disposed of in 2024, but 21,256 POCSO cases were still pending investigation at the end of the year, 23.7% of the 89,658 cases police had to investigate.
text.hg: Police filed chargesheets in 95.3% of the POCSO cases they disposed of in 2024, but 21,256 POCSO cases were still pending investigation at the end of the year, 23.7% of the 89,658 cases police had to investigate.

facts.caveat: Chargesheeting rate is chargesheets divided by cases disposed of by police; it does not indicate strength of evidence.

text.en: Courts in India convicted the accused in only 32.3% of POCSO cases whose trials ended in 2024: 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals and 1,101 discharges.
text.hg: 2024 mein India ki courts mein POCSO ke jin cases ka trial khatam hua, unme se sirf 32.3% mein accused ko saza hui: 12,672 convictions, jabki 25,476 acquittals aur 1,101 discharges.

facts.caveat: Conviction rate = convictions / trials completed. Acquittals often follow victims or families turning hostile, compromises, age-proof disputes and consensual adolescent cases.

text.en: At the end of 2024, 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial in Indian courts, 87.7% of all POCSO cases that were before the courts that year.
text.hg: 2024 ke end mein India ki courts mein POCSO ke 2,86,903 cases ka trial pending tha, jo us saal courts ke saamne rahe POCSO ke saare cases ka 87.7% hai.

facts.caveat: Pending cases grew from 2,62,089 at end-2023 to 2,86,903 at end-2024. Section 35 of the POCSO Act asks Special Courts to complete trials, as far as possible, within one year of taking cognizance (see ch-pocso-section35-timelines).

text.en: For penetrative sexual assault on children (POCSO Sections 4 and 6), the conviction rate in 2024 was 30.2%, and 1,70,455 such cases were pending trial at the end of the year.
text.hg: Bachchon par penetrative sexual assault (POCSO Sections 4 aur 6) ke cases mein 2024 mein conviction rate 30.2% tha, aur saal ke end mein aise 1,70,455 cases ka trial pending tha.

facts.caveat: Covers Sections 4 and 6 only.

text.en: Across all crimes against children, India's conviction rate was 33.9% in 2024, and 6,44,887 cases were pending trial at the end of the year (pendency 91.1%).
text.hg: 2024 mein bachchon ke khilaf saare crimes ko milakar India ka conviction rate 33.9% tha, aur saal ke end mein 6,44,887 cases ka trial pending tha (pendency 91.1%).

facts.caveat: Includes kidnapping, POCSO and all other child-related heads.

text.en: Cases registered under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act in India rose from 1,002 in 2022 to 6,038 in 2023, then fell to 1,499 in 2024.
text.hg: India mein Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke tahat register hue cases 2022 ke 1,002 se badhkar 2023 mein 6,038 ho gaye, phir 2024 mein ghatkar 1,499 reh gaye.

facts.caveat: FIRs are a tiny fraction of child marriages (NFHS-5 finds about 1 in 4 young women married before 18). Spikes track state police drives, not prevalence. Where the bride is a minor and the marriage is consummated, a POCSO charge may be the principal offence instead.

text.en: Assam (471 cases) and Tamil Nadu (408) registered the most Prohibition of Child Marriage Act cases in India in 2024, out of 1,499 cases with 1,511 victims nationwide.
text.hg: 2024 mein Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke sabse zyada cases Assam (471 cases) aur Tamil Nadu (408) mein register hue; desh bhar mein total 1,499 cases register hue, jinme 1,511 victims the.

facts.caveat: Registration depends on enforcement drives; states with high NFHS-5 prevalence such as West Bengal and Bihar registered few cases (132 and 22).

text.en: Only 209 Prohibition of Child Marriage Act cases ended in conviction in India in 2024, against 625 acquittals, a conviction rate of 25.0%, with 8,553 cases pending trial at year-end.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke sirf 209 cases mein conviction hua, jabki 625 cases mein acquittal hua, yaani conviction rate 25.0% raha; saal ke end mein 8,553 cases ka trial pending tha.

facts.caveat: Court disposal in a year includes cases registered in earlier years.

text.en: Police in India registered 1,099 cases in 2024 for publishing or transmitting material depicting children in sexually explicit acts (Section 67B of the IT Act), with 1,123 child victims.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne bachchon ko sexually explicit acts mein dikhane wala material publish ya transmit karne ke 1,099 cases register kiye (IT Act ka Section 67B), jinme 1,123 child victims the.

facts.caveat: Cases where POCSO is the heavier charge are counted under POCSO, not here. Compare with the millions of CyberTipline reports NCMEC attributes to India each year.

text.en: In 2024 Indian courts convicted in 65 cases of publishing or transmitting child sexual abuse material (IT Act Section 67B), a 39.4% conviction rate, while 2,765 such cases were pending trial at year-end.
text.hg: 2024 mein India ki courts ne child sexual abuse material publish ya transmit karne (IT Act Section 67B) ke 65 cases mein saza sunayi, yaani conviction rate 39.4% raha, jabki saal ke end mein aise 2,765 cases ka trial pending tha.

facts.caveat: Court disposal in a year includes cases from earlier years.

text.en: India recorded 2,135 human trafficking cases in 2024, based on data from states' Anti-Human Trafficking Units, down 2.2% from 2,183 in 2023 (2,250 in 2022).
text.hg: India recorded 2,135 human trafficking cases in 2024, based on data from states' Anti-Human Trafficking Units, down 2.2% from 2,183 in 2023 (2,250 in 2022).

facts.caveat: Counts only cases reported to Anti-Human Trafficking Units. Trafficking is often booked under other heads (kidnapping, ITPA, child labour), so this undercounts.

text.en: 6,018 people were recorded as trafficked in India in 2024, of whom 2,297 (38%) were children under 18: 1,384 boys and 913 girls.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein 6,018 log trafficking ke shikaar ke roop mein record kiye gaye, jinme se 2,297 (38%) 18 saal se kam umar ke bachche the: 1,384 ladke aur 913 ladkiyan.

facts.caveat: Boy victims are concentrated in Bihar (410) and Rajasthan (271). NCRB does not cross-tabulate the purpose of trafficking by age or sex. Counts cover only cases reported to Anti-Human Trafficking Units.

text.en: Of 5,839 trafficking victims rescued in India in 2024, 2,347 (40%) had been trafficked for sexual exploitation for prostitution, 1,493 (26%) for forced labour, 105 for domestic servitude and 98 for forced marriage.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein rescue kiye gaye trafficking ke 5,839 victims mein se 2,347 (40%) ki trafficking prostitution ke liye sexual exploitation ke maqsad se hui thi, 1,493 (26%) ki forced labour ke liye, 105 ki domestic servitude ke liye aur 98 ki forced marriage ke liye.

facts.value: Sexual exploitation 2347; forced labour 1493; domestic servitude 105; forced marriage 98
facts.caveat: Purpose is recorded for rescued victims (including from earlier cases) and is not split by age; 1,771 were recorded under 'other reasons'.

text.en: Courts in India convicted in just 43 human trafficking cases in 2024, out of 586 cases in which trials were completed, a conviction rate of 7.3%.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein human trafficking ke jin 586 cases ka trial complete hua, unme se courts ne sirf 43 mein saza sunayi; conviction rate 7.3% raha.

facts.caveat: Acquitted and discharged cases are combined (543). Covers AHTU-reported cases only.

text.en: 98,375 children were reported missing in India in 2024 (75,603 girls, 22,768 boys and 4 transgender children), up 7.8% from 91,296 in 2023.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein 98,375 bachchon ke missing hone ki report darj hui (75,603 ladkiyan, 22,768 ladke aur 4 transgender bachche), jo 2023 ke 91,296 se 7.8% zyada hai.

facts.caveat: Many missing children are traced. Under the Supreme Court's 2013 direction in Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India, a missing-child complaint must be registered as an FIR with an initial presumption of abduction or trafficking.

text.en: POCSO cases registered by police in India rose from 53,874 in 2021 to 63,414 in 2022 and 67,694 in 2023 (and to 69,191 in 2024), an increase of about 28% in three years.
text.hg: India mein police ke register kiye POCSO cases 2021 ke 53,874 se badhkar 2022 mein 63,414 aur 2023 mein 67,694 ho gaye (aur 2024 mein 69,191), yaani teen saal mein lagbhag 28% ki badhotri hui.

facts.caveat: The 2024 figure (69,191) is from Crime in India 2024; the 28% rise is calculated from 53,874 to 69,191. Rising counts can reflect greater willingness to report and register cases as well as more offending.

text.en: In 2023 Indian courts convicted the accused in 29.0% of POCSO cases whose trials ended (11,087 convictions against 25,803 acquittals), and 2,62,089 POCSO cases were pending trial at the end of the year.
text.hg: 2023 mein India ki courts mein POCSO ke jin cases ka trial khatam hua, unme se 29.0% mein accused ko saza hui (11,087 convictions, jabki 25,803 acquittals), aur saal ke end mein POCSO ke 2,62,089 cases ka trial pending tha.

facts.caveat: Compare 2024: 32.3% conviction and 2,86,903 pending. Across all crimes against children, the 2023 conviction rate was 28.5% with 5,90,755 cases pending trial.

text.en: Assam alone accounted for 5,267 of the 6,038 cases registered under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act across India in 2023; national registrations fell back to 1,499 in 2024, when Assam registered 471.
text.hg: 2023 mein poore India mein Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke tahat register hue 6,038 cases mein se 5,267 akele Assam mein the; 2024 mein desh bhar ke cases ghatkar phir 1,499 par aa gaye, aur us saal Assam mein 471 cases register hue.

facts.caveat: The spike coincides with a widely reported Assam police drive against child marriage in 2023; that context was not verified in a primary source this session, so do not state it as fact without checking. The 2024 Assam figure (471) is from Crime in India 2024. Case counts reflect enforcement, not prevalence.

text.en: In the Ministry of Women and Child Development's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 53.22% of the 12,447 children surveyed across 13 Indian states reported one or more forms of sexual abuse; 21.90% reported severe forms and 5.69% reported being sexually assaulted.
text.hg: Ministry of Women and Child Development ki 2007 ki 'Study on Child Abuse' mein India ke 13 states mein survey kiye gaye 12,447 bachchon mein se 53.22% ne ek ya usse zyada tarah ke sexual abuse ki baat batayi; 21.90% ne iske severe forms ki aur 5.69% ne sexual assault ka shikaar hone ki baat batayi.

facts.value: 53.22% any form; 21.90% severe forms; 5.69% sexual assault
facts.caveat: Not a national prevalence rate: the study used multi-stage purposive (non-random) sampling and deliberately included street children, working children and children in institutions. Its definition is broad: severe forms included assault, fondling, forcing a child to exhibit private parts and nude photography; 'other forms' included forcible kissing, sexual advances during travel and exposure to pornography. The report lists its own data-quality limitations. It is nearly two decades old, and India has had no national survey of child sexual abuse since.

text.en: Contrary to common belief, boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse in the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, against 47.06% girls, and 9 of the 13 states surveyed found a higher share among boys.
text.hg: Aam soch ke ulat, sarkar ki 2007 ki 'Study on Child Abuse' mein sexual abuse ki baat batane wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the aur 47.06% ladkiyan, aur survey wale 13 mein se 9 states mein ladkon ka hissa zyada paya gaya.

facts.caveat: The split is among children who reported abuse in a purposive sample that included many working and street children, who are disproportionately boys. Contrast with police data, where boys are about 2% of POCSO penetrative-assault victims.

text.en: The 2007 government Study on Child Abuse found that 50% of abusers were persons known to the child or in a position of trust and responsibility, and that most children did not report the abuse to anyone.
text.hg: Sarkar ki 2007 ki 'Study on Child Abuse' mein paya gaya ki abuse karne walon mein se 50% bachche ke jaan-pehchaan wale the ya bharose aur zimmedari wali position mein the, aur zyadatar bachchon ne abuse ke baare mein kisi ko nahi bataya.

facts.caveat: Survey of a purposive sample; see sampling caveats on the study's prevalence figure. Among children who reported sexual assault, the study separately found 72.1% did not report it to anyone.

text.en: Of children who reported being sexually assaulted in the government's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 72.1% had told no one, and only 3.4% had reported it to the police.
text.hg: Sarkar ki 2007 ki 'Study on Child Abuse' mein jin bachchon ne sexual assault ka shikaar hone ki baat batayi, unme se 72.1% ne kisi ko nahi bataya tha, aur sirf 3.4% ne police ko report kiya tha.

facts.value: 72.1% told no one; 3.4% reported to police
facts.caveat: Applies to the 5.69% of respondents who reported sexual assault, in a purposive, non-representative 2007 sample. Predates POCSO (2012) and its mandatory reporting rule.

text.en: The 2007 government Study on Child Abuse found that sexual abuse reported by children began as early as age 5, gained momentum from age 10 and peaked at ages 12 to 15.
text.hg: Sarkar ki 2007 ki 'Study on Child Abuse' mein paya gaya ki bachchon ne jis sexual abuse ki baat batayi, woh 5 saal ki umar se hi shuru ho jata tha, 10 saal ki umar se badhne lagta tha aur 12 se 15 saal ki umar mein sabse zyada tha.

facts.caveat: Self-reported, purposive sample.

text.en: 23.3% of Indian women aged 20-24 were married before age 18, according to the National Family Health Survey 2019-21 (NFHS-5).
text.hg: National Family Health Survey 2019-21 (NFHS-5) ke mutabik, India mein 20-24 saal ki 23.3% women ki shaadi 18 saal ki umar se pehle ho gayi thi.

facts.caveat: Survey estimate (self-reported age at marriage) from fieldwork in 2019-21. Superseded as the latest figure by NFHS-6 (2023-24): 20.1%.

text.en: 17.7% of Indian men aged 25-29 were married before the legal age of 21, according to NFHS-5 (2019-21).
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) ke mutabik, India mein 25-29 saal ke 17.7% mardon ki shaadi 21 saal ki legal umar se pehle ho gayi thi.

facts.caveat: Survey estimate. NFHS-6 (2023-24) puts this at 15.9%.

text.en: 4.8% of Indian women aged 20-24 in NFHS-5 (2019-21) had been married by age 15.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India ki 20-24 saal ki 4.8% women ki shaadi 15 saal ki umar tak ho chuki thi.

facts.caveat: Survey estimate.

text.en: The share of Indian women aged 20-24 married before 18 fell from 47.4% in NFHS-3 (2005-06) to 26.8% in NFHS-4 (2015-16), 23.3% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) and 20.1% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).
text.hg: India mein 20-24 saal ki un women ka hissa, jinki shaadi 18 se pehle hui, NFHS-3 (2005-06) ke 47.4% se ghatkar NFHS-4 (2015-16) mein 26.8%, NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 23.3% aur NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 20.1% reh gaya.

facts.caveat: NFHS-3 and NFHS-4 values confirmed in the national reports hosted by the DHS Program; NFHS-5 in its national report; NFHS-6 in the provisional IIPS fact sheets. The pace of decline slowed after 2015-16.

text.en: 20.1% of Indian women aged 20-24 were married before age 18 in 2023-24, down from 23.3% in 2019-21, according to provisional NFHS-6 fact sheets; the rate was 23.3% in rural and 11.4% in urban areas.
text.hg: NFHS-6 ki provisional fact sheets ke mutabik, 2023-24 mein India mein 20-24 saal ki 20.1% women ki shaadi 18 saal ki umar se pehle ho gayi thi, jabki 2019-21 mein yeh 23.3% tha; rural areas mein yeh rate 23.3% aur urban areas mein 11.4% tha.

facts.caveat: Provisional results; fieldwork 28 May 2023 to 31 December 2024 (679,238 households, 716,397 women, 100,977 men); Manipur not covered. IIPS cautions that some states have small samples, and the urban sampling frame changed from NFHS-5. Seen in a copy of the official IIPS fact-sheet compilation hosted by a news site.

text.en: 15.9% of Indian men aged 25-29 were married before the legal age of 21 in 2023-24, down from 17.7% in 2019-21 (NFHS-6, provisional).
text.hg: 2023-24 mein India mein 25-29 saal ke 15.9% mardon ki shaadi 21 saal ki legal umar se pehle ho gayi thi, jabki 2019-21 mein yeh 17.7% tha (NFHS-6, provisional).

facts.caveat: Provisional; smaller sample of men than women.

text.en: In NFHS-6 (2023-24), West Bengal had India's highest share of women aged 20-24 married before 18 at 36.4%, followed by Bihar (34.6%), Tripura (34.0%), Jharkhand (28.1%), Assam (25.3%) and Andhra Pradesh (25.1%).
text.hg: NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 18 se pehle shaadi hone wali 20-24 saal ki women ka hissa desh mein sabse zyada West Bengal mein tha (36.4%), uske baad Bihar (34.6%), Tripura (34.0%), Jharkhand (28.1%), Assam (25.3%) aur Andhra Pradesh (25.1%) ka number tha.

facts.value: West Bengal 36.4%; Bihar 34.6%; Tripura 34.0%; Jharkhand 28.1%; Assam 25.3%; Andhra Pradesh 25.1%
facts.caveat: Provisional. Rajasthan's NFHS-6 value is 24.6%, seventh highest.

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), the share of women aged 20-24 married before 18 was highest in West Bengal (41.6%), Bihar (40.8%) and Tripura (40.1%).
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 18 se pehle shaadi hone wali 20-24 saal ki women ka hissa sabse zyada West Bengal (41.6%), Bihar (40.8%) aur Tripura (40.1%) mein tha.

facts.caveat: NFHS-5 values as printed for comparison in the NFHS-6 fact sheets; also reported by CEDA.

text.en: In NFHS-6 (2023-24), Kerala and Lakshadweep had the lowest share of women aged 20-24 married before 18 (2.9% each), but against the national decline the share rose in eight states and UTs, including Nagaland (5.6% to 10.2%), Himachal Pradesh (5.4% to 7.9%), Delhi (9.9% to 11.4%) and Punjab (8.7% to 10.2%).
text.hg: NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 18 se pehle shaadi hone wali 20-24 saal ki women ka hissa Kerala aur Lakshadweep mein sabse kam tha (dono mein 2.9%), lekin national level par aayi giravat ke ulat aath states aur UTs mein yeh hissa badh gaya, jinme Nagaland (5.6% se 10.2%), Himachal Pradesh (5.4% se 7.9%), Delhi (9.9% se 11.4%) aur Punjab (8.7% se 10.2%) shamil hain.

facts.value: Kerala 2.9%; rises in Nagaland, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi, Punjab, Goa, J&K, Ladakh, Lakshadweep
facts.caveat: Provisional. Small states and UTs have small samples and wide margins of error, so these rises may not be statistically significant. The other rises were in Goa (5.8% to 6.8%), Jammu & Kashmir (4.5% to 5.1%), Ladakh (2.5% to 3.5%) and Lakshadweep (1.3% to 2.9%).

text.en: 6.7% of Indian women aged 15-19 were already mothers or pregnant at the time of NFHS-6 (2023-24), almost unchanged from 6.8% in NFHS-5; the rural rate (7.9%) was more than double the urban rate (3.4%).
text.hg: NFHS-6 (2023-24) ke time India mein 15-19 saal ki 6.7% women pehle hi maa ban chuki thi ya pregnant thi; NFHS-5 mein yeh 6.8% tha, yaani lagbhag koi badlaav nahi hua. Rural areas ka rate (7.9%) urban areas ke rate (3.4%) se double se bhi zyada tha.

facts.caveat: Provisional. Includes women aged 18-19 who are adults; it is an indicator of early marriage and early childbearing, not only of under-18 pregnancies.

text.en: On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court of India held that storing or possessing child sexual abuse material is itself an offence under Section 15 of the POCSO Act when the circumstances show the intent the law specifies, even if it is never shared; it set aside a Madras High Court ruling of 11 January 2024 that had quashed such a case, calling it an 'egregious error'.
text.hg: 23 September 2024 ko Supreme Court of India ne faisla diya ki child sexual abuse material ko store karna ya apne paas rakhna khud mein POCSO Act ke Section 15 ke tahat offence hai, agar halaat se woh intent dikhe jo law mein bataya gaya hai, chahe woh material kabhi kisi se share na kiya gaya ho. Court ne Madras High Court ka 11 January 2024 ka woh faisla palat diya jisme aisa ek case quash kar diya gaya tha, aur us faisle ko 'egregious error' bataya.

facts.value: Storage or possession punishable without transmission
facts.caveat: Intent still matters: sub-section (1) covers failure to delete, destroy or report with intent to share; (2) transmission or facilitation; (3) commercial purpose. The ruling restored a trial; it convicted no one. Refer to it as the Just Rights for Children Alliance case (2024 INSC 716) and do not name the accused.

text.en: The Supreme Court ruled in September 2024 that viewing child sexual abuse material online without downloading it can amount to 'possession' under the POCSO Act, through the doctrine of constructive possession, if the viewer exercised control over the material.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne September 2024 mein faisla diya ki child sexual abuse material ko download kiye bina online dekhna bhi 'constructive possession' ke doctrine ke zariye POCSO Act ke tahat 'possession' maana ja sakta hai, agar dekhne wale ka us material par control raha ho.

facts.value: Online viewing can be constructive possession
facts.caveat: The court also held that Section 67B of the IT Act punishes the creation, possession, propagation and consumption of such material.

text.en: The Supreme Court in September 2024 directed all Indian courts to stop using the term 'child pornography' and to use 'child sexual exploitation and abuse material' (CSEAM) instead, and urged Parliament to amend the POCSO Act to make the change.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne September 2024 mein desh ki saari courts ko nirdesh diya ki woh 'child pornography' term ka istemaal band karein aur uski jagah 'child sexual exploitation and abuse material' (CSEAM) ka istemaal karein, aur Parliament se aagrah kiya ki yeh badlaav karne ke liye POCSO Act mein amendment kare.

facts.caveat: The court explained that such images 'are not merely pornographic but are records of incidents' of abuse. Whether Parliament has since amended the Act was not verified.

text.en: The Supreme Court held in September 2024 that social media platforms which report child sexual abuse material to the US-based NCMEC must also report it to India's Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police under the POCSO Act, and that IT Act safe-harbour compliance does not absolve them.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne September 2024 mein kaha ki jo social media platforms child sexual abuse material ki report US-based NCMEC ko karte hain, unhe POCSO Act ke tahat iski report India ki Special Juvenile Police Unit ya local police ko bhi karni hogi, aur IT Act ke 'safe harbour' rules ka paalan karne bhar se woh is zimmedari se bach nahi sakte.

facts.value: Platforms must also report to Indian police
facts.caveat: Para 255 describes the existing route: under an MoU between NCRB and NCMEC, platforms report to NCMEC, which passes reports to NCRB, which forwards them to the states through the national cybercrime reporting portal. The court held that this alone does not meet the POCSO reporting duty.

text.en: In its September 2024 ruling the Supreme Court recommended comprehensive sex education covering consent and the harms of child sexual exploitation, and suggested the Union government set up an expert committee on health and sex education and POCSO awareness for children from an early age.
text.hg: September 2024 ke apne faisle mein Supreme Court ne comprehensive sex education ki sifarish ki, jisme consent aur child sexual exploitation se hone wale nuksaan ki jaankari shamil ho, aur suggest kiya ki Union government bachchon ke liye kam umar se hi health aur sex education aur POCSO awareness par ek expert committee banaye.

facts.value: Recommendation for sex education and an expert committee
facts.caveat: These are suggestions to the government, not binding directions. Implementation status not verified.

text.en: Under Sections 19 and 21 of the POCSO Act, anyone who knows or suspects that a child sexual offence has been or is likely to be committed must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police; failing to report is punishable with up to six months in jail, a fine, or both, and with up to one year and a fine for heads of companies or institutions who fail to report offences by subordinates.
text.hg: Under Sections 19 and 21 of the POCSO Act, anyone who knows or suspects that a child sexual offence has been or is likely to be committed must report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police; failing to report is punishable with up to six months in jail, a fine, or both, and with up to one year and a fine for heads of companies or institutions who fail to report offences by subordinates.

facts.value: Up to 6 months; up to 1 year for institution heads
facts.caveat: The duty does not apply to children (Section 21(3)). In 2024 the Supreme Court (Just Rights for Children Alliance, para 259) told courts not to show leniency to schools, children's homes, shelter homes, hostels and similar institutions that fail to report.

text.en: India's Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 defines a child as a male under 21 or a female under 18, and a child marriage as one in which either party is a child.
text.hg: India ke Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke mutabik 21 saal se kam umar ka male ya 18 saal se kam umar ki female 'child' hai, aur child marriage woh shaadi hai jisme dono mein se koi bhi ek party child ho.

facts.caveat: Gazette text; the same definitions are quoted in the Supreme Court's October 2024 judgment.

text.en: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, a child marriage is not automatically void: it is voidable at the option of the party who was a child, who must petition a district court within two years of reaching adulthood.
text.hg: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke tahat child marriage apne aap void nahi hoti: yeh voidable hai, yaani jo party shaadi ke waqt child thi woh chahe toh ise radd karwa sakti hai, lekin iske liye use baalig hone ke do saal ke andar district court mein petition deni hoti hai.

facts.value: Voidable; petition within 2 years of majority
facts.caveat: Majority is 18, so the window closes at 20. Section 12 makes a marriage void where the minor was taken or enticed away, compelled by force or deceit, or sold for marriage, or was sold, trafficked or used for immoral purposes after the marriage.

text.en: The maximum punishment under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act for an adult groom, for anyone who performs a child marriage, and for anyone who promotes or permits one is two years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with no mandatory minimum sentence; all offences are cognisable and non-bailable.
text.hg: Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke tahat adult groom, child marriage karwane wale, aur use promote karne ya permission dene wale, sabke liye maximum saza do saal ki rigorous imprisonment aur Rs 1 lakh ka fine hai, aur koi mandatory minimum saza nahi hai; is law ke saare offences cognisable aur non-bailable hain.

facts.value: Max 2 years RI + Rs 1 lakh; no minimum
facts.caveat: The Supreme Court observed that the lack of a minimum sentence 'has led to ineffective enforcement of the PCMA'. Section 9 applies to a man above 18 and allows imprisonment, a fine or both; Sections 10 and 11 require both, but Section 11 bars imprisonment of women.

text.en: On 18 October 2024 the Supreme Court issued guidelines to enforce the child marriage law, directing states to appoint district Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with no other duties, publish their quarterly reports online, set up special child marriage prohibition units, and have magistrates issue suo motu injunctions, especially around 'auspicious days' for mass weddings.
text.hg: 18 October 2024 ko Supreme Court ne child marriage law lagu karwane ke liye guidelines jaari kiye aur states ko nirdesh diya ki woh districts mein aise Child Marriage Prohibition Officers appoint karein jinke paas koi aur zimmedari na ho, in officers ki quarterly reports online publish karein, child marriage rokne ke liye special units banayein, aur magistrates se suo motu injunctions jaari karwayein, khaaskar mass weddings wale 'shubh dinon' ke aaspaas.

facts.caveat: Bench of CJI D.Y. Chandrachud, J.B. Pardiwala and Manoj Misra JJ. The guidelines also make district Collectors and SPs responsible for prevention and direct action against neglectful officials. Compliance has not been verified.

text.en: The Supreme Court said in October 2024 that its child marriage guidelines prioritise 'prevention before protection and protection before penalisation', warning that enforcement 'must not be solely focused on increasing prosecutions'.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne October 2024 mein kaha ki child marriage par uske guidelines 'protection se pehle prevention aur penalisation se pehle protection' ko priority dete hain, aur warning di ki enforcement ka focus 'sirf prosecutions badhane par nahi hona chahiye'.

facts.caveat: The court added that it was not discouraging prosecution of offenders.

text.en: The Supreme Court urged Parliament in October 2024 to consider outlawing child betrothals, noting that the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act does not cover them and that marriages fixed during childhood violate a child's free choice, autonomy and childhood.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne October 2024 mein Parliament se aagrah kiya ki woh child betrothals, yaani bachpan mein sagai, ko illegal banane par vichaar kare. Court ne kaha ki Prohibition of Child Marriage Act aisi sagaiyon par lagu nahi hota, aur bachpan mein tay ki gayi shaadiyan bachche ki free choice, autonomy aur bachpan ka ullanghan karti hain.

facts.value: Parliament urged to outlaw child betrothals
facts.caveat: A recommendation to Parliament, not a binding direction.

text.en: The Supreme Court did not rule in October 2024 on whether the child marriage law overrides personal laws, noting that the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021, introduced on 21 December 2021 to raise women's minimum age of marriage from 18 to 21 and to make the Act override any other law, custom or practice, was pending before Parliament.
text.hg: The Supreme Court did not rule in October 2024 on whether the child marriage law overrides personal laws, noting that the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021, introduced on 21 December 2021 to raise women's minimum age of marriage from 18 to 21 and to make the Act override any other law, custom or practice, was pending before Parliament.

facts.value: Personal-law question left to Parliament; 2021 Bill would raise women's marriage age to 21
facts.caveat: The Bill was referred to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth and Sports on 21 December 2021. A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses when the House is dissolved (Constitution, Article 107(5)), so it would have lapsed when the 17th Lok Sabha was dissolved in June 2024; PRS still lists it as in committee, and its current status was not confirmed in a source this session.

text.en: State figures cited by the Supreme Court in October 2024 show that few child marriage cases end in a police case: over the previous three years Telangana reported 4,440 child marriage cases but filed only 149 FIRs, Andhra Pradesh about 3,400 cases (most of them marriages that were stopped) but 10 FIRs, and Maharashtra prevented 2,043 marriages but registered 178 FIRs, while Tamil Nadu filed 2,392 FIRs on 8,966 cases.
text.hg: State figures cited by the Supreme Court in October 2024 show that few child marriage cases end in a police case: over the previous three years Telangana reported 4,440 child marriage cases but filed only 149 FIRs, Andhra Pradesh about 3,400 cases (most of them marriages that were stopped) but 10 FIRs, and Maharashtra prevented 2,043 marriages but registered 178 FIRs, while Tamil Nadu filed 2,392 FIRs on 8,966 cases.

facts.value: Telangana 4440 cases/149 FIRs; Andhra Pradesh about 3,400 cases/10 FIRs; Maharashtra 2043 prevented/178 FIRs; Tamil Nadu 8966 cases/2392 FIRs
facts.caveat: Figures were submitted by states for 'the last three years' before the 2024 judgment; exact years were not stated. The judgment gives Andhra Pradesh as 3,413 cases with 3,136 prevented (para 113) and as 3,416 cases with 10 FIRs (para 114). A marriage stopped before it happens may not lead to an FIR. Karnataka reported 8,348 cases and prevented 7,306.

text.en: In Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court struck down the marital-rape exception in Section 375 IPC as it applied to wives under 18, so sex with a minor wife is rape.
text.hg: Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017) case mein Supreme Court ne IPC ke Section 375 mein marital rape ke exception ko, jahan tak woh 18 saal se kam umar ki wives par lagu hota tha, radd kar diya; isliye minor wife ke saath sex rape hai.

facts.value: Marital exception struck down for wives under 18
facts.caveat: The 2017 judgment formally 'read down' Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC so that it applies only to wives aged 18 or older, with prospective effect. Since 1 July 2024, Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita keeps that threshold ('the wife not being under eighteen years of age'), so sex with a wife under 18 remains rape.

text.en: India was linked to 8,923,738 CyberTipline reports in 2023, most of them concerning suspected child sexual abuse material, more than any other country, out of 36.2 million reports worldwide, according to the US-based NCMEC.
text.hg: India was linked to 8,923,738 CyberTipline reports in 2023, most of them concerning suspected child sexual abuse material, more than any other country, out of 36.2 million reports worldwide, according to the US-based NCMEC.

facts.caveat: NCMEC: 'These numbers are not indicative of the level of child sexual abuse in a particular country.' Reports are geolocated by upload location and can be affected by proxies; one report can cover many files. Counting changed in 2024 (bundling), so 2023 is not comparable with later years.

text.en: NCMEC attributed 2,252,528 CyberTipline reports to India in 2024, the most of any country, including 1,521,666 referrals with enough information for police action.
text.hg: NCMEC ne 2024 mein 2,252,528 CyberTipline reports India se judi batayi, jo kisi bhi desh se zyada thi; inme 1,521,666 aise referrals shamil the jinme police action ke liye kaafi jaankari thi.

facts.caveat: Not a measure of abuse levels. NCMEC says the fall from 2023 came partly from a new CyberTipline feature that lets platforms 'bundle' related reports (used by Meta in 2024) and partly from fewer submissions by some platforms, not from fewer crimes. Reports can be made available to more than one country.

text.en: NCMEC attributed 1,933,900 CyberTipline reports to India in 2025, including 1,769,595 actionable referrals, the second-highest total of any identified country after the United States (2,061,893).
text.hg: NCMEC ne 2025 mein 1,933,900 CyberTipline reports India se judi batayi, jinme 1,769,595 actionable referrals the; identified countries mein yeh United States (2,061,893) ke baad doosra sabse bada total tha.

facts.caveat: NCMEC says country numbers are not indicative of the level of abuse. A referral is a report in which the platform gave enough information for law enforcement. Compare with 1,099 Section 67B IT Act cases registered by Indian police in 2024.

text.en: NCMEC's CyberTipline received 36.2 million reports worldwide in 2023, 20.5 million in 2024 and 21.3 million in 2025; NCMEC says the 2024 drop came from report 'bundling' and fewer reports from some platforms, not because the crimes stopped.
text.hg: NCMEC ki CyberTipline ko duniya bhar se 2023 mein 36.2 million, 2024 mein 20.5 million aur 2025 mein 21.3 million reports mili; NCMEC kehta hai ki 2024 ki giravat reports ki 'bundling' aur kuch platforms se kam reports aane ki wajah se thi, isliye nahi ki crimes ruk gaye the.

facts.caveat: The 2025 figure is from NCMEC's CyberTipline data page (https://www.missingkids.org/cybertiplinedata). NCMEC also cites end-to-end encryption as limiting detection.

text.en: In 2025 NCMEC's CyberTipline received 1.4 million reports of online enticement of children and more than 400,000 reports with a generative-AI link, and an average of 137 financial sextortion reports a day.
text.hg: 2025 mein NCMEC ki CyberTipline ko bachchon ke online enticement ki 1.4 million reports aur generative AI se judi 400,000 se zyada reports mili, aur har din average 137 financial sextortion reports aayi.

facts.caveat: Global figures, not India-specific. Sextortion figure described by NCMEC as a 37% increase over the prior year.

text.en: India's 24x7 Child Helpline 1098 is run under the Mission Vatsalya scheme by state and district child-protection functionaries and integrated with the Ministry of Home Affairs' Emergency Response Support System (ERSS-112); when the operating procedures were issued in March 2023 the service covered 568 districts, 135 railway stations and 11 bus stands and was to be extended to every district.
