text.hg: India ki 24x7 Child Helpline 1098 Mission Vatsalya scheme ke tahat state aur district level ke child-protection officials chalate hain, aur yeh Ministry of Home Affairs ke Emergency Response Support System (ERSS-112) se judi hai; March 2023 mein jab iske operating procedures jaari hue, tab yeh service 568 districts, 135 railway stations aur 11 bus stands par chal rahi thi, aur ise har district tak pahunchaya jaana tha.

facts.caveat: MWCD's Mission Vatsalya page (https://wcd.gov.in/child/mission_vatsalya, undated, read November 2026) says C-DAC Kerala is the technology provider for automating 1098 and integrating it with ERSS-112, that the helpline is 100% funded by the Government of India, and that all 36 States/UTs have started implementing it. The date of full national go-live and call volumes were not verified.

text.en: Mission Vatsalya, the Centre's child-protection scheme, replaced the Child Protection Services scheme (begun in 2009-10 as the Integrated Child Protection Scheme) from 2021-22, with new norms from 1 April 2022 and costs shared 60:40 between the Centre and most states (90:10 for north-eastern and Himalayan states and Jammu & Kashmir).
text.hg: Mission Vatsalya, Centre ki child-protection scheme, ne 2021-22 se Child Protection Services scheme ki jagah li, jo 2009-10 mein Integrated Child Protection Scheme ke roop mein shuru hui thi. Mission Vatsalya ke naye norms 1 April 2022 se lagu hue, aur iska kharcha Centre aur zyadatar states ke beech 60:40 mein baanta jata hai (north-eastern aur Himalayan states aur Jammu & Kashmir ke liye 90:10).

facts.caveat: It funds Child Welfare Committees, Juvenile Justice Boards, District Child Protection Units, child care institutions, Childline and family-based care. Budget figures not verified.

text.en: In November 2023 the Ministry of Women and Child Development launched a Nirbhaya Fund scheme to give minor girls made pregnant by rape (POCSO Sections 4 and 6) shelter, medical and maternity care, legal aid, counselling and education support under one roof.
text.hg: November 2023 mein Ministry of Women and Child Development ne Nirbhaya Fund se ek scheme shuru ki, taaki rape (POCSO Sections 4 aur 6) se pregnant hui minor ladkiyon ko ek hi chhat ke neeche shelter, medical aur maternity care, legal aid, counselling aur padhai mein support mil sake.

facts.caveat: The ministry's letter notes that 'a disproportionate number of the victims are girl children between the age of 13-18 years'. Uptake figures not verified.

text.en: The child-protection nonprofit Darkness to Light describes grooming as a deliberate process by which offenders gradually build and keep a secret sexual relationship with a child, and lists red flags including special attention to one child, gift giving, touching or hugging, acting as a sympathetic listener, offering to help the family, and gaining access through the internet.
text.hg: Child-protection par kaam karne wali nonprofit Darkness to Light grooming ko ek sochi-samjhi process batati hai, jiske zariye offenders dheere-dheere kisi bachche ke saath ek secret sexual relationship banate aur use banaye rakhte hain. Sanstha iske red flags mein yeh baatein ginati hai: kisi ek bachche par khaas dhyaan dena, gifts dena, chhoona ya gale lagana, humdard banke baatein sunna, family ki madad ki offer karna, aur internet ke zariye bachche tak pahunch banana.

facts.caveat: US-based organisation; signs are indicators, not proof. Pairs with NCRB data showing most offenders are known to the child.

text.en: Darkness to Light notes that emotional and behavioural signs of child sexual abuse are more common than physical ones, and include anxiety or depression, sleep problems and nightmares, unusual fear of a person or reluctance to be alone with them, regression such as bedwetting, changes in mood or in attitude to school, and sexual knowledge beyond the child's age.
text.hg: Darkness to Light notes that emotional and behavioural signs of child sexual abuse are more common than physical ones, and include anxiety or depression, sleep problems and nightmares, unusual fear of a person or reluctance to be alone with them, regression such as bedwetting, changes in mood or in attitude to school, and sexual knowledge beyond the child's age.

facts.value: Behavioural signs more common than physical
facts.caveat: Signs 'can be indistinguishable from other signs of child stress, distress, or trauma'; they call for attention, not conclusions.

text.en: UNICEF warns that online abusers may be someone the child knows or a stranger, and often first win the trust of the child or a caregiver before manipulating the child into sharing sexual images or videos; some abuse is livestreamed.
text.hg: UNICEF warn karta hai ki online abuse karne wala bachche ka koi jaan-pehchaan wala bhi ho sakta hai aur koi stranger bhi, aur aksar woh pehle bachche ya uski dekhbhaal karne wale ka bharosa jeetta hai, phir bachche ko manipulate karke usse sexual photos ya videos share karwata hai; kuch abuse livestream bhi kiya jata hai.

facts.caveat: General UNICEF guidance, not India-specific data.

text.en: UNICEF lists signs that a child may be distressed by something that happened online: headaches or stomach aches, trouble sleeping, appetite changes, unexplained sadness or anxiety, distress after being online, avoiding devices or being unusually secretive about online activity, and fear of going to school.
text.hg: UNICEF un signs ki list deta hai jinse pata chal sakta hai ki online hui kisi baat se bachcha pareshaan hai: sir dard ya pet dard, sone mein dikkat, bhookh mein badlaav, bina wajah udaasi ya anxiety, online rehne ke baad pareshaan dikhna, devices se katrana ya online activity ko lekar unusually secretive rehna, aur school jaane se darr.

facts.caveat: Signs of distress in general, not specific to sexual abuse.

text.en: The POCSO Act requires a Special Court to record the child's evidence within 30 days of taking cognisance and to complete the trial, as far as possible, within one year (Section 35).
text.hg: The POCSO Act requires a Special Court to record the child's evidence within 30 days of taking cognisance and to complete the trial, as far as possible, within one year (Section 35).

facts.caveat: Courts must record reasons for any delay in taking the child's evidence. Against the one-year target, NCRB shows 87.7% of POCSO cases pending trial at the end of 2024.

text.en: The POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019 raised the minimum sentence for penetrative sexual assault on a child under 16 to 20 years and allowed the death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.
text.hg: The POCSO (Amendment) Act, 2019 raised the minimum sentence for penetrative sexual assault on a child under 16 to 20 years and allowed the death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault.

facts.caveat: In force from 16 August 2019. The same amendment raised the minimum for penetrative sexual assault on a child aged 16 or 17 from 7 to 10 years (Section 4(1)). Death is an alternative punishment only for aggravated penetrative sexual assault (Section 6).

text.en: Of the 69,191 POCSO cases registered in India in 2024, 44,126 (63.8%) were for penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault (Sections 4 and 6), 20,845 (30.1%) for sexual assault or aggravated sexual assault (Sections 8 and 10), 3,502 for sexual harassment (Section 12), 500 for using children to make, or storing, sexual abuse material (Sections 14 and 15) and 218 under Sections 17 to 22, which cover abetment, attempt, failure to report and false complaints.
text.hg: Of the 69,191 POCSO cases registered in India in 2024, 44,126 (63.8%) were for penetrative or aggravated penetrative sexual assault (Sections 4 and 6), 20,845 (30.1%) for sexual assault or aggravated sexual assault (Sections 8 and 10), 3,502 for sexual harassment (Section 12), 500 for using children to make, or storing, sexual abuse material (Sections 14 and 15) and 218 under Sections 17 to 22, which cover abetment, attempt, failure to report and false complaints.

facts.caveat: Each FIR is counted once, under its most serious offence; cases registered under these sections read with the IPC/BNS rape, molestation or insult-to-modesty sections are included. The 500 Section 14-15 cases are separate from the 1,099 IT Act Section 67B cases.

text.en: Police in India traced 98,826 missing children in 2024, 67.1% of the 1,47,175 children on the missing list that year (98,375 newly reported plus 48,800 still missing from earlier years), leaving 48,349 children untraced at the end of the year, 36,352 of them girls.
text.hg: Police in India traced 98,826 missing children in 2024, 67.1% of the 1,47,175 children on the missing list that year (98,375 newly reported plus 48,800 still missing from earlier years), leaving 48,349 children untraced at the end of the year, 36,352 of them girls.

facts.caveat: Traced counts include 22,230 children who went missing in earlier years. The table does not say why children went missing or how many were trafficked.

text.en: Police in India registered 1,20,227 cases of cruelty by husband or his relatives (Section 85 BNS / Section 498A IPC) in 2024, the single largest category of crimes against women.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne pati ya uske rishtedaron dwara cruelty (Section 85 BNS / Section 498A IPC) ke 1,20,227 cases register kiye, jo crimes against women ki sabse badi category hai.

facts.caveat: Police-registered FIRs, not prevalence; NCRB counts only the most serious offence in each FIR (principal offence rule). 2024 figures combine cases registered under the IPC (offences before 1 July 2024) and under BNS (from 1 July 2024).

text.en: Cruelty by husband or relatives made up 27.2% of the 4,41,534 crimes against women registered in India in 2024.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein crimes against women ke jo 4,41,534 cases register hue, unmein 27.2% pati ya rishtedaron dwara cruelty ke the.

facts.caveat: The share was 31.4% in 2022 and 29.8% in 2023 (see dv-cruelty-series-2022-2024).

text.en: Registered cases of cruelty by husband or relatives in India rose from 1,11,549 in 2020 to 1,36,234 in 2021 and 1,40,019 in 2022 (31.4% of crimes against women), then fell to 1,33,676 in 2023 (29.8%) and 1,20,227 in 2024 (27.2%).
text.hg: India mein pati ya rishtedaron dwara cruelty ke registered cases 2020 mein 1,11,549 se badhkar 2021 mein 1,36,234 aur 2022 mein 1,40,019 (crimes against women ka 31.4%) ho gaye, phir ghatkar 2023 mein 1,33,676 (29.8%) aur 2024 mein 1,20,227 (27.2%) reh gaye.

facts.caveat: 2020 and the 2022 share are from CII 2022 (ncrb-cii-2022); 2024 is from CII 2024 (ncrb-cii-2024). A fall in registered cases is not evidence of less violence: NFHS-5 shows most survivors never report.

text.en: India registered 4,41,534 cases of crime against women in 2024, 1.5% fewer than the 4,48,211 cases of 2023, a rate of 64.6 cases per lakh women.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein crime against women ke 4,41,534 cases register hue, jo 2023 ke 4,48,211 cases se 1.5% kam hain; inka rate har lakh mahilaon par 64.6 cases raha.

facts.caveat: NCRB itself warns that 'rise in crime' and 'increase in registration of crime by police' are different things; 2024 was the changeover year from IPC to BNS.

text.en: In 2024 Uttar Pradesh (21,266) and West Bengal (19,330) registered the most cruelty-by-husband cases, while Telangana had the highest rate at 52.8 cases per lakh women, followed by Delhi at 45.3.
text.hg: 2024 mein pati dwara cruelty ke sabse zyada cases Uttar Pradesh (21,266) aur West Bengal (19,330) mein register hue, jabki rate ke hisaab se Telangana sabse aage raha — har lakh mahilaon par 52.8 cases — aur uske baad Delhi (45.3).

facts.value: UP 21,266; WB 19,330; Telangana rate 52.8; Delhi rate 45.3
facts.caveat: NCRB warns that states should not be compared purely on crime figures; higher numbers can reflect better registration.

text.en: Of 1,20,390 cruelty-by-husband cases that police disposed of in India in 2024, 4,593 (about 3.8%) were closed as 'false', while 1,08,574 were charge-sheeted, a charge-sheeting rate of 90.2%.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne pati dwara cruelty ke jin 1,20,390 cases ko dispose kiya, unmein se 4,593 (lagbhag 3.8%) 'false' bata kar band kiye gaye, jabki 1,08,574 cases mein chargesheet file hui — yaani charge-sheeting rate 90.2% raha.

facts.value: 4,593 closed as false; 1,08,574 charge-sheeted; 90.2% charge-sheeting rate
facts.caveat: 3.8% is 4,593 divided by 1,20,390 (calculated). A further 3,459 cases were closed as 'mistake of fact or law or civil dispute'. 'Final report false' is a police closure category, not a court finding.

text.en: Indian courts completed trials in only 53,137 of the 9,27,199 cruelty-by-husband cases before them in 2024; 10,689 ended in conviction, a conviction rate of 20.1%, and 8,54,798 cases (92.2%) were still pending at year end.
text.hg: 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne pati dwara cruelty ke 9,27,199 cases the, lekin inmein se sirf 53,137 mein hi trial poora hua; 10,689 cases mein conviction hua, yaani conviction rate 20.1% raha, aur saal ke end mein 8,54,798 cases (92.2%) ab bhi pending the.

facts.caveat: NCRB conviction rate = convictions divided by trials completed in the year.

text.en: In 2024, 16,396 cruelty-by-husband cases in Indian courts ended in compromise or compounding, more than the 10,689 that ended in conviction.
text.hg: 2024 mein Indian courts mein pati dwara cruelty ke 16,396 cases compromise ya compounding se khatam hue — conviction par khatam hue 10,689 cases se zyada.

facts.caveat: Compromise can reflect reconciliation, mediation or pressure on the woman; the data do not say which.

text.en: Courts in India convicted the accused in 25.7% of crimes-against-women trials completed in 2024, and 24,32,527 such cases (92.1%) were pending trial at the end of the year.
text.hg: 2024 mein complete hue crimes against women ke trials mein se 25.7% mein Indian courts ne accused ko convict kiya, aur saal ke end mein aise 24,32,527 cases (92.1%) trial ke intezaar mein pending the.

facts.caveat: Covers all crime-against-women heads, including rape, POCSO and kidnapping.

text.en: India recorded 5,737 dowry-death cases (Section 80 BNS / Section 304B IPC) with 5,811 victims in 2024, about 16 a day.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein dowry death (Section 80 BNS / Section 304B IPC) ke 5,737 cases register hue, 5,811 victims ke saath — yaani roz lagbhag 16.

facts.caveat: 'About 16 a day' is 5,737 divided by 366 days (calculated). Dowry death is a legal category; deaths logged as suicide or accident are often not registered under it. 2024 figures combine cases registered under the IPC (offences before 1 July 2024) and under BNS (from 1 July 2024).

text.en: Registered dowry deaths in India fell from 6,966 in 2020 and 6,753 in 2021 to 6,450 in 2022, 6,156 in 2023 and 5,737 in 2024.
text.hg: India mein register hui dowry deaths 2020 mein 6,966 aur 2021 mein 6,753 se ghatkar 2022 mein 6,450, 2023 mein 6,156 aur 2024 mein 5,737 reh gayi.

facts.caveat: 2020 and 2021 values are from ncrb-cii-2022 (Table 1.2). Registered cases only.

text.en: Uttar Pradesh registered 2,038 dowry-death cases in 2024, over a third of India's total, followed by Bihar with 1,078.
text.hg: 2024 mein Uttar Pradesh mein dowry death ke 2,038 cases register hue, jo poore desh ke total ke ek-tihaai se zyada hain; iske baad Bihar raha, jahan 1,078 cases register hue.

facts.caveat: 2,038 of 5,737 is 35.5% (calculated).

text.en: Only 4,043 dowry-death trials were completed in Indian courts in 2024 out of 63,516 cases before them; 1,869 ended in conviction (a 46.2% conviction rate) and 59,446 cases (93.6%) were still pending.
text.hg: 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne dowry death ke 63,516 cases the, lekin inmein se sirf 4,043 mein trial poora hua; 1,869 cases mein conviction hua (conviction rate 46.2%) aur 59,446 cases (93.6%) ab bhi pending the.

facts.caveat: Police charge-sheeted 90.3% of dowry-death cases they disposed of in 2024 (Table 3A.5).

text.en: Dowry was recorded as the motive in 701 murders in India in 2024, down from 1,171 in 2020, 952 in 2021, 951 in 2022 and 833 in 2023; these are separate from cases booked as dowry deaths.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein 701 murders mein dowry ko motive ke taur par record kiya gaya, jo 2020 ke 1,171, 2021 ke 952, 2022 ke 951 aur 2023 ke 833 se kam hai; yeh cases dowry death ke taur par darj cases se alag hain.

facts.caveat: Earlier years are from ncrb-cii-2020, ncrb-cii-2021, ncrb-cii-2022 and ncrb-cii-2023 (Table 2A.2 in each). Motive data cover murder cases (Section 103 BNS / 302 IPC) only.

text.en: Police registered 12,343 cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 in 2024, with Uttar Pradesh (4,482), Bihar (3,780) and Karnataka (1,991) accounting for most of them.
text.hg: 2024 mein police ne Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ke tahat 12,343 cases register kiye, jinmein se zyaadatar Uttar Pradesh (4,482), Bihar (3,780) aur Karnataka (1,991) ke the.

facts.caveat: Several large states register almost no Dowry Prohibition Act cases (West Bengal 0, Maharashtra 12), which reflects police practice rather than an absence of dowry.

text.en: Cases under the Dowry Prohibition Act in India rose from 10,366 in 2020 to 13,568 in 2021, 13,479 in 2022 and 15,489 in 2023, before falling to 12,343 in 2024.
text.hg: India mein Dowry Prohibition Act ke tahat cases 2020 mein 10,366 se badhkar 2021 mein 13,568, 2022 mein 13,479 aur 2023 mein 15,489 ho gaye, phir 2024 mein ghatkar 12,343 reh gaye.

facts.caveat: 2020 value from ncrb-cii-2022 (SLL table), 2024 value from ncrb-cii-2024 (Table 3A.2 (ii)).

text.en: Trials under the Dowry Prohibition Act ended in conviction in only 17.4% of cases decided in 2024, and 83,298 such cases were pending in Indian courts at year end.
text.hg: 2024 mein Dowry Prohibition Act ke jin trials mein faisla aaya, unmein se sirf 17.4% mein conviction hua, aur saal ke end mein Indian courts mein aise 83,298 cases pending the.

text.en: In 2024 police registered 4,220 cases of abetment of suicide of women (Sections 107/108 BNS / Sections 305/306 IPC), involving 4,284 victims, down from 4,963 in 2022 and 4,825 in 2023.
text.hg: 2024 mein police ne mahilaon ko suicide ke liye uksaane (abetment of suicide; Sections 107/108 BNS / Sections 305/306 IPC) ke 4,220 cases register kiye, 4,284 victims ke saath; yeh 2022 ke 4,963 aur 2023 ke 4,825 cases se kam hai.

facts.caveat: Maharashtra (670), Madhya Pradesh (646) and Telangana (424) registered the most cases in 2024. Court conviction rate for this head was 15.5% in 2024 (Table 3A.7). 2022 and 2023 values are from ncrb-cii-2022 and ncrb-cii-2023.

text.en: Only 616 cases were registered across India in 2024 under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, and 496 of them came from Kerala.
text.hg: 2024 mein poore India mein Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 ke tahat sirf 616 cases register hue, aur inmein se 496 Kerala ke the.

facts.caveat: The 2005 Act mainly provides civil protections (the NFHS-5 report notes that with it 'civil protections were afforded to victims of domestic violence'), so police-registered criminal cases under it do not measure domestic violence. 2020-2023 values are from ncrb-cii-2022 and ncrb-cii-2023.

text.en: Police recorded 118 acid attacks on women (Section 124(1) BNS / Section 326A IPC) with 126 victims, and 32 attempted acid attacks on women, in India in 2024; West Bengal had the most, 30.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne mahilaon par acid attack (Section 124(1) BNS / Section 326A IPC) ke 118 cases, 126 victims ke saath, aur mahilaon par acid attack ki koshish ke 32 cases record kiye; acid attack ke sabse zyada cases, 30, West Bengal mein the.

facts.caveat: Counts only cases where the victim is a woman. Acid attacks on women were 124 in 2022 and 113 in 2023 (ncrb-cii-2022 and ncrb-cii-2023, Table 3A.2 (i)).

text.en: Across all victims, India registered 202 acid attacks in 2022, 207 in 2023 and 207 in 2024, plus 71, 65 and 68 attempted acid attacks in those years.
text.hg: Sabhi victims ko milakar, India mein 2022 mein 202, 2023 mein 207 aur 2024 mein 207 acid attacks register hue; inhi saalon mein acid attack ki koshish ke 71, 65 aur 68 cases bhi register hue.

facts.caveat: Includes male victims. NCRB records only cases registered under the acid-attack sections.

text.en: Of 804 acid-attack cases on women before Indian courts in 2024, trials were completed in just 24 and 13 ended in conviction; 778 cases (96.8%) were still pending at year end.
text.hg: 2024 mein Indian courts ke saamne mahilaon par acid attack ke 804 cases the; inmein se sirf 24 mein trial poora hua aur 13 mein conviction hua, jabki 778 cases (96.8%) saal ke end mein bhi pending the.

facts.caveat: The conviction rate (54.2%) looks high only because so few trials finish.

text.en: Police in India recorded only 36 murders with 'honour killing' as the motive in 2024, compared with 1,391 murders attributed to 'love affairs'.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne sirf 36 murders mein 'honour killing' ko motive ke taur par record kiya, jabki 1,391 murders ki wajah 'love affairs' batayi gayi.

facts.caveat: Widely regarded as a large under-count: there is no separate offence of honour killing, and many such murders are logged under 'love affairs' or other motives, or charged as lesser offences.

text.en: NCRB's count of honour killings in India was 25 in 2020, 33 in 2021, 18 in 2022, 38 in 2023 and 36 in 2024.
text.hg: NCRB ki ginti ke mutaabik India mein honour killings ki sankhya 2020 mein 25, 2021 mein 33, 2022 mein 18, 2023 mein 38 aur 2024 mein 36 thi.

facts.caveat: Values are from five separate NCRB reports: ncrb-cii-2020, ncrb-cii-2021, ncrb-cii-2022, ncrb-cii-2023 and ncrb-cii-2024 (Table 2A.2 in each).

text.en: NCRB data record zero honour killings in Tamil Nadu in each year from 2020 to 2023 and just one in 2024.
text.hg: NCRB data mein Tamil Nadu mein 2020 se 2023 tak har saal honour killings ki sankhya zero darj hai, aur 2024 mein sirf ek.

facts.caveat: 2020 to 2023 rows are from ncrb-cii-2020, ncrb-cii-2021, ncrb-cii-2022 and ncrb-cii-2023. Compare with the Madras High Court's figure of 59 honour killings in the state over ten years (dv-madras-hc-59-honour-killings).

text.en: In June 2026 the Madras High Court observed that Tamil Nadu had seen 59 honour killings over the past 10 years, while hearing a bail plea in a 2025 honour killing in Tirunelveli district.
text.hg: June 2026 mein Madras High Court ne Tirunelveli district mein 2025 mein hui ek honour killing ke case mein bail plea par sunvaai karte hue observe kiya ki pichhle 10 saal mein Tamil Nadu mein 59 honour killings hui hain.

facts.caveat: A judge's observation in a bail appeal (judgment dated 11 June 2026, reported by LiveLaw on 13 June 2026); the judgment does not say where the count comes from. The accused in the case have not been convicted and are not named here.

text.en: NCRB recorded witchcraft as the motive in 88 murders in 2020, 68 in 2021, 85 in 2022, 74 in 2023 and 54 in 2024; in 2024 Madhya Pradesh (17) and Chhattisgarh (10) reported the most.
text.hg: NCRB ne 2020 mein 88, 2021 mein 68, 2022 mein 85, 2023 mein 74 aur 2024 mein 54 murders mein witchcraft (jaadu-tona) ko motive ke taur par record kiya; 2024 mein sabse zyada cases Madhya Pradesh (17) aur Chhattisgarh (10) se report hue.

facts.caveat: NCRB does not publish the sex of victims in this table; witch-hunting is widely reported to target women, often widows and older women, but these counts cover all victims and only murders, not assaults or expulsions.

text.en: NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence (the 'principal offence rule'), so an FIR that includes both dowry death and cruelty is counted only as a dowry death.
text.hg: NCRB har FIR ko sirf ek baar, uske sabse gambhir offence ke tahat ginta hai ('principal offence rule'), isliye jis FIR mein dowry death aur cruelty dono shaamil hon, use sirf dowry death ke roop mein gina jaata hai.

facts.caveat: The dowry example is an illustration of the rule, not an example quoted by NCRB.

text.en: 29.3% of ever-married women aged 18-49 in India reported physical or sexual violence by a husband in NFHS-5 (2019-21).
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India mein 18-49 saal ki kabhi na kabhi shaadishuda rahi mahilaon mein se 29.3% ne pati dwara physical ya sexual violence report kiya.

facts.caveat: Survey of 62,381 ever-married women; NFHS-5 fieldwork ran 2019-21. 29.2% refers to the current or most recent husband and 29.3% to any husband.

text.en: Nearly one in three ever-married women in India (31.9%) have faced physical, sexual or emotional violence from their husband, and 26.8% faced it in the 12 months before NFHS-5.
text.hg: India mein kabhi na kabhi shaadishuda rahi lagbhag har teen mein se ek mahila (31.9%) ne pati ki taraf se physical, sexual ya emotional violence jheli hai, aur NFHS-5 se pehle ke 12 mahinon mein 26.8% ne aisi violence jheli.

facts.caveat: Self-reported survey data; under-reporting is likely.

text.en: 6.3% of ever-married women aged 18-49 in India reported sexual violence by their husband in NFHS-5, and 4.6% said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to.
text.hg: NFHS-5 mein India mein 18-49 saal ki kabhi na kabhi shaadishuda rahi 6.3% mahilaon ne pati dwara sexual violence report kiya, aur 4.6% ne kaha ki jab woh nahi chahti thin, tab bhi pati ne physically force karke unhe intercourse ke liye majboor kiya.

facts.caveat: These acts are not 'rape' under Indian law when the wife is 18 or older because of the marital exception. The NFHS key findings round this to 'six percent'.

text.en: Among ever-married women in India who have ever experienced sexual violence, 82% named their current husband and 14% a former husband as the perpetrator (NFHS-5).
text.hg: India mein kabhi na kabhi shaadishuda rahi jin mahilaon ne kabhi sexual violence jheli hai, unmein se 82% ne hinsa karne wale ke taur par apne maujooda pati ka aur 14% ne ex-husband ka naam liya (NFHS-5).

facts.caveat: Self-reported survey data.

text.en: Only 14.1% of Indian women aged 18-49 who had experienced physical or sexual violence ever sought help, and 77.2% never sought help or told anyone (NFHS-5).
text.hg: Physical ya sexual violence jhel chuki 18-49 saal ki Indian mahilaon mein se sirf 14.1% ne kabhi help maangi, aur 77.2% ne na kabhi help maangi, na kisi ko bataya (NFHS-5).

facts.caveat: Covers violence by anyone, not only husbands. Women facing both physical and sexual violence were more likely to seek help (26.3%). In the published table the three columns of the Total row sum to 100.9, an inconsistency in the source rather than rounding.

text.en: Of Indian women who sought help after physical or sexual violence, 60.9% turned to their own family and only 6.3% went to the police (NFHS-5).
text.hg: Physical ya sexual violence ke baad help maangne wali Indian mahilaon mein se 60.9% ne apne hi parivaar ka sahaara liya aur sirf 6.3% police ke paas gayin (NFHS-5).

facts.caveat: Combined with the 14.1% help-seeking rate, this implies fewer than 1 in 100 women who face violence go to the police (calculated, not an NFHS figure).

text.en: 45% of women and 44% of men aged 15-49 in India agreed in NFHS-5 that a husband is justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations; agreement had fallen among women from 52% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) but risen among men from 42%.
text.hg: NFHS-5 mein India mein 15-49 saal ki umar ki 45% mahilayein aur 44% purush is baat se sehmat the ki saat mein se kam se kam ek situation mein pati ka patni ko peetna jaayaz hai; NFHS-4 (2015-16) ke muqaable mahilaon mein yeh sehmati 52% se ghati, lekin purushon mein 42% se badhi.

facts.value: Women 45% (52% in NFHS-4); men 44% (42% in NFHS-4)
facts.caveat: The most accepted reason was 'disrespect for in-laws' (32% of women, 31% of men); 11% of women and 10% of men accepted beating a wife who refuses sex.

text.en: In NFHS-5, 84% of women in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and 78% in Tamil Nadu said wife-beating could be justified, and among men the figure reached 82% in Karnataka.
text.hg: NFHS-5 mein Andhra Pradesh aur Telangana mein 84% aur Tamil Nadu mein 78% mahilaon ne kaha ki patni ko peetna jaayaz ho sakta hai, aur purushon mein yeh figure Karnataka mein 82% tak pahuncha.

facts.value: AP and Telangana women 84%; TN women 78%; Karnataka men 82%

text.en: Karnataka had the highest share of ever-married women reporting spousal violence in NFHS-5 (48.4% physical, sexual or emotional), followed by Bihar (42.5%), Manipur (41.6%) and Telangana (40.4%); Lakshadweep was lowest at 1.3%.
text.hg: NFHS-5 mein pati dwara hinsa (spousal violence) report karne wali kabhi na kabhi shaadishuda rahi mahilaon ka hissa Karnataka mein sabse zyada tha (48.4% physical, sexual ya emotional), iske baad Bihar (42.5%), Manipur (41.6%) aur Telangana (40.4%) rahe; Lakshadweep mein yeh sabse kam, 1.3% tha.

facts.caveat: Last column is emotional, physical or sexual violence by the current or most recent husband.

text.en: 71% of Indian women whose husbands often get drunk reported spousal physical or sexual violence, against 23% of women whose husbands do not drink (NFHS-5).
text.hg: Jin Indian mahilaon ke pati aksar sharaab ke nashe mein dhut rehte hain, unmein se 71% ne pati dwara physical ya sexual violence report kiya, jabki jinke pati sharaab nahi peete, unmein yeh figure 23% tha (NFHS-5).

facts.caveat: Association, not proof that alcohol causes violence.

text.en: Women whose fathers beat their mothers were more than twice as likely to face spousal violence themselves (58% against 25%), according to NFHS-5.
text.hg: NFHS-5 ke mutaabik, jin mahilaon ke pita unki maa ko peette the, unke khud pati ki hinsa jhelne ki sambhavna doguni se bhi zyada thi (58% vs 25%).

text.en: One in four Indian women (25%) who faced spousal physical or sexual violence were injured, including 6% with deep wounds, broken bones or broken teeth and 3% with severe burns (NFHS-5).
text.hg: Pati dwara physical ya sexual violence jhelne wali har chaar mein se ek Indian mahila (25%) ghayal hui; inmein 6% woh thin jinhe gehre ghaav hue ya jinki haddiyan ya daant toote, aur 3% woh jo gambhir roop se jal gayin (NFHS-5).

facts.value: 25% injured; 6% serious wounds or fractures; 3% severe burns

text.en: Among currently married women married only once, 11.2% first faced spousal physical or sexual violence within two years of marriage and 20.9% within five years (NFHS-5).
text.hg: Jo mahilayein abhi shaadishuda hain aur jinki sirf ek baar shaadi hui hai, unmein se 11.2% ko shaadi ke do saal ke andar aur 20.9% ko paanch saal ke andar pehli baar pati dwara physical ya sexual violence jhelni padi (NFHS-5).

text.en: 22.3% of ever-married women aged 18-49 in India reported physical or sexual violence by a husband in NFHS-6 (2023-24), down from 29.2% in NFHS-5; the rate was 24.4% in rural and 17.5% in urban areas.
text.hg: NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein India mein 18-49 saal ki kabhi na kabhi shaadishuda rahi 22.3% mahilaon ne pati dwara physical ya sexual violence report kiya, jo NFHS-5 ke 29.2% se kam hai; rural areas mein yeh rate 24.4% aur urban areas mein 17.5% raha.

facts.caveat: Provisional fact sheets released in 2026; NFHS-6 did not cover Manipur. Experts quoted by Deccan Herald doubt the fall reflects reality (see dv-nfhs6-doubts).

text.en: In NFHS-6 (2023-24) Bihar had the highest share of ever-married women reporting spousal violence (36.1%), followed by Telangana (30.8%), Uttar Pradesh (28.5%) and Tamil Nadu (28.5%).
text.hg: NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein pati dwara hinsa (spousal violence) report karne wali kabhi na kabhi shaadishuda rahi mahilaon ka hissa Bihar mein sabse zyada (36.1%) tha, iske baad Telangana (30.8%), Uttar Pradesh (28.5%) aur Tamil Nadu (28.5%) rahe.

facts.caveat: Manipur, which ranked third in NFHS-5, was not surveyed in NFHS-6.

text.en: Karnataka's reported spousal violence fell from 44.4% in NFHS-5 to 14.1% in NFHS-6, while Kerala's rose from 9.8% to 17.7%; experts quoted by Deccan Herald doubt that such falls reflect real change, pointing to women's reluctance to disclose abuse in survey interviews.
text.hg: Karnataka's reported spousal violence fell from 44.4% in NFHS-5 to 14.1% in NFHS-6, while Kerala's rose from 9.8% to 17.7%; experts quoted by Deccan Herald doubt that such falls reflect real change, pointing to women's reluctance to disclose abuse in survey interviews.

facts.caveat: See dv-nfhs6-doubts for expert concerns about privacy during interviews.

text.en: Experts quoted by Deccan Herald in June 2026, among them a Mumbai-based public-health researcher, doubted that the NFHS-6 fall in spousal violence reflects reality, saying women may not disclose abuse to a surveyor in front of family members and questioning whether interviews were private; the paper headlined that the decline 'may be true only on paper'.
text.hg: Experts quoted by Deccan Herald in June 2026, among them a Mumbai-based public-health researcher, doubted that the NFHS-6 fall in spousal violence reflects reality, saying women may not disclose abuse to a surveyor in front of family members and questioning whether interviews were private; the paper headlined that the decline 'may be true only on paper'.

facts.caveat: Expert opinion reported by a newspaper, not a statistical finding.

text.en: India's new criminal codes, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), were enacted in December 2023 and, under Home Ministry gazette notifications dated 23 February 2024, came into force on 1 July 2024, replacing the IPC and CrPC.
text.hg: India's new criminal codes, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), were enacted in December 2023 and, under Home Ministry gazette notifications dated 23 February 2024, came into force on 1 July 2024, replacing the IPC and CrPC.

facts.value: in force from 1 July 2024 (commencement notified 23 February 2024)
facts.caveat: The BNS was published in the Gazette on 25 December 2023 (indiacode-bns-2023). Offences committed before 1 July 2024 continue to be registered under the IPC, which is why NCRB's 2024 tables show IPC and BNS columns side by side.

text.en: Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 says that sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ke Section 63 ke Exception 2 ke mutaabik, koi purush apni hi patni ke saath sexual intercourse ya sexual acts kare, aur patni 18 saal se kam umar ki na ho, to yeh rape nahi hai.

facts.caveat: BNS (in force from 1 July 2024) carried over the marital exception of Section 375 IPC, with the age set at 18 as read down by the Supreme Court in 2017.

text.en: Under Section 67 BNS, non-consensual intercourse by a husband with his wife who is living separately is punishable with 2 to 7 years in prison, far below the minimum 10 years for rape.
text.hg: Section 67 BNS ke tahat, alag reh rahi patni ke saath pati dwara uski consent ke bina intercourse karne par 2 se 7 saal ki jail ki saza hai — jo rape ke liye tay minimum 10 saal ki saza se kaafi kam hai.

facts.caveat: The 10-year minimum for rape is in Section 64(1) BNS.

text.en: Section 80 BNS defines a dowry death as a woman's death by burns, bodily injury or other abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage after dowry-linked cruelty, punishable with at least seven years and up to life imprisonment.
text.hg: Section 80 BNS ke mutaabik, shaadi ke saat saal ke andar dowry se judi cruelty ke baad kisi mahila ki jalne, shaareerik chot ya doosri asaamaanya paristhitiyon mein hui maut dowry death hai; iske liye kam se kam saat saal aur zyada se zyada umrqaid ki saza hai.

facts.caveat: Same as Section 304B IPC.

text.en: Section 85 BNS punishes a husband or his relative who subjects a woman to cruelty with up to three years in prison and a fine.
text.hg: Section 85 BNS mein kisi mahila ke saath cruelty karne wale pati ya uske rishtedaar ke liye teen saal tak ki jail aur jurmaane ki saza ka provision hai.

facts.caveat: Same as Section 498A IPC; Section 86 defines cruelty.

text.en: Section 124 BNS punishes an acid attack with at least 10 years and up to life imprisonment plus a fine to be paid to the victim, and an attempted acid attack with 5 to 7 years.
text.hg: Section 124 BNS mein acid attack ke liye kam se kam 10 saal se lekar umrqaid tak ki saza aur victim ko diye jaane wale jurmaane ka, aur acid attack ki koshish ke liye 5 se 7 saal ki saza ka provision hai.

facts.caveat: Same as Sections 326A and 326B IPC, which were added in 2013.

text.en: On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read down the marital rape exception so that sex with a wife under 18 is rape, but expressly left the question of adult wives undecided.
text.hg: 11 October 2017 ko Independent Thought v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne marital rape exception ko 'read down' kiya, jisse 18 saal se kam umar ki patni ke saath sex rape ki category mein aa gaya, lekin adult patniyon ke sawaal par saaf taur par koi faisla nahi diya.

facts.caveat: Bench: Justices Madan B. Lokur and Deepak Gupta. Before the ruling, the exception covered wives aged 15 and above.

text.en: On 11 May 2022 the Delhi High Court delivered a split verdict on the marital rape exception in RIT Foundation v. Union of India: Justice Rajiv Shakdher struck it down as unconstitutional, while Justice C. Hari Shankar upheld it.
text.hg: 11 May 2022 ko Delhi High Court ne RIT Foundation v. Union of India case mein marital rape exception par split verdict diya: Justice Rajiv Shakdher ne ise unconstitutional bata kar radd kar diya, jabki Justice C. Hari Shankar ne ise barqaraar rakha.

facts.caveat: The judges certified the case for appeal to the Supreme Court, where it is pending with connected petitions.

text.en: In March 2022 the Karnataka High Court held that the marital rape exception is not absolute and that a husband who forces non-consensual sex on his wife can be prosecuted under the rape provision; his appeal is the lead case now before the Supreme Court.
text.hg: March 2022 mein Karnataka High Court ne faisla diya ki marital rape exception absolute nahi hai aur patni ke saath uski consent ke bina zabardasti sex karne wale pati par rape provision ke tahat case chalaya ja sakta hai; usi pati ki appeal ab Supreme Court mein lead case hai.

facts.caveat: LiveLaw (9 September 2026) describes it as a judgment holding 'that the exception is not absolute' and that the husband 'was liable to be prosecuted under Section 376 IPC'. The High Court ruled on 23 March 2022 and the Supreme Court stayed that judgment in July 2022 (Bar and Bench, 22 December 2022 and 16 January 2023). The accused is not named because he has not been convicted.

text.en: In an affidavit verified on 3 October 2024, the Union government told the Supreme Court that marital rape is 'more of a social issue rather than a legal issue' and that making it 'rape' could be 'excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate'.
text.hg: 3 October 2024 ko verify kiye gaye ek affidavit mein Union government ne Supreme Court se kaha ki marital rape 'legal issue se zyada ek social issue' hai aur ise 'rape' ki category mein laana 'had se zyada harsh aur isliye disproportionate' ho sakta hai.

facts.caveat: The affidavit argues that other laws (cruelty, outraging modesty, the Domestic Violence Act) already protect married women.

text.en: A Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud began hearing the marital rape petitions on 17 October 2024 but adjourned them on 23 October 2024 because the hearing could not finish before his retirement.
text.hg: Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki aguwaai wali Supreme Court bench ne 17 October 2024 ko marital rape petitions par sunvaai shuru ki, lekin 23 October 2024 ko inhe adjourn kar diya, kyunki unke retirement se pehle sunvaai poori nahi ho sakti thi.

facts.caveat: The CJI retired on 10 November 2024.

text.en: On 9 September 2026 a three-judge Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana posted the marital rape cases for final hearing, saying it would decide both whether the exception is valid and whether a husband can be prosecuted while it stands.
text.hg: 9 September 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi aur Justice V. Mohana ki teen judges wali Supreme Court bench ne marital rape cases ko final hearing ke liye list kiya aur kaha ki woh dono sawaalon par faisla karegi — exception valid hai ya nahi, aur jab tak yeh laagu hai, tab tak pati par case chalaya ja sakta hai ya nahi.

facts.caveat: Status as of 20 November 2026: pending, with no verdict found. The latest reports seen are from 9-10 September 2026 (indianexpress-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026 said final hearing would start 'after three weeks'). LiveLaw, Bar and Bench and Indian Express marital-rape topic pages checked on 20 November 2026 showed no later hearing report, but a hearing that went unreported there cannot be ruled out. Lead case: a husband's appeal against the Karnataka High Court's 2022 ruling, SLP (Crl) 4063-4064/2022; the accused is not named here because he has not been convicted.

text.en: A public interest petition filed on 24 April 2025, Aweksha Women's Charitable Trust v. Union of India, challenges the marital exception in Section 63 BNS; the Supreme Court issued notice on 23 May 2025 and tagged it with the pending cases.
text.hg: 24 April 2025 ko daakhil ek public interest petition, Aweksha Women's Charitable Trust v. Union of India, Section 63 BNS ke marital exception ko chunauti deti hai; Supreme Court ne 23 May 2025 ko is par notice jaari kiya aur ise pending cases ke saath tag kar diya.

facts.caveat: CLPR is counsel for the petitioner.

text.en: In December 2024 the Union government told the Rajya Sabha that it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape, pointing instead to the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and to BNS sections 74, 75, 76 and 85 (assault to outrage a woman's modesty, sexual harassment, assault with intent to disrobe, and cruelty by husband or relatives).
text.hg: In December 2024 the Union government told the Rajya Sabha that it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape, pointing instead to the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and to BNS sections 74, 75, 76 and 85 (assault to outrage a woman's modesty, sexual harassment, assault with intent to disrobe, and cruelty by husband or relatives).

facts.caveat: Reported by Scroll on 12 December 2024 as a paraphrase; the original Rajya Sabha answer was not checked.

text.en: By 2018 only 77 of 185 countries (42%) had laws explicitly criminalising marital rape, and in 34 countries marital rape was neither criminalised nor could a wife file a rape complaint against her husband, according to UN Women.
text.hg: UN Women ke mutaabik, 2018 tak 185 deshon mein se sirf 77 (42%) mein aise kaanoon the jo marital rape ko saaf taur par crime ghoshit karte hain, aur 34 deshon mein na to marital rape crime tha, na hi patni apne pati ke khilaf rape ki complaint darj kara sakti thi.

facts.value: 77 of 185 criminalise explicitly; 34 offer no recourse
facts.caveat: Data are from 2018 and some countries have since changed their laws. The same report notes 12 countries still exempted rapists who marry their victims.

text.en: UNFPA reported in 2021 that 43 countries have no legislation at all addressing marital rape.
text.hg: UNFPA ne 2021 mein bataya ki 43 deshon mein marital rape se juda koi bhi kaanoon nahi hai.

facts.caveat: UN agencies use different country samples and definitions, so this figure differs from UN Women's 2018 count.

text.en: In most countries with data, fewer than 40% of women who experience violence seek help of any sort, and in almost all of them fewer than 10% of the women who seek help go to the police, according to UN Women, citing the UN's World's Women 2015 report.
text.hg: In most countries with data, fewer than 40% of women who experience violence seek help of any sort, and in almost all of them fewer than 10% of the women who seek help go to the police, according to UN Women, citing the UN's World's Women 2015 report.

facts.value: <40% seek help; <10% of help-seekers go to the police (most / almost all countries with data)
facts.caveat: Country-by-country survey findings (mostly 2005-2014), not one global average. India's NFHS-5 figures (14.1% sought help; 6.3% of them went to the police) are below both benchmarks.

text.en: In Laxmi v. Union of India, the Supreme Court on 18 July 2013 barred over-the-counter acid sales unless the seller keeps a register of buyers, required buyers to show government photo ID and state a purpose, banned sales to anyone under 18, and allowed fines of up to Rs 50,000 for violations.
text.hg: Laxmi v. Union of India case mein Supreme Court ne 18 July 2013 ko acid ki over-the-counter bikri par tab tak rok lagaayi jab tak seller khareedaron ka register na rakhe; khareedaron ke liye government photo ID dikhana aur khareed ka maqsad batana zaroori kiya; 18 saal se kam umar ke kisi ko bhi bikri par ban lagaya; aur niyam todne par Rs 50,000 tak ke jurmaane ki ijaazat di.

facts.caveat: Bench: Justices R.M. Lodha and Fakkir Mohamed Ibrahim Kalifulla. These interim directions applied until states framed rules under the Poisons Act, 1919.

text.en: The same 18 July 2013 order directed states to pay every acid attack victim at least Rs 3 lakh for after-care and rehabilitation, with Rs 1 lakh within 15 days of the attack and the rest within two months.
text.hg: 18 July 2013 ke usi order mein states ko nirdesh diya gaya ki woh har acid attack victim ko after-care aur rehabilitation ke liye kam se kam Rs 3 lakh dein — attack ke 15 din ke andar Rs 1 lakh aur baaki rakam do mahine ke andar.

facts.caveat: Before the order, victim-compensation schemes varied widely; the order notes Bihar offered Rs 25,000 and Rajasthan Rs 2 lakh.

text.en: On 27 October 2026 the Supreme Court, hearing Shaheen Malik v. Union of India, told the Centre that rising acid attacks showed its acid-sale guidelines had 'miserably failed' and asked it to revisit the policy, including whether retail sale of acid is needed at all.
text.hg: 27 October 2026 ko Shaheen Malik v. Union of India ki sunvaai karte hue Supreme Court ne Centre se kaha ki badhte acid attacks dikhaate hain ki acid ki bikri par uski guidelines 'buri tarah fail' ho gayi hain, aur use policy par dobaara vichaar karne ko kaha — isme yeh sawaal bhi shaamil hai ki kya acid ki retail bikri ki zaroorat hai bhi.

facts.caveat: Bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana; W.P.(C) No. 1112/2025. NCRB data show acid attacks roughly flat at 202-207 a year in 2022-2024.

text.en: On 4 May 2026 Chief Justice Surya Kant said the acid-attack provisions added to the IPC in 2013, including the 5-to-7-year term for attempted attacks under Section 326B, had had 'no deterrent effect', and asked whether punishment should be harsher and illegal acid sellers made liable.
text.hg: 4 May 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ne kaha ki 2013 mein IPC mein jode gaye acid-attack provisions ka — jinmein Section 326B ke tahat attack ki koshish ke liye 5 se 7 saal ki saza bhi shaamil hai — 'koi deterrent effect nahi' pada, aur poocha ki kya saza aur sakht honi chahiye aur illegal tareeke se acid bechne walon ko bhi zimmedaar thehraya jaana chahiye.

facts.caveat: Oral remarks during hearing, not a judgment.

text.en: In Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018), the Supreme Court held that the right to choose a life partner is a facet of individual liberty and ordered preventive, remedial and punitive measures to safeguard couples' autonomy against honour crimes.
text.hg: Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018) case mein Supreme Court ne faisla diya ki life partner chunne ka adhikaar individual liberty ka ek pehlu hai, aur honour crimes se couples ki autonomy bachaane ke liye preventive, remedial aur punitive measures ka aadesh diya.

facts.caveat: Judgment of 27 March 2018 by Chief Justice Dipak Misra and Justices A.M. Khanwilkar and D.Y. Chandrachud (LiveLaw report of the judgment). The PIL concerned khap panchayats' interference in inter-caste marriages (LiveLaw, January 2018). The judgment text itself was not re-read in this check.

text.en: In December 2025 the Delhi High Court was told that no fast-track courts for honour-killing cases had been set up in Delhi, more than seven years after Shakti Vahini directed special cells, fast-track and special courts and district-level monitoring committees.
text.hg: December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ko bataya gaya ki Delhi mein honour killing cases ke liye koi fast-track court nahi banayi gayi thi, jabki Shakti Vahini faisle ko saat saal se zyada ho chuke the, jisme special cells, fast-track aur special courts aur district-level monitoring committees banane ka nirdesh diya gaya tha.

facts.caveat: The petition was closed after the court asked petitioners to approach the High Court's administrative side and the Delhi government.

text.en: The Law Commission's 242nd Report (August 2012) proposed a special law against interference with couples' marriages in the name of 'honour'; it was still unimplemented when the Supreme Court's amicus curiae urged its adoption in January 2018.
text.hg: Law Commission ki 242nd Report (August 2012) mein 'honour' ke naam par couples ki shaadi mein dakhal ke khilaf ek special law ka prastaav rakha gaya tha; January 2018 mein jab Supreme Court ke amicus curiae ne ise apnaane ki apeel ki, tab bhi yeh laagu nahi hua tha.

facts.caveat: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 also contains no separate offence of honour killing (checked against the Gazette text); such killings are prosecuted as murder or other general offences.

text.en: In April 2025 the Supreme Court set aside orders that had let an alleged honour killing be tried as culpable homicide instead of murder, calling it 'a clear case of honour killing' and ordering a murder charge.
text.hg: April 2025 mein Supreme Court ne un orders ko radd kar diya jinke chalte ek kathit honour killing ka trial murder ki jagah culpable homicide ke taur par chalne diya gaya tha; court ne ise 'honour killing ka saaf case' bataya aur murder charge lagaane ka order diya.

facts.caveat: Shows one way honour killings drop out of the data: they are charged as lesser offences.

text.hg: India mein bachchon ke khilaf cyber crime ke roop mein darj, bachchon ko dikhane wale sexually explicit material se jude cases ki sankhya 2022 mein 1,171, 2023 mein 1,499 aur 2024 mein 1,099 rahi.

facts.caveat: NCRB counts FIRs registered by police (principal offence rule applies), not complaints; online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported, and from 1 July 2024 IPC heads were replaced by BNS heads, which affects comparisons.

text.en: India's toll-free cyber crime helpline number is 1930, and complaints can also be filed online at cybercrime.gov.in, the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C).
text.hg: India ka toll-free cyber crime helpline number 1930 hai, aur shikayat cybercrime.gov.in par online bhi darj ki ja sakti hai, jo Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) dwara chalaya jaane wala National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal hai.

text.en: The US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) attributed 5,675,324 CyberTipline reports of suspected child sexual exploitation to India in 2022, 8,923,738 in 2023, 2,252,528 in 2024 and 1,933,900 in 2025.
text.hg: America ke National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) ke mutabik, bachchon ke sandigdh sexual exploitation ki CyberTipline reports mein se 2022 mein 5,675,324, 2023 mein 8,923,738, 2024 mein 2,252,528 aur 2025 mein 1,933,900 reports India se judi thin.

facts.caveat: NCMEC says country numbers are not indicative of the level of child sexual abuse in a country and can be affected by proxies and anonymizers; most reports concern uploads of CSAM detected by US platforms. The fall after 2023 reflects 'bundling' of related reports by large platforms and reduced reporting by some platforms, not a fall in abuse (NCMEC 2024 CyberTipline Report).

text.en: India received more NCMEC CyberTipline reports than any other country in 2022, 2023 and 2024; in 2025 it ranked second in total reports behind the United States (2,061,893), but first in referrals to law enforcement, with 1,769,595 against 1,480,183 for the US.
text.hg: 2022, 2023 aur 2024 mein kisi bhi doosre desh ke muqable sabse zyada NCMEC CyberTipline reports India ke hisse aayin. 2025 mein total reports mein India United States (2,061,893) ke baad doosre number par raha, lekin law enforcement ko bheje gaye referrals mein pehle number par raha: India ke 1,769,595, jabki US ke 1,480,183.

facts.value: Rank 1 (2022-2024); 2025: rank 2 in reports, rank 1 in referrals (1,769,595)
facts.caveat: Ranking computed from NCMEC country tables; 3,331,777 reports in 2025 had an 'Unknown' location. India's large user base drives volume; per-capita rates are lower than several countries.

text.en: NCMEC's CyberTipline received 36.2 million reports of suspected child sexual exploitation worldwide in 2023, 20.5 million in 2024 (equivalent to 29.2 million separate incidents once bundled reports are counted) and 21.3 million in 2025.
text.hg: NCMEC ki CyberTipline ko duniya bhar se bachchon ke sandigdh sexual exploitation ki 2023 mein 36.2 million, 2024 mein 20.5 million (bundled reports ko ginne par 29.2 million alag-alag incidents ke barabar) aur 2025 mein 21.3 million reports mileen.

facts.caveat: Report counts reflect platform detection and reporting practices, not prevalence.

text.en: NCMEC received 1.4 million reports of online enticement of children in 2025, a 158% increase on 2024, including more than 80,000 reports concerning sextortion and more than 800 in which an offender travelled to meet a child in person.
text.hg: NCMEC ko 2025 mein bachchon ki online enticement (online behlane-phuslane) ki 1.4 million reports mileen, jo 2024 se 158% zyada hain. Inmein sextortion se judi 80,000 se zyada reports thin, aur 800 se zyada aisi reports jinmein offender bachche se aamne-saamne milne ke liye travel karke gaya.

facts.caveat: Part of the rise reflects the US REPORT Act (2024), which requires platforms to report online enticement and child sex trafficking.

text.en: NCMEC received more than 50,000 reports of financially motivated sextortion of children in 2025, an average of 137 a day, up from more than 36,000 in 2024.
text.hg: NCMEC ko 2025 mein bachchon ke financially motivated sextortion (paise ainthne ke maqsad se kiya gaya sextortion) ki 50,000 se zyada reports mileen, yaani average roz 137; 2024 mein yeh sankhya 36,000 se zyada thi.

facts.caveat: Global reports to a US clearinghouse; not India-specific.

text.en: NCMEC says that since 2021 it has known of at least 36 teenage boys in the United States who took their own lives after being victimised by sextortion.
text.hg: NCMEC says that since 2021 it has known of at least 36 teenage boys in the United States who took their own lives after being victimised by sextortion.

facts.caveat: Cases known to NCMEC, in the US, mostly linked to financial sextortion; the true number is likely higher.

text.en: NCMEC reports that teenage boys have been the most common targets of recent sextortion cases, and that online enticement reports rose by more than 300% between 2021 and 2023.
text.hg: NCMEC ke mutabik haal ke sextortion cases mein sabse zyada nishana teenage ladke bane hain, aur 2021 se 2023 ke beech online enticement (online behlane-phuslane) ki reports 300% se zyada badhin.

text.en: Reports to NCMEC involving generative AI rose from about 4,700 in 2023 to 67,000 in 2024 (a 1,325% increase) and to more than 400,000 in 2025, of which more than 182,000 involved offenders possessing, generating or trying to generate AI-made child sexual abuse material.
text.hg: NCMEC ko mili generative AI se judi reports 2023 mein lagbhag 4,700 se badhkar 2024 mein 67,000 (1,325% ki badhotri) aur 2025 mein 400,000 se zyada ho gayin. Inmein se 182,000 se zyada reports aise offenders se judi thin jinke paas AI se bana child sexual abuse material tha, ya jo use bana rahe the ya banane ki koshish kar rahe the.

text.en: Since it began tracking generative AI abuse in 2023, NCMEC has identified more than 275 child victims of AI-generated sexual abuse material and categorised more than 158,000 images and videos as AI-generated CSAM.
text.hg: 2023 mein generative AI abuse ko track karna shuru karne ke baad se NCMEC ne AI-generated sexual abuse material ke 275 se zyada child victims ki pehchaan ki hai, aur 158,000 se zyada images aur videos ko AI-generated CSAM ki category mein rakha hai.

text.en: NCMEC's Take It Down is a free, anonymous service, available in Hindi and other languages, that helps people remove nude or sexually explicit images taken when they were under 18 by sending only a digital fingerprint (hash) of the image to participating platforms.
text.hg: NCMEC ki 'Take It Down' ek free aur anonymous service hai, jo Hindi aur doosri bhashaon mein available hai. Yeh logon ko unki aisi nude ya sexually explicit tasveerein hatwane mein madad karti hai jo 18 saal se kam umr mein li gayi thin; iske liye tasveer ka sirf digital fingerprint (hash) participating platforms ko bheja jaata hai.

facts.caveat: Works only on public or unencrypted platforms that have agreed to participate.

text.en: StopNCII.org, the adult intimate-image hashing tool run by the UK charity SWGfL, was protecting 2 million images by November 2025 (a 97% increase on 2024) and had supported over 785,000 cases since its launch four years earlier.
text.hg: UK ki charity SWGfL dwara chalaya jaane wala StopNCII.org, jo adults ki intimate images ko hash karne wala tool hai, November 2025 tak 2 million tasveeron ko protect kar raha tha (2024 ke muqable 97% zyada), aur chaar saal pehle launch hone ke baad se 785,000 se zyada cases mein madad kar chuka tha.

facts.caveat: StopNCII covers images taken at 18 or older (NCMEC's Take It Down covers images taken under 18). It works by sharing hashes (digital fingerprints) with partner platforms, and only partner platforms act on them.

text.en: Rule 3(2)(b) of India's IT Rules, 2021 required platforms to take down, within 24 hours of a complaint by the person or someone on their behalf, any content that exposes a person's private area, shows them in full or partial nudity or in a sexual act, or impersonates them, including artificially morphed images.
text.hg: India ke IT Rules, 2021 ke Rule 3(2)(b) ke tahat platforms ko us vyakti ya uski taraf se kisi aur ki complaint ke 24 ghante ke andar aisa koi bhi content hatana hota tha jo kisi vyakti ke private parts dikhata ho, use poori ya aanshik nudity mein ya sexual act mein dikhata ho, ya uski pehchaan ki nakal (impersonation) karta ho, jismein artificially morph ki gayi tasveerein bhi shaamil hain.

facts.caveat: Replaced by a two-hour deadline from 20 February 2026.

text.en: Since 20 February 2026, platforms in India must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint, down from 24 hours, under the IT Amendment Rules, 2026 notified on 10 February 2026.
text.hg: 10 February 2026 ko notify kiye gaye IT Amendment Rules, 2026 ke tahat, 20 February 2026 se India mein platforms ke liye kisi vyakti ki nude, sexual ya morphed tasveerein uski complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatana zaroori hai; pehle yeh deadline 24 ghante thi.

text.en: The IT Amendment Rules, 2026 cut the time platforms have to remove unlawful content after a court order or authorised government notice from 36 hours to three hours, and cut the deadline for resolving user grievances from 15 days to seven.
text.hg: IT Amendment Rules, 2026 ne court order ya sarkar ke authorised notice ke baad platforms ke paas gair-kanooni content hatane ka samay 36 ghante se ghatakar teen ghante kar diya, aur users ki shikayatein (grievances) niptane ki deadline 15 din se ghatakar saat din kar di.

facts.caveat: Police intimations under Rule 3(1)(d) must come from officers not below the rank of Deputy Inspector General.

text.en: India's IT Amendment Rules, 2026 define 'synthetically generated information' as audio, visual or audio-visual content artificially or algorithmically created or altered so that it appears real and depicts a person or event in a way likely to be perceived as indistinguishable from reality.
text.hg: India ke IT Amendment Rules, 2026 'synthetically generated information' ko aise audio, visual ya audio-visual content ke roop mein define karte hain jo artificially ya algorithm ke zariye is tarah banaya ya badla gaya ho ki asli lage, aur kisi vyakti ya ghatna ko is tarah dikhaye ki log use asliyat se alag na pehchaan paayein, iski sambhavna ho.

facts.caveat: Routine editing, accessibility and good-faith document creation are excluded.

text.en: Under the 2026 amendment, platforms offering AI tools must use technical measures to block synthetic content that contains child sexual exploitative and abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery, and must prominently label other synthetic content and, to the extent technically feasible, embed permanent metadata or another provenance marker identifying the tool used to make it.
text.hg: Under the 2026 amendment, platforms offering AI tools must use technical measures to block synthetic content that contains child sexual exploitative and abuse material or non-consensual intimate imagery, and must prominently label other synthetic content and, to the extent technically feasible, embed permanent metadata or another provenance marker identifying the tool used to make it.

facts.caveat: Large platforms (significant social media intermediaries) must also take user declarations and verify them before publishing (Rule 4(1A)).

text.en: MeitY's October 2025 draft of the deepfake rules had proposed that AI-generated visuals carry a label covering at least 10% of the screen, and audio a disclosure during its first 10%; the final February 2026 rules dropped the fixed 10% size and require 'prominent' labelling instead.
text.hg: MeitY ke deepfake rules ke October 2025 ke draft mein proposal tha ki AI se bane visuals par aisa label ho jo screen ke kam se kam 10% hisse ko cover kare, aur audio mein uske shuruaati 10% hisse ke dauraan disclosure ho; February 2026 ke final rules mein 10% ka fixed size hata diya gaya aur uski jagah 'prominent' labelling zaroori ki gayi.

facts.caveat: Comparison with final text in G.S.R. 120(E), which requires labelling 'in a manner that ensures prominent visibility'.

text.en: On 11 November 2025 MeitY issued a Standard Operating Procedure on non-consensual intimate imagery, framed on the Madras High Court's directions, that requires all platforms to remove flagged content within 24 hours, large platforms to use hash-matching to stop re-uploads, and I4C to keep a secure NCII hash bank.
text.hg: 11 November 2025 ko MeitY ne non-consensual intimate imagery (bina consent ki intimate tasveeron) par ek Standard Operating Procedure jaari kiya, jo Madras High Court ke nirdeshon ke aadhaar par taiyaar kiya gaya hai. Iske tahat sabhi platforms ke liye flag kiya gaya content 24 ghante ke andar hatana, bade platforms ke liye dobara upload rokne ke liye hash-matching use karna, aur I4C ke liye ek secure NCII hash bank rakhna zaroori hai.

facts.caveat: The SOP's 24-hour window has since been tightened to two hours by the IT Amendment Rules, 2026 (in force 20 February 2026).

text.en: In Mrs X v. Union of India (26 April 2023), the Delhi High Court directed that the cybercrime.gov.in portal carry a complaint status tracker for non-consensual intimate image cases, that a 24x7 NCII helpline be set up, and that search engines use a token-based system so that de-indexed images do not resurface.
text.hg: Mrs X v. Union of India (26 April 2023) case mein Delhi High Court ne nirdesh diya ki cybercrime.gov.in portal par non-consensual intimate image cases ke liye complaint status tracker ho, ek 24x7 NCII helpline shuru ki jaye, aur search engines token-based system use karein taaki de-index ki gayi tasveerein dobara saamne na aayein.

facts.caveat: The court chose not to use the term 'revenge porn', calling it a subset of NCII.

text.en: Uttar Pradesh (633 cases) and Maharashtra (544) recorded the most cyber crimes with a sexual exploitation motive in India in 2024, together accounting for 37% of the national total of 3,190; Rajasthan (280) and Kerala (225) followed.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein sexual exploitation ke motive se hue cyber crimes sabse zyada Uttar Pradesh (633 cases) aur Maharashtra (544) mein darj hue; dono milkar desh ke kul 3,190 cases ka 37% the. Inke baad Rajasthan (280) aur Kerala (225) rahe.

facts.caveat: Ranking computed from state rows of Table 9A.3; NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures, as higher numbers can reflect better registration. NCRB counts FIRs registered by police (principal offence rule applies), not complaints; online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported, and from 1 July 2024 IPC heads were replaced by BNS heads, which affects comparisons.

text.en: Indian police registered 601 cases of cyber blackmailing or threatening in 2024; of 1,221 such cases before the courts that year, only two ended in conviction and 98% were still pending at year end.
text.hg: Indian police ne 2024 mein cyber blackmailing ya dhamki dene ke 601 cases register kiye; us saal courts ke saamne aise 1,221 cases the, jinmein se sirf do mein saza hui aur saal ke aakhir mein 98% cases abhi bhi pending the.

facts.caveat: Sextortion is not a separate NCRB crime head; cases can also be filed under IT Act s.67/67A, extortion or fraud. NCRB counts FIRs registered by police (principal offence rule applies), not complaints; online sexual abuse is heavily under-reported, and from 1 July 2024 IPC heads were replaced by BNS heads, which affects comparisons.

text.en: In 2024, the year the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC, Indian police registered 99 cyber crime cases under the new offence of 'sexual intercourse by deceitful means' (Section 69 BNS).
text.hg: 2024 mein, jis saal Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne IPC ki jagah li, Indian police ne 'sexual intercourse by deceitful means' (dhokhe se sexual sambandh banana; BNS Section 69) ke naye offence ke tahat cyber crime ke 99 cases register kiye.

facts.caveat: New BNS offence in force from 1 July 2024, so this covers only part of the year.

text.en: Complaints registered on India's National Cybercrime Reporting Portal rose from 4.52 lakh in 2021 to 10.29 lakh in 2022, 15.96 lakh in 2023 and 22.68 lakh in 2024, a 42.08% rise in the last year, the Home Ministry told the Lok Sabha.
text.hg: Home Ministry ne Lok Sabha ko bataya ki India ke National Cybercrime Reporting Portal par darj complaints 2021 mein 4.52 lakh se badhkar 2022 mein 10.29 lakh, 2023 mein 15.96 lakh aur 2024 mein 22.68 lakh ho gayin; aakhiri saal mein yeh badhotri 42.08% rahi.

facts.caveat: Portal complaints are not FIRs; most concern financial fraud. Compare with only 1,01,928 cyber crime FIRs recorded by NCRB in 2024.

text.en: About 1.94 lakh complaints about child sexual abuse material ('child pornography') and rape or gang-rape content had been reported on India's National Cybercrime Reporting Portal as of 30 April 2024, the Women and Child Development Minister told the Rajya Sabha.
text.hg: Women and Child Development Minister ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki 30 April 2024 tak India ke National Cybercrime Reporting Portal par child sexual abuse material ('child pornography') aur rape ya gang-rape content se judi lagbhag 1.94 lakh complaints report hui thin.

facts.caveat: Cumulative since the portal's launch in 2019; complaints, not FIRs.

text.en: More than 69.05 lakh NCMEC CyberTipline reports on child sexual abuse material had been passed on to Indian states and union territories by 31 March 2024, the government told the Rajya Sabha.
text.hg: Sarkar ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki 31 March 2024 tak child sexual abuse material par NCMEC ki 69.05 lakh se zyada CyberTipline reports India ke states aur union territories ko bheji ja chuki thin.

facts.caveat: Cumulative figure as on 31 March 2024; reports reach states via NCRB under its 2019 MoU with NCMEC. Compare: NCRB recorded only 1,036 FIRs under IT Act s.67B in 2024.

text.en: India's National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) was launched on a pilot basis on 30 August 2019 with a specific focus on crimes against women and children, including child sexual abuse material and rape or gang-rape videos, and was dedicated to the nation with the I4C on 10 January 2020.
text.hg: India ka National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) 30 August 2019 ko pilot basis par shuru kiya gaya tha. Iska khaas focus mahilaon aur bachchon ke khilaf crimes par tha, jinmein child sexual abuse material aur rape ya gang-rape videos shaamil hain. 10 January 2020 ko ise I4C ke saath desh ko samarpit kiya gaya.

text.en: Under India's IT Act, capturing or sharing images of a person's private parts without consent (Section 66E) carries up to three years in jail or a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh; publishing sexually explicit material (Section 67A) carries up to five years and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh on first conviction, and up to seven years on repeat conviction.
text.hg: India ke IT Act ke tahat kisi vyakti ke private parts ki tasveerein bina consent ke kheenchne ya share karne (Section 66E) par teen saal tak ki jail ya Rs 2 lakh tak ka fine ho sakta hai; sexually explicit material publish karne (Section 67A) par pehli baar doshi paaye jaane par paanch saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10 lakh tak ka fine, aur dobara doshi paaye jaane par saat saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai.

facts.value: 66E: 3 years/Rs 2 lakh; 67: 3 years/Rs 5 lakh; 67A and 67B: 5 years/Rs 10 lakh (7 years on repeat)
facts.caveat: Section 67 (obscene material): up to three years and Rs 5 lakh fine on first conviction, five years on repeat.

text.en: Section 67B of India's IT Act punishes not only publishing child sexual abuse material but also creating, collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging it, enticing children into online sexual relationships, and recording abuse, with up to five years in jail and a Rs 10 lakh fine on first conviction and seven years on repeat.
text.hg: India ke IT Act ka Section 67B sirf child sexual abuse material publish karne par hi nahin, balki use banane, collect karne, browse karne, download karne ya exchange karne, bachchon ko behla-phuslakar online sexual relationships mein phansane, aur abuse ko record karne par bhi saza deta hai: pehli baar doshi paaye jaane par paanch saal tak ki jail aur Rs 10 lakh ka fine, aur dobara doshi paaye jaane par saat saal tak.

facts.caveat: Penalties are maximums; NCRB data show very few convictions under this section (see dig-it67b-court-2024).

text.en: On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court of India ruled that viewing, storing or possessing child sexual abuse material is an offence under Section 15 of the POCSO Act and Section 67B of the IT Act, overturning a Madras High Court ruling; it told all courts to stop using the term 'child pornography' and urged Parliament to amend the POCSO Act to replace it with 'child sexual exploitation and abuse material' (CSEAM).
text.hg: On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court of India ruled that viewing, storing or possessing child sexual abuse material is an offence under Section 15 of the POCSO Act and Section 67B of the IT Act, overturning a Madras High Court ruling; it told all courts to stop using the term 'child pornography' and urged Parliament to amend the POCSO Act to replace it with 'child sexual exploitation and abuse material' (CSEAM).

facts.caveat: Refer to it as the Just Rights for Children Alliance case (2024); do not name the accused, who has not been convicted. Under Section 15(1) the offence is storing or possessing such material without deleting, destroying or reporting it; the court read possession broadly, including constructive possession. The case began with an NCMEC CyberTipline report routed through NCRB to Tamil Nadu police.

text.en: On 26 December 2023, citing growing concern over AI deepfakes, MeitY issued an advisory directing all platforms to tell users clearly, at registration, at every login and while uploading, what content is prohibited under Rule 3(1)(b) of the IT Rules and what penalties apply.
text.hg: On 26 December 2023, citing growing concern over AI deepfakes, MeitY issued an advisory directing all platforms to tell users clearly, at registration, at every login and while uploading, what content is prohibited under Rule 3(1)(b) of the IT Rules and what penalties apply.

facts.caveat: An advisory is guidance to platforms; binding rules on synthetic media came with the IT Amendment Rules, 2026.

text.en: In 2015 India's telecom department ordered internet providers to block 857 pornographic websites, but within days, after public outrage, it modified the order and asked providers to block only sites carrying child sexual abuse material.
text.hg: 2015 mein India ke telecom department ne internet providers ko 857 pornographic websites block karne ka order diya, lekin public outrage ke baad kuch hi dinon mein order badalkar providers se sirf child sexual abuse material wali sites block karne ko kaha.

facts.caveat: BBC reported the block on 3 August 2015 and the reversal on 5 August 2015 ('India lifts porn ban after widespread outrage', source bbc-india-lifts-porn-ban-2015).

text.en: In July 2015 the Supreme Court refused an interim order to block pornographic websites in a PIL filed by advocate Kamlesh Vaswani, with Chief Justice H.L. Dattu observing that the court could not stop an adult from watching pornography in the privacy of their room, citing personal liberty under Article 21.
text.hg: July 2015 mein Supreme Court ne advocate Kamlesh Vaswani ki PIL (janhit yachika) par pornographic websites block karne ka interim order dene se inkaar kar diya. Chief Justice H.L. Dattu ne Article 21 ke tahat personal liberty ka hawala dete hue kaha ki court kisi adult ko apne kamre ki privacy mein pornography dekhne se nahin rok sakta.

facts.caveat: Watching adult pornography in private is not an offence in India; producing, distributing or publishing obscene material is.

text.en: In July 2025 the government ordered intermediaries to disable access to 25 streaming platforms, including Ullu, ALTT and Desiflix, covering 26 websites and 14 apps, for hosting obscene and sexually explicit content, using powers under the IT Act, 2000 and the IT Rules, 2021.
text.hg: In July 2025 the government ordered intermediaries to disable access to 25 streaming platforms, including Ullu, ALTT and Desiflix, covering 26 websites and 14 apps, for hosting obscene and sexually explicit content, using powers under the IT Act, 2000 and the IT Rules, 2021.

facts.caveat: The blocking order was passed on 23 July 2025 under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act (Hindustan Times). In March 2024 the I&B Ministry had blocked 18 OTT platforms (19 websites, 10 apps and 57 social media accounts) for obscene content (Times of India, 14 March 2024).

text.en: In February 2026 the Information and Broadcasting Ministry blocked five more streaming platforms (MoodXVIP, Koyal Playpro, Digi Movieplex, Feel and Jugnu) for allegedly obscene content, and officials said platforms blocked in March 2024 had resurfaced on new domains.
text.hg: February 2026 mein Information and Broadcasting Ministry ne kathit taur par obscene content ke chalte paanch aur streaming platforms (MoodXVIP, Koyal Playpro, Digi Movieplex, Feel aur Jugnu) block kiye. Officials ne kaha ki March 2024 mein block kiye gaye platforms naye domains par phir se saamne aa gaye the.

facts.caveat: Shows the limits of domain blocking: blocked services reappear on new domains.

text.en: NCMEC analysed just over 32 million reports of child sexual abuse material in 2022, an 87% increase on 2019, according to the WeProtect Global Alliance's Global Threat Assessment 2023.
text.hg: WeProtect Global Alliance ki Global Threat Assessment 2023 ke mutabik, NCMEC ne 2022 mein child sexual abuse material ki 32 million se thodi zyada reports ka analysis kiya, jo 2019 ke muqable 87% zyada tha.

facts.caveat: Report volume reflects detection and reporting, not prevalence alone.

text.en: Offenders in social gaming environments can draw children into high-risk grooming conversations within 19 seconds of the first message, and within 45 minutes on average, according to risk-intelligence data cited in WeProtect's Global Threat Assessment 2023.
text.hg: WeProtect ki Global Threat Assessment 2023 mein quote kiye gaye risk-intelligence data ke mutabik, social gaming environments mein offenders pehle message ke 19 second ke andar hi bachchon ko high-risk grooming conversations mein kheench sakte hain, aur average 45 minute ke andar.

facts.caveat: Figure from the risk-intelligence firm Crisp, cited by WeProtect.

text.en: In an analysis of more than 6,500 first-hand accounts by sexual extortion victims, the Canadian Centre for Child Protection found that 98% were male where gender could be identified, WeProtect's Global Threat Assessment 2023 reports.
text.hg: WeProtect ki Global Threat Assessment 2023 ke mutabik, Canadian Centre for Child Protection ne sexual extortion ke victims ke 6,500 se zyada first-hand accounts (khud ke anubhav) ka analysis kiya aur paaya ki jin cases mein gender pata chal saka, unmein 98% male the.

facts.caveat: Self-selected public posts, not a representative survey.

text.en: The Internet Watch Foundation recorded a 360% increase in 'self-generated' sexual imagery of children aged 7 to 10 from the first half of 2020 to 2022, according to WeProtect's Global Threat Assessment 2023.
text.hg: WeProtect ki Global Threat Assessment 2023 ke mutabik, Internet Watch Foundation ne 2020 ki pehli chhamahi (first half) se 2022 tak 7 se 10 saal ke bachchon ki 'self-generated' sexual imagery mein 360% ki badhotri darj ki.

facts.caveat: 'Self-generated' imagery is usually produced under grooming or coercion; the term does not imply consent.

text.en: A senior Maharashtra Cyber police officer estimated in a March 2022 op-ed that fewer than 0.5% of sextortion cases in India are registered as FIRs, and linked the silence to victims' shame and social stigma; sextortion has no separate crime category in NCRB data.
text.hg: A senior Maharashtra Cyber police officer estimated in a March 2022 op-ed that fewer than 0.5% of sextortion cases in India are registered as FIRs, and linked the silence to victims' shame and social stigma; sextortion has no separate crime category in NCRB data.

facts.caveat: An official's estimate in an op-ed, not a measured rate. NCRB tables (9A.3, 9A.4) have no sextortion head; such cases are filed under extortion, blackmail, IT Act s.67/67A or fraud.

text.en: Police in Rajasthan's Alwar district caught more than 60 sextortion gangs in the year to September 2021, and 13 of those caught were minors aged 14 to 16, Dainik Bhaskar reported; a senior Maharashtra Cyber police officer wrote in March 2022 that such rackets operate from towns such as Mewat, Bharatpur and Alwar in Rajasthan and Haryana.
