text.hg: 10 November 2023 ko Parliament ki Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne warning di thi ki Section 377 hatane se aadmiyon, transgender logon aur jaanvaron ke khilaf bina consent ke sexual offences bina saza ke reh jayenge, aur ise bana rehne dene ki recommendation ki thi; sarkar ne yeh recommendation nahi maani.

facts.caveat: Committee chaired by Brij Lal. That the recommendation was not adopted follows from the enacted BNS, which has no equivalent of Section 377.

text.en: On 14 October 2024, a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud refused to entertain a plea to make sexual offences against men and transgender persons crimes under the BNS, saying it cannot direct Parliament to create an offence.
text.hg: 14 October 2024 ko Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki aguwai wali Supreme Court bench ne aadmiyon aur transgender logon ke khilaf sexual offences ko BNS ke tahat crime banane ki maang wali petition par sunwai se inkaar kar diya, aur kaha ki court Parliament ko koi offence banane ka direction nahi de sakta.

facts.caveat: Pooja Sharma v. Union of India, W.P.(Crl.) No. 398/2024; the petitioner was allowed to make a representation to the Union.

text.en: On 28 August 2024, the Delhi High Court asked the Centre to decide within six months on a demand to restore punishment for non-consensual "unnatural" sex, remarking that "there can't be a vacuum to an offence".
text.hg: 28 August 2024 ko Delhi High Court ne Centre se kaha ki woh bina consent ke "unnatural" sex ke liye saza wapas laane ki maang par chhah mahine ke andar faisla kare, aur remark kiya ki "there can't be a vacuum to an offence", yaani kisi offence ko lekar kanoon mein khaali jagah nahi ho sakti.

facts.caveat: PIL by advocate Gantavya Gulati; Bar and Bench report dated 28 August 2024.

text.en: In March 2026, the Delhi High Court revived the PIL on the missing offence after about a year and a half without a government decision, saying "the decision is nowhere in sight", and ordered the Centre to file an affidavit within four weeks.
text.hg: March 2026 mein Delhi High Court ne kanoon se gayab is offence par PIL ko phir se khola, kyunki lagbhag dedh saal baad bhi sarkar ka koi faisla nahi aaya tha; court ne kaha ki "the decision is nowhere in sight" aur Centre ko chaar hafte ke andar affidavit file karne ka order diya.

facts.caveat: PTI report dated 20 March 2026; bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia; petitioner Gantavya Gulati. In August 2026 the court said it cannot create a Section 377-like offence and that this is a question of legislative policy for Parliament (Bar and Bench, 12 August 2026); whether the PIL was formally disposed of is not confirmed.

text.en: In the Ministry of Women and Child Development's 2007 Study on Child Abuse, 53.22% of children surveyed across India said they had faced one or more forms of sexual abuse.
text.hg: Ministry of Women and Child Development ki 2007 ki Study on Child Abuse mein poore India mein survey kiye gaye bachchon mein se 53.22% ne bataya ki unhone ek ya usse zyada tarah ka sexual abuse jhela tha.

facts.caveat: Survey of 12,447 children in 13 states, conducted with UNICEF, Save the Children and Prayas; a convenience rather than nationally representative sample, so treat as indicative. The original report was read (copy at https://dylbw5db8047o.cloudfront.net/uploads/4978.pdf).

text.en: Boys made up 52.94% of the children who reported sexual abuse in India's 2007 national Study on Child Abuse, more than girls (47.06%).
text.hg: India ki 2007 ki national Study on Child Abuse mein sexual abuse report karne wale bachchon mein 52.94% ladke the, yaani ladkiyon (47.06%) se zyada.

facts.caveat: Convenience sample; see gen-mwcd-2007-csa-prevalence. The figure is a share of abused children, not a prevalence rate among boys.

text.en: Of 38,444 child victims registered under Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act (penetrative sexual assault) in India in 2022, 414 were boys and 38,030 were girls, according to NCRB data.
text.hg: NCRB data ke mutabik, 2022 mein India mein POCSO Act ke Sections 4 aur 6 (penetrative sexual assault) ke tahat register hue 38,444 child victims mein se 414 ladke aur 38,030 ladkiyan thi.

facts.caveat: NCRB Crime in India 2022, Table 4A.9 (also reported by IANS on 4 December 2023). Police data record only reported cases; abuse of boys may also be recorded under other heads. The 1% share is a calculation.

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 44% of Indian men aged 15-49 agreed that a husband is justified in beating his wife in at least one of seven situations, up from 42% in NFHS-4 (2015-16), while the share among women fell from 52% to 45%.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ke 44% Indian aadmiyon ne maana ki saat mein se kam se kam ek situation mein pati ka patni ko peetna justified hai, jo NFHS-4 (2015-16) ke 42% se zyada hai, jabki auraton mein yeh share 52% se ghatkar 45% reh gaya.

facts.caveat: Attitude data, not reported violence. Men's figure in the report table is 44.2%.

text.en: Showing disrespect to in-laws was the reason most often accepted for wife-beating in NFHS-5 (2019-21), by 31% of men and 32% of women; refusing sex was the least accepted, by 10% of men and 11% of women.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein wife-beating ki jo wajah sabse zyada accept ki gayi, woh thi sasural walon ki disrespect karna, jise 31% aadmiyon aur 32% auraton ne sahi maana; sabse kam accept ki gayi wajah sex se inkaar karna thi, jise 10% aadmiyon aur 11% auraton ne sahi maana.

text.en: In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 12.2% of Indian men aged 15-49, about one in eight, said a husband has the right to use force to have sex if his wife refuses, and 19.2% said he has the right to get angry and reprimand her.
text.hg: NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 15-49 saal ke 12.2% Indian aadmiyon ne, yaani lagbhag har aath mein se ek ne, kaha ki agar patni sex se mana kare to pati ko zabardasti sex karne ka haq hai, aur 19.2% ne kaha ki pati ko gussa hone aur patni ko daantne ka haq hai.

facts.caveat: Table 14.18 columns: get angry and reprimand (19.2), refuse financial support (13.0), use force to have sex (12.2), have sex with another woman (12.6), all four (5.5), none (72.2). Sample: 93,144 men aged 15-49.

text.en: The share of Indian men who rejected all four coercive responses to a wife refusing sex fell from 77% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 72% in NFHS-5 (2019-21).
text.hg: Patni ke sex se inkaar karne par zor-zabardasti wale chaaron responses ko reject karne wale Indian aadmiyon ka share NFHS-4 (2015-16) ke 77% se ghatkar NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 72% reh gaya.

facts.caveat: Below 50% in Punjab (21%), Chandigarh (28%), Karnataka (45%) and Ladakh (46%).

text.en: In a 2014 ICRW-UNFPA survey of 9,205 men and 3,158 women in seven Indian states, 60% of men said they had acted violently against their wife or partner at some point, and 52% of women reported experiencing some form of violence.
text.hg: Saat Indian states mein 9,205 aadmiyon aur 3,158 auraton par hue 2014 ke ICRW-UNFPA survey mein 60% aadmiyon ne kaha ki unhone kabhi na kabhi apni patni ya partner ke saath violence ki thi, aur 52% auraton ne kisi na kisi tarah ki violence jhelne ki baat kahi.

facts.caveat: States: Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana (counted as one), Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; men and women aged 18-49. The study adapts the IMAGES (International Men and Gender Equality Survey) method. 'Violence' includes emotional and economic violence.

text.en: The 2014 ICRW-UNFPA study classified 32% of surveyed Indian men as having "rigid" masculinity, 45% as moderate and only 23% as gender-equitable.
text.hg: 2014 ki ICRW-UNFPA study ne survey kiye gaye Indian aadmiyon mein se 32% ko "rigid" masculinity wali category mein, 45% ko moderate aur sirf 23% ko gender-equitable category mein rakha.

facts.caveat: The same study found 66% of men said they had more say than their partner on important decisions. The two ICRW documents differ on how many men expected their partner to agree when they wanted sex (executive summary: more than three-fourths; full report: over two-thirds), so that figure is not used.

text.en: Indian men who frequently experienced discrimination as children were four times more likely to perpetrate violence against their partners, the 2014 ICRW-UNFPA study found.
text.hg: 2014 ki ICRW-UNFPA study mein paaya gaya ki jin Indian aadmiyon ne bachpan mein aksar discrimination jhela tha, unke apne partners ke saath violence karne ke chances chaar guna zyada the.

facts.caveat: The study also links men's economic stress to higher perpetration.

text.en: Men raised in families where fathers did household chores were two times more likely to hold gender-equitable attitudes, the 2014 ICRW-UNFPA study of seven Indian states found.
text.hg: Saat Indian states mein hui 2014 ki ICRW-UNFPA study mein paaya gaya ki jin families mein pita ghar ke kaam karte the, wahan pale-bade aadmiyon mein gender-equitable soch hone ke chances do guna zyada the.

facts.caveat: Families where parents made decisions jointly were 1.4 times more likely to raise gender-equitable men.

text.en: In the 2014 ICRW-UNFPA survey in seven Indian states, 76% of men and 81% of women said it was very important to have at least one son.
text.hg: Saat Indian states mein hue 2014 ke ICRW-UNFPA survey mein 76% aadmiyon aur 81% auraton ne kaha ki kam se kam ek beta hona bahut zaroori hai.

text.en: India recorded 1,70,746 suicides in 2024, slightly down from 1,71,418 in 2023, according to NCRB's Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 2024 report released in May 2026.
text.hg: India recorded 1,70,746 suicides in 2024, slightly down from 1,71,418 in 2023, according to NCRB's Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 2024 report released in May 2026.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded data; suicides are believed to be under-reported. The NCRB PDF was not reachable by script.

text.en: Student suicides in India rose about 80% in a decade to 14,488 in 2024, and 1,23,918 students died by suicide over 2014-2024, according to NCRB data.
text.hg: Student suicides in India rose about 80% in a decade to 14,488 in 2024, and 1,23,918 students died by suicide over 2014-2024, according to NCRB data.

facts.caveat: Series: 13,044 (2022), 13,892 (2023), 14,488 (2024). The 2014 base differs between sources (8,068 in The Wire; 8,032 in Careers360), so it is not quoted; the rise is about 80% either way.

text.en: India recorded 1,71,418 suicides in 2023, a rate of 12.3 per lakh population, up 0.3% from 2022; NCRB released the 2023 report at the end of September 2025.
text.hg: India mein 2023 mein 1,71,418 suicides record hue, jo 2022 se 0.3% zyada hain, aur suicide rate 12.3 per lakh population rahi; NCRB ne 2023 ki report September 2025 ke end mein jaari ki.

facts.caveat: Family problems (31.9%) and illness (19.0%) were the main recorded causes in 2023 as reported by PTI (not independently checked).

text.en: 13,892 students died by suicide in India in 2023, 8.1% of all suicides and the highest count in a decade, up from 13,044 (7.6%) in 2022.
text.hg: 2023 mein India mein 13,892 students ki suicide se maut hui; yeh kul suicides ka 8.1% aur ek decade mein sabse badi sankhya thi, jo 2022 ke 13,044 (7.6%) se zyada hai.

facts.caveat: Maharashtra reported the most student suicides (2,046) in 2023 (Careers360).

text.en: India recorded 1,70,924 suicides in 2022 (12.4 per lakh population), including 25,309 housewives (14.8% of all suicides and 52.5% of the 48,172 women who died by suicide), 13,044 students (7.6%) and 45,185 daily wage earners (26.4%).
text.hg: India recorded 1,70,924 suicides in 2022 (12.4 per lakh population), including 25,309 housewives (14.8% of all suicides and 52.5% of the 48,172 women who died by suicide), 13,044 students (7.6%) and 45,185 daily wage earners (26.4%).

facts.caveat: Female total (48,172) is the overall total minus 1,22,724 men and 28 transgender persons; the Hindi edition prints 88,172, an evident typo. It also gives students as 13,088, while all English-language sources (ThePrint, Careers360, The Wire, Business Standard/IC3) give 13,044. Daily wage earners: 41,433 men plus 3,752 women (9 transgender persons not included).

text.en: India's National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 found that 10.6% of adults had a mental disorder at the time of the survey and 13.7% had one in their lifetime, excluding tobacco use.
text.hg: India ke National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 mein paaya gaya ki tobacco use ko chhodkar, survey ke waqt 10.6% adults ko koi mental disorder tha aur 13.7% ko zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi koi mental disorder hua tha.

facts.caveat: Survey of 34,802 adults in 12 states, conducted by NIMHANS for the Health Ministry in 2015-16. No newer national survey results were found.

text.en: The National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 estimated that nearly 150 million Indians need mental health care but fewer than 30 million seek it.
text.hg: National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 ka estimate tha ki lagbhag 150 million Indians ko mental health care ki zaroorat hai, lekin 30 million se bhi kam log yeh care lene aage aate hain.

facts.value: 150 million need care; under 30 million seek it

text.en: The National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 found treatment gaps of 28% to 83% for mental disorders and 86% for alcohol use disorders in India.
text.hg: National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 mein India mein mental disorders ke liye 28% se 83% tak aur alcohol use disorders ke liye 86% ka treatment gap paaya gaya.

facts.caveat: Except for epilepsy, all disorders had a treatment gap above 60%.

text.en: Overall mental morbidity in India was higher among men (13.9%) than women (7.5%) in the National Mental Health Survey 2015-16, and alcohol use disorder affected 9% of men against 0.5% of women, while depression and anxiety disorders were higher in women.
text.hg: National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 mein India mein overall mental morbidity (mental bimariyon ki kul dar) auraton (7.5%) ke mukable aadmiyon (13.9%) mein zyada thi, aur alcohol use disorder 9% aadmiyon mein tha jabki auraton mein 0.5% mein; wahin depression aur anxiety disorders auraton mein zyada the.

facts.caveat: Men aged 30-49 were the most affected group.

text.en: Nearly 1% of Indian adults reported high suicidal risk in the National Mental Health Survey 2015-16, rising to 1.71% in urban metros and 1.14% among women.
text.hg: National Mental Health Survey 2015-16 mein lagbhag 1% Indian adults ne high suicidal risk report kiya, jo urban metros mein badhkar 1.71% aur auraton mein 1.14% tha.

facts.caveat: Half of those at high suicidal risk had no co-occurring mental disorder.

text.en: Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 presumes that a person who attempts suicide has severe stress, bars their trial and punishment under Section 309 IPC, and obliges the government to provide care and rehabilitation.
text.hg: Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 ka Section 115 maan kar chalta hai ki suicide attempt karne wala vyakti severe stress mein hai, IPC ke Section 309 ke tahat us par trial aur saza par rok lagata hai, aur sarkar par uski care aur rehabilitation ki zimmedari daalta hai.

facts.caveat: Checked against the Gazette text of the Act (PRS copy).

text.en: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 no longer has a general offence of attempted suicide; Section 226 punishes only an attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain a public servant, with simple imprisonment of up to one year, a fine, or community service.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 mein ab attempted suicide ka koi general offence nahi hai; Section 226 sirf us suicide attempt ko punish karta hai jo kisi public servant ko majboor karne ya rokne ke liye kiya jaye, aur iski saza ek saal tak ki simple imprisonment, fine ya community service hai.

facts.caveat: Replaces Section 309 IPC from 1 July 2024. A full-text search of the official BNS finds no other attempted-suicide offence (only abetment of suicide, Sections 107-108, and cruelty, Section 86).

text.en: About 840 million women and girls worldwide, nearly 1 in 3 (31.6%), have experienced physical or sexual violence from an intimate partner or sexual violence from a non-partner in their lifetime, including about 263 million (8% of women aged 15 and older) sexually assaulted by a non-partner, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, duniya bhar mein lagbhag 840 million auraton aur ladkiyon ne, yaani lagbhag har 3 mein se 1 (31.6%) ne, apni zindagi mein kisi intimate partner se physical ya sexual violence ya kisi non-partner se sexual violence jheli hai; inmein lagbhag 263 million (15 saal aur usse zyada umar ki 8% auratein) aisi hain jin par kisi non-partner ne sexual assault kiya.

facts.caveat: WHO fact sheet dated 18 June 2026 using 2023 estimates (published 2025). UN Women states the same 840 million as about 30% of women aged 15 and older. Not directly comparable with the 2018 estimate (736 million) because of new data and methods.

text.en: Globally, 25.8% of women aged 15-49 have experienced physical or sexual violence from a husband or male intimate partner at least once in their lives, and Southern Asia is among the worst regions at 31%, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, duniya bhar mein 15-49 saal ki 25.8% auraton ne zindagi mein kam se kam ek baar pati ya male intimate partner se physical ya sexual violence jheli hai, aur 31% ke saath Southern Asia sabse bure regions mein se ek hai.

facts.caveat: Regional figures as summarised from the fact sheet; the exact age base of the regional estimates was not verified.

text.en: WHO's previous estimates, released on 9 March 2021 using 2000-2018 data, found that about 736 million women, 1 in 3, had faced physical or sexual violence in their lifetime, and that 35% of women aged 15-49 in Southern Asia had faced intimate partner violence.
text.hg: WHO ke pichhle estimates, jo 9 March 2021 ko 2000-2018 ke data ke aadhaar par jaari hue the, mein paaya gaya tha ki lagbhag 736 million auraton ne, yaani har 3 mein se 1 ne, apni zindagi mein physical ya sexual violence jheli thi, aur Southern Asia mein 15-49 saal ki 35% auraton ne intimate partner violence jheli thi.

facts.caveat: Superseded by the 2023 estimates (840 million); different data and methods, so do not read the change as a trend.

text.en: Around 50,000 women and girls were killed by intimate partners or other family members worldwide in 2024, about 60% of all intentional killings of women and girls, or an average of 137 a day, according to UNODC and UN Women.
text.hg: UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik, 2024 mein duniya bhar mein lagbhag 50,000 auraton aur ladkiyon ki hatya unke intimate partners ya family ke doosre members ne ki; yeh auraton aur ladkiyon ki sabhi intentional killings ka lagbhag 60% hai, yaani average har din 137.

facts.caveat: Report published November 2025. UN Women notes the 2024 figure is lower than 2023 because of differences in country data, not because violence fell; WHO's fact sheet gives 140 a day for 2023. 137 a day is roughly one every 10.5 minutes (calculation).

text.en: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 is gender-neutral towards victims: it defines a child as any person below 18 years and its offences are committed against 'a child', so boys are covered as victims.
text.hg: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 is gender-neutral towards victims: it defines a child as any person below 18 years and its offences are committed against 'a child', so boys are covered as victims.

facts.caveat: Act No. 32 of 2012, in force from 14 November 2012. NCRB recorded 414 boys among victims of penetrative sexual assault under POCSO in 2022 (gen-ncrb-2022-pocso-boys).

text.en: India's 2007 national Study on Child Abuse found that most children who faced sexual abuse did not report it to anyone, and only 26.8% of young adults who had been sexually assaulted in childhood had ever told anyone.
text.hg: India's 2007 national Study on Child Abuse found that most children who faced sexual abuse did not report it to anyone, and only 26.8% of young adults who had been sexually assaulted in childhood had ever told anyone.

facts.caveat: Convenience sample (12,447 children and 2,324 young adults in 13 states). For specific forms of abuse, between 64% and 82.2% of affected children kept quiet; of those who did tell someone, most told a parent.

text.en: Men made up 71.8% of India's suicide victims in 2022 (male-to-female ratio 71.8:28.2), and about 68% of the men who died by suicide were married, according to NCRB.
text.hg: Men made up 71.8% of India's suicide victims in 2022 (male-to-female ratio 71.8:28.2), and about 68% of the men who died by suicide were married, according to NCRB.

facts.caveat: 1,22,724 men of 1,70,924 victims (ADSI 2022, chapter 2). Police-recorded data.

text.en: Family problems other than marriage-related problems (31.7%), illness (18.4%) and marriage-related problems (4.8%) together accounted for 54.9% of suicides in India in 2022, according to NCRB.
text.hg: Family problems other than marriage-related problems (31.7%), illness (18.4%) and marriage-related problems (4.8%) together accounted for 54.9% of suicides in India in 2022, according to NCRB.

facts.caveat: Causes are as recorded by police.

text.en: In 2022, daily wage earners were the largest group among men who died by suicide in India (41,433 of 1,22,724), while housewives were the largest group among women (25,309), according to NCRB.
text.hg: In 2022, daily wage earners were the largest group among men who died by suicide in India (41,433 of 1,22,724), while housewives were the largest group among women (25,309), according to NCRB.

facts.caveat: NCRB ADSI 2022, chapter 2 (Hindi edition). Group sizes reflect the size of each group in the population, not suicide rates.

text.en: Daily wage earners were the largest single group among India's suicide victims in 2023: 47,170 deaths, about 27.5% of all suicides.
text.hg: Daily wage earners were the largest single group among India's suicide victims in 2023: 47,170 deaths, about 27.5% of all suicides.

facts.caveat: Business Standard analysis of NCRB ADSI 2023 (30 September 2025). 47,170 / 1,71,418 = 27.5%.

text.en: Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock tele-mental-health helpline (14416), was launched in October 2022 and offers counselling to anyone in need, including transgender persons.
text.hg: Tele-MANAS, the Health Ministry's free, round-the-clock tele-mental-health helpline (14416), was launched in October 2022 and offers counselling to anyone in need, including transgender persons.

facts.caveat: Government statement in a Lok Sabha reply of 19 August 2025.

text.en: In August 2025, 429 transgender persons were living in the Garima Greh shelters supported by the Social Justice Ministry, which had released Rs 8.25 crore to them under the SMILE scheme.
text.hg: In August 2025, 429 transgender persons were living in the Garima Greh shelters supported by the Social Justice Ministry, which had released Rs 8.25 crore to them under the SMILE scheme.

facts.caveat: Lok Sabha reply of 19 August 2025, when 18 Garima Grehs in 15 States/UTs were supported (see gen-garima-greh-2025).

text.en: In the 12 months before they were surveyed, 316 million women worldwide, 11% of those aged 15 and older, were subjected to physical or sexual violence by an intimate partner, WHO and UN partners estimated in November 2025; progress has been only about 0.2% a year over two decades.
text.hg: In the 12 months before they were surveyed, 316 million women worldwide, 11% of those aged 15 and older, were subjected to physical or sexual violence by an intimate partner, WHO and UN partners estimated in November 2025; progress has been only about 0.2% a year over two decades.

facts.caveat: Same 2023 estimate series as gen-who-vaw-2023-estimates. Southern Asia's past-year rate is 19% (Oceania excluding Australia and New Zealand: 38%).

title.en: Harassment at work and in public

text.en: Police in India registered 48,303 cases of assault on women with intent to outrage their modesty (Section 74 BNS / Section 354 IPC) in 2024, a rate of 7.1 per lakh women, up from 45,086 in 2023 and 44,867 in 2022.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne mahilaon ki lajja bhang karne (outraging modesty) ke iraade se un par assault (Section 74 BNS / Section 354 IPC) ke 48,303 cases register kiye, jo 2023 ke 45,086 aur 2022 ke 44,867 cases se zyada hain; yeh har lakh mahilaon par 7.1 ka rate hai.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures. The 2022 and 2023 figures here are restated for the narrower head (excluding Sections 354A-354D).

text.en: Taken together, the five sexual offences that NCRB grouped under Section 354 IPC until 2023 (assault to outrage modesty, sexual harassment, assault to disrobe, voyeurism and stalking) were registered 83,908 times in India in 2024, against 83,891 in 2023 and 83,344 in 2022, roughly 230 cases a day.
text.hg: NCRB 2023 tak jin paanch sexual offences ko Section 354 IPC ke tahat ek saath ginta tha (lajja bhang karne ke iraade se assault, sexual harassment, kapde utaarne yaani disrobe karne ke iraade se assault, voyeurism aur stalking), unhe milakar dekhein to 2024 mein India mein inke 83,908 cases register hue, jabki 2023 mein 83,891 aur 2022 mein 83,344 cases register hue the; yaani roz lagbhag 230 cases.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures. Totals are the researcher's sum of five NCRB heads; the 2023 sum (83,891) matches the single 'Sec 354' figure NCRB published in CII 2023. 'About 230 a day' = 83,908 / 366 days.

text.en: Police in India registered 15,609 cases of sexual harassment of women (Section 75 BNS / Section 354A IPC) in 2024, down from 17,544 in 2023 and 17,809 in 2022; the 2024 rate was 2.3 per lakh women.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne mahilaon ke sexual harassment (Section 75 BNS / Section 354A IPC) ke 15,609 cases register kiye, jo 2023 ke 17,544 aur 2022 ke 17,809 cases se kam hain; 2024 mein iska rate har lakh mahilaon par 2.3 raha.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures.

text.en: Police in India registered only 388 cases of sexual harassment at office premises in 2024, compared with 381 in 2023 and 419 in 2022.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne office premises mein sexual harassment ke sirf 388 cases register kiye, jabki 2023 mein 381 aur 2022 mein 419 cases register hue the.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures. Most workplace complaints go to Internal Committees under the POSH Act (a civil process) and never become FIRs, so police counts capture only a small fraction.

text.en: A new NCRB category for sexual harassment at other work premises such as shops, malls, factories and homes recorded 512 cases in India in the second half of 2024, in addition to 388 cases at office premises.
text.hg: Shops, malls, factories aur gharon jaise doosre work premises par sexual harassment ke liye NCRB ki ek nayi category mein 2024 ki doosri chhamahi (second half) mein India mein 512 cases darj hue. Yeh office premises mein darj 388 cases ke alawa hain.

facts.caveat: The category exists only for cases registered under the BNS from 1 July 2024, so it covers half a year. Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures.

text.en: Police in India registered 459 cases of sexual harassment of women in public transport in 2024, compared with 525 in 2023 and 422 in 2022.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne public transport mein mahilaon ke sexual harassment ke 459 cases register kiye, jabki 2023 mein 525 aur 2022 mein 422 cases register hue the.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures. Harassment on buses and trains is rarely reported to police, so these counts are far below the prevalence that surveys find.

text.en: In the second half of 2024 alone, police in India registered 1,469 cases of sexual harassment at public places or pathways under a new BNS category, with Odisha (549), Uttar Pradesh (184) and Tamil Nadu (136) recording the most.
text.hg: Sirf 2024 ki doosri chhamahi mein India mein police ne BNS ki ek nayi category ke tahat public jagahon ya raaston par sexual harassment ke 1,469 cases register kiye. Sabse zyada cases Odisha (549), Uttar Pradesh (184) aur Tamil Nadu (136) mein darj hue.

facts.value: 1,469 cases (July-December 2024); Odisha 549, Uttar Pradesh 184, Tamil Nadu 136
facts.caveat: Category covers BNS cases only (from 1 July 2024). Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures.

text.en: Of the 15,609 sexual harassment cases police registered in India in 2024, 12,592 (81%) were recorded at 'other places'; the rest were at public places or pathways (1,469), work premises such as shops, factories and homes (512), public transport (459), office premises (388) and shelter homes for women and children (189).
text.hg: Of the 15,609 sexual harassment cases police registered in India in 2024, 12,592 (81%) were recorded at 'other places'; the rest were at public places or pathways (1,469), work premises such as shops, factories and homes (512), public transport (459), office premises (388) and shelter homes for women and children (189).

facts.value: Other places 12,592 (81%); public places 1,469; work premises 512; public transport 459; office premises 388; shelter homes 189
facts.caveat: The public places and work premises categories exist only for BNS cases from 1 July 2024, so they cover half a year; NCRB's table labels both 'public places' and 'other places' as row 6D. text.en: Kerala recorded the most police cases of sexual harassment at office premises in India in 2024 (89), followed by Himachal Pradesh (58) and Maharashtra (57), while Rajasthan, Odisha and West Bengal recorded none.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein office premises mein sexual harassment ke sabse zyada police cases Kerala mein darj hue (89), uske baad Himachal Pradesh (58) aur Maharashtra (57) rahe, jabki Rajasthan, Odisha aur West Bengal mein aisa ek bhi case darj nahi hua.

facts.value: Kerala 89; Himachal Pradesh 58; Maharashtra 57; Rajasthan, Odisha, West Bengal 0
facts.caveat: Zero or low counts reflect reporting and recording practice, not safer offices; higher counts can signal better reporting. Several smaller states and UTs (including Manipur, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry) also recorded none. text.en: Kerala also recorded the most police cases of sexual harassment in public transport in 2024 (100), followed by Madhya Pradesh (65), Maharashtra (61) and Uttar Pradesh (54); Delhi recorded 18.
text.hg: 2024 mein public transport mein sexual harassment ke sabse zyada police cases bhi Kerala mein hi darj hue (100), uske baad Madhya Pradesh (65), Maharashtra (61) aur Uttar Pradesh (54) rahe; Delhi mein 18 cases darj hue.

NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures.

text.en: Police in India registered 9,865 cases of stalking (Section 78 BNS / Section 354D IPC) in 2024, down from 10,495 in 2023 and 10,116 in 2022, a rate of 1.4 per lakh women.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne stalking yaani peechha karne (Section 78 BNS / Section 354D IPC) ke 9,865 cases register kiye, jo 2023 ke 10,495 aur 2022 ke 10,116 cases se kam hain; yeh har lakh mahilaon par 1.4 ka rate hai.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures. Stalking became a separate offence only in 2013 (Criminal Law Amendment Act).

text.en: Police in India registered 9,338 cases of words, gestures or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman (Section 79 BNS / Section 509 IPC) in 2024, compared with 8,823 in 2023 and 8,972 in 2022.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne kisi mahila ki lajja (modesty) ka apmaan karne ke iraade se kahe gaye shabdon, kiye gaye ishaaron ya harkaton (Section 79 BNS / Section 509 IPC) ke 9,338 cases register kiye, jabki 2023 mein 8,823 aur 2022 mein 8,972 cases register hue the.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded FIRs only; NCRB counts each FIR once under its most serious offence (principal offence rule), and sexual harassment is heavily under-reported. 2024 figures combine IPC cases (to 30 June 2024) and BNS cases (from 1 July 2024). From CII 2024, NCRB shows sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking as separate heads instead of inside 'assault to outrage modesty'. NCRB warns states should not be compared purely on crime figures. Until 2023 NCRB listed this head under miscellaneous IPC crimes; from 2024 it sits under offences against women.

text.en: Courts in India completed trials in 22,796 cases of assault on women with intent to outrage modesty in 2024 and convicted in only 20.1% of them, while 3,17,491 such cases (92.3% of those on trial) were still pending at the end of the year.
text.hg: 2024 mein India ki courts ne mahilaon ki lajja bhang karne ke iraade se assault ke 22,796 cases mein trial poora kiya aur inmein se sirf 20.1% mein saza sunayi, jabki saal ke aakhir tak aise 3,17,491 cases (trial ke liye aaye cases ka 92.3%) ab bhi pending the.

facts.caveat: Conviction rate = convictions / trials completed in the year; pendency covers cases from many earlier years.

text.en: In 2024 Indian courts convicted in 41.9% of completed sexual harassment trials, 25.2% of stalking trials and 15.4% of trials for insulting a woman's modesty, while more than nine in ten such cases were still pending at year-end (1,22,888, 52,273 and 53,210 cases respectively).
text.hg: 2024 mein Indian courts ne poore hue trials mein se sexual harassment ke 41.9%, stalking ke 25.2% aur mahila ki lajja ka apmaan karne ke 15.4% cases mein saza sunayi, jabki saal ke aakhir tak aise das mein se nau se zyada cases pending the (sexual harassment ke 1,22,888, stalking ke 52,273 aur lajja ke apmaan ke 53,210 cases).

facts.caveat: Conviction rate = convictions / trials completed in the year.

text.en: On 13 August 1997, in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, a three-judge Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice J.S. Verma laid down guidelines against sexual harassment of working women and declared them binding until Parliament passed a law.
text.hg: 13 August 1997 ko Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan case mein Chief Justice J.S. Verma ki aguvaai wali Supreme Court ki teen judges ki bench ne working women ke sexual harassment ke khilaf guidelines tay kin aur kaha ki jab tak Parliament kanoon nahi banati, tab tak yeh binding rahengi.

facts.caveat: The guidelines held the field until the POSH Act replaced them in 2013 (enacted 22 April, in force 9 December). Also reported as AIR 1997 SC 3011.

text.en: The Supreme Court said the immediate cause of the Vishaka petition was the alleged brutal gang rape of a social worker in a Rajasthan village, an incident that revealed 'the hazards to which a working woman may be exposed'.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne kaha ki Vishaka petition ki fauri wajah Rajasthan ke ek gaon mein ek social worker ke saath hua alleged brutal gang rape tha, ek aisi ghatna jisne 'un khatron ko saamne la diya jinka saamna ek working woman ko karna pad sakta hai'.

facts.value: Trigger: gang rape of a social worker (village of Rajasthan)
facts.caveat: The survivor is not named here: Indian law bars identifying survivors of sexual offences (Section 72 BNS; Supreme Court, Nipun Saxena v. Union of India, 2018).

text.en: The 1997 Vishaka guidelines defined sexual harassment at work as unwelcome sexually determined behaviour, including physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, and any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.
text.hg: 1997 ki Vishaka guidelines ne kaam ki jagah par sexual harassment ko aise unwelcome sexual behaviour ke roop mein define kiya, jismein physical contact aur advances, sexual favours ki maang ya request, sexually coloured remarks, pornography dikhana, aur sexual nature ka koi bhi doosra unwelcome physical, verbal ya non-verbal conduct shaamil hai.

text.en: The Vishaka guidelines required each employer's complaints committee to be headed by a woman, to have at least half women members and to include a third party such as an NGO, to prevent pressure from senior levels.
text.hg: Vishaka guidelines mein yeh zaroori kiya gaya ki har employer ki complaints committee ki head ek mahila ho, uske kam se kam aadhe members mahilayein hon aur usmein kisi NGO jaisa koi third party bhi shaamil ho, taaki senior levels se pressure na daala ja sake.

facts.value: Woman head; at least 50% women; external third party

text.en: On 19 October 2012, in Medha Kotwal Lele v. Union of India, the Supreme Court, finding that several state governments had not complied with the Vishaka guidelines, ordered states and union territories to have complaints committees working at taluka, district and state level, gave those with only one state-wide committee two months to form more, and warned that 'laws with sloppy enforcement are not enough'.
text.hg: On 19 October 2012, in Medha Kotwal Lele v. Union of India, the Supreme Court, finding that several state governments had not complied with the Vishaka guidelines, ordered states and union territories to have complaints committees working at taluka, district and state level, gave those with only one state-wide committee two months to form more, and warned that 'laws with sloppy enforcement are not enough'.

facts.value: 19 October 2012; two months for states and UTs with a single committee
facts.caveat: Quoted from the 2023 Supreme Court judgment, which reproduces the 2012 order (reported at (2013) 1 SCC 297).

text.en: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act was enacted on 22 April 2013, more than 15 years after the Vishaka judgment, and came into force on 9 December 2013.
text.hg: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, yaani POSH Act, Vishaka judgment ke 15 saal se bhi zyada baad 22 April 2013 ko enact hua aur 9 December 2013 ko laagu hua.

facts.caveat: Some sources give 23 April 2013 (Gazette publication) as the date; 22 April is the date of assent cited by the Supreme Court.

text.en: Under the POSH Act every employer must constitute an Internal Complaints Committee headed by a senior woman employee, with at least two employee members and one external member from an NGO or a person familiar with sexual harassment issues; at least half the members must be women and members serve up to three years.
text.hg: POSH Act ke tahat har employer ko ek Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) banani hoti hai, jiski head koi senior mahila employee ho, jismein kam se kam do employee members hon aur ek external member ho, jo kisi NGO se ho ya sexual harassment ke muddon ki jaankari rakhne wala vyakti ho; kam se kam aadhe members mahilayein honi chahiye aur members zyada se zyada teen saal tak pad par rehte hain.

facts.value: Woman presiding officer; at least 2 employees + 1 external member; at least 50% women; term up to 3 years
facts.caveat: If no senior woman employee is available at the workplace, the presiding officer can be nominated from another office of the same employer or another organisation (section 4(2)(a)). PRS notes that an Internal Complaints Committee is required at each office or branch with 10 or more employees; smaller establishments are covered by the district's Local Committee.

text.en: Under the POSH Act each district's District Officer must set up a Local Complaints Committee for complaints from establishments with fewer than ten workers or where the complaint is against the employer, and complaints by domestic workers go to this committee, which must forward a prima facie case to the police within seven days.
text.hg: POSH Act ke tahat har district ke District Officer ko ek Local Complaints Committee banani hoti hai, jo un establishments ki complaints sunti hai jahan das se kam workers hain, ya jahan complaint khud employer ke khilaf ho. Domestic workers ki complaints bhi isi committee ke paas jaati hain, jise prima facie case saat din ke andar police ko bhejna hota hai.

facts.value: Local Committee for workplaces with fewer than 10 workers; police referral within 7 days for domestic workers
facts.caveat: The Act defines this body as the 'Local Committee' (section 2(i)) and courts now use that name. A domestic worker's complaint is forwarded to the police for registering a case under Section 509 IPC, now Section 79 BNS.

text.en: The POSH Act requires a written complaint within three months of the incident (or of the last incident in a series), extendable by up to three more months; the inquiry must be completed within 90 days, the report sent to the employer within 10 days, the employer must act within 60 days, and an appeal can be filed within 90 days.
text.hg: POSH Act ke tahat incident (ya silsilewar incidents mein aakhri incident) ke teen mahine ke andar likhit complaint deni hoti hai, aur yeh samay-seema zyada se zyada teen mahine aur badhayi ja sakti hai; inquiry 90 din mein poori karni hoti hai, report 10 din mein employer ko bhejni hoti hai, employer ko 60 din mein action lena hota hai, aur 90 din ke andar appeal file ki ja sakti hai.

facts.value: 3 (+3) months to complain; 90-day inquiry; 10-day report; 60-day action; 90-day appeal
facts.caveat: The committee may extend the three-month limit by up to three more months only if it records in writing that circumstances prevented the woman from complaining in time.

text.en: The POSH Act's definition of 'workplace' expressly covers private entertainment businesses, hospitals, any sports institute, stadium or competition venue, places visited in the course of work including employer-provided transport, and homes where domestic workers are employed.
text.hg: POSH Act mein 'workplace' ki definition mein saaf taur par private entertainment businesses, hospitals, koi bhi sports institute, stadium ya competition venue, kaam ke silsile mein jin jagahon par jaana pade woh jagahein (employer ki taraf se diye gaye transport samet), aur woh ghar shaamil hain jahan domestic workers kaam karte hain.

facts.value: Workplace includes entertainment, sports venues, transport, dwelling houses
facts.caveat: Clause (vi) covers any 'dwelling place or a house'; section 2(a)(ii) makes any woman employed in such a house, such as a domestic worker, an 'aggrieved woman' under the Act.

text.en: The POSH Act protects any woman 'of any age whether employed or not' who alleges sexual harassment at a workplace, and any woman of any age employed in a dwelling place or house, such as a domestic worker.
text.hg: The POSH Act protects any woman 'of any age whether employed or not' who alleges sexual harassment at a workplace, and any woman of any age employed in a dwelling place or house, such as a domestic worker.

facts.value: Covers women of any age, employed or not
facts.caveat: The Kerala High Court has orally questioned whether women who are only seeking work are covered.

text.en: An employer who fails to constitute an Internal Committee or to act on its findings under the POSH Act can be fined up to Rs 50,000, with double the punishment and possible cancellation of the business licence or registration for a repeat offence.
text.hg: POSH Act ke tahat Internal Committee na banane ya uske findings par action na lene wale employer par Rs 50,000 tak ka jurmana lag sakta hai; dobara aisa karne par double saza ho sakti hai aur business licence ya registration bhi cancel kiya ja sakta hai.

facts.value: Fine up to Rs 50,000; doubled on repeat; licence cancellation
facts.caveat: A court can take up an offence under the Act only on a complaint by the aggrieved woman or a person authorised by the Internal or Local Committee (section 27).

text.en: The POSH Act allows conciliation only at the complainant's request and forbids any monetary settlement as its basis; it also says that a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant, and that malicious intent must be established through an inquiry before any action is recommended.
text.hg: The POSH Act allows conciliation only at the complainant's request and forbids any monetary settlement as its basis; it also says that a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant, and that malicious intent must be established through an inquiry before any action is recommended.

facts.value: No monetary settlement; lack of proof is no ground for action; malice must be proved after inquiry
facts.caveat: PRS noted that the clause allowing action against complainants for false or malicious complaints could deter victims.

text.en: On 12 May 2023 a Supreme Court bench of Justices A.S. Bopanna and Hima Kohli found 'serious lapses in the enforcement' of the POSH Act a decade after it was passed, calling it 'a sorry state of affairs'.
text.hg: On 12 May 2023 a Supreme Court bench of Justices A.S. Bopanna and Hima Kohli found 'serious lapses in the enforcement' of the POSH Act a decade after it was passed, calling it 'a sorry state of affairs'.

text.en: The Supreme Court in May 2023 cited a newspaper survey of 30 national sports federations which reported that 16 of them had not constituted an Internal Complaints Committee required by the POSH Act, and that existing ones lacked members or the mandatory external member.
text.hg: The Supreme Court in May 2023 cited a newspaper survey of 30 national sports federations which reported that 16 of them had not constituted an Internal Complaints Committee required by the POSH Act, and that existing ones lacked members or the mandatory external member.

facts.caveat: The underlying Indian Express survey found 16 non-compliant federations, of which 5 had no ICC at all and 11 had defective ones (see wp-ie-nsf-icc-2023).

text.en: The Supreme Court observed in 2023 that women facing sexual harassment at work are often reluctant to report it and 'many of them even drop out from their job', partly because they do not know whom to approach and lack confidence in the process.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne 2023 mein kaha ki kaam ki jagah par sexual harassment jhelne wali mahilayein aksar iski shikayat karne se hichkichaati hain aur 'unmein se kai to naukri hi chhod deti hain', jiski ek wajah yeh hai ki unhe pata nahi hota ki kiske paas jaayein aur unhe is process par bharosa nahi hota.

text.en: In May 2023 the Supreme Court ordered the Union, all states and union territories to verify in a time-bound exercise whether every ministry, department, public sector undertaking and public body had a properly constituted complaints committee, and to publish committee members, contact details and complaint procedures online.
text.hg: May 2023 mein Supreme Court ne Centre, sabhi states aur union territories ko order diya ki woh ek time-bound exercise mein check karein ki har ministry, department, public sector undertaking aur public body mein theek se bani complaints committee hai ya nahi, aur committee members, contact details aur complaint ki process online publish karein.

facts.caveat: The directions also cover professional bodies, universities and hospitals.

text.en: The Supreme Court warned in 2023 that unless the POSH Act was strictly enforced it would 'remain an empty formality', and that women who are not assured a safe workplace 'will fear stepping out of their homes to make a dignified living'.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne 2023 mein chetaya ki agar POSH Act ko sakhti se laagu nahi kiya gaya to yeh 'ek khokhli formality bankar reh jaayega', aur jin mahilaon ko safe workplace ka bharosa nahi milega, woh 'izzat se rozi-roti kamane ke liye ghar se bahar nikalne se darengi'.

text.en: On 3 December 2024 the Supreme Court ordered every state to notify a District Officer for each district by 31 December 2024, to constitute Local Committees and government Internal Committees by 31 January 2025, and to survey public and private organisations in every district for Internal Committees.
text.hg: 3 December 2024 ko Supreme Court ne har state ko order diya ki woh 31 December 2024 tak har district ke liye ek District Officer notify kare, 31 January 2025 tak Local Committees aur sarkari Internal Committees banaye, aur har district mein public aur private organisations ka survey karke pata lagaye ki unmein Internal Committees hain ya nahi.

facts.caveat: Directions passed in the Supreme Court's continuing follow-up to its May 2023 POSH judgment (MA Diary No. 22553 of 2023), heard with a public interest petition on POSH implementation (W.P.(C) 1224/2017). The district survey report was due by 31 March 2025.

text.en: In August 2025 the Supreme Court was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed the district-wise survey of Internal Committees in private as well as government institutions that it had ordered in December 2024; on 12 August 2025 it directed states and union territories to complete the survey within six weeks with help from labour departments.
text.hg: In August 2025 the Supreme Court was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed the district-wise survey of Internal Committees in private as well as government institutions that it had ordered in December 2024; on 12 August 2025 it directed states and union territories to complete the survey within six weeks with help from labour departments.

facts.value: Only 1 of 36 states/UTs reported to have completed the survey; six-week deadline
facts.caveat: LiveLaw reported the Court orally warned it could order non-renewal of licences of non-compliant entities. '1 of 36' assumes 28 states and 8 UTs. The amicus curiae's May 2025 status report listed 13 states and UTs that had conducted or were conducting surveys including private institutions, but none except Andaman and Nicobar was reported as complete.

text.en: Compliance affidavits filed in the Supreme Court by May 2025 showed every state had appointed District Officers under the POSH Act, but Local Committee compliance was unclear in Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand and Kerala and several states gave no information on the district-level survey.
text.hg: May 2025 tak Supreme Court mein file kiye gaye compliance affidavits se pata chala ki har state ne POSH Act ke tahat District Officers appoint kar diye the, lekin Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand aur Kerala mein Local Committees ke compliance ki sthiti saaf nahi thi, aur kai states ne district-level survey ke baare mein koi jaankari nahi di.

facts.caveat: Based on the amicus curiae's status report annexed to the Supreme Court's order of 21 May 2025; Jharkhand reported Local Committees in 22 of its 24 districts and Haryana gave no details for Jind, Karnal and Nuh.

text.en: An Indian Express investigation published on 4 May 2023 found that 16 of the 30 national sports federations it reviewed (those of disciplines India contested at the 2018 Asian Games, the Tokyo Olympics and the 2022 Commonwealth Games) did not comply with the POSH Act: five, including wrestling, had no Internal Complaints Committee, four lacked the required number of members, six lacked the mandatory external member and one had two panels with no independent member.
text.hg: An Indian Express investigation published on 4 May 2023 found that 16 of the 30 national sports federations it reviewed (those of disciplines India contested at the 2018 Asian Games, the Tokyo Olympics and the 2022 Commonwealth Games) did not comply with the POSH Act: five, including wrestling, had no Internal Complaints Committee, four lacked the required number of members, six lacked the mandatory external member and one had two panels with no independent member.

facts.value: 16 of 30 federations reviewed non-compliant (5 with no ICC)
facts.caveat: Snapshot as of May 2023; some federations said they were setting up committees.

text.en: A government-appointed oversight committee that examined sexual harassment allegations made by India's top women wrestlers in 2023 flagged as a 'major finding' that the Wrestling Federation of India had no Internal Complaints Committee as required by law.
text.hg: India ki top women wrestlers ne 2023 mein jo sexual harassment ke aarop lagaye the, unki jaanch karne wali, sarkar dwara appoint ki gayi oversight committee ne ise ek 'major finding' bataya ki Wrestling Federation of India mein kanoon ke tahat zaroori Internal Complaints Committee thi hi nahi.

facts.value: No ICC at the Wrestling Federation of India (2023)
facts.caveat: The official the wrestlers accused is not named here, in line with this site's rule for people who have not been convicted; he has denied the allegations.

text.en: The Kerala government set up the three-member Justice K. Hema Committee in 2017, after the abduction and sexual assault of an actor in February 2017 and a petition by the Women in Cinema Collective, to study sexual harassment and gender inequality in the Malayalam film industry.
text.hg: Kerala sarkar ne 2017 mein Malayalam film industry mein sexual harassment aur gender inequality ka adhyayan karne ke liye teen members wali Justice K. Hema Committee banayi. Yeh committee February 2017 mein ek actor ke abduction aur sexual assault, aur Women in Cinema Collective ki ek petition ke baad banayi gayi.

facts.value: Formed 2017; 3 members (Justice K. Hema, former actor Sharada, retired IAS officer K.B. Valsala Kumari)
facts.caveat: The survivor of the February 2017 assault is not named here, as Indian law requires (Section 72 BNS).

text.en: The Hema Committee submitted its report to the Kerala government in December 2019, but it was made public only on 19 August 2024, nearly five years later, after the State Information Commission ordered its release and the Kerala High Court rejected a challenge.
text.hg: Hema Committee ne December 2019 mein Kerala sarkar ko apni report saunp di thi, lekin yeh lagbhag paanch saal baad 19 August 2024 ko hi public ki gayi, jab State Information Commission ne ise jaari karne ka order diya aur Kerala High Court ne iske khilaf di gayi chunauti khaarij kar di.

text.en: The Hema Committee report was released under the Right to Information Act after 63 pages were removed from the 295-page draft to protect the identities of witnesses and those accused.
text.hg: Hema Committee ki report Right to Information (RTI) Act ke tahat jaari ki gayi, lekin usse pehle witnesses aur accused logon ki pehchaan surakshit rakhne ke liye 295 pages ke draft se 63 pages hata diye gaye.

facts.caveat: Page counts differ slightly between outlets (BBC: 290 pages).

text.en: The Hema Committee found that an all-male 'power group' of 10 to 15 directors, producers and actors controls the Malayalam film industry, decides who stays in it and can ban even prominent figures; the committee was told that a prominent actor had called this lobby a 'mafia'.
text.hg: The Hema Committee found that an all-male 'power group' of 10 to 15 directors, producers and actors controls the Malayalam film industry, decides who stays in it and can ban even prominent figures; the committee was told that a prominent actor had called this lobby a 'mafia'.

facts.caveat: The report's findings are based on testimony and the names in it are redacted; no individuals are named here. Some outlets rounded the group to 15.

text.en: The Hema Committee called sexual harassment the 'worst evil' faced by women in Malayalam cinema, saying it 'remains shockingly rampant' and 'goes on unchecked and uncontrolled', and that men in the industry 'make open demands for sex without any qualms as if it's their birthright'.
text.hg: Hema Committee ne sexual harassment ko Malayalam cinema mein mahilaon ke saamne 'sabse badi buraai' bataya aur kaha ki yeh 'hairaan karne wali had tak bekaaboo hai' aur 'bina kisi rok-tok aur control ke jaari hai', aur industry ke purush 'bina kisi jhijhak ke khuleaam sex ki maang karte hain, maano yeh unka janamsiddh adhikaar ho'.

text.en: The Hema Committee confirmed a casting couch in Malayalam cinema: junior artists were told they would be given a chance in films if they complied with demands for sex, and women who agreed were referred to by the code name 'cooperating artists'.
text.hg: Hema Committee ne Malayalam cinema mein casting couch ki pushti ki: junior artists se kaha jaata tha ki agar woh sex ki maangein maan lein to unhe films mein mauka milega, aur jo mahilayein iske liye raazi ho jaati thin, unhe 'cooperating artists' ke code name se bulaya jaata tha.

text.en: The Hema Committee found that junior women artists on Malayalam film sets had no toilets or changing rooms, forcing them to go into the bushes and hold urine for long hours, which in some cases led to hospitalisation.
text.hg: Hema Committee ne paaya ki Malayalam film sets par junior women artists ke liye na toilets the, na changing rooms, isliye unhe jhaadiyon mein jaana padta tha aur ghanton tak peshaab rok kar rakhna padta tha; kuch maamlon mein iski wajah se unhe hospital mein bharti hona pada.

text.en: Many women approached by the Hema Committee were initially afraid to testify because they feared losing their jobs, and the panel concluded the fear was 'well-founded' and that it was concerned for the safety of witnesses and their relatives.
text.hg: Hema Committee ne jin mahilaon se sampark kiya, unmein se kai shuru mein gawahi dene se dar rahi thin, kyunki unhe apna kaam chhin jaane ka dar tha; panel ne nishkarsh nikaala ki yeh dar 'jaayaz' tha aur kaha ki use witnesses aur unke rishtedaron ki suraksha ki chinta hai.

text.en: India's #MeToo movement gathered momentum in the Hindi film industry in late 2018 and spread within weeks, as many women in the news media, films and government publicly made allegations of sexual harassment.
text.hg: India's #MeToo movement gathered momentum in the Hindi film industry in late 2018 and spread within weeks, as many women in the news media, films and government publicly made allegations of sexual harassment.

facts.caveat: Allegations are not findings of guilt, and many of the men accused denied them. This site does not name people who have not been convicted or identify women who reported harassment.

text.en: In October 2018, at the height of India's #MeToo movement, a Union minister of state filed a criminal defamation case in a Delhi court against a woman journalist who had accused him of sexual harassment; several other women also accused him, he denied the allegations, and he resigned from the government days later.
text.hg: In October 2018, at the height of India's #MeToo movement, a Union minister of state filed a criminal defamation case in a Delhi court against a woman journalist who had accused him of sexual harassment; several other women also accused him, he denied the allegations, and he resigned from the government days later.

facts.caveat: Names are withheld under this site's rules: no court has found him guilty of any sexual offence, and she is a woman who reported harassment. Allegations are not findings of guilt.

text.en: On 17 February 2021, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Ravindra Kumar Pandey of a Delhi court acquitted a woman journalist in a criminal defamation case filed by a former Union minister over her #MeToo allegation of sexual harassment, ruling that 'the right of reputation cannot be protected at the cost of the right of life and dignity of woman' guaranteed by Article 21.

facts.caveat: A trial-court ruling; the complainant's appeal was pending in the Delhi High Court as of March 2026.

text.en: In the 2021 #MeToo criminal defamation verdict, a Delhi court held that 'the woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades'.
text.hg: In the 2021 #MeToo criminal defamation verdict, a Delhi court held that 'the woman has a right to put her grievance at any platform of her choice and even after decades'.

text.en: The Delhi court in the 2021 #MeToo defamation verdict observed that sexual harassment is mostly committed 'in the close doors or privately', and that most women who suffer abuse do not speak up, often for years, because of 'The Shame' and social stigma, which takes away 'her dignity and her self confidence'.

text.en: The 2021 #MeToo defamation verdict took into consideration 'the systematic abuse at the workplace due to lack of the mechanism to redress the grievance of sexual-harassment' before the 1997 Vishaka guidelines and the 2013 POSH Act, and women's choice not to complain because of the social stigma attached to sexual harassment.

text.en: Police in India registered 504, 485 and 418 cases of sexual harassment at work or office premises in 2019, 2020 and 2021, and 607, 375 and 357 cases in public transport in the same years.
text.hg: India mein police ne 2019, 2020 aur 2021 mein work ya office premises mein sexual harassment ke 504, 485 aur 418 cases register kiye, aur inhi saalon mein public transport mein 607, 375 aur 357 cases.

facts.caveat: The 2020 and 2021 dips coincide with COVID-19 lockdowns and work from home. NCRB principal-offence rule; heavy under-reporting. CII 2024 labels the head 'at Office Premises'.

text.en: NCRB's figures for sexual harassment by place start in 2017: that year police in India recorded 479 cases at work or office premises and 599 in public transport, and in 2018 recorded 401 and 730.
text.hg: Jagah ke hisaab se sexual harassment ke NCRB ke aankde 2017 se shuru hote hain: us saal India mein police ne work ya office premises mein 479 aur public transport mein 599 cases darj kiye, aur 2018 mein 401 aur 730.

facts.caveat: No place-wise figures for 2016 ('-'). Across 2017-2024 the office-premises total is about 3,475 FIRs (researcher's sum of 479, 401, 504, 485, 418, 419, 381, 388).

text.en: Police in India registered 88,259 cases under Section 354 IPC (assault to outrage modesty, including sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking) in 2019, 85,392 in 2020 and 89,200 in 2021; stalking alone accounted for 8,810, 8,512 and 9,285.
text.hg: India mein police ne Section 354 IPC (lajja bhang karne ke iraade se assault, jismein sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism aur stalking shaamil hain) ke tahat 2019 mein 88,259, 2020 mein 85,392 aur 2021 mein 89,200 cases register kiye; inmein akele stalking ke 8,810, 8,512 aur 9,285 cases the.

facts.caveat: Figures as published in CII 2021; earlier editions may show slightly different numbers for 2019 after revisions. Principal-offence rule; under-reporting.

text.en: Police in India registered 84,746 cases under Section 354 IPC in 2016, 86,001 in 2017 and 89,097 in 2018, while recorded stalking cases rose from 7,190 in 2016 to 9,438 in 2018.
text.hg: India mein police ne Section 354 IPC ke tahat 2016 mein 84,746, 2017 mein 86,001 aur 2018 mein 89,097 cases register kiye, jabki darj stalking cases 2016 ke 7,190 se badhkar 2018 mein 9,438 ho gaye.

facts.caveat: CII 2018 notes clarifications were pending from West Bengal, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Sikkim. Taken with later editions, the Section 354 group has hovered between about 83,000 and 89,000 cases a year from 2016 to 2024.

text.en: India's female labour force participation rate (women aged 15 and above, usual status) rose from 23.3% in 2017-18 to 24.5% in 2018-19, 30.0% in 2019-20, 32.5% in 2020-21, 32.8% in 2021-22, 37.0% in 2022-23 and 41.7% in 2023-24, against 78.8% for men in 2023-24.
text.hg: India mein mahilaon ka labour force participation rate (15 saal aur usse zyada umar ki mahilayein, usual status) 2017-18 ke 23.3% se badhkar 2018-19 mein 24.5%, 2019-20 mein 30.0%, 2020-21 mein 32.5%, 2021-22 mein 32.8%, 2022-23 mein 37.0% aur 2023-24 mein 41.7% ho gaya, jabki 2023-24 mein purushon ke liye yeh rate 78.8% tha.

facts.caveat: PLFS years run July to June. 'Usual status' (principal plus subsidiary) counts women who did even subsidiary work, including unpaid help in family enterprises; much of the rise is rural self-employment (see wp-plfs-urban-cws-status-2023-24). From 2025 MoSPI moved to monthly and quarterly bulletins; a newer annual report was not found during research. The Economic Survey 2025-26 (January 2026) still cites 2023-24 as the latest annual figure.

text.en: In 2023-24 only 28.0% of urban Indian women aged 15 and above were in the labour force, up from 20.4% in 2017-18, while the rural rate nearly doubled from 24.6% to 47.6%; the female rate by current weekly status was 35.6%, and 73.5% of rural women workers were self-employed while just 7.8% had regular salaried jobs.
text.hg: 2023-24 mein India ki 15 saal aur usse zyada umar ki urban mahilaon mein se sirf 28.0% labour force mein thin, jo 2017-18 ke 20.4% se zyada hai, jabki rural mahilaon ka rate lagbhag double hokar 24.6% se 47.6% ho gaya; current weekly status ke hisaab se mahilaon ka rate 35.6% tha, aur rural working women mein se 73.5% self-employed thin, jabki sirf 7.8% ke paas regular salaried naukri thi.

facts.value: Urban women 28.0% (20.4% in 2017-18); rural women 47.6% (24.6% in 2017-18); female CWS 35.6%; rural women workers: 73.5% self-employed, 7.8% regular wage
facts.caveat: July 2023-June 2024. Urban women are the group most exposed to formal workplaces and public transport, and their participation remains low; in urban areas 49.4% of women workers are salaried.

text.en: Only 10.8% of employed rural women in India held regular wage or salaried jobs in July-September 2025, while 37.5% were own-account workers or employers and 34.2% were helpers in household enterprises.
text.hg: July-September 2025 mein India mein employed rural mahilaon mein se sirf 10.8% ke paas regular wage ya salaried naukri thi, jabki 37.5% own-account workers ya employers thin aur 34.2% household enterprises mein helpers thin.

facts.value: Regular wage 10.8%; own-account 37.5%; household helpers 34.2% (rural women, Q2 FY26)
facts.caveat: PLFS quarterly bulletin, current weekly status, age 15+. Workplace protections like POSH matter most for women in formal and salaried work, which remains a small share.

text.en: In a 2019 World Bank survey in Mumbai, 31% of 2,388 non-working women said commuting was a barrier to working, mostly because of domestic duties (19%) and childcare (13%), and only 1.6% named unsafe commuting; but as public transport worsened women shifted to costlier auto-rickshaws and taxis, a 'pink tax' on their mobility.
text.hg: Mumbai mein World Bank ke 2019 ke ek survey mein kaam na karne wali 2,388 mahilaon mein se 31% ne commuting ko kaam karne mein rukawat bataya, zyadatar gharelu zimmedariyon (19%) aur bachchon ki dekhbhaal (13%) ki wajah se, aur sirf 1.6% ne unsafe commuting ko wajah bataya; lekin jaise-jaise public transport ki haalat bigdi, mahilayein zyada mehenge auto-rickshaws aur taxis ki taraf chali gayin, jo unki mobility par ek 'pink tax' hai.

facts.value: 31% see commuting as barrier; 1.6% cite unsafe commuting; pink tax
facts.caveat: One city; the report notes Mumbai is seen as one of India's safer cities for women, so safety may weigh more elsewhere. Respondents aged 18-45; multiple answers allowed. The Economic Survey 2025-26 cites this study.

text.en: The International Labour Office estimated in 2017 that abuse, harassment or discrimination at work lowers women's probability of taking part in the labour market by 4.2 percentage points in low-income ('developing') countries, and limited access to safe transport by 16.5 points; for middle-income ('emerging') countries, the group that includes India, its estimates were 2.0 and 5.7 points.
text.hg: The International Labour Office estimated in 2017 that abuse, harassment or discrimination at work lowers women's probability of taking part in the labour market by 4.2 percentage points in low-income ('developing') countries, and limited access to safe transport by 16.5 points; for middle-income ('emerging') countries, the group that includes India, its estimates were 2.0 and 5.7 points.

facts.value: Low-income countries: -4.2 pp (abuse, harassment or discrimination), -16.5 pp (transport); middle-income countries incl. India: -2.0 pp, -5.7 pp
facts.caveat: Cross-country estimates from ILO analysis of 2016 ILO-Gallup survey data, not India-specific; each compares women who named that challenge as their main one with women who named a lack of flexible hours. The World Bank's 2021 Mumbai note cites the low-income-country figures.

text.en: By early 2026 around 22 states and union territories allowed women to work night shifts in factories and 33 in commercial establishments, and 17 had lifted bans on women working in 'hazardous' industries, the Economic Survey 2025-26 reported.
text.hg: Economic Survey 2025-26 ke mutabik, 2026 ki shuruaat tak lagbhag 22 states aur union territories ne mahilaon ko factories mein night shift mein kaam karne ki ijaazat de di thi aur 33 ne commercial establishments mein, jabki 17 ne 'hazardous' industries mein mahilaon ke kaam karne par lagi rok hata di thi.

facts.value: Night work in factories ~22 states/UTs; commercial establishments 33; hazardous-industry bans lifted in 17
facts.caveat: Night-shift permissions usually come with employer duties (transport, CCTV, security); Uttar Pradesh's rules require employer-provided transport, CCTV and security personnel.

text.en: In a Jagori study of 270 women domestic workers in Delhi-NCR, surveyed between May and November 2024, 45% said they felt very unsafe in the city at night (a further 17% felt somewhat unsafe) and 24% had experienced sexual harassment in the previous two years; those earning under Rs 5,000 a month spent about 20% of their income on commuting.
text.hg: In a Jagori study of 270 women domestic workers in Delhi-NCR, surveyed between May and November 2024, 45% said they felt very unsafe in the city at night (a further 17% felt somewhat unsafe) and 24% had experienced sexual harassment in the previous two years; those earning under Rs 5,000 a month spent about 20% of their income on commuting.

facts.value: 45% very unsafe at night (62% somewhat or very unsafe); 24% harassed in 2 years; 20% of income on commuting (n=270)
facts.caveat: Small sample (270 women) in one region; not representative of all women. Jagori's website summary and some news reports give 65% for feeling unsafe at night and call it a 2023 study, but in the published report (March 2025) 65% is the share who felt very unsafe in parks at night, and the survey ran from May to November 2024.

text.en: Under the Nirbhaya Fund, the Centre approved Safe City projects in eight cities (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow and Mumbai) to make public places safer for women through better urban infrastructure and faster access to police.
text.hg: Nirbhaya Fund ke tahat Centre ne aath shehron (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow aur Mumbai) mein Safe City projects approve kiye, taaki behtar urban infrastructure aur police tak jaldi pahunch ke zariye public jagahon ko mahilaon ke liye zyada safe banaya ja sake.

facts.caveat: Total sanctioned cost not confirmed during research.

text.en: Safe City projects in eight cities had received Rs 1,686.73 crore from India's Nirbhaya Fund by July 2026, the largest of three schemes, with One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) and fast-track courts for rape and POCSO cases (Rs 1,234.55 crore), that together took 63% of all money released.
text.hg: July 2026 tak aath shehron ke Safe City projects ko India ke Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 1,686.73 crore mil chuke the. Yeh un teen schemes mein sabse badi rakam thi, jinmein baaki do hain One Stop Centres (Rs 1,299.10 crore) aur rape aur POCSO cases ke liye fast-track courts (Rs 1,234.55 crore); in teenon ko milakar jaari hui kul rakam ka 63% mila.

facts.value: Rs 1,686.73 crore (Safe City); 63% of releases for three schemes
facts.caveat: Based on a Rajya Sabha written reply reported by ThePrint; the reply combines 'released' and 'utilised' into one figure.

text.en: Of Rs 7,990.85 crore set aside for India's Nirbhaya Fund since 2013-14, Rs 1,287.83 crore (about 16%) remained unutilised in July 2026, and the 2025-26 allocation of Rs 278 crore was the lowest in the fund's history.
text.hg: 2013-14 se India ke Nirbhaya Fund ke liye rakhe gaye Rs 7,990.85 crore mein se Rs 1,287.83 crore (lagbhag 16%) July 2026 tak istemaal nahi hue the, aur 2025-26 ka Rs 278 crore ka allocation fund ke itihaas mein sabse kam tha.

facts.value: Rs 1,287.83 crore unspent (16%); 2025-26 allocation Rs 278 crore
facts.caveat: Government says allocations account for the unspent balance already in the non-lapsable corpus.

text.en: Several Nirbhaya Fund projects had spent nothing by July 2026, according to a Rajya Sabha reply: an AI-based facial recognition pilot at seven railway stations and a Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men were listed as 'ongoing' with zero spending, while a proposal for CCTV cameras at village panchayats was still awaiting financial approval.
text.hg: Several Nirbhaya Fund projects had spent nothing by July 2026, according to a Rajya Sabha reply: an AI-based facial recognition pilot at seven railway stations and a Panchayati Raj programme to sensitise men were listed as 'ongoing' with zero spending, while a proposal for CCTV cameras at village panchayats was still awaiting financial approval.

facts.caveat: PIB's March 2025 release listed the railway facial-recognition project at 7 major stations among projects 'implemented', which sits oddly with the zero-spending status reported to Rajya Sabha in July 2026.

text.en: On 10 September 2024 the Kerala High Court asked why the state government had been 'inactive or silent' on the Hema Committee report since 31 December 2019, even though the police chief had a copy from February 2021, and ordered the unredacted report handed to a Special Investigation Team.
text.hg: 10 September 2024 ko Kerala High Court ne poochha ki state government 31 December 2019 se Hema Committee report par 'inactive ya chup' kyon rahi, jabki February 2021 se police chief ke paas iski ek copy thi; court ne bina kaat-chhaant wali (unredacted) report ek Special Investigation Team (SIT) ko saunpne ka order diya.

facts.value: Report with state from 31 Dec 2019; DGP copy Feb 2021; HC order 10 Sept 2024
facts.caveat: Special Bench of Justices A.K. Jayasankaran Nambiar and C.S. Sudha (WP(C) 29846/2024).

text.en: The Kerala High Court has orally remarked that the POSH Act does not cover sexual harassment faced by women who are seeking employment, and on 8 October 2025 the Kerala government told the court that a draft law for the entertainment industry would go to the state cabinet in the first week of November and that the SIT investigation was over.
text.hg: The Kerala High Court has orally remarked that the POSH Act does not cover sexual harassment faced by women who are seeking employment, and on 8 October 2025 the Kerala government told the court that a draft law for the entertainment industry would go to the state cabinet in the first week of November and that the SIT investigation was over.

facts.value: Draft law expected before Council of Ministers in November 2025
facts.caveat: The court's remark was made orally, not in a ruling; the Act itself defines an 'aggrieved woman' at a workplace as a woman 'of any age whether employed or not', so whether job-seekers are covered is contested. Whether the draft law was approved or enacted after November 2025, and how many SIT cases ended in chargesheets, was not confirmed.

text.en: The Women in Cinema Collective went to the Kerala High Court in 2018 arguing that the Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) was bound by the Vishaka guidelines and the POSH Act to have an Internal Complaints Committee or grievance cell, and had none; by 2022 the collective said AMMA and the Cine and TV Artists Association still had none.
text.hg: The Women in Cinema Collective went to the Kerala High Court in 2018 arguing that the Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA) was bound by the Vishaka guidelines and the POSH Act to have an Internal Complaints Committee or grievance cell, and had none; by 2022 the collective said AMMA and the Cine and TV Artists Association still had none.

facts.caveat: Status as reported in February 2022.
