On 17 March 2022 the Kerala High Court held that film associations such as AMMA are not the employers of actors and must have an Internal Complaints Committee only for their own office staff, that each film's production unit must have one, and recorded that AMMA had volunteered to set one up (see wp-kerala-hc-film-units-icc-2022).

text.en: On 17 March 2022, deciding petitions filed by the Women in Cinema Collective in 2018, the Kerala High Court held that each film's production unit is a workplace that must have an Internal Complaints Committee under the POSH Act if it engages more than 10 workers, and recorded that the actors' association AMMA had volunteered to set up a committee.
text.hg: On 17 March 2022, deciding petitions filed by the Women in Cinema Collective in 2018, the Kerala High Court held that each film's production unit is a workplace that must have an Internal Complaints Committee under the POSH Act if it engages more than 10 workers, and recorded that the actors' association AMMA had volunteered to set up a committee.

facts.caveat: Division Bench of Chief Justice S. Manikumar and Justice Shaji P. Chaly. The same judgment held that political parties, which have no employer-employee relationship with members, are not required to form Internal Complaints Committees.

text.en: On 20 August 2024, after the rape and murder of a trainee doctor at R.G. Kar Medical College Hospital in Kolkata, the Supreme Court set up a National Task Force on the safety of medical professionals, with Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud saying 'if women cannot go to a place of work and feel safe, we are denying them equal opportunity'.
text.hg: Kolkata ke R.G. Kar Medical College Hospital mein ek trainee doctor ke rape aur murder ke baad, 20 August 2024 ko Supreme Court ne medical professionals ki safety par ek National Task Force banayi. Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ne kaha, 'agar mahilayein kaam ki jagah par jaakar khud ko safe mehsoos nahi kar saktin, to hum unhe barabari ke mauke se vanchit kar rahe hain'.

facts.caveat: The Chief Justice's words were spoken in court and reports differ slightly (Al Jazeera: 'If women cannot go to a place of work and be safe, then we are denying them the basic conditions of equality'). The victim is not named here, as Indian law requires (Section 72 BNS).

text.en: Only 22% of women and 31% of men aged 15-49 in India had comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS in 2019-21, according to the fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5).
text.hg: Paanchve National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) ke mutabik, 2019-21 mein India mein 15-49 saal ke logon mein sirf 22% mahilaon aur 31% purushon ko HIV/AIDS ki comprehensive jaankari thi.

facts.caveat: 'Comprehensive knowledge' is a strict composite: knowing that condoms and one faithful uninfected partner reduce risk, that a healthy-looking person can have HIV, and rejecting two misconceptions. Survey fieldwork ran 2019-21.

text.en: Only 20.1% of young women and 28.5% of young men aged 15-24 in India had comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS in 2019-21, down from 22% and 32% in NFHS-4 (2015-16).
text.hg: 2019-21 mein India mein 15-24 saal ke yuvaon mein sirf 20.1% young women aur 28.5% young men ko HIV/AIDS ki comprehensive jaankari thi; yeh NFHS-4 (2015-16) ke 22% aur 32% se kam hai.

facts.value: 20.1% of women and 28.5% of men age 15-24 (NFHS-5); 22% and 32% (NFHS-4)
facts.caveat: Survey data (self-reported answers to prompted questions). The NFHS-4 to NFHS-5 decline is small and the report calls it marginal.

text.en: Only 54.4% of young women aged 15-24 in India knew where to get a condom in 2019-21, against 87.3% of young men, according to NFHS-5.
text.hg: NFHS-5 ke mutabik, 2019-21 mein India mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 54.4% young women ko pata tha ki condom kahan se mil sakta hai, jabki young men mein yeh figure 87.3% tha.

facts.value: 54.4% of women vs 87.3% of men age 15-24
facts.caveat: For men only, anyone who used a condom in the past year is counted as knowing a source, which slightly inflates the male figure.

text.en: Among young women aged 15-24 in India, comprehensive HIV knowledge tracks privilege: in 2019-21 it was 8.7% among those with no schooling against 28.0% among those with 12 or more years of school, 11.6% among those in the poorest fifth of households against 29.2% in the richest fifth, and 18.2% among Scheduled Caste young women.
text.hg: Among young women aged 15-24 in India, comprehensive HIV knowledge tracks privilege: in 2019-21 it was 8.7% among those with no schooling against 28.0% among those with 12 or more years of school, 11.6% among those in the poorest fifth of households against 29.2% in the richest fifth, and 18.2% among Scheduled Caste young women.

facts.value: Young women 15-24: 8.7% (no schooling) vs 28.0% (12+ years); 11.6% (lowest wealth quintile) vs 29.2% (highest); 18.2% (Scheduled Caste)
facts.caveat: Survey data; caste, schooling and wealth overlap, so these gradients are not independent effects.

text.en: In 2019-21 only 10% of young women aged 15-24 in Bihar and 12% in Uttar Pradesh and Tripura had comprehensive knowledge of HIV, compared with 69% in Mizoram; among young men it ranged from 14% in West Bengal and Meghalaya to 73% in Goa.
text.hg: 2019-21 mein Bihar mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 10% young women aur Uttar Pradesh aur Tripura mein sirf 12% young women ko HIV ki comprehensive jaankari thi, jabki Mizoram mein yeh figure 69% tha; young men mein yeh West Bengal aur Meghalaya ke 14% se lekar Goa ke 73% tak tha.

facts.value: Bihar 10%, UP 12%, Mizoram 69% (young women); West Bengal/Meghalaya 14%, Goa 73% (young men)
facts.caveat: State estimates for small states have wider confidence intervals.

text.en: In 2019-21 nearly half of Indian women aged 15-49 (46%) did not know that HIV cannot be transmitted by mosquito bites, and 55% did not know it cannot spread by sharing food with a person who has AIDS.
text.hg: 2019-21 mein 15-49 saal ki lagbhag aadhi Indian mahilaon (46%) ko yeh nahi pata tha ki machchhar ke kaatne se HIV nahi phail sakta, aur 55% ko yeh nahi pata tha ki jis insaan ko AIDS hai, uske saath khana share karne se yeh nahi phail sakta.

facts.value: 54% of women know HIV is not spread by mosquito bites; 45% know it is not spread by sharing food (men: 64% and 59%)
facts.caveat: The 46% and 55% figures are complements of the published 54% and 45%; they include women who answered wrongly and those who said they did not know.

text.en: The UN's International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education (revised 2018), whose evidence chapter rests mainly on two UNESCO-commissioned reviews (a 2008 review of 87 studies and a 2016 University of Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised controlled trials), states that sexuality education, in or out of school, does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI/HIV infection rates.
text.hg: The UN's International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education (revised 2018), whose evidence chapter rests mainly on two UNESCO-commissioned reviews (a 2008 review of 87 studies and a 2016 University of Oxford review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised controlled trials), states that sexuality education, in or out of school, does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI/HIV infection rates.

facts.value: No increase in sexual activity, risk-taking or STI/HIV rates (evidence base: 2008 review of 87 studies; 2016 review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 RCTs)
facts.caveat: Published jointly by UNESCO, UNAIDS, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women and WHO. The guidance itself notes that evidence on biological outcomes (STI/HIV rates) is limited.

text.en: According to UNESCO's 2018 guidance, curriculum-based sexuality education contributes to delayed first sex, less frequent sex, fewer sexual partners, reduced risk-taking and increased condom and contraceptive use.
text.hg: UNESCO ki 2018 ki guidance ke mutabik, curriculum-based sexuality education se pehla sex der se hone, kam baar sex karne, kam sexual partners hone, risk-taking ghatne aur condom aur contraceptives ka istemaal badhne mein madad milti hai.

facts.caveat: Effects depend on programmes being comprehensive and delivered as intended; most trials are from outside India.

text.en: UNESCO's 2018 technical guidance found that abstinence-only programmes are ineffective in delaying first sex, reducing how often young people have sex or reducing their number of partners, while programmes combining delay with condom and contraception information are effective.
text.hg: UNESCO ki 2018 ki technical guidance ne paaya ki abstinence-only programmes pehla sex taalne, young log kitni baar sex karte hain usmein kami laane, ya unke partners ki sankhya ghatane mein effective nahi hain, jabki jo programmes sex ko delay karne ke message ke saath condom aur contraception ki jaankari bhi dete hain, woh effective hain.

facts.caveat: Evidence base is largely from studies outside India.

text.en: Police in India registered 55,698 cases of crimes and atrocities against Scheduled Castes in 2024, a fall of 3.6% from 57,789 in 2023, a rate of 27.7 cases per lakh SC population.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne Scheduled Castes (SC) ke khilaf crimes aur atrocities ke 55,698 cases register kiye, jo 2023 ke 57,789 cases se 3.6% kam hai; yeh har lakh SC aabadi par 27.7 cases ka rate hai.

facts.value: 55,698 cases; rate 27.7 per lakh SC population
facts.caveat: Counts only cases registered with SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act sections; crimes by SC/ST persons against SCs, or cases where police did not invoke the Act, are excluded. Rate uses the 2011 Census SC population. Police records, not total incidence.

text.en: Registered crimes against Scheduled Castes in India rose from 50,291 in 2020 to 50,900 in 2021, 57,582 in 2022 and 57,789 in 2023, before dipping to 55,698 in 2024.
text.hg: India mein Scheduled Castes (SC) ke khilaf registered crimes 2020 ke 50,291 se badhkar 2021 mein 50,900, 2022 mein 57,582 aur 2023 mein 57,789 ho gaye, phir 2024 mein ghatkar 55,698 reh gaye.

facts.caveat: Same counting rule every year (only cases with the SC/ST Act invoked). Changes in registration can reflect reporting and policing as much as crime. 2024 data mix IPC and BNS cases (BNS in force from 1 July 2024).

text.en: Police in India registered 4,262 rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims in 2024, about 12 a day, making rape 7.6% of all registered crimes against Scheduled Castes.
text.hg: Police in India registered 4,262 rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims in 2024, about 12 a day, making rape 7.6% of all registered crimes against Scheduled Castes.

facts.value: 4,262 rape cases (7.6% of crimes against SCs)
facts.caveat: 'About 12 a day' = 4,262 / 366 days (2024 was a leap year). Only rapes registered together with the SC/ST Act are counted, so rapes of Dalit women by Dalit men, or cases where police left out the SC/ST Act, are not in this figure. The rape head also includes child rape cases under POCSO Sections 4 and 6, which are gender-neutral (in 2023 one in three SC rape cases involved a child). Sexual violence is heavily under-reported.

text.en: In 2023 police in India registered 4,214 rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims (4,261 victims): 2,835 cases involved adult women and 1,379 involved children under 18.
text.hg: In 2023 police in India registered 4,214 rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims (4,261 victims): 2,835 cases involved adult women and 1,379 involved children under 18.

facts.caveat: Counts only rapes registered together with the SC/ST (PoA) Act. One in three SC rape cases involved a child. The child category (POCSO Sections 4 and 6) is gender-neutral, so it is not limited to girls.

text.en: Among states, Uttar Pradesh (645), Rajasthan (630), Madhya Pradesh (560) and Maharashtra (504) registered the most rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims in 2023; Rajasthan's rate of 5.2 per lakh SC population was more than twice the national rate of 2.1.
text.hg: States mein 2023 mein Scheduled Caste (SC) victims wale rape ke sabse zyada cases Uttar Pradesh (645), Rajasthan (630), Madhya Pradesh (560) aur Maharashtra (504) mein register hue; Rajasthan ka rate, yaani har lakh SC aabadi par 5.2, national rate 2.1 se double se bhi zyada tha.

facts.value: UP 645; Rajasthan 630 (rate 5.2); MP 560 (4.9); Maharashtra 504 (3.8); India rate 2.1
facts.caveat: NCRB warns that states should not be compared purely on crime figures; higher numbers can reflect better registration. Rajasthan's rate is not the highest: Kerala recorded 6.9 rapes per lakh SC population (210 cases), the highest among states.

text.en: In 2023 Indian courts convicted the accused in only 508 rape cases involving Scheduled Caste victims while acquitting in 1,073; the conviction rate was 30.5% and 20,622 cases (92.3%) were still pending trial at the end of the year.
text.hg: 2023 mein India ki courts ne Scheduled Caste (SC) victims wale rape ke sirf 508 cases mein accused ko saza sunayi, jabki 1,073 cases mein accused bari hue; conviction rate 30.5% raha aur saal ke end mein 20,622 cases (92.3%) ka trial ab bhi pending tha.

facts.value: Conviction rate 30.5%; 508 convicted, 1,073 acquitted, 86 discharged; 20,622 pending (92.3%)
facts.caveat: Conviction rate = convictions / trials completed in that year, mostly for cases filed in earlier years. Acquittals can reflect hostile witnesses, delay and pressure on survivors as well as weak cases.

text.en: Of all crimes against Scheduled Castes tried in India in 2023, only 31.9% of completed trials ended in conviction, and 3,11,986 cases, 93.8% of the 3,32,606 cases before the courts for trial that year, were still pending at the end of the year.
text.hg: Of all crimes against Scheduled Castes tried in India in 2023, only 31.9% of completed trials ended in conviction, and 3,11,986 cases, 93.8% of the 3,32,606 cases before the courts for trial that year, were still pending at the end of the year.

facts.value: Conviction rate 31.9%; 3,11,986 of 3,32,606 cases for trial still pending (93.8%)
facts.caveat: Courts are clearing far fewer cases each year than are sent for trial, so the backlog keeps growing.

text.en: Police filed charge sheets in 81.2% of disposed cases of crimes against Scheduled Castes in 2023, and in 88.1% of rape cases with SC victims.
text.hg: 2023 mein police ne Scheduled Castes (SC) ke khilaf crimes ke jin cases ko dispose kiya, unmein se 81.2% mein chargesheet file ki, aur SC victims wale rape cases mein se 88.1% mein.

facts.caveat: Charge-sheeting rate is calculated on cases disposed of by police during the year, not on all cases registered.

text.en: Uttar Pradesh registered the most crimes against Scheduled Castes in 2023 (15,130 cases), while Madhya Pradesh (72.6 per lakh SC population) and Rajasthan (69.1) had the highest rates, more than double the national rate of 28.7.
text.hg: 2023 mein Scheduled Castes (SC) ke khilaf sabse zyada crimes Uttar Pradesh mein register hue (15,130 cases), jabki sabse ooncha rate Madhya Pradesh (har lakh SC aabadi par 72.6) aur Rajasthan (69.1) mein tha, jo national rate 28.7 se double se bhi zyada hai.

facts.value: UP 15,130 cases; MP rate 72.6; Rajasthan 69.1; Bihar 42.6; India 28.7
facts.caveat: NCRB cautions against comparing states purely on crime figures.

text.en: NCRB counts a crime as an atrocity against a Scheduled Caste person only when the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is invoked; cases registered only under the general penal code are excluded on the assumption that they were committed by SC or ST persons.
text.hg: NCRB kisi crime ko Scheduled Caste (SC) insaan ke khilaf atrocity tabhi ginta hai jab usmein SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act lagaya gaya ho; jo cases sirf general penal code ke tahat register hote hain, unhe yeh maan kar ginti se bahar rakha jaata hai ki woh SC ya ST logon ne kiye the.

facts.value: Only cases with SC/ST Act sections counted
facts.caveat: This means any case where police fail to add SC/ST Act sections drops out of the caste statistics entirely, so the published figures are a floor.

text.en: Police in India registered 1,268 rape cases with Scheduled Tribe victims in 2024, 12.7% of the 9,966 registered crimes against Scheduled Tribes.
text.hg: 2024 mein India mein police ne Scheduled Tribe (ST) victims wale rape ke 1,268 cases register kiye, jo Scheduled Tribes ke khilaf register hue 9,966 crimes ka 12.7% hain.

facts.caveat: Same counting rule as for SCs. The large fall from 2023 should be read with caution.

text.en: Since the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015, intentionally touching a Dalit or Adivasi woman in a sexual manner without consent, or using words, acts or gestures of a sexual nature towards her, knowing her caste or tribe, is a specific atrocity under Section 3(1)(w), punishable with six months to five years in prison and a fine.
text.hg: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 ke baad se, kisi Dalit ya Adivasi mahila ki caste ya tribe jaante hue, uski consent ke bina jaan-boojhkar use sexual tareeke se chhoona, ya uske prati sexual nature ke shabdon, harkaton ya ishaaron ka istemaal karna Section 3(1)(w) ke tahat ek specific atrocity hai, jiske liye chhah mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail aur jurmane ki saza hai.

facts.caveat: The amending Act received assent on 31 December 2015 (Act No. 1 of 2016) after passing the Lok Sabha on 4 August 2015 and the Rajya Sabha on 21 December 2015 (PRS bill tracker), and came into force on a date notified by the Centre (not verified). Separate from rape, which is punished under the BNS.

text.en: The 2015 amendment to the SC/ST Atrocities Act defines consent as 'an unequivocal voluntary agreement' and says a Dalit or Adivasi woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, to be regarded as consenting, and that her sexual history does not imply consent.
text.hg: SC/ST Atrocities Act mein 2015 ke amendment ne consent ko 'an unequivocal voluntary agreement' (bilkul saaf, apni marzi se di gayi razamandi) ke roop mein define kiya hai, aur kaha hai ki agar koi Dalit ya Adivasi mahila physically resist nahi karti, to sirf is wajah se use consenting nahi maana jaayega, aur uski sexual history ka matlab consent nahi hai.

facts.caveat: Applies to Section 3(1)(w)(i).

text.en: Under Section 3(1)(k) of the SC/ST Atrocities Act, as amended in 2015, dedicating a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe woman to a deity or temple as a devadasi, or any similar practice, is a punishable atrocity.
text.hg: 2015 mein amend hue SC/ST Atrocities Act ki Section 3(1)(k) ke tahat, Scheduled Caste ya Scheduled Tribe ki kisi mahila ko devadasi ke roop mein kisi devta ya mandir ko samarpit karna, ya aisi koi bhi milti-julti pratha, punishable atrocity hai.

text.en: Under Section 4 of the SC/ST Atrocities Act, as amended in 2015, a non-SC/ST public servant who wilfully neglects duties under the Act, including registering the FIR under the correct sections and filing a charge sheet within 60 days, faces six months to one year in prison.
text.hg: 2015 mein amend hue SC/ST Atrocities Act ki Section 4 ke tahat, agar koi non-SC/ST public servant is Act ke tahat apni duties ki jaan-boojhkar anadekhi karta hai, jismein sahi sections mein FIR register karna aur 60 din ke andar chargesheet file karna shaamil hai, to use chhah mahine se ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai.

facts.value: Charge sheet within 60 days; 6 months to 1 year for neglect

text.en: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 requires states to set up Exclusive Special Courts for atrocity cases, to hear trials day to day and, as far as possible, to finish them within two months of the charge sheet being filed.
text.hg: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 ke tahat states ko atrocity cases ke liye Exclusive Special Courts banana zaroori hai, jo day-to-day sunwai karein aur jahan tak ho sake, chargesheet file hone ke do mahine ke andar trial poora karein.

facts.value: Trial within 2 months of charge sheet (statutory target)
facts.caveat: Compare with NCRB data: 93.8% of atrocity cases were pending trial at the end of 2023 (fact soc-ncrb-sc-conviction-pendency-2023).

text.en: Section 15A, added to the SC/ST Atrocities Act in 2015, makes it the state's duty to protect victims, their dependants and witnesses from intimidation, coercion, inducement or violence, and gives victims the right to timely notice of court proceedings, including bail hearings.
text.hg: 2015 mein SC/ST Atrocities Act mein jodi gayi Section 15A victims, unke dependants aur gawahon ko dhamkane, dabaav, laalach ya hinsa se bachana state ki duty banati hai, aur victims ko court proceedings ki, jismein bail hearings bhi shaamil hain, samay par soochna paane ka right deti hai.

text.en: After a 2018 Supreme Court ruling required senior police approval before arrests under the SC/ST Atrocities Act and allowed a preliminary enquiry before an FIR, Parliament passed an amendment in August 2018 saying no preliminary enquiry or approval is needed and that the bar on anticipatory bail applies despite any court judgment.
text.hg: 2018 mein Supreme Court ke ek faisle ne SC/ST Atrocities Act ke tahat arrest se pehle senior police approval zaroori kar diya tha aur FIR se pehle preliminary enquiry ki ijazat di thi; iske baad Parliament ne August 2018 mein ek amendment paas kiya, jismein kaha gaya ki na preliminary enquiry ki zaroorat hai na approval ki, aur anticipatory bail par rok kisi bhi court judgment ke bawajood lagu rahegi.

facts.value: Passed Lok Sabha 6 Aug 2018, Rajya Sabha 9 Aug 2018
facts.caveat: Neither the PRS page nor the Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons names the March 2018 judgment; its title, and any later Supreme Court ruling on the amendment's validity, were not verified in this session.

text.en: Human Rights Watch's April 2018 report 'Invisible Victims of Sexual Violence' documented 17 rape and gang-rape cases involving eight girls and nine women with disabilities in eight Indian states: Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand and West Bengal.
text.hg: Human Rights Watch ki April 2018 ki report 'Invisible Victims of Sexual Violence' mein rape aur gang-rape ke 17 cases document kiye gaye, jo disabilities wali aath ladkiyon aur nau mahilaon se jude the; yeh cases India ke aath states ke the: Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand aur West Bengal.

facts.caveat: Qualitative case study, not a representative survey; HRW says the scale and geographic scope are not comprehensive. Survivor names in the report are pseudonyms and should not be reproduced.

text.en: In 15 of the 17 cases of sexual violence against women and girls with disabilities that Human Rights Watch documented in India (2018), police and court officials did not follow the legal provisions requiring them to accommodate the survivor's disability.
text.hg: Human Rights Watch ne India mein (2018) disabilities wali mahilaon aur ladkiyon ke khilaf sexual violence ke jin 17 cases ko document kiya, unmein se 15 mein police aur court officials ne un legal provisions ko follow nahi kiya, jinke tahat unhe survivor ki disability ke hisaab se zaroori intezaam (accommodations) karne hote hain.

facts.caveat: Small qualitative sample. HRW says all 17 cases took place after POCSO (2012) and the 2013 criminal law amendments but before the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.

text.en: In 16 of the 17 cases Human Rights Watch documented, disabled survivors of sexual violence and their families did not know about the disability-specific protections in India's 2013 criminal law amendments or the POCSO Act.
text.hg: Human Rights Watch ne jin 17 cases ko document kiya, unmein se 16 mein sexual violence ke disabled survivors aur unke parivaar India ke 2013 ke criminal law amendments ya POCSO Act mein disability se judi khaas protections ke baare mein nahi jaante the.

facts.caveat: Small qualitative sample.

text.en: A 2004 survey of 729 respondents across 12 districts of Odisha, cited by Human Rights Watch in 2018, found that 25% of women with intellectual disabilities had been raped and nearly all the disabled women and girls surveyed had been beaten at home.
text.hg: Odisha ke 12 districts mein 729 logon par kiye gaye 2004 ke ek survey mein, jiska hawala Human Rights Watch ne 2018 mein diya, paaya gaya ki intellectual disabilities wali 25% mahilaon ke saath rape hua tha aur survey mein shaamil lagbhag saari disabled mahilaon aur ladkiyon ko ghar par peeta gaya tha.

facts.value: 25% of women with intellectual disabilities raped (Odisha, 2004)
facts.caveat: Old, single-state survey quoted second-hand by HRW (original: Mohapatra and Mohanty, Swabhiman, 2004, not seen). India has no national prevalence data on sexual violence against disabled women.

text.en: India's 2011 Census counted 26.8 million people with disabilities (2.21% of the population), far below the WHO-World Bank global estimate of 15%, and in 2018 Human Rights Watch noted that neither the National Family Health Survey nor NCRB published data disaggregated by disability.
text.hg: India's 2011 Census counted 26.8 million people with disabilities (2.21% of the population), far below the WHO-World Bank global estimate of 15%, and in 2018 Human Rights Watch noted that neither the National Family Health Survey nor NCRB published data disaggregated by disability.

facts.caveat: HRW attributes the gap between estimates to differing definitions, stigma and under-reporting. NCRB does count one narrow slice: rape cases registered under the aggravated clause for rape of a woman with a mental or physical disability (117 in 2021; 144 of 29,536 rape cases in 2024, Table 3A.11). It does not record victims' disability status for other crimes, and there is still no national prevalence data.

text.en: Police across India registered just 56 cases under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 in 2024, the first year NCRB's Crime in India report counted offences under that law.
text.hg: 2024 mein poore India mein police ne Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 ke tahat sirf 56 cases register kiye; yeh pehla saal tha jab NCRB ki 'Crime in India' report ne is law ke tahat offences gine.

facts.caveat: Covers all offences under the RPwD Act, not only sexual ones. Rapes of disabled women are charged under the rape law, not the RPwD Act: NCRB's section-wise rape table (Table 3A.11) counted 144 cases in 2024 under the aggravated clause for rape of a woman with a mental or physical disability. Neither figure measures how much sexual violence disabled people face.

text.en: Under Section 64(2)(k) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, rape of a woman with a mental or physical disability is an aggravated form of rape, punishable with at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life imprisonment for the rest of the offender's natural life, plus a fine.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 ki Section 64(2)(k) ke tahat mental ya physical disability wali mahila ka rape, rape ka aggravated (zyada gambhir) roop hai, jiski saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai aur yeh offender ki baaki natural life tak ki umar-qaid tak ho sakti hai; saath mein jurmana bhi lagta hai.

facts.value: Minimum 10 years RI; up to life (remainder of natural life)
facts.caveat: Equivalent to Section 376(2)(l) of the IPC (added in 2013). The BNS replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024.

text.en: Under Section 173(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, if a survivor of rape or another sexual offence has a temporary or permanent mental or physical disability, police must record her complaint at her home or a place of her choice, in the presence of an interpreter or special educator, and the recording must be videographed.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ki Section 173(1) ke tahat, agar rape ya kisi aur sexual offence ki survivor ko temporary ya permanent mental ya physical disability hai, to police ko uski complaint uske ghar par ya uski chuni hui jagah par, kisi interpreter ya special educator ki maujoodgi mein record karni hogi, aur is recording ki videography karni hogi.

facts.value: FIR at home/place of choice; interpreter or special educator; videographed
facts.caveat: Carries over the 2013 amendment to Section 154 CrPC. HRW found such provisions widely ignored in practice (2018).

text.en: Under Section 183(6) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, a magistrate recording the statement of a disabled survivor of a sexual offence must use an interpreter or special educator and record it on audio-video, preferably by mobile phone, and that statement counts as her examination-in-chief so she does not have to repeat it at trial, though she can be cross-examined.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ki Section 183(6) ke tahat, sexual offence ki kisi disabled survivor ka statement record karne wale magistrate ko interpreter ya special educator ki madad leni hogi aur statement ko audio-video par record karna hoga, behtar ho ki mobile phone se; yeh statement uska examination-in-chief maana jaata hai, taaki use trial mein ise dohrana na pade, haalanki uska cross-examination ho sakta hai.

text.en: Under Section 179(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, police investigating a case cannot require a woman or a mentally or physically disabled person to come anywhere other than the place where she or he lives.
text.hg: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ki Section 179(1) ke tahat, kisi case ki investigation kar rahi police kisi mahila ya mentally ya physically disabled insaan ko uske rehne ki jagah ke alawa kahin aur aane ke liye majboor nahi kar sakti.

text.en: Under Section 92(d) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, anyone in a position to dominate the will of a disabled woman or child who uses that position to exploit her sexually faces six months to five years in prison and a fine.
text.hg: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 ki Section 92(d) ke tahat, jo insaan kisi disabled mahila ya bachche ki marzi par haavi hone ki position mein ho aur us position ka istemaal uska sexual exploitation karne ke liye kare, use chhah mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail aur jurmane ki saza ho sakti hai.

facts.caveat: Act No. 49 of 2016, dated 27 December 2016. Rape itself is punished under the BNS, which carries far heavier sentences.

text.en: Section 92(f) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 makes it a crime, punishable with six months to five years in prison, to terminate a disabled woman's pregnancy without her express consent, except in severe cases of disability with a registered doctor's opinion and the guardian's consent.
text.hg: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 ki Section 92(f) kisi disabled mahila ki express consent ke bina uski pregnancy terminate karne ko crime banati hai, jiski saza chhah mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail hai; exception sirf severe disability ke woh cases hain jinmein kisi registered doctor ki raay aur guardian ki consent ho.

facts.caveat: Act No. 49 of 2016, dated 27 December 2016. The exception allows termination with a guardian's consent in 'severe cases of disability'.

text.en: Only about half of adolescent girls in India (48%) had been told about menstruation before their first period, according to a 2016 systematic review and meta-analysis in BMJ Open; the estimate pools the 88 of its 138 studies that reported on this.
text.hg: Only about half of adolescent girls in India (48%) had been told about menstruation before their first period, according to a 2016 systematic review and meta-analysis in BMJ Open; the estimate pools the 88 of its 138 studies that reported on this.

facts.caveat: Pooled estimate from studies of very different quality, places and years (very high heterogeneity, I2 98.6%); not a national survey.

text.en: A 2016 BMJ Open meta-analysis found that about a quarter (24%) of adolescent girls in India missed school during their periods, 77% were kept from religious activities such as visiting places of worship or praying, and only one in eight faced no menstrual restriction at all.
text.hg: A 2016 BMJ Open meta-analysis found that about a quarter (24%) of adolescent girls in India missed school during their periods, 77% were kept from religious activities such as visiting places of worship or praying, and only one in eight faced no menstrual restriction at all.

facts.value: 24% miss school; 77% face religious restrictions; 1 in 8 face no restriction
facts.caveat: Pooled from heterogeneous studies, mostly published before 2016.

text.en: Of 155 countries with data, 85% reported having policies or laws related to sexuality education, according to UNESCO's 2021 global status report on comprehensive sexuality education.
text.hg: Comprehensive sexuality education par UNESCO ki 2021 ki global status report ke mutabik, jin 155 deshon ka data available tha, unmein se 85% ne bataya ki unke yahan sexuality education se judi policies ya laws hain.

facts.caveat: Self-reported by governments; having a policy does not mean it is implemented.

text.en: UNESCO's 2021 global status report found that in 24 sub-Saharan African countries whose curricula were assessed, only a little more than a quarter had advanced or established content on sexuality and sexual behaviour, and that in a survey of countries in Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America, 'access to safe abortion', 'sexual orientation and gender identity' and 'online media and technology' were the topics least included in secondary-school curricula.
text.hg: UNESCO's 2021 global status report found that in 24 sub-Saharan African countries whose curricula were assessed, only a little more than a quarter had advanced or established content on sexuality and sexual behaviour, and that in a survey of countries in Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America, 'access to safe abortion', 'sexual orientation and gender identity' and 'online media and technology' were the topics least included in secondary-school curricula.

facts.value: Just over 25% of 24 assessed sub-Saharan African countries
facts.caveat: Based on SERAT curriculum reviews of 24 sub-Saharan African countries (India is not among them) and on a self-reported 2019-2020 survey of countries in Asia-Pacific, sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean, with self-defined terms such as 'extensively'.

text.en: UNESCO's 2021 global status report says sexuality education in India is left to the states and identifies Jharkhand's Udaan programme, run in schools since 2006 and reaching over one million students by September 2019, as the only at-scale, state-run initiative of its kind in the country.
text.hg: UNESCO ki 2021 ki global status report kehti hai ki India mein sexuality education states ke zimme chhod di gayi hai, aur Jharkhand ke 'Udaan' programme ko desh mein apni tarah ki akeli aisi pehal batati hai jo badi scale par aur state sarkar dwara chalayi ja rahi hai; yeh programme 2006 se schools mein chal raha hai aur September 2019 tak das lakh se zyada students tak pahunch chuka tha.

facts.value: Udaan: since 2006; >1 million students by Sept 2019
facts.caveat: UNESCO's assessment as of 2019-2021.

text.en: In 2023 the Supreme Court of India issued a Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, with a foreword by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud, to help judges identify and stop using language and reasoning based on stereotypes about women.
text.hg: 2023 mein Supreme Court of India ne 'Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes' jaari ki, jiska foreword Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ne likha tha, taaki judges mahilaon ke baare mein stereotypes par based language aur reasoning ko pehchan sakein aur unka istemaal band karein.

facts.caveat: The launch date (widely reported as 16 August 2023) was not confirmed in this session; the PDF records a clarification added on 22 August 2023 and the Supreme Court website lists the document as uploaded on 04/09/2023.

text.en: The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook tells judges to replace 'eve teasing' with 'street sexual harassment', 'forcible rape' with 'rape', 'ravished' or 'violated' with 'sexually harassed / assaulted or raped', and 'provocative clothing' with simply 'clothing'.
text.hg: Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook judges se kehti hai ki woh 'eve teasing' ki jagah 'street sexual harassment', 'forcible rape' ki jagah 'rape', 'ravished' ya 'violated' ki jagah 'sexually harassed / assaulted or raped', aur 'provocative clothing' ki jagah sirf 'clothing' likhein.

facts.value: Eve teasing -> street sexual harassment; forcible rape -> rape; provocative clothing -> clothing

text.en: The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook replaces labels such as 'chaste woman', 'fallen woman', 'harlot', 'whore', 'slut', 'seductress' and 'woman of easy virtue' with simply 'woman', 'housewife' with 'homemaker', 'spinster' with 'unmarried woman', 'unwed mother' with 'mother', 'prostitute' with 'sex worker' and 'child prostitute' with 'child who has been trafficked'.
text.hg: Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook 'chaste woman', 'fallen woman', 'harlot', 'whore', 'slut', 'seductress' aur 'woman of easy virtue' jaise labels ki jagah sirf 'woman' shabd rakhti hai; isi tarah 'housewife' ki jagah 'homemaker', 'spinster' ki jagah 'unmarried woman', 'unwed mother' ki jagah 'mother', 'prostitute' ki jagah 'sex worker' aur 'child prostitute' ki jagah 'child who has been trafficked' rakhti hai.

facts.caveat: The glossary has 42 entries plus a note on 'survivor' or 'victim' (counted in the PDF).

text.en: On whether to say 'survivor' or 'victim', the Supreme Court's 2023 handbook says both terms are applicable and that the preference of the person affected by sexual violence should be respected.
text.hg: 'Survivor' kaha jaaye ya 'victim', is sawaal par Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook kehti hai ki dono shabd applicable hain, aur sexual violence se prabhavit insaan ki pasand ka samman kiya jaana chahiye.

text.en: The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook rejects as stereotypes the beliefs that a woman who delays reporting rape is lying, that a 'real' survivor cries incessantly, that women are very likely to make false rape allegations, and that marrying the rapist restores a survivor's honour, stating that 'Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape.'
text.hg: Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook in maanyataon ko stereotypes bata kar reject karti hai ki rape ki complaint der se karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai, ki 'asli' survivor lagataar roti rehti hai, ki auraton ke rape ke jhoothe aarop lagane ki bahut zyada sambhavna hoti hai, aur ki rapist se shaadi karne par survivor ki izzat laut aati hai; handbook kehti hai: 'Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape.'

text.en: The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook calls it a stereotype that dominant-caste men would not have sex with women from oppressed castes, so their rape complaints must be false, and states that 'Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies.'
text.hg: Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook is soch ko stereotype kehti hai ki dominant caste ke mard oppressed castes ki auraton ke saath sex nahi karenge, isliye un auraton ki rape complaints jhoothi hi hongi; handbook kehti hai: 'Dominant caste men have historically used sexual violence as a tool to reinforce and maintain caste hierarchies.'

text.en: The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook recalls that in 1995 a Rajasthan trial court acquitted the dominant-caste men accused of the 1992 gang rape of a government social worker from an oppressed caste, reasoning partly that dominant-caste men would not rape an oppressed-caste woman; the outrage led to the Supreme Court's 1997 Vishaka guidelines against workplace sexual harassment.
text.hg: Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook yaad dilati hai ki 1995 mein Rajasthan ki ek trial court ne oppressed caste ki ek sarkari social worker ke 1992 ke gang rape ke accused dominant caste ke mardon ko bari kar diya tha, aur iska ek aadhaar yeh tark tha ki dominant caste ke mard oppressed caste ki aurat ka rape nahi karenge; is par utthe aakrosh (outrage) ke chalte Supreme Court ne 1997 mein workplace sexual harassment ke khilaf Vishaka guidelines di.

facts.caveat: The survivor intervened to stop a child marriage. Following this site's privacy rule, her name is not recorded here, although she has spoken publicly and the handbook names her.

text.en: The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook calls it a stereotype that able-bodied men do not want sex with disabled women and that their complaints are therefore false, noting that women whose disabilities affect communication are particularly vulnerable to sexual violence.
text.hg: Supreme Court ki 2023 ki handbook is soch ko stereotype kehti hai ki able-bodied mard disabled auraton ke saath sex nahi chahte aur isliye un auraton ki complaints jhoothi hain; handbook yeh bhi dhyaan dilati hai ki jin auraton ki disability unke communication par asar daalti hai, woh sexual violence ke prati khaas taur par vulnerable hoti hain.

text.en: In Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (2018), the Supreme Court held that a rape survivor is identified, and the law broken, even without her name, when reports give details such as her exam rank and state, or blur her face but show her relatives, neighbours or village.
text.hg: Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (2018) case mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki agar reports mein rape survivor ki exam rank aur state jaisi details di jaayein, ya uska chehra blur karke uske rishtedaar, padosi ya gaon dikhaye jaayein, to uska naam liye bina bhi uski pehchaan ujagar ho jaati hai aur kanoon tootta hai.

facts.caveat: Section 228A IPC, discussed in the judgment, is now Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

text.en: The Supreme Court ruled in December 2018 that a rape victim's identity must not be disclosed even if she is dead or of unsound mind, even with her family's consent, unless a Sessions Judge decides that disclosure is justified, noting that 'Nirbhaya' became India's most effective symbol of protest without her identity being revealed.
text.hg: Supreme Court ne December 2018 mein faisla diya ki rape victim ki identity disclose nahi ki jaani chahiye, chahe uski maut ho chuki ho ya woh unsound mind ki ho, aur family ki consent ho tab bhi nahi, jab tak koi Sessions Judge yeh tay na kare ki identity batana justified hai; court ne dhyaan dilaya ki 'Nirbhaya' apni identity ujagar hue bina hi India mein protest ka sabse effective symbol bani.

text.en: On 18 April 2018 the Delhi High Court directed 12 media houses that had revealed the identity of the eight-year-old Kathua rape and murder victim to pay Rs 10 lakh each to Jammu and Kashmir's victim compensation fund; their lawyers said they wrongly believed a dead victim could be named.
text.hg: 18 April 2018 ko Delhi High Court ne Kathua rape aur murder case ki aath saal ki victim ki identity reveal karne wale 12 media houses ko nirdesh diya ki woh Jammu and Kashmir ke victim compensation fund mein 10-10 lakh rupaye jama karein; unke lawyers ne kaha ki unhe galatfehmi thi ki mrit victim ka naam bataya ja sakta hai.

facts.caveat: The court acted suo motu. Note: The Hindu's article describes Section 228A IPC as carrying a 'minimum two years' term, which is inaccurate; the section provided up to two years.

text.en: The Press Council of India's Norms of Journalistic Conduct (2022 edition) say that when reporting rape, abduction or kidnap of women, or sexual assault on children, newspapers must not publish the victims' names, photographs or other particulars that directly or indirectly lead to their identity (Norm 42(ii), 'Caution against Identification').
text.hg: The Press Council of India's Norms of Journalistic Conduct (2022 edition) say that when reporting rape, abduction or kidnap of women, or sexual assault on children, newspapers must not publish the victims' names, photographs or other particulars that directly or indirectly lead to their identity (Norm 42(ii), 'Caution against Identification').

facts.value: Norm 42(ii), Norms of Journalistic Conduct, Edition 2022
facts.caveat: The Press Council's norms are ethical standards for the print press; the legal bans are Section 72 BNS, Section 23 POCSO and Nipun Saxena v. Union of India (2018).

text.en: India's Adolescence Education Programme (AEP) for schools was launched in 2005 by the Ministry of Human Resource Development and the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO), according to a 2023 peer-reviewed scoping review.
text.hg: India's Adolescence Education Programme (AEP) for schools was launched in 2005 by the Ministry of Human Resource Development and the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO), according to a 2023 peer-reviewed scoping review.

facts.caveat: Other accounts date the revised AEP curriculum, prepared with NACO, to 2006-07: a 2023 review in the Indian Journal of Psychological Medicine (source ijpm-joseph-cse-india-2023) says 'In 2006–2007, NACO and the Ministry of Human Resource and Development (MHRD) introduced' the AEP. Safest wording: launched 2005, curriculum rolled out 2006-07.

text.en: By May 2007 six Indian states, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka, had banned or refused to implement the new school sex education curriculum, saying it was too explicit or against Indian culture, Reuters reported.
text.hg: Reuters ki report ke mutabik, May 2007 tak Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh aur Karnataka samet India ke chhah states ne schools ke naye sex education curriculum par ban laga diya tha ya use lagu karne se inkaar kar diya tha; unka kehna tha ki yeh bahut zyada explicit hai ya Indian culture ke khilaf hai.

facts.caveat: Reuters names only five of the six states. Counts differ by source and date (see soc-aep-12-states).

text.en: In 2007 the Madhya Pradesh government said sex education had 'no place in Indian culture' and planned to introduce yoga in schools instead, Reuters reported.
text.hg: Reuters ki report ke mutabik, 2007 mein Madhya Pradesh sarkar ne kaha ki sex education ki 'Indian culture mein koi jagah nahi hai', aur uski jagah schools mein yoga shuru karne ka plan banaya.

text.en: In May 2007, as states banned sex education, Reuters reported a warning from the head of India's National AIDS Control Organisation, Sujatha Rao, that the bans put young lives at risk; addressing MPs who were also doctors, she had asked: 'Are you more concerned about culture than the lives of young people?'
text.hg: In May 2007, as states banned sex education, Reuters reported a warning from the head of India's National AIDS Control Organisation, Sujatha Rao, that the bans put young lives at risk; addressing MPs who were also doctors, she had asked: 'Are you more concerned about culture than the lives of young people?'

facts.caveat: Quote addressed to MPs who are also doctors, as reported by Reuters.

text.en: In late March 2007 the Maharashtra government banned sex education in the state's schools: after Shiv Sena and BJP legislators raised the issue in the Legislative Assembly, it banned the CBSE's sex education textbooks in the state and dropped a planned adolescence life-skills programme.
text.hg: In late March 2007 the Maharashtra government banned sex education in the state's schools: after Shiv Sena and BJP legislators raised the issue in the Legislative Assembly, it banned the CBSE's sex education textbooks in the state and dropped a planned adolescence life-skills programme.

facts.value: Ban announced in the Assembly on 30 March 2007
facts.caveat: The Hindu piece is an opinion column. The date and the cancelled programme come from a UNI wire report (https://www.oneindia.com/2007/03/30/mah-govt-bans-sex-education-books-1175265228.html), and BBC News reported the same ban. The column's claim that the ban also covered ICSE schools does not appear in the news reports and is left out.

text.en: Counts of how many states banned or refused to implement the Adolescence Education Programme after the 2007 backlash vary: Reuters counted six in May 2007, while a 2020 study in the journal Reproductive Health says 12 states banned all AEP and comprehensive sexuality education programmes.
text.hg: Counts of how many states banned or refused to implement the Adolescence Education Programme after the 2007 backlash vary: Reuters counted six in May 2007, while a 2020 study in the journal Reproductive Health says 12 states banned all AEP and comprehensive sexuality education programmes.

facts.caveat: There is no official list. The 2020 study does not name the 12 states (it cites a 2018 paper by the same research group), and other accounts give other numbers: the RSS weekly Organiser said in May 2009 that eleven state governments had refused to implement the programme. Use the range, not a single figure.

text.en: In June 2014 Union Health Minister Harsh Vardhan denied proposing a ban on sex education but called the original 2007 Adolescence Education Programme 'so-called sex education' marked by 'crudity', saying chief ministers had objected to it and it was later modified.
text.hg: June 2014 mein Union Health Minister Harsh Vardhan ne is baat se inkaar kiya ki unhone sex education par ban ka proposal rakha tha, lekin 2007 ke original Adolescence Education Programme ko 'so-called sex education' kaha jismein 'crudity' thi; unhone kaha ki chief ministers ne is par objection kiya tha aur baad mein ise modify kiya gaya.

text.en: In 2009 the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions, chaired by M. Venkaiah Naidu, reporting on a petition that sought a national debate before sex education was introduced in schools, recommended that there should be no sex education in schools.
text.hg: In 2009 the Rajya Sabha Committee on Petitions, chaired by M. Venkaiah Naidu, reporting on a petition that sought a national debate before sex education was introduced in schools, recommended that there should be no sex education in schools.

facts.value: 2009 report (submitted 2 April 2009): 'no sex education in schools'
facts.caveat: The report itself was not seen; details come from press coverage. The committee also proposed moving chapters on adolescent development and HIV/AIDS into biology textbooks at the Plus Two stage and telling students that sex before marriage is 'immoral, unethical and unhealthy' (DNA, Organiser, Radiance Weekly).

text.en: The Health Ministry launched the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK), India's national adolescent health programme, on 7 January 2014 to reach 253 million adolescents, widening adolescent health beyond sexual and reproductive health to nutrition, injuries and violence including gender-based violence, mental health and substance misuse.
text.hg: Health Ministry ne 7 January 2014 ko India ka national adolescent health programme, Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK), shuru kiya taaki 253 million adolescents tak pahuncha ja sake; is programme ne adolescent health ka daayra sexual aur reproductive health se aage badha kar nutrition, injuries aur violence (jismein gender-based violence bhi shaamil hai), mental health aur substance misuse (nashe ka galat istemaal) tak phailaya.

facts.caveat: 253 million is the programme's target population, not the number reached.

text.en: India's Adolescent Friendly Health Centres began in 2006 as Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health clinics and, under RKSK, offer counselling and clinical care at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges; national guidance says they should not be placed near labour rooms or STI and HIV testing centres so that adolescents can visit without hesitation.
text.hg: India ke Adolescent Friendly Health Centres 2006 mein Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health clinics ke roop mein shuru hue the, aur RKSK ke tahat yeh primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling aur clinical care dete hain; national guidance kehti hai ki inhe labour rooms ya STI aur HIV testing centres ke paas nahi banaya jaana chahiye, taaki adolescents bina jhijhak yahan aa sakein.

facts.caveat: The number of functioning centres was not confirmed. In October 2025 the Ministry renamed them from 'Clinics' to 'Centres' because the word 'clinic' deterred adolescents, and said 1.7 crore adolescents used AFHC services in 2024-25 (fact soc-afhc-renamed-2025).

text.en: Under RKSK's peer education programme, four adolescent 'Saathiya' peer educators (two boys and two girls) are to be selected per village or 1,000 population, each running weekly one- to two-hour sessions for groups of 15-20 adolescents.
text.hg: RKSK ke peer education programme ke tahat har gaon ya 1,000 ki aabadi par chaar adolescent 'Saathiya' peer educators (do ladke aur do ladkiyan) chune jaane hain, aur inmein se har ek ko 15-20 adolescents ke groups ke liye har hafte ek se do ghante ke sessions chalane hote hain.

facts.value: 4 per village/1,000 population; groups of 15-20; weekly sessions
facts.caveat: This is the programme design; the number of peer educators actually selected and trained was not confirmed. States may prioritise districts with many out-of-school adolescents.

text.en: Under the School Health and Wellness Programme of Ayushman Bharat, whose curriculum was launched on 12 February 2020, two teachers in every government and government-aided school (preferably one man and one woman) are to be trained as 'Health and Wellness Ambassadors' to run one-hour weekly sessions on 11 health themes for 24 weeks a year, starting with schools in aspirational districts.
text.hg: Under the School Health and Wellness Programme of Ayushman Bharat, whose curriculum was launched on 12 February 2020, two teachers in every government and government-aided school (preferably one man and one woman) are to be trained as 'Health and Wellness Ambassadors' to run one-hour weekly sessions on 11 health themes for 24 weeks a year, starting with schools in aspirational districts.

facts.value: Curriculum launched 12 Feb 2020; 2 teachers per school; 11 themes; 1 hour a week for 24 weeks a year
facts.caveat: The 11 themes (PIB): growing up healthy; emotional well-being and mental health; interpersonal relationships; values and responsible citizenship; gender equality; nutrition, health and sanitation; promotion of healthy lifestyles; prevention and management of substance misuse; reproductive health and HIV prevention; safety and security against violence and injuries; promotion of safe use of internet, media and social media. Covers government and government-aided schools only; private schools are not covered.

text.en: India's National Education Policy 2020 names girls and transgender students, Scheduled Castes and Tribes, OBCs, minorities and children with disabilities among 'Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups' (SEDGs), commits the Government of India to constitute a 'Gender-Inclusion Fund' for girls and transgender students, and asks all higher education institutions to sensitise faculty, counsellors and students on gender identity and to strictly enforce no-discrimination and anti-harassment rules.
text.hg: India's National Education Policy 2020 names girls and transgender students, Scheduled Castes and Tribes, OBCs, minorities and children with disabilities among 'Socio-Economically Disadvantaged Groups' (SEDGs), commits the Government of India to constitute a 'Gender-Inclusion Fund' for girls and transgender students, and asks all higher education institutions to sensitise faculty, counsellors and students on gender identity and to strictly enforce no-discrimination and anti-harassment rules.

facts.value: SEDG framework; Gender-Inclusion Fund; HEI gender-identity sensitisation
facts.caveat: NEP 2020 does not mention sexuality education at all (fact soc-nep-2020-silent-on-sexuality). UGC's official summary paraphrases SEDGs as 'Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Groups'.

text.en: Of 29,536 rape cases registered in India in 2024, police recorded only 144 under the aggravated charge for raping a woman with a mental or physical disability (Section 64(2)(k) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, formerly Section 376(2)(l) IPC); Maharashtra (32), Madhya Pradesh (19), Tamil Nadu (18) and Kerala (17) accounted for 86 of them, while Uttar Pradesh recorded 3 and Bihar none.
text.hg: Of 29,536 rape cases registered in India in 2024, police recorded only 144 under the aggravated charge for raping a woman with a mental or physical disability (Section 64(2)(k) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, formerly Section 376(2)(l) IPC); Maharashtra (32), Madhya Pradesh (19), Tamil Nadu (18) and Kerala (17) accounted for 86 of them, while Uttar Pradesh recorded 3 and Bihar none.

facts.caveat: A floor, not a prevalence figure: it counts only cases in which police invoked the disability clause, and each case is listed under one category, so cases filed as ordinary rape or under another category (such as 'woman incapable of giving consent', 151 cases) are not included. Very low counts in the largest states suggest the clause is rarely used.

text.en: India's National Education Policy 2020 does not once use the words 'sex', 'sexual', 'sexuality', 'reproductive', 'puberty' or 'menstruation' in its 66 pages; it lists 'health and nutrition' and 'gender sensitivity' among skills every student should learn and asks for safe reporting mechanisms for adolescents facing 'substance or drug abuse and forms of discrimination and harassment including violence'.
text.hg: India's National Education Policy 2020 does not once use the words 'sex', 'sexual', 'sexuality', 'reproductive', 'puberty' or 'menstruation' in its 66 pages; it lists 'health and nutrition' and 'gender sensitivity' among skills every student should learn and asks for safe reporting mechanisms for adolescents facing 'substance or drug abuse and forms of discrimination and harassment including violence'.

facts.value: 0 mentions of sex, sexuality, reproductive health, puberty or menstruation
facts.caveat: Checked by machine search of the English text. NEP does mention 'gender identities', 'gender equality' and 'Holistic Health' as a subject; adolescent sexual health is handled outside NEP through health-ministry programmes such as RKSK and the School Health and Wellness Programme.

text.en: In October 2025 India's Health Ministry renamed 'Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics' as 'Adolescent Friendly Health Centres', saying adolescents hesitated to visit because the word 'clinic' carried stigma and a visit to a 'clinic' was 'looked upon with suspicion'; about 1.7 crore adolescents used these services in 2024-25.
text.hg: In October 2025 India's Health Ministry renamed 'Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics' as 'Adolescent Friendly Health Centres', saying adolescents hesitated to visit because the word 'clinic' carried stigma and a visit to a 'clinic' was 'looked upon with suspicion'; about 1.7 crore adolescents used these services in 2024-25.

facts.value: Renamed 22 Oct 2025; 1.7 crore adolescents served in 2024-25
facts.caveat: The 1.7 crore figure is the Ministry's and may count visits rather than unique adolescents. States that already use local names such as 'Yuva Clinic', 'Nayi Disha Kendra', 'Sneha', 'Umang' or 'Yuva Maitri Kendra' may keep them.

text.en: In 2019-21, 29% of urban women and 37% of urban men aged 15-49 in India had comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS, compared with 18% of rural women and 27% of rural men, according to NFHS-5.
text.hg: In 2019-21, 29% of urban women and 37% of urban men aged 15-49 in India had comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS, compared with 18% of rural women and 27% of rural men, according to NFHS-5.

facts.caveat: Survey data; 'comprehensive knowledge' is a strict composite (see soc-nfhs5-hiv-knowledge-adults).

text.en: About 840 million women aged 15 and older, 30.4% of all women in that age group worldwide, had been subjected to physical or sexual violence by an intimate partner, sexual violence by a non-partner, or both at least once in their lives as of 2023, according to WHO estimates published in 2025; among women aged 15-49 the share is 31.6%.
text.hg: WHO ke 2025 mein publish hue estimates ke mutabik, 2023 tak duniya bhar mein 15 saal aur usse zyada umar ki lagbhag 840 million mahilayein, yaani is age group ki sabhi mahilaon ka 30.4%, zindagi mein kam se kam ek baar pati ya partner ki physical ya sexual violence, pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur ki sexual violence, ya dono ka shikaar ho chuki thin; 15-49 saal ki mahilaon mein yeh hissa 31.6% hai.

facts.caveat: Modelled survey-based estimates from data collected 2000-2023 in 168 countries. WHO's fact sheet rounds this to 'nearly 1 in 3 (32%)'. WHO says all surveys likely underestimate violence because many women never disclose it.

text.en: Worldwide, 25.8% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49, and 24.7% of those aged 15 and older (about 682 million women), have been subjected to physical or sexual violence by a current or former husband or male partner at least once in their lives, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, duniya bhar mein kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15-49 saal ki mahilaon mein se 25.8%, aur 15 saal ya usse zyada umar ki aisi mahilaon mein se 24.7% (lagbhag 682 million mahilayein), zindagi mein kam se kam ek baar maujooda ya poorv pati ya male partner ki physical ya sexual violence ka shikaar ho chuki hain.

facts.caveat: Covers physical and sexual partner violence only; psychological abuse and controlling behaviour are not included in this indicator.

text.en: In the 12 months before they were surveyed, at least 316 million women worldwide, 11.4% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15 and older and 13.7% of those aged 15-49, were subjected to physical or sexual violence by an intimate partner, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, survey se pehle ke 12 mahinon mein duniya bhar mein kam se kam 316 million mahilayein, yaani kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15 saal aur usse zyada umar ki mahilaon mein se 11.4% aur 15-49 saal ki aisi mahilaon mein se 13.7%, pati ya partner ki physical ya sexual violence ka shikaar huin.

facts.caveat: WHO's news release rounds this to '316 million women – 11% of those aged 15 or older'.

text.en: More than one in five (23.3%) ever-married or partnered adolescent girls aged 15-19 worldwide have already been subjected to physical or sexual violence by an intimate partner, and 16% experienced it in the past 12 months alone, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, duniya bhar mein kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15-19 saal ki har paanch kishoriyon (adolescent girls) mein se ek se zyada (23.3%) pehle hi pati ya partner ki physical ya sexual violence ka shikaar ho chuki hain, aur 16% ne sirf pichhle 12 mahinon mein hi yeh violence jheli.

facts.caveat: Denominator is girls who have ever been married or partnered, a group that is large in countries with high child marriage. WHO's news release of 19 November 2025 puts the past-year figure at 12.5 million girls.

text.en: About 263 million women worldwide, 8.2% of women aged 15 and older, have been subjected to sexual violence by someone other than a partner since age 15, and 2.4% experienced it in the past 12 months, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, duniya bhar mein lagbhag 263 million mahilayein, yaani 15 saal aur usse zyada umar ki mahilaon ka 8.2%, 15 saal ki umar ke baad se pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur ki sexual violence ka shikaar ho chuki hain, aur 2.4% ne pichhle 12 mahinon mein yeh violence jheli.

facts.caveat: The report says actual prevalence is likely much higher because sexual violence is particularly stigmatised; WHO's 19 November 2025 news release says experts caution the figure is 'significantly under-reported due to stigma and fear' and that this is the first report with national estimates of non-partner sexual violence. Excludes sexual abuse before age 15.

text.en: In Southern Asia, the region that includes India, 31.2% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49 have experienced physical or sexual violence by a partner in their lifetime and 20.5% in the past 12 months, against global averages of 25.8% and 13.7%, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, Southern Asia mein, jis region mein India aata hai, kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15-49 saal ki mahilaon mein se 31.2% ne zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi pati ya partner ki physical ya sexual violence jheli hai aur 20.5% ne pichhle 12 mahinon mein, jabki inke global average kramashah 25.8% aur 13.7% hain.

facts.caveat: Southern Asia is the UN SDG subregion; the report lists eight countries with data in it (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka), and India, by far the most populous of them, weighs heavily in the regional figure. WHO's fact sheet rounds the lifetime figure to 31%.

text.en: In the regional ranking in WHO's 19 November 2025 news release, Southern Asia came second only to Oceania excluding Australia and New Zealand for recent partner violence: 19% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15 and older there were subjected to physical or sexual violence by a partner in the past 12 months, against 38% in Oceania excluding Australia and New Zealand and a global average of 11%, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.
text.hg: In the regional ranking in WHO's 19 November 2025 news release, Southern Asia came second only to Oceania excluding Australia and New Zealand for recent partner violence: 19% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15 and older there were subjected to physical or sexual violence by a partner in the past 12 months, against 38% in Oceania excluding Australia and New Zealand and a global average of 11%, according to WHO's 2023 estimates.

facts.value: Southern Asia 19% (18.6% in the SDG database) vs Oceania excl. Australia/NZ 38% and world 11% (women 15+)
facts.caveat: The release ranks only broad regions and a few subregions. In the UN SDG Indicators Database (indicator 5.2.1, women 15+, 2023) the Pacific subregions Melanesia (38.5%), Micronesia (22.3%) and Polynesia (18.9%) are also above Southern Asia (18.6%), so do not call Southern Asia the second-worst subregion in the world. Southern Asia is a subregion of 'Central and Southern Asia' (18%).

text.en: WHO's modelled national estimate for India is that 29.9% of ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49 have experienced physical or sexual violence by a partner in their lifetime and 22.4% in the past 12 months, placing India among the 33 countries and territory with the highest past-year rates in the 2023 estimates (Afghanistan is the only other South Asian country in that group).
text.hg: India ke liye WHO ka modelled national estimate hai ki kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15-49 saal ki mahilaon mein se 29.9% ne zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi pati ya partner ki physical ya sexual violence jheli hai aur 22.4% ne pichhle 12 mahinon mein; iske chalte 2023 ke estimates mein India pichhle ek saal ki violence ki sabse oonchi dar wale un 33 countries aur territory mein shaamil hai (is group mein Afghanistan South Asia ka akela doosra desh hai).

facts.caveat: Output of WHO's statistical model of eligible survey data, so it will not exactly match the figures in India's own NFHS reports. Not comparable with WHO's 2018 estimate for India (35% lifetime) because methods and data changed.

text.en: WHO's 2023 estimates put lifetime non-partner sexual violence (since age 15) at 4.1% for women aged 15-49 in India, against 39.8% in Sweden; WHO cautions that such gaps reflect differences in disclosure, stigma and survey methods as well as real differences in violence.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, India mein 15-49 saal ki 4.1% mahilaon ne (15 saal ki umar ke baad se) zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur ki sexual violence jheli hai, jabki Sweden mein yeh figure 39.8% hai; WHO chetavni deta hai ki aise antar violence mein asli farq ke saath-saath disclosure (khulkar batane), stigma aur survey ke tareekon mein farq ko bhi dikhate hain.

facts.caveat: Annex 18's heading says 'women aged 15-49 years'; the table title also contains 'ever-married/-partnered', which looks like an editing slip because non-partner violence is measured for all women. Do not present the India figure as proof that sexual violence is rare in India: WHO says actual prevalence is likely much higher where stigma is high and services are lacking.

text.en: Among India's neighbours, WHO's 2023 estimates of lifetime partner violence against ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49 are 50.9% in Afghanistan, 48.9% in Bangladesh, 26.1% in Nepal, 24.8% in Pakistan, 17.6% in Bhutan and 17.2% in Sri Lanka, against 29.9% in India; for violence in the past 12 months, India's 22.4% is second only to Afghanistan (39.7%) and above Bangladesh (15.7%), Pakistan (13.1%) and Nepal (12.3%).
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, India ke padosi deshon mein kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15-49 saal ki mahilaon mein zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi pati ya partner ki violence jhelne wali mahilaon ka hissa Afghanistan mein 50.9%, Bangladesh mein 48.9%, Nepal mein 26.1%, Pakistan mein 24.8%, Bhutan mein 17.6% aur Sri Lanka mein 17.2% hai, jabki India mein yeh 29.9% hai; pichhle 12 mahinon ki violence ke maamle mein India ka 22.4% sirf Afghanistan (39.7%) se peeche hai aur Bangladesh (15.7%), Pakistan (13.1%) aur Nepal (12.3%) se upar hai.

facts.value: Lifetime: Afghanistan 50.9%, Bangladesh 48.9%, India 29.9%, Nepal 26.1%, Pakistan 24.8%, Bhutan 17.6%, Sri Lanka 17.2%; past year: Afghanistan 39.7%, India 22.4%, Bangladesh 15.7%, Pakistan 13.1%, Nepal 12.3%, Sri Lanka 8.0%, Bhutan 5.9%
facts.caveat: Modelled estimates with wide uncertainty intervals (India's past-year range is 17.4-27.7%); national survey designs differ, so small gaps between countries are not meaningful.

text.en: WHO's 2023 estimates put lifetime non-partner sexual violence among women aged 15-49 at 4.7% in Southern Asia, compared with 17.8% in Western Europe, 19.5% in Australia and New Zealand and 23.3% in Central America; WHO warns that some regions are more affected by under-reporting than others.
text.hg: WHO ke 2023 ke estimates ke mutabik, 15-49 saal ki mahilaon mein zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur ki sexual violence jhelne wali mahilaon ka hissa Southern Asia mein 4.7% hai, jabki Western Europe mein yeh 17.8%, Australia aur New Zealand mein 19.5% aur Central America mein 23.3% hai; WHO chetata hai ki kuch regions par under-reporting ka asar doosron se zyada hai.

facts.value: Southern Asia 4.7%; Western Europe 17.8%; Australia/NZ 19.5%; Central America 23.3%; world 8.4%
facts.caveat: WHO: 'some regions may be more affected by underreporting than others, given different levels of stigma, services available, and support women may receive when disclosing sexual violence.'

text.en: WHO's 2025 report states that women in more gender-equal societies are more likely to disclose sexual violence, which raises measured prevalence, while in countries with high stigma, few services and serious repercussions for reporting, actual non-partner sexual violence is likely much higher than the estimates show.
text.hg: WHO ki 2025 ki report kehti hai ki zyada gender-equal samaajon mein mahilaon ke sexual violence ke baare mein khulkar batane ki sambhavna zyada hoti hai, jisse measured prevalence badh jaati hai, jabki jin deshon mein stigma zyada hai, services kam hain aur report karne ke gambhir nateeje bhugatne padte hain, wahan pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur ki sexual violence asal mein estimates mein dikhne se kahin zyada hone ki sambhavna hai.

text.en: WHO notes that dedicated violence-against-women surveys draw higher disclosure than short modules inside broader surveys such as the Demographic and Health Surveys, and that this, together with stigma and the range of acts asked about, limits the comparability of sexual violence data across countries.
text.hg: WHO batata hai ki sirf violence against women par focused surveys mein mahilayein, Demographic and Health Surveys jaise bade surveys ke andar rakhe gaye chhote modules ke muqable, violence ke baare mein zyada khulkar batati hain; aur yeh baat, stigma aur survey mein poochhe gaye acts ke daayre ke saath milkar, alag-alag deshon ke sexual violence data ki aapas mein tulna ko seemit karti hai.

facts.caveat: India's NFHS uses a domestic violence module within a broader health survey, the type WHO says tends to draw lower disclosure.

text.en: WHO states that its 2023 violence-against-women estimates are not comparable with its earlier 2018 and 2010 estimates because of changes in methods and data, so differences between the rounds should not be read as a trend.
text.hg: WHO ka kehna hai ki violence against women par uske 2023 ke estimates ki tulna uske pehle ke 2018 aur 2010 ke estimates se nahin ki ja sakti, kyunki methods aur data mein badlaav hue hain; isliye in rounds ke beech ke farq ko kisi trend ki tarah nahin padha jaana chahiye.

facts.caveat: For example, the 2018 round counted about 736 million women and the 2023 round 840 million (see gl-who-2018-736m and gl-who-840m-lifetime-2023); WHO separately reports that partner violence has fallen by only about 0.2% a year over two decades.

text.en: Intimate partner violence against women has declined by only about 0.2% a year on average over the past 20 years and the 'one in three' figure has stagnated, which WHO says makes it very unlikely that the SDG target 5.2 to eliminate violence against women and girls will be met by 2030.
text.hg: Mahilaon ke khilaf pati ya partner ki violence pichhle 20 saalon mein average har saal sirf lagbhag 0.2% ghati hai aur 'har teen mein se ek' wala figure jas ka tas bana hua hai; WHO ka kehna hai ki is wajah se iski sambhavna bahut kam hai ki mahilaon aur ladkiyon ke khilaf violence khatam karne wala SDG target 5.2 saal 2030 tak poora ho payega.

facts.caveat: WHO's 19 November 2025 news release says the 840 million figure 'has barely changed since 2000'.

text.en: In 2022 only 0.2% of global development aid went to programmes focused on preventing violence against women, and WHO reported that such funding fell further in 2025.
text.hg: 2022 mein duniya bhar ki development aid ka sirf 0.2% mahilaon ke khilaf violence rokne par focused programmes ko mila, aur WHO ne bataya ki 2025 mein aisi funding aur ghat gayi.

text.en: Intimate partner violence is the fourth leading cause of poor health among women worldwide in terms of disability-adjusted life years, according to Global Burden of Disease estimates published in 2025 and cited by WHO.
text.hg: Global Burden of Disease ke 2025 mein publish hue aur WHO dwara quote kiye gaye estimates ke mutabik, disability-adjusted life years ke hisaab se pati ya partner ki violence duniya bhar mein mahilaon ki kharab sehat ka chautha sabse bada kaaran hai.

facts.caveat: WHO cites Flor L et al., The Lancet, 2025 (GBD 2023 analysis).

text.en: In some countries, violence against women costs between 1% and 6% of GDP through police, justice, social protection and health service costs, according to WHO.
text.hg: WHO ke mutabik, kuch deshon mein mahilaon ke khilaf violence ki keemat police, justice, social protection aur health services par hone wale kharch ke roop mein GDP ke 1% se 6% tak padti hai.

facts.caveat: Range drawn from selected country costing studies, not a global estimate.

text.en: WHO's previous estimates, released on 9 March 2021 using 2000-2018 data, found that about 736 million women, roughly 1 in 3, had been subjected to physical or sexual violence by a partner or sexual violence by a non-partner, with partner violence affecting about 641 million and 6% of women reporting sexual assault by a non-partner.
text.hg: WHO ke pichhle estimates mein, jo 2000-2018 ke data ke aadhaar par 9 March 2021 ko jaari hue the, paaya gaya ki lagbhag 736 million mahilayein, yaani kareeb har 3 mein se 1, pati ya partner ki physical ya sexual violence ya pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur ki sexual violence ka shikaar hui thin; pati ya partner ki violence lagbhag 641 million mahilaon ne jheli thi aur 6% mahilaon ne bataya ki pati ya partner ke alawa kisi aur ne un par sexual assault kiya.

facts.value: 736 million; 641 million IPV; 6% non-partner sexual assault
facts.caveat: Superseded by the 2023 estimates; WHO says the two rounds are not comparable.

text.en: WHO's 2018 estimates found that 1 in 4 young women aged 15-24 who had been in a relationship had already experienced partner violence by their mid-twenties, and that 16% of them had experienced it in the past 12 months, the highest rate of any age group.
text.hg: WHO ke 2018 ke estimates mein paaya gaya ki kisi relationship mein reh chuki 15-24 saal ki har 4 mein se 1 yuvati pachchis ke aaspaas ki umar tak pahunchte-pahunchte pati ya partner ki violence jhel chuki thi, aur inmein se 16% ne pichhle 12 mahinon mein yeh violence jheli thi, jo kisi bhi age group ki sabse oonchi dar thi.

facts.caveat: 2018 estimates; not comparable with 2023 estimates.

text.en: WHO's 2018 estimates put lifetime partner violence among ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49 at 35% in Southern Asia, the highest of any region apart from Oceania's subregions (only the least developed countries grouping, at 37%, was higher), with 19% experiencing it in the past 12 months.
text.hg: WHO ke 2018 ke estimates ke mutabik, Southern Asia mein kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15-49 saal ki 35% mahilaon ne zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi pati ya partner ki violence jheli thi, jo Oceania ke subregions ko chhodkar kisi bhi region mein sabse zyada tha (sirf least developed countries ka group 37% ke saath isse upar tha), aur 19% ne pichhle 12 mahinon mein yeh violence jheli thi.

facts.caveat: 2018 estimates; WHO says they are not comparable with the 2023 estimates (31.2% for Southern Asia).

text.en: WHO's 2018 estimates put lifetime non-partner sexual violence in Southern Asia at 2%, level with Central Asia as the lowest of any region, while high-income regions such as Australia and New Zealand (19%) and Northern America (15%) recorded the highest; WHO warned that these variations must be interpreted with caution because of differences in measurement and reporting.
text.hg: WHO's 2018 estimates put lifetime non-partner sexual violence in Southern Asia at 2%, level with Central Asia as the lowest of any region, while high-income regions such as Australia and New Zealand (19%) and Northern America (15%) recorded the highest; WHO warned that these variations must be interpreted with caution because of differences in measurement and reporting.

facts.value: Southern Asia 2% (tied lowest with Central Asia); Australia/NZ 19%; Northern America 15%
facts.caveat: Low reported prevalence reflects under-disclosure as much as real differences.

text.en: WHO's 2018 estimates, published in 2021, put lifetime physical or sexual partner violence against ever-married or partnered women aged 15-49 in India at 35% and past-year violence at 18%.
