text.hg: 2021 mein publish hue WHO ke 2018 ke estimates ke mutabik, India mein kabhi shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein rahi 15-49 saal ki mahilaon mein se 35% ne zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi pati ya partner ki physical ya sexual violence jheli thi aur 18% ne pichhle ek saal mein.

facts.caveat: Not comparable with the 2023 estimate (29.9% lifetime, 22.4% past year) because of changes in methodology and data; do not present the difference as a trend.

text.en: More than 370 million girls and women alive today, about 1 in 8, were raped or sexually assaulted before the age of 18, according to UNICEF's first global estimates of sexual violence against children, released on 10 October 2024.
text.hg: 10 October 2024 ko jaari, bachchon ke khilaf sexual violence ke UNICEF ke pehle global estimates ke mutabik, aaj zinda 370 million se zyada ladkiyan aur mahilayein, yaani lagbhag har 8 mein se 1, 18 saal ki umar se pehle rape ya sexual assault ka shikaar huin.

facts.caveat: Based mainly on nationally representative surveys from 120 countries and areas conducted 2010-2022; counts survivors alive today, not cases per year.

text.en: When non-contact sexual violence such as online or verbal sexual abuse is included, about 650 million girls and women alive today, 1 in 5, experienced sexual violence in childhood, according to UNICEF (October 2024).
text.hg: UNICEF (October 2024) ke mutabik, jab online ya verbal sexual abuse jaisi non-contact (bina chhue ki jaane wali) sexual violence ko bhi joda jaata hai, to aaj zinda lagbhag 650 million ladkiyon aur mahilaon, yaani har 5 mein se 1, ne bachpan mein sexual violence jheli.

facts.caveat: UNICEF says estimates on non-contact violence used a broader range of data sources and some indirect methods.

text.en: An estimated 240 million to 310 million boys and men alive today, around 1 in 11, were raped or sexually assaulted during childhood, rising to 410-530 million when non-contact forms are included, according to UNICEF (October 2024).
text.hg: UNICEF (October 2024) ke anumaan ke mutabik, aaj zinda 240 million se 310 million ladke aur purush, yaani lagbhag har 11 mein se 1, bachpan mein rape ya sexual assault ka shikaar hue; non-contact (bina chhue ki jaane wali) sexual violence ko bhi jodne par yeh sankhya 410-530 million tak pahunch jaati hai.

facts.caveat: Data on boys are thinner; UNICEF used indirect methods, hence the range.

text.en: In Central and Southern Asia, which includes India, an estimated 73 million girls and women alive today, 9%, were raped or sexually assaulted as children; Sub-Saharan Africa has the most victims (79 million, 22%) and Oceania the highest share (34%), according to UNICEF (October 2024).
text.hg: UNICEF (October 2024) ke mutabik, Central aur Southern Asia mein, jis region mein India aata hai, aaj zinda anumaanit 73 million ladkiyan aur mahilayein, yaani 9%, bachpan mein rape ya sexual assault ka shikaar huin; sabse zyada victims Sub-Saharan Africa mein hain (79 million, 22%) aur sabse ooncha anupaat Oceania mein (34%) hai.

facts.caveat: Regional shares rest on what survivors disclose in surveys; as WHO notes for adult sexual violence, under-reporting varies by region, so lower percentages may partly reflect under-disclosure rather than lower risk.

text.en: Most childhood sexual violence happens in adolescence, with a significant spike between ages 14 and 17, and in fragile settings slightly more than 1 in 4 girls are raped or sexually assaulted in childhood, according to UNICEF (October 2024).
text.hg: UNICEF (October 2024) ke mutabik, bachpan mein hone wali zyadatar sexual violence adolescence (kishoravastha) mein hoti hai, aur 14 se 17 saal ki umar ke beech ismein tez uchhaal aata hai; fragile settings, yaani asthir aur sankatgrast halaat mein, har 4 mein se 1 se thodi zyada ladkiyan bachpan mein rape ya sexual assault ka shikaar hoti hain.

facts.value: Peak ages 14-17; >1 in 4 in fragile settings

text.en: About 50,000 women and girls worldwide were killed by an intimate partner or another family member in 2024, 60% of the roughly 83,000 women and girls killed intentionally that year, or an average of 137 every day, according to UNODC and UN Women (November 2025).
text.hg: UNODC aur UN Women (November 2025) ke mutabik, 2024 mein duniya bhar mein lagbhag 50,000 mahilaon aur ladkiyon ki hatya unke pati ya partner ya parivaar ke kisi doosre sadasya ne ki; yeh us saal jaanboojhkar maari gayi lagbhag 83,000 mahilaon aur ladkiyon ka 60% hai, yaani average har din 137.

facts.caveat: The briefs are published each November; no edition with 2025 data had been found as of 20 November 2026. UNODC says the fall from 51,100 reflects changes in country data, not a real decline. 137 a day is about one killing every 10.5 minutes (our calculation).

text.en: About 51,100 women and girls worldwide were killed by intimate partners or other family members in 2023, 60% of almost 85,000 intentional killings of women and girls, an average of 140 a day; the 2022 estimate was 48,800, according to UNODC and UN Women (2024).
text.hg: UNODC aur UN Women (2024) ke mutabik, 2023 mein duniya bhar mein lagbhag 51,100 mahilaon aur ladkiyon ki hatya unke pati ya partner ya parivaar ke doosre sadasyon ne ki; yeh mahilaon aur ladkiyon ki jaanboojhkar ki gayi kareeb 85,000 hatyaon ka 60% hai, yaani average har din 140; 2022 ka estimate 48,800 tha.

facts.caveat: Year-to-year changes in these estimates mostly reflect which countries reported data, so they should not be presented as a trend.

text.en: Asia recorded an estimated 17,400 women and girls killed by partners or family members in 2024, the second-highest number after Africa (22,600), although Asia's rate of 0.7 per 100,000 women was lower than Africa's (3), the Americas' (1.5) and Oceania's (1.4), according to UNODC and UN Women.
text.hg: UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik, 2024 mein Asia mein anumaanit 17,400 mahilaon aur ladkiyon ki hatya unke pati ya partner ya parivaar ke sadasyon ne ki, jo Africa (22,600) ke baad doosri sabse badi sankhya hai; haalanki Asia ki dar, prati 100,000 mahilaon par 0.7, Africa (3), Americas (1.5) aur Oceania (1.4) se kam thi.

facts.caveat: UNODC says regional estimates carry significant uncertainty because data remain patchy in Africa, Asia and Oceania. In 2023 Asia's estimate was 18,500.

text.en: Men and boys made up 80% of the world's homicide victims in 2024, but almost 60% of women and girls who were killed died at the hands of a partner or family member, compared with 11% of male victims; in Asia the share for women was 55%, according to UNODC and UN Women.
text.hg: UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik, 2024 mein duniya bhar mein hatya ke victims mein 80% purush aur ladke the, lekin maari gayi mahilaon aur ladkiyon mein se kareeb 60% ki maut pati ya partner ya parivaar ke kisi sadasya ke haathon hui, jabki male victims mein yeh hissa 11% tha; Asia mein mahilaon ke liye yeh hissa 55% tha.

facts.value: ~60% of female vs 11% of male homicides; Asia 55%

text.en: Outside Europe and the Americas, women and girls killed in the private sphere in 2023 were more often killed by other family members (59%) than by intimate partners (41%), based on available data, whereas in Europe 64% of such victims were killed by partners, according to UNODC and UN Women.
text.hg: UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik, upalabdh data ke aadhaar par, Europe aur Americas ke bahar 2023 mein private sphere (ghar-parivaar) mein maari gayi mahilaon aur ladkiyon ki hatya pati ya partner (41%) ke muqable parivaar ke doosre sadasyon (59%) ne zyada ki, jabki Europe mein aisi 64% victims ki hatya pati ya partner ne ki.

facts.value: 59% family members vs 41% partners (rest of world)
facts.caveat: Based on the limited set of countries outside Europe and the Americas that report the victim-perpetrator relationship.

text.en: Data from France (2019-2022), South Africa (2020-2021) and Colombia (2014-2017) show that between 22% and 37% of women killed by their intimate partners had previously reported physical, sexual or psychological violence by that partner, which UNODC and UN Women say suggests many killings are preventable.
text.hg: France (2019-2022), South Africa (2020-2021) aur Colombia (2014-2017) ka data dikhata hai ki pati ya partner ke haathon maari gayi mahilaon mein se 22% se 37% ne pehle hi usi partner ki physical, sexual ya psychological violence report ki thi; UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik isse sanket milta hai ki kai hatyayein roki ja sakti hain.

facts.caveat: Three countries only; no comparable Indian data were found.

text.en: The number of countries reporting data on women and girls killed by partners or family members peaked at 75 in 2020 and had fallen by half by 2023, according to UNODC and UN Women, which warned that attention to femicide may have waned after the COVID-19 pandemic.
text.hg: UNODC aur UN Women ke mutabik, pati ya partner ya parivaar ke sadasyon ke haathon maari gayi mahilaon aur ladkiyon ka data dene wale deshon ki sankhya 2020 mein 75 ke peak par thi aur 2023 tak ghatkar aadhi reh gayi; in sansthaon ne chetaya ki COVID-19 mahamari ke baad femicide par dhyaan shayad kam ho gaya hai.

text.en: Where countries do not report partner or family femicides, UNODC and UN Women build their global estimates from related offences such as dowry death and honour killing in countries whose national law defines those crimes.
text.hg: Jahan desh pati ya partner ya parivaar dwara kiye gaye femicides ka data report nahin karte, wahan UNODC aur UN Women apne global estimates un deshon mein dowry death (dahej mrityu) aur honour killing jaise related apradhon ke aadhaar par banate hain, jinke national kanoon mein in apradhon ki paribhasha di gayi hai.

facts.caveat: India defines 'dowry death' as an offence (Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, earlier Section 304B IPC).

text.en: Dowry deaths made up 40% to 50% of all female homicides recorded each year in India between 1999 and 2016, according to UNODC's analysis of National Crime Records Bureau data in its 2018 Global Study on Homicide.
text.hg: UNODC ki 2018 ki 'Global Study on Homicide' mein National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ke data ke analysis ke mutabik, 1999 se 2016 ke beech India mein har saal darj mahilaon ki kul hatyaon mein 40% se 50% maamle dowry death (dahej mrityu) ke the.

facts.caveat: Police-recorded data. UNODC notes the dowry death provision (Section 304-B IPC, introduced in 1986) 'may apply in any unnatural death of a woman within seven years of marriage', so the category includes some deaths that are not murders in the narrow sense.

text.en: UNODC estimated that 87,000 women were intentionally killed worldwide in 2017, of whom 50,000 (58%) were killed by intimate partners or family members, 137 a day, and 30,000 (34%) by intimate partners alone.
text.hg: UNODC ke anumaan ke mutabik, 2017 mein duniya bhar mein 87,000 mahilaon ki jaanboojhkar hatya ki gayi; inmein se 50,000 (58%) ki hatya pati ya partner ya parivaar ke sadasyon ne ki, yaani har din 137, aur 30,000 (34%) ki hatya sirf pati ya partner ne ki.

facts.caveat: Earlier methodology; not directly comparable with the 2023 and 2024 estimates.

text.en: An estimated 640 million girls and women alive today were married in childhood, one third of them in India alone, according to the UN's Sustainable Development Goals Report 2024; one in five girls is now married before 18, compared with one in four 25 years earlier, and 68 million child marriages were averted over that period.
text.hg: UN ki Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Report 2024 ke mutabik, aaj zinda anumaanit 640 million ladkiyon aur mahilaon ki shaadi bachpan mein hui, jinmein se ek-tihai akele India mein hain; ab har paanch mein se ek ladki ki shaadi 18 saal se pehle ho jaati hai, jabki 25 saal pehle yeh har chaar mein se ek thi, aur is dauraan 68 million child marriages taali gayin.

facts.value: 640 million; one third in India; 68 million averted
facts.caveat: UNFPA uses the same 640 million figure, which comes from UNICEF's 2023 child marriage analysis (not opened directly). One third of 640 million is about 210 million women (our calculation). 'Alive today' counts women of all ages, including those married decades ago.

text.en: Each year about 12 million adolescent girls are married before the age of 18, roughly one every three seconds, and 4% of girls worldwide are married before 15, according to UNFPA (February 2025).
text.hg: UNFPA (February 2025) ke mutabik, har saal lagbhag 12 million kishoriyon ki shaadi 18 saal ki umar se pehle ho jaati hai, yaani lagbhag har teen second mein ek, aur duniya bhar mein 4% ladkiyon ki shaadi 15 saal se pehle ho jaati hai.

facts.caveat: 'Every three seconds' is UNFPA's own conversion of the annual figure.

text.en: UNFPA notes that where the bride's family pays a dowry to the groom's family, younger brides typically command smaller dowries, which gives poor parents an incentive to marry daughters off early.
text.hg: UNFPA batata hai ki jahan dulhan ka parivaar dulhe ke parivaar ko dahej deta hai, wahan kam umar ki dulhanon ke liye aam taur par kam dahej dena padta hai, jisse gareeb maa-baap ko betiyon ki jaldi shaadi karne ka incentive milta hai.

facts.caveat: General observation by UNFPA, not an India-specific estimate.

text.en: Sub-Saharan Africa and Southern Asia have the highest child marriage rates in the world, with 31% and 25% of young women respectively married before 18, while worldwide nearly one in five young women was married in childhood and the pace of decline in 2015-2024 was double that of the previous decade, according to the UN's SDG Report 2026.
text.hg: UN ki SDG Report 2026 ke mutabik, duniya mein child marriage ki sabse oonchi dar Sub-Saharan Africa aur Southern Asia mein hai, jahan kramashah 31% aur 25% young women ki shaadi 18 saal se pehle hui, jabki duniya bhar mein lagbhag har paanch mein se ek young woman ki shaadi bachpan mein hui aur 2015-2024 mein giraavat ki raftaar pichhle dashak se dogni rahi.

facts.value: Sub-Saharan Africa 31%; Southern Asia 25%; world nearly 1 in 5
facts.caveat: 'Young women' in SDG indicator 5.3.1 means women aged 20-24 married or in union before 18.

text.en: The UN's SDG Report 2025 says child marriage has become less common worldwide largely because of progress in Southern Asia, while sub-Saharan Africa, with the highest level (31%), is projected to see the absolute number of child brides rise by 2030.
text.hg: UN ki SDG Report 2025 kehti hai ki duniya bhar mein child marriage kam hone ki badi wajah Southern Asia mein hui progress hai, jabki sabse oonche level (31%) wale Sub-Saharan Africa mein 2030 tak child brides ki kul sankhya badhne ka anumaan hai.

facts.value: Global decline driven by Southern Asia

text.en: Worldwide, 18% of young women were married as children before age 18, down from 22% in 2015, and the pace of reduction almost doubled in the last decade, driven largely by girls' education, economic empowerment and poverty reduction, according to UN Women and UN DESA's Gender Snapshot 2026.
text.hg: UN Women aur UN DESA ki 'Gender Snapshot 2026' ke mutabik, duniya bhar mein 18% young women ki shaadi bachpan mein, 18 saal ki umar se pehle hui, jabki 2015 mein yeh figure 22% tha; pichhle dashak mein ismein kami ki raftaar lagbhag dogni ho gayi, jiski badi wajah ladkiyon ki padhai, economic empowerment aur gareebi mein kami rahi.

facts.caveat: The Gender Snapshot 2025 gave 18.6% (down from 22% in 2014), so baselines differ slightly between editions.

text.en: UNICEF India estimates that at least 1.5 million girls under 18 are married in India every year and that nearly 16% of adolescent girls aged 15-19 are currently married; marriage before 18 fell from 47% to 27% between 2005-06 and 2015-16.
text.hg: UNICEF India ka anumaan hai ki India mein har saal 18 saal se kam umar ki kam se kam 1.5 million ladkiyon ki shaadi hoti hai, aur 15-19 saal ki lagbhag 16% kishoriyan is samay shaadishuda hain; 18 saal se pehle shaadi ka figure 2005-06 aur 2015-16 ke beech 47% se ghatkar 27% reh gaya.

facts.value: 1.5 million a year; 16% of girls 15-19 married; 47% to 27%
facts.caveat: The page relies on NFHS-3 (2005-06) and NFHS-4 (2015-16) and shows no date. Newer national rates for women aged 20-24 married before 18: 23.3% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) and 20.1% in NFHS-6 (2023-24) (http://www.nfhsiips.in/nfhsnew/nfhsuser/assets/National%20Family%20Health%20Survey%20(NFHS-6)%202023-2024%20Fact%20Sheets.pdf). The 1.5 million and 16% figures are UNICEF estimates whose basis is not given on the page.

text.en: UNICEF says girls who marry before 18 are more likely to experience domestic violence and less likely to stay in school, and that worldwide the prevalence of child marriage among boys is just one sixth of that among girls.
text.hg: UNICEF ka kehna hai ki 18 saal se pehle shaadi karne wali ladkiyon ke domestic violence jhelne ki aashanka zyada hoti hai aur unke school mein bane rehne ki sambhavna kam hoti hai, aur yeh bhi ki duniya bhar mein ladkon mein child marriage ka prachalan ladkiyon ke muqable sirf chhatha hissa hai.

facts.value: Boys' prevalence one sixth of girls'
facts.caveat: Page last updated July 2023.

text.en: More than 230 million girls and women alive today have undergone female genital mutilation, 30 million (15%) more than estimated in 2016, with about 144 million in Africa, 80 million in Asia and 6 million in the Middle East; UNICEF said in March 2024 that the global decline would have to be 27 times faster to end the practice by 2030.
text.hg: Aaj zinda 230 million se zyada ladkiyan aur mahilayein female genital mutilation (FGM) jhel chuki hain; yeh sankhya 2016 ke anumaan se 30 million (15%) zyada hai, aur inmein se lagbhag 144 million Africa mein, 80 million Asia mein aur 6 million Middle East mein hain; UNICEF ne March 2024 mein kaha ki 2030 tak is pratha ko khatam karne ke liye global giraavat ko 27 guna tez hona hoga.

facts.caveat: UNICEF says FGM is not becoming more common globally; the number of girls born in practising countries is growing rapidly.

text.en: UNICEF says at least 230 million girls and women from 31 countries across three continents have been subjected to FGM, and that about one in four survivors, some 52 million, were cut by health personnel.
text.hg: UNICEF ka kehna hai ki teen mahadweepon ke 31 deshon ki kam se kam 230 million ladkiyan aur mahilayein FGM (female genital mutilation) jhel chuki hain, aur har chaar mein se lagbhag ek survivor, yaani kareeb 52 million, ke saath yeh health workers ke haathon hua.

facts.value: 31 countries with data; 52 million cut by health workers
facts.caveat: India has no nationally representative FGM data (see gl-bohra-no-official-data-2017), so the headline figure is unlikely to include khatna in India. UNFPA's FGM FAQ says 'around 2 in 3 girls' who were cut were cut by a health worker; that appears to use a different denominator (girls), and its own age figures (34% of women 15-19, 16% of women 45-49) fit UNICEF's one-in-four for all survivors. UNICEF is the custodian agency for FGM data.

text.en: Each year about 4 million girls undergo female genital mutilation, more than 2 million of them before the age of five, according to the UN's SDG Report 2025.
text.hg: UN ki SDG Report 2025 ke mutabik, har saal lagbhag 4 million ladkiyon ko female genital mutilation (FGM) se guzarna padta hai, jinmein se 2 million se zyada ke saath yeh paanch saal ki umar se pehle hota hai.

facts.value: 4 million a year; 2 million+ before age 5
facts.caveat: The SDG Report 2026 repeats 'around 4 million girls subjected to it every year'.

text.en: UNFPA estimates that 4.5 million girls are at risk of female genital mutilation in 2026 alone, over half of them younger than five, and that an additional 27 million girls could undergo it by 2030 if the current pace continues.
text.hg: UNFPA ka anumaan hai ki akele 2026 mein 4.5 million ladkiyon par female genital mutilation (FGM) ka khatra hai, jinmein se aadhi se zyada paanch saal se chhoti hain, aur agar maujooda raftaar jaari rahi to 2030 tak 27 million aur ladkiyan isse guzar sakti hain.

facts.value: 4.5 million at risk (2026); 27 million more by 2030
facts.caveat: 'At risk' is a projection, not a count of girls cut.

text.en: UNFPA says FGM is documented in at least 94 countries, and its list for Asia includes India alongside Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Maldives and others; citing the World Bank's 2025 compendium, it lists India among 92 countries whose laws either specifically prohibit FGM or allow it to be prosecuted through other laws.
text.hg: UNFPA ke mutabik FGM (female genital mutilation) kam se kam 94 deshon mein documented hai, aur Asia ki uski list mein Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Maldives aur doosre deshon ke saath India bhi shaamil hai; World Bank ke 2025 ke compendium ka hawala dete hue, UNFPA India ko un 92 deshon mein ginta hai jinke kanoon ya to khaas taur par FGM par rok lagate hain ya doosre kanoonon ke zariye is par mukadma chalane ki ijaazat dete hain.

facts.caveat: India appears in the 'prosecutable through other laws' sense: no Indian statute names FGM (see gl-bohra-no-specific-law-2026).

text.en: Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India (W.P.(C) 286/2017), a public interest petition filed in the Supreme Court in 2017, seeks a ban on 'khatna', the female genital cutting practised in the Dawoodi Bohra community, arguing it violates girls' rights to equality, non-discrimination and bodily autonomy under Articles 14, 15 and 21, while community members argue it is a religious practice protected by Articles 25 and 26.
text.hg: Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India (W.P.(C) 286/2017), 2017 mein Supreme Court mein daayar ek public interest petition, Dawoodi Bohra community mein prachalit female genital cutting 'khatna' par ban ki maang karti hai; petition ki daleel hai ki yeh Articles 14, 15 aur 21 ke tahat ladkiyon ke barabari, bhedbhav se mukti aur bodily autonomy ke adhikaaron ka ullanghan karti hai, jabki community ke sadasyon ka tark hai ki yeh Articles 25 aur 26 se protected ek dharmik pratha hai.

facts.caveat: The petition asked that FGM be made an offence under the Indian Penal Code (Supreme Court order, 24 September 2018).

text.en: On 24 September 2018 a three-judge Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Dipak Misra, with Justices A.M. Khanwilkar and D.Y. Chandrachud, ordered that the khatna petition be placed before a larger bench after the Attorney General and counsel for community groups asked for a reference, leaving the larger bench to consider the issue 'in its entirety from all perspectives'.
text.hg: 24 September 2018 ko Chief Justice Dipak Misra ki aguvaai wali Supreme Court ki teen judges ki bench ne, jismein Justice A.M. Khanwilkar aur Justice D.Y. Chandrachud bhi the, Attorney General aur community groups ke vakeelon ki taraf se reference ki maang ke baad aadesh diya ki khatna petition badi bench ke saamne rakhi jaaye, jisse is mudde par 'har nazariye se, poori tarah' vichaar karne ka kaam badi bench par chhod diya gaya.

facts.value: Referred to a larger (Constitution) bench, 24 Sept 2018
facts.caveat: News reports (Times of India) described it as a reference to a five-judge Constitution Bench.

text.en: Attorney General K.K. Venugopal had told the Supreme Court in 2018 that the Union government opposed khatna as a violation of fundamental rights, noting it was banned in countries including the US, the UK, Australia and around 27 African nations, before he supported referring the case to a larger bench on 24 September 2018, according to the Times of India.
text.hg: Times of India ke mutabik, Attorney General K.K. Venugopal ne 2018 mein Supreme Court se kaha tha ki Union government khatna ko fundamental rights ka ullanghan maante hue iska virodh karti hai, aur yeh bhi bataya tha ki US, UK, Australia aur kareeb 27 African deshon samet kai deshon mein is par ban hai; iske baad 24 September 2018 ko unhone case badi bench ko bhejne ka samarthan kiya.

text.en: In December 2017, responding to the Supreme Court petition seeking a ban, the Ministry of Women and Child Development said 'there is no official data or study which supports the existence of FGM in India', a position Bohra campaigners rejected, as reported by The Guardian.
text.hg: The Guardian ki report ke mutabik, December 2017 mein, ban ki maang wali Supreme Court petition ke jawaab mein, Ministry of Women and Child Development ne kaha ki 'India mein FGM ke hone ki pushti karne wala koi official data ya study nahin hai'; Bohra campaigners ne is stand ko khaarij kar diya.

facts.caveat: NCRB records only offences registered with police; with no specific FGM offence, the absence of police data does not show absence of the practice.

text.en: On 14 November 2019 the Supreme Court's Sabarimala review bench, led by Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi, called FGM in the Dawoodi Bohra community a 'seminal issue' about courts' power to decide whether a practice is essential to religion, and said such questions needed an authoritative ruling by a larger bench of not less than seven judges.
text.hg: 14 November 2019 ko Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi ki aguvaai wali Supreme Court ki Sabarimala review bench ne Dawoodi Bohra community mein FGM ko ek 'seminal issue' (buniyadi mudda) bataya, jo is baat se juda hai ki kya courts yeh tay kar sakti hain ki koi pratha dharm ke liye essential hai ya nahin, aur kaha ki aise sawaalon par kam se kam saat judges ki badi bench ka authoritative faisla zaroori hai.

facts.caveat: Majority opinion in a 3:2 decision (see gl-bohra-pending-2019); the larger bench was later constituted with nine judges.

text.en: A nine-judge Constitution Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant began hearing the Sabarimala reference on 7 April 2026; the Dawoodi Bohra FGM petition is one of three pending cases tagged to it.
text.hg: Chief Justice Surya Kant ki aguvaai wali nau judges ki Constitution Bench ne 7 April 2026 ko Sabarimala reference par sunvaai shuru ki; Dawoodi Bohra FGM petition un teen pending cases mein se ek hai jo isse tag kiye gaye hain.

facts.caveat: The nine-judge bench is answering general questions on religious freedom referred in 2019; how and when the khatna petition itself is decided depends on that ruling.

text.en: The nine-judge bench reserved judgment in the Sabarimala reference on 14 May 2026 after 16 days of hearings on denominational autonomy, constitutional morality and the essential religious practices doctrine, which will shape the outcome of the Dawoodi Bohra FGM case.
text.hg: Nau judges ki bench ne denominational autonomy (dharmik sampradayon ki swayattata), constitutional morality aur essential religious practices doctrine par 16 dinon ki sunvaai ke baad 14 May 2026 ko Sabarimala reference mein faisla reserve kar liya; isi se Dawoodi Bohra FGM case ke nateeje ki disha tay hogi.

facts.caveat: Supreme Court Observer reported on 11 November 2026 that the judgment was still pending (Justice B.V. Nagarathna reportedly began writing in October). Check for a verdict before publishing.

text.en: At the nine-judge bench hearing on 7 May 2026, Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra argued that genital cutting of seven-year-old girls could not survive constitutional scrutiny merely because it is asserted as faith, and Supreme Court Observer's report notes that no specific Indian law bans FGM while around 59 countries prohibit it; counsel for the review petitioners called the practice 'a symbolic form of circumcision', and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said male circumcision could not be equated with genital cutting involving the clitoris.
text.hg: 7 May 2026 ko nau judges ki bench ke saamne sunvaai mein Senior Advocate Siddharth Luthra ne daleel di ki saat saal ki bachchiyon ki genital cutting constitutional scrutiny par sirf isliye khari nahin utar sakti ki use aastha ka maamla bataya jaata hai; Supreme Court Observer ki report batati hai ki India mein koi specific kanoon FGM par rok nahin lagata, jabki kareeb 59 desh is par rok lagate hain; review petitioners ke vakeel ne is pratha ko 'circumcision ka ek symbolic roop' bataya, aur Justice Joymalya Bagchi ne kaha ki male circumcision ki tulna clitoris se judi genital cutting se nahin ki ja sakti.

facts.value: No FGM-specific law in India; ~59 countries prohibit (as argued)
facts.caveat: The '59 countries' line appears in the report's summary of Luthra's submissions; it counts countries that prohibit FGM and differs from UNFPA's count of 92 countries whose laws can be used against it. Remarks by judges during hearings are not rulings.

text.en: When a five-judge Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi referred religious-freedom questions to a larger bench by a 3:2 majority on 14 November 2019, the Dawoodi Bohra khatna petition was still pending, along with intervention applications by individual Bohra women, as the Hindustan Times reported.
text.hg: When a five-judge Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi referred religious-freedom questions to a larger bench by a 3:2 majority on 14 November 2019, the Dawoodi Bohra khatna petition was still pending, along with intervention applications by individual Bohra women, as the Hindustan Times reported.

facts.caveat: Published 15 November 2019. The Hindustan Times also wrote of 'two' PILs and dated the 2018 referral to 28 August 2018; both details are unconfirmed or wrong (the referral order is dated 24 September 2018).

text.en: By 2018 only 77 of 185 countries (42%) had laws explicitly criminalising marital rape; in 34 countries marital rape was not criminalised and a wife could not file a criminal complaint of rape against her husband, and 12 countries still let rapists escape prosecution by marrying the victim, according to UN Women.
text.hg: UN Women ke mutabik, 2018 tak 185 mein se sirf 77 deshon (42%) mein aise kanoon the jo marital rape ko saaf taur par apradh ghoshit karte hain; 34 deshon mein marital rape apradh nahin tha aur patni apne pati ke khilaf rape ki criminal complaint darj nahin kara sakti thi, aur 12 deshon mein rapist us samay bhi victim se shaadi karke prosecution se bach sakte the.

facts.caveat: UN Women's figure note says the data come from the World Bank and are current as of 1 June 2017, so 'by 2018' describes mid-2017 law. 108 of 185 countries (58%) did not explicitly criminalise marital rape (our subtraction). Some countries have reformed their laws since.

text.en: Forty-three countries have no legislation at all addressing marital rape, and 35 of the 54 Commonwealth countries still apply some form of marital exemption to sexual offences, according to UNFPA's State of World Population 2021, which cites a 2020 study.
text.hg: UNFPA ki 'State of World Population 2021' report ke mutabik, jo 2020 ki ek study ka hawala deti hai, forty-three deshon mein marital rape se juda koi kanoon hai hi nahin, aur 54 Commonwealth deshon mein se 35 ab bhi sexual offences mein kisi na kisi roop mein marital exemption laagu karte hain.

facts.caveat: UN agencies use different country samples and definitions, so this count differs from UN Women's 2018 figures. India is a Commonwealth member with a marital exemption.

text.en: Of 131 countries with data, just 38% have consent-based rape laws that explicitly criminalise marital rape, and only 23% set 18 as the minimum age of marriage without exception, according to the UN's SDG Report 2026.
text.hg: UN ki SDG Report 2026 ke mutabik, jin 131 deshon ka data upalabdh hai, unmein se sirf 38% mein consent par aadhaarit aise rape kanoon hain jo marital rape ko saaf taur par apradh maante hain, aur sirf 23% bina kisi exception ke shaadi ki minimum umar 18 saal tay karte hain.

facts.caveat: 38% of 131 is about 50 countries, leaving roughly 81 whose rape laws are either not consent-based or do not explicitly cover marital rape (our calculation). The indicator combines both conditions, so it is not a pure count of countries that criminalise marital rape. The SDG Report 2025 gave 29% (38 countries) for the age-18 rule in 2024; the 2026 report does not explain the lower 23%.

text.en: In 2024, only 63 of 131 countries (48%) had rape laws based on lack of consent and only 38 (29%) set 18 as the minimum marriage age without exceptions, according to the UN's SDG Report 2025.
text.hg: UN ki SDG Report 2025 ke mutabik, 2024 mein 131 mein se sirf 63 deshon (48%) mein consent na hone par aadhaarit rape kanoon the, aur sirf 38 deshon (29%) ne bina kisi exception ke shaadi ki minimum umar 18 saal tay ki thi.

facts.value: 63 of 131 consent-based rape laws; 38 with 18 without exceptions
facts.caveat: SDG indicator 5.1.1 legal-framework data (UN Women, World Bank, OECD Development Centre).

text.en: India's Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the Indian Penal Code, keeps the marital rape exception: Exception 2 to Section 63 says sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under 18, is not rape, while Section 67 punishes non-consensual sex with a wife living separately with two to seven years in prison.
text.hg: Indian Penal Code (IPC) ki jagah lene wali Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 mein marital rape ka exception barkaraar hai: Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki kisi purush ka apni patni ke saath, jiski umar 18 saal se kam na ho, sexual intercourse ya sexual acts rape nahin hain, jabki Section 67 alag reh rahi patni ke saath bina consent ke sex ke liye do se saat saal ki jail ki saza ka provision karta hai.

facts.caveat: The age in the exception is 18, in line with the Supreme Court's 2017 Independent Thought ruling. As of 20 November 2026 the Supreme Court had not ruled on the challenge to the exception and said it would hear it on 9 or 10 December 2026; re-check before publishing (see the law-framework facts).

text.en: In July 2014 the UN CEDAW Committee urged India to amend its criminal law so that marital rape is defined as a criminal offence, repeating a request from its previous review of India in 2007, and to implement the Justice Verma Committee's recommendations on violence against women.
text.hg: July 2014 mein UN ki CEDAW Committee ne India se aagrah kiya ki woh apne criminal law mein sanshodhan kare taaki marital rape ko criminal offence ke roop mein define kiya jaaye, aur is tarah India ke 2007 ke apne pichhle review mein ki gayi maang dohrayi; committee ne violence against women par Justice Verma Committee ki sifarishein laagu karne ka bhi aagrah kiya.

facts.caveat: The previous review (CEDAW/C/IND/CO/3) took place in 2007. These remain the latest concluding observations on India: under the simplified procedure India's combined sixth and seventh report is due on 3 February 2027 (see gl-cedaw-india-loipr-2026).

text.en: Across 78 countries with data for 2025, 75.4% of married or partnered women aged 15-49 said they could refuse sex, but only 56.3% had full decision-making power over sex, contraception and their own health care, according to the UN's SDG Report 2026.
text.hg: UN ki SDG Report 2026 ke mutabik, 2025 ke data wale 78 deshon mein 15-49 saal ki shaadishuda ya kisi partner ke saath relationship mein reh rahi 75.4% mahilaon ne kaha ki woh sex se inkaar kar sakti hain, lekin sirf 56.3% ke paas sex, contraception aur apni health care par faisle lene ka poora adhikaar tha.

facts.caveat: SDG indicator 5.6.1; country coverage is limited to 78 countries with survey data.

text.en: UNODC's International Classification of Crime for Statistical Purposes (2015) warns that national crime statistics follow each country's own criminal law, so the same act can be classed under very different provisions or be a crime in one country and not another, and that only a varying share of offences is ever reported and recorded, which makes cross-country crime comparisons particularly difficult.
text.hg: UNODC ka 'International Classification of Crime for Statistical Purposes' (2015) chetavni deta hai ki national crime statistics har desh ke apne criminal law ke hisaab se bante hain, isliye ek hi act bilkul alag-alag provisions mein darj ho sakta hai, ya ek desh mein crime ho sakta hai aur doosre mein nahin; saath hi crimes ka sirf ek hissa hi kabhi report aur record hota hai, aur yeh hissa alag-alag hota hai; in wajahon se alag-alag deshon ke crime data ki tulna khaas taur par mushkil ho jaati hai.

facts.caveat: India's legal definition of rape widened in 2013 and still excludes marital rape of adult wives, so Indian police counts measure a narrower set of acts than some other countries' counts.

text.en: In most countries with data, fewer than 40% of women who experienced violence sought help of any kind, and in almost all of them fewer than 10% of those who sought help went to the police, according to the UN's World's Women 2015 report.
text.hg: UN ki 'World's Women 2015' report ke mutabik, jin deshon ka data upalabdh hai, unmein se zyadatar mein violence jhelne wali 40% se kam mahilaon ne kisi bhi tarah ki madad maangi, aur lagbhag sabhi deshon mein madad maangne wali mahilaon mein se 10% se kam police ke paas gayin.

facts.value: <40% sought any help; <10% of help-seekers went to police
facts.caveat: Survey data from various years before 2015; it explains why police-recorded rape figures capture only a small fraction of sexual violence.

text.en: In a list of issues dated 5 February 2026, the UN CEDAW Committee asked India what steps it has taken to review the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita to criminalise marital rape, as the Committee had requested in its previous concluding observations, and asked for data on the prevalence of female genital mutilation/cutting and any plans and timeline for a law prohibiting it; India's combined sixth and seventh periodic report is due on 3 February 2027.
text.hg: In a list of issues dated 5 February 2026, the UN CEDAW Committee asked India what steps it has taken to review the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita to criminalise marital rape, as the Committee had requested in its previous concluding observations, and asked for data on the prevalence of female genital mutilation/cutting and any plans and timeline for a law prohibiting it; India's combined sixth and seventh periodic report is due on 3 February 2027.

facts.value: CEDAW/C/IND/QPR/6-7 (5 Feb 2026), paras 10(d) and 11(a); report due 3 Feb 2027
facts.caveat: A list of issues is a set of questions, not a finding. The document is dated 5 February 2026 and its footnote says it was adopted at the Committee's 92nd session (2-20 February 2026); OHCHR lists the State report as due on 3 February 2027.

text.en: In an exploratory online survey by Sahiyo, a group of Dawoodi Bohra women campaigning against khatna, run from July 2015 to January 2016 and released in February 2017, 80% of 385 Bohra women respondents (34% of them living in India) said they had undergone khatna, and 82% said they were unlikely to continue it on their daughters.
text.hg: In an exploratory online survey by Sahiyo, a group of Dawoodi Bohra women campaigning against khatna, run from July 2015 to January 2016 and released in February 2017, 80% of 385 Bohra women respondents (34% of them living in India) said they had undergone khatna, and 82% said they were unlikely to continue it on their daughters.

facts.value: 80% of 385 respondents cut; 82% unlikely to cut their daughters; 34% of respondents in India
facts.caveat: Snowball sample of English-literate internet users recruited through an anti-khatna group's networks (80% held at least a bachelor's degree); it cannot estimate prevalence. Only 34% of respondents lived in India (31% in the US). Self-reported survey answers. India has no official prevalence data (see gl-bohra-no-official-data-2017).
